children.text:
Pañcaviṃśatisāhasrikā prajñāpāramitā
00101 namo bhagavadyai āryaprajñāpāramitāyai//
children.translated_text:
<s>Pañcaviṃśatisāhasrikā Prajñāpāramitā</s> (The Perfection of Wisdom in Twenty-Five Thousand Lines)
Homage to the Blessed Noble <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> (Perfection of Wisdom)!

children.text:
00102 nirvikalpe namas tubhyaṃ prajñāpāramite 'mite/
00103 yā tvaṃ sarvān avadyāṅgi niravadyair nirīkṣyase//
children.translated_text: Homage to you, O <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> (Perfection of Wisdom), who are beyond conceptual elaboration and immeasurable! You, O faultless one, are beheld by those who are without fault.

children.text: 00104 ākāśam iva nirlepāṃ niṣprapañcāṃ nirakṣarām//
children.translated_text: Like space, you are unstained, free from conceptual proliferation, and beyond syllables.

children.text: 00105 yas tvāṃ paśyati bhāvena sa paśyati tathāgatam//
children.translated_text: Whoever sees you as a real entity, that one sees the <s>Tathāgata</s>.

children.text:
00106 tava cāryaguṇādyāyā buddhasya ca jagadguroḥ/
00107 na paśyanty antaraṃ santaś candracandrikayor iva//
children.translated_text: Between you, O lady of noble qualities, and the <s>Buddha</s>, the teacher of the world, the wise ones perceive no difference, as between the moon and moonlight.

children.text:
00108 kṛpātmakāḥ prapadya tvāṃ buddhadharmapuraḥsarām/
00109 sukhenāyānti māhātmām atulaṃ bhaktivatsale//
children.translated_text: Those whose nature is compassion, taking refuge in you who are accompanied by the <s>buddhadharmas</s> (qualities of a Buddha), easily attain great majesty, the incomparable one, O you who are tender toward the devoted.

children.text:
00110 sakṛd apy āśaye śuddhe yas tvāṃ vidhivad īkṣate/
00111 tenāpi niyataṃ siddhiḥ prāpyate 'moghadarśane//
children.translated_text: Whoever, even once, with a pure mind, beholds you in the proper manner, that one too surely attains accomplishment, O you of unfailing vision.

children.text:
00201 sarveṣām api vīrāṇāṃ parārthe niyatātmanām/
00202 poṣikā janayitrī ca mātā tvam asi vatsalā//
children.translated_text: Of all the heroes whose minds are set on the welfare of others, you are the nourisher, the mother who gives birth, tender and loving.

children.text:
00203 yad buddhā lokaguravaḥ putrās tava kṛpālavaḥ/
00204 tena tvam asi kalyāṇi sarvasattvapitāmahī//
children.translated_text: Since the <s>Buddhas</s>, those compassionate teachers of the world, are your sons, therefore, O auspicious one, you are the grandmother of all beings.

children.text:
00205 sarvapāramitābhis tvaṃ nirmalābhir anindite/
00206 candralekheva tārābhir anuyātāsi sarvadā//
children.translated_text: You are always accompanied by all the <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections), which are pure, O blameless one, like the crescent moon by the stars.

children.text:
00207 vineyaṃ janamāsādya tatra tatra tathāgathaiḥ/
00208 bahurūpā tvam evaikā nānānāmabhir īḍyase//
children.translated_text: Having found beings to be trained, you, though one, assume many forms and are praised by the <s>Tathāgatas</s> in various places under many names.

children.text:
00209 prabhāṃ prāpyeva dīptāṃśor avaśyāyodabindavaḥ/
00210 tvāṃ prāpya pralayaṃ yānti doṣā vādāś ca vādinām//
children.translated_text: Just as dewdrops dissolve upon reaching the radiance of the blazing sun, so the faults and doctrines of disputants dissolve upon reaching you.

children.text:
00211 tvam eva trāsajananī bālānāṃ bhīmadarśanā/
00212 āśvāsajananī cāsi viduṣāṃ saumyadarśanā//
children.translated_text: You yourself are the source of terror for the childish, fearsome in appearance, yet you are also the source of reassurance for the wise, gentle in appearance.

children.text:
00213 yasya tvayy apy abhiṣvaṅgas tvannāthasya na vidyate/
00214 tasyāṃba katham anyatra rāgadveṣau bhaviṣyataḥ//
children.translated_text: When even toward you there is no attachment for one whose lord you are, O mother, how then could passion and hatred arise in him toward anything else?

children.text:
00215 nāgacchasi kutaś cittaṃ na ca kvacana gacchasi/
00216 sthāneṣv api ca sarveṣu vidvadbhir nopalabhyase//
children.translated_text: You do not come from anywhere, O mind, nor do you go anywhere; and in all places you are not apprehended by the wise.

children.text:
00217 ye tvām evaṃ na paśyanti prapadyante ca bhāvataḥ/
00218 prapadya ca vimucyante tad idaṃ mahad adbhutam//
children.translated_text: Those who do not see you thus yet take refuge in you sincerely, and having taken refuge are liberated—this indeed is a great wonder.

children.text:
00301 tvām eva badhyate paśyann apaśyann api badhyate/
00302 tvām eva mucyate paśyann apaśyann api mucyate//
children.translated_text: One who sees you is bound, and one who does not see you is also bound; one who sees you is liberated, and one who does not see you is also liberated.

children.text:
00303 aho vismayanīyāsi gambhīrāsi yaśasvinī/
00304 sudurbodhāsi māyeva dṛśyase na ca dṛśyase//
children.translated_text: Ah, you are wondrous! You are profound and glorious! You are very hard to understand; like an illusion, you are seen and yet not seen.

children.text:
00305 buddhaiḥ prayekabuddhaiś ca śrāvakaiś ca niṣevitā/
00306 mārgas tvam eko mokṣasya nāsty anya iti niścayaḥ//
children.translated_text: Frequented by <s>Buddhas</s>, <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, and <s>Śrāvakas</s> alike, you are the one path to liberation—there is no other. This is certain.

children.text:
00307 vyavahāraṃ puraskṛtya prajñaptyarthaṃ śarīriṇām/
00308 kṛpayā lokanāthais tvam ucyase ca na cocyase//
children.translated_text: For the sake of conventional usage, for the purpose of designation to embodied beings, you are spoken of by the protectors of the world out of compassion—and yet you are not spoken of.

children.text:
00309 śaktaḥ kas tvām iha stotuṃ nirnimittāṃ nirañjanām/
00310 sarvavāgvisayātītā yā tvaṃ kvacid aniḥśritā//
children.translated_text: Who here is capable of praising you, who are without cause, without stain, who have transcended the domain of all speech, and who are not established anywhere?

children.text:
00311 saty evam api saṃvṛtyā vākpathair vayam īdṛśaiḥ/
00312 tvām astutyām api stutvā tuṣṭūṣantaḥ sunirvṛtāaḥ/
00313 prajñāpāramitāṃ stutvā yan mayopacitaṃ śubham/
00314 tenās tv āśu jagat kṛtsnaṃ prajñāpāraparāyaṇam//
children.translated_text:
Even so, through conventional usage, with such paths of speech, having praised you who are beyond praise, we are content and well-satisfied.
Having praised the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> (Perfection of Wisdom), may the merit I have accumulated thereby cause the entire world to quickly become devoted to the far shore of wisdom!

children.text:
00401 evaṃ mayā śrutam/ ekasmin samaye bhagavān rājagṛhe viharati sma
00402 gṛdhrakūṭe parvate mahatā bhikṣusaṃghena sārdhaṃ pañcamātrair bhikṣusahasraiḥ sarvair arhadbhiḥ
00403 kṣīṇāsravair niṣkleśair vaśībhūtaiḥ suvimuktacittaiḥ suvimuktaprajñair ājāneyai-
00404 r mahānāgaiḥ kṛtakṛtyaiḥ kṛtakaraṇīyair apahṛtabhārair anuprāprasvakārthaiḥ parikṣīṇa-
00405 bhavasaṃyojanaiḥ samyagājñāsuvimuktacittaiḥ sarvacetovaśiparamapāramitāprāptaiḥ,
00406 pañcamātrair bhikṣuṇīśatair upāsakair upāsikābhiś ca sārdhaṃ sarvair dṛṣṭadharmair apari-
00407 māṇairś ca bodhisattvakoṭīniyutaśatasahasraiḥ sārdhaṃ sarvair dhāraṇīpratilabdhaiḥ
00408 śūnyatāvihāribhir animittagocaraiḥ praṇidhānākalpitaiḥ kṣāntisamatāprati-
00409 labdhair asaṅgadhāraṇīpratilabdhair acyutābhijñair ādeyavacanair akuhakair alapakair arapagata-
00410 jñātralābhacittair nirāmiṣadharmadeśakair gaṃbhīradharmakṣāntipāraṃgatair vaiśāradya-
00411 prāptair mārakarmasamatikrāntaiḥ karmāvaraṇapratiprasrabdhair dharmapravicayavibhakti-
00412 nirdeśakuśalair asaṃkhyeyakalpapraṇidhānasusamārabdhaiḥ smitamukhaiḥ pūrvālāpibhi-
00413 r vigatabhṛkuṭīmukhair gāthābhir gītālapanakuśalair apagatalīnacittair anācchedyaprati-
00414 bhānair anantaparṣadabhibhavanavaiśāradyasamanvāgair anantakalpakoṭīniḥsaraṇakuśalai-
00415 r māyāmarīcidakacandrasvapnapratiśrutkāpratibhāsapratibimbanirmāṇopamadharmā-
children.translated_text: Thus have I heard. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at <s>Rājagṛha</s>, on <s>Gṛdhrakūṭa</s> (Vulture Peak) mountain, together with a great assembly of <s>bhikṣus</s> (monks), with approximately five thousand <s>bhikṣus</s>, all of them <s>arhats</s> (worthy ones), whose <s>āsravas</s> (outflows) were exhausted, who were free from <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), who had attained mastery, whose minds and wisdom were well-liberated, who were thoroughbreds, great <s>nāgas</s> (serpent-beings), who had done what was to be done, who had accomplished their task, who had laid down their burden, who had attained their own goal, whose bonds of existence were completely destroyed, whose minds were well-liberated through right knowledge, who had reached the supreme perfection of mastery over all minds; together with approximately five hundred <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s> (nuns), <s>upāsakas</s> (male lay followers), and <s>upāsikās</s> (female lay followers), all of whom had seen the truth; and together with immeasurable hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭi-niyutas</s> of <s>bodhisattvas</s>, all of whom had attained <s>dhāraṇī</s> (power of retention), who dwelt in <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness), whose domain was <s>animitta</s> (signlessness), who were unshaped by <s>praṇidhāna</s> (aspiration), who had attained the equanimity of <s>kṣānti</s> (patience), who had obtained unobstructed <s>dhāraṇī</s>, who possessed unfailing <s>abhijñā</s> (supernatural knowledge), whose words were to be heeded, who were without hypocrisy and without guile, whose minds were free from craving for gain and renown, who taught the <s>Dharma</s> without worldly motivation, who had reached the far shore of patience regarding the profound <s>Dharma</s>, who had attained fearlessness, who had transcended the work of <s>Māra</s>, who had calmed the obscuration of <s>karma</s>, who were skilled in the analysis, classification, and exposition of <s>Dharma</s>, whose noble efforts had been well-initiated through aspirations over incalculable <s>kalpas</s> (aeons), who bore smiling faces, who spoke first, whose brows were unfurrowed, who were skilled in verses, songs, and playful discourse, whose minds were free from torpor, whose ready wit was unbreakable, who possessed the fearlessness of prevailing over infinite assemblies, who were skilled in traversing infinite <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s>, who had the conviction that all <s>dharmas</s> are like

children.text:
00501 dhimuktaiḥ sattvagaticaritasūkṣmanānādhimuktyavatārakuśalair apratihatacittai-
00502 r adhimātraksāntisamanvāgatair yāthātmāvatāraṇakuśalaiḥ sarvabuddhakṣetraānantavyūha-
00503 praṇidhānaprasthānaparigṛhītair asaṃkhyeyalokadhātubuddhānusmṛtisamāhita-
00504 satatasamitābhimukhībhūtair aparimitabuddhādhyeṣaṇakuśalair nānādṛṣṭyanuśayaparyava-
00505 sthānakleśapraśamanakuśalaiḥ samādhivikrīḍitaśatasahasranirhārakuśalaiḥ tad yathā
00506 bhadrapālena ca bodhisattvena mahāsattvena ratnākareṇa ca sārthavāhena ca nara-
00507 dattena ca varuṇadattena ca śubhaguptena ca indradattena ca uttaramatinā ca viśeṣa-
00508 matinā ca vardhamānamatinā ca amoghadarśinā ca susamprasthitena ca suvi-
00509 krāntavikramiṇā ca nityodyuktena ca anikṣiptadhureṇa ca sūryagarbheṇa ca
00510 anupamacintinā ca avalokiteśvareṇa ca mahāsthāmaprāptena ca mañju-
00511 śriyā ca vajramatinā ca ratnamudrāhastena ca nityokṣiptahastena ca maitre-
00512 yeṇa ca bodhisattvena mahāsattvena evam pramukhair anekair bodhisattvakoṭīniyuta-
00513 śatasahasraiḥ sārdham/
00514 atha khalu bhagavān svayam eva siṃhāsanaṃ prajñapya nyaṣīdat paryaṅkaṃ baddhvā
00515 ṛjukāyaṃ praṇidhāya abhimukhīṃ smṛtim upasthāpya samādhirājaṃ nāma
00516 samādhiṃ samāpadyate sma yatra sarvasamādhayo 'ntargamān saṃgrahaṃ samava-
00517 saraṇaṃ gacchanti/
00518 atha khalu bhagavān smṛtimān samprajānaṃs tasmāt samādher vyutthāya
children.translated_text:
illusions, mirages, the reflection of the moon in water, dreams, echoes, appearances, reflections, and magical creations; who were skilled in penetrating the subtle variety of aspirations, conducts, and dispositions of beings; whose minds were unobstructed; who were endowed with the highest patience; who were skilled in penetrating things as they really are; who had embraced the departure through aspirations for the infinite arrays of all <s>buddhakṣetras</s> (buddha-fields); who were settled in the <s>buddhānusmṛti-samādhi</s> (concentration of recollecting the Buddha) in innumerable world-realms, constantly and continuously facing [the Buddhas]; who were skilled in requesting the immeasurable <s>Buddhas</s> [to teach]; who were skilled in pacifying the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), latent tendencies, entanglements, and various wrong views; who were skilled in producing hundreds of thousands of <s>samādhi</s> (concentration) displays—namely: the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Bhadrapāla</s>, and <s>Ratnākara</s>, and <s>Sārthavāha</s>, and <s>Naradatta</s>, and <s>Varuṇadatta</s>, and <s>Śubhagupta</s>, and <s>Indradatta</s>, and <s>Uttaramati</s>, and <s>Viśeṣamati</s>, and <s>Vardhamānamati</s>, and <s>Amoghadarśin</s>, and <s>Susamprasthita</s>, and <s>Suvikrāntavikramin</s>, and <s>Nityodyukta</s>, and <s>Anikṣiptadhura</s>, and <s>Sūryagarbha</s>, and <s>Anupamacintrin</s>, and <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, and <s>Mahāsthāmaprāpta</s>, and <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, and <s>Vajramati</s>, and <s>Ratnamudrāhasta</s>, and <s>Nityotkṣiptahasta</s>, and the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Maitreya</s>—led by these, together with many hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭi-niyutas</s> of <s>bodhisattvas</s>.
Then the Blessed One himself prepared a lion-throne and sat down, crossing his legs, holding his body erect, establishing mindfulness face-to-face, and entered the <s>samādhi</s> (concentration) called <s>Samādhirāja</s> (King of Concentrations), wherein all <s>samādhis</s> find their entry, their inclusion, and their convergence.
Then the Blessed One, mindful and fully aware, arose from that <s>samādhi</s>

children.text:
00601 divyena cakṣuṣā sarvalokadhātuṃ vyavalokya sarvakāyāt smitam akarot/
00602 tasyādhastāt pādatalayoḥ sahasrārābhyāṃ cakrābhyāṃ ṣaṣṭiṣaṣṭīraśmikoṭī-
00603 niyutaśatasahasrāṇi niśceruḥ daśabhyaḥ pādāṅgulibhyaḥ ṣaṣṭiṣaṣṭīraśmikoṭī-
00604 niyutaśatasahasrāṇi niśceruḥ/ evaṃ ṣaṣṭiṣaṣṭigulphābhyāṃ ṣaṣṭiṣaṣṭir jaṃghābhyāṃ
00605 ṣaṣṭiṣaṣṭir jānumaṇḍalābhyām evaṃ dvābhyām ūrubhyāṃ kaṭinābhimaṇḍalābhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ
00606 pārśvābhyāṃ hṛdayaśrīvatsāt mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇāt/ evaṃ ṣaṣṭiṣaṣṭir daśabhyo
00607 hastāṅgulibhyaḥ ṣaṣṭiṣaṣṭir dvābhyāṃ bāhubhyāṃ ṣaṣṭiṣaṣṭir dvābhyām aṃśābhyām evaṃ grīvā-
00608 yāś catvāriṃśadbhyo dantebhyo dvābhyāṃ ghrāṇābhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ śrotrābhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ
00609 cakṣurbhyāṃ madhyādūrṇāyā upariṣṭād uṣṇīṣāt ṣaṣṭiṣaṣṭī raśmikoṭīniyuta-
00610 śatasahasrāṇi niśceruḥ yai raśmibhir ayaṃ trisāhasramahāsāhasro lokadhāur a-
00611 vabhāsito 'bhūt parisphuṭaḥ/ pūrvasyāṃ diśi gaṅgānadīvālukopamā loka-
00612 dhātavas tena mahatā raśmyavabhāsena sphuṭā avabhāsitāś cābhūvan/ evaṃ dakṣi-
00613 ṇasyāṃ diśi paścimāyām uttarasyām uttarapūrvasyāṃ pūrvadakṣiṇasyāṃ dakṣiṇapaścimāyāṃ
00614 paścimottarasyām adhastād upariṣṭād diśi gaṅgānadīvālukopamā lokadhātava-
00615 s tena mahatā raśmyavabhāsena sphuṭā avabhāsitāś cābhūvan/ ye ca sattvās tena
00616 mahatā raśmyavabhāsena sphuṭā avabhāsitās te sarve niyatā abhūvan anu-
00617 ttarāyāṃ samyaksambodhau/
children.translated_text: Having surveyed the entire world-realm with the divine eye, he produced a smile from his entire body. From the undersides of his feet, from the two wheels with their thousand spokes, sixty times sixty <s>koṭi</s>-<s>niyuta</s>-hundred-thousands of rays issued forth. From his ten toes, sixty times sixty <s>koṭi</s>-<s>niyuta</s>-hundred-thousands of rays issued forth. Likewise, sixty times sixty from both ankles; sixty times sixty from both shins; sixty times sixty from both kneecaps; likewise from both thighs, from the hip and navel circles, from both sides, from the <s>śrīvatsa</s> on the heart — the mark of a <s>mahāpuruṣa</s> (great being). Likewise, sixty times sixty from the ten fingers of his hands; sixty times sixty from both arms; sixty times sixty from both shoulders; likewise from the neck, from the forty teeth, from both nostrils, from both ears, from both eyes, from the <s>ūrṇā</s> (mid-brow curl) in the center, from the <s>uṣṇīṣa</s> (crown protuberance) above — sixty times sixty <s>koṭi</s>-<s>niyuta</s>-hundred-thousands of rays issued forth. By those rays, this entire trichiliocosm was illuminated and made radiant. In the eastern direction, world-realms as numerous as the sands of the river <s>Gaṅgā</s> became radiant and illuminated by that great flood of light. Likewise in the southern direction, the western, the northern, the northeastern, the southeastern, the southwestern, the northwestern, below, and above — world-realms as numerous as the sands of the river <s>Gaṅgā</s> became radiant and illuminated by that great flood of light. And all those beings who were touched and illuminated by that great flood of light became destined for <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> (supreme, perfect awakening).

children.text:
00701 atha khalu bhagavān punar eva sarvaromakūpebhyaḥ smitam akarot/ evakikataś ca
00702 romakūpāt ṣaṣṭiṣaṣṭīraśmikoṭīniyutaśatasahasrāṇi niśceruḥ/ yair ayaṃ
00703 trisāhasramahāsāhasro lokadhātur avabhāsitaḥ sphuṭo 'bhūt/ taiś ca pūrvasyāṃ
00704 diśi gaṅgānadīvālukopamāḥ sarvalokadhātavo 'vabhāsenāvabhāsitāḥ sphuṭā-
00705 ś cābhūvan/ evaṃ dakṣiṇasyāṃ {{diśi paścimāyām uttarasyām uttarapūrvasyāṃ pūrvadakṣiṇasyāṃ dakṣiṇapaścimāyāṃ paścimottarasyām adhastād upariṣṭād diśi gaṅgānadīvālukopamā lokadhātavas tena mahatā raśmyavabhāsena sphuṭā avabhāsitāś cābhūvan/ ye ca sattvās tena mahatā raśmyavabhāsena sphuṭā avabhāsitās te sarve niyatā abhūvan anuttarāyāṃ}} samyak-
00706 sambodhau/
00707 atha khalu bhagavān punar eva yā sā buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ prakṛtiprabhā tayā
00708 prabhayā trisāhasramahāsāhasraṃ lokadhātum avabhāsayāmāsa/ yāvat sarvāsu
00709 daśasu dikṣu ekaikasyāṃ diśi gaṅgānadīvālukopamā lokadhātavayas tā
00710 prabhayā avabhāsitā abhūvan/ ye ca sattvās tayā prabhayā spṛṣṭās te sarve
00711 niyatā abhūvan anuttarāyāṃ samyaksambodhau//
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One again produced a smile from all his pores. From each and every pore, sixty times sixty <s>koṭi</s>-<s>niyuta</s>-hundred-thousands of rays issued forth, by which this entire trichiliocosm was illuminated and made radiant. By those [rays], in the eastern direction, all world-realms as numerous as the sands of the river <s>Gaṅgā</s> were illuminated and made radiant. Likewise in the southern direction, the western, the northern, the northeastern, the southeastern, the southwestern, the northwestern, below, and above — world-realms as numerous as the sands of the river <s>Gaṅgā</s> were illuminated and made radiant by that great flood of light. And all those beings who were touched and illuminated by that great flood of light became destined for <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> (supreme, perfect awakening). Then the Blessed One again, with that natural radiance which belongs to the <s>Buddhas</s>, Blessed Ones — with that radiance he illuminated the trichiliocosm. And in all ten directions, in each and every direction, world-realms as numerous as the sands of the river <s>Gaṅgā</s> were illuminated by that radiance. And all those beings who were touched by that radiance became destined for <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> (supreme, perfect awakening).

children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, at that moment, extended his tongue-faculty, with which he covered this entire trichiliocosm. And those beings who heard that <s>Dharma</s>-teaching became destined for <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> (supreme, perfect awakening). Then the Blessed One, seated on that very lion-throne, entered the <s>samādhi</s> (meditative absorption) called <s>Siṃhavikrīḍita</s> (Lion's Sport). He performed a miraculous transformation of such a kind that, by means of that miraculous transformation, this trichiliocosm trembled in six ways: it trembled, greatly trembled, and trembled all around; it shook, greatly shook, and shook all around; it quaked, greatly quaked, and quaked all around; it rumbled, greatly rumbled, and rumbled all around; it surged, greatly surged, and surged all around; it roared, greatly roared, and roared all around. At the edges it rose up while the center sank down; at the center it rose up while the edges sank down. It was gentle, smooth, and delightful to all beings. Then, in that very instant, all the hells, animal realms, and realms of <s>Yama</s> (the dead) in this trichiliocosm were completely emptied and made void. All inopportune births disappeared. And those beings who passed away from those destinies — from the hells, the animal realms, and the realms of <s>Yama</s> — all of them, with that very joy and delight, were reborn among the community of humans. Likewise, they were reborn among the community of the <s>Cāturmahārājika</s> gods, the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> (Thirty-Three) gods, the <s>Yāma</s> gods, the <s>Tuṣita</s> gods, the <s>Nirmāṇarati</s> gods, and the <s>Paranirmitavaśavartin</s> gods.

children.translated_text: Then those humans and those gods, by the power of the Blessed One, remembered their former births. Having remembered, with that very joy and delight, they approached the Blessed One. Having approached, they bowed their heads at the feet of the Blessed One, and with palms joined together, they paid homage to the Blessed One. Thus, in the eastern direction, in world-realms as numerous as the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> river, in the southern, western, and northern directions, in the intermediate quarters, above, below, and on every side in the ten directions, in each quarter, in world-realms as numerous as the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> river, all hells, all animal realms, and all realms of <s>Yama</s> (the dead) were cut off and became empty. All inopportune births ceased. And those beings who passed away from those destinies of hell, animal birth, and the realm of <s>Yama</s> were all reborn among gods and humans. And those who were reborn among gods and humans, by the power of the Blessed One, remembered their former abodes. Having remembered, with that very joy and delight, they approached the <s>Buddhas</s> and Blessed Ones who had arisen in their respective <s>buddhakṣetras</s> (buddha-fields). Having approached and having bowed at the feet of those <s>Buddhas</s> and Blessed Ones, they all stood with palms joined together and paid homage to the Blessed One. Then, those beings in this <s>trisāhasramahāsāhasra lokadhātu</s> (trichiliocosm) who were blind from birth saw forms with their eyes. Deaf beings heard sounds with their ears. The insane regained their mindfulness. Those with distracted minds became single-pointed in mind. The hungry became full-bowled. The thirsty became free from thirst. Those afflicted with disease became free from disease. Those with deficient faculties became endowed with complete faculties. Those not free from unwholesome bodily, verbal, and mental actions and livelihood became free from unwholesome bodily, verbal, and mental actions and livelihood,

They became celibate, pure, free from the odor of illness, and all beings were endowed with all happiness. The <s>Buddhas</s> and Blessed Ones abiding in other <s>buddhakṣetras</s> uttered this <s>udāna</s> (inspired utterance): "Excellent is taming! Excellent is restraint! Excellent is the dwelling in the holy life of a hero! Excellent is non-harmfulness toward living beings!" Then the Blessed One, seated upon that very lion-throne, surpassing this <s>trisāhasramahāsāhasra lokadhātu</s> (trichiliocosm), the <s>Tathāgata</s> abided, shone, blazed, and radiated with splendor, beauty, glory, and brilliance. Just as <s>Sumeru</s>, the king of mountains, surpassing all mountains, abides and shines with brilliance, even so, the Blessed One, surpassing all world-realms, abided and shone with brilliance. And the beings in those world-realms as numerous as the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> — all of them beheld this <s>Sahā</s> world-realm and <s>Śākyamuni</s> <s>Tathāgata</s> together with the community of monks. When this was said, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnākara</s> addressed the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Samantaraśmi</s> thus: 'There is, son of good family, in the western direction from here, passing beyond world-realms as numerous as the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, a world-realm called <s>Sahā</s>. There the <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Śākyamuni</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly and Fully Awakened One, abides, endures, and maintains himself. He is now fully illuminating the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> (Perfection of Wisdom) for <s>bodhisattvas</s> <s>mahāsattvas</s> — such is the power of that (teaching).' Then the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Samantaraśmi</s> addressed the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnākara</s> thus: 'I wish to go, Blessed One, to that <s>Sahā</s> world-realm, to see, honor, and attend upon that <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Śākyamuni</s>, and also those <s>bodhisattvas</s> <s>mahāsattvas</s>, most of whom are in the youthful stage (<s>kumārabhūta</s>), who have attained <s>dhāraṇīs</s> (retentive powers), are skilled in the production of <s>samādhis</s> (concentrations), and have reached the perfection of mastery over all <s>samādhis</s>.' The Blessed One said: 'Go, son of good family, whenever you think it is the right time.' Then the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnākara</s> gave to the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Samantaraśmi</s> thousand-petaled lotuses made of various jewels, shining with golden radiance: 'With these lotuses, son of good family, scatter offerings upon that <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Śākyamuni</s>. And speak thus: "The Blessed One <s>Ratnākara</s> inquires of the Blessed One about his health, whether he has few ailments, few troubles, lightness in rising, comfort in his activities, strength, and pleasant abiding. And these lotuses have been sent by that Blessed One, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnākara</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly and Fully Awakened One, for the Blessed One." And you, son of good family, should be fully aware in that <s>buddhakṣetra</s> (buddha-field). For what reason? Because those <s>bodhisattvas</s> who have been reborn in that <s>Sahā</s> world-realm are difficult to approach.'

children.translated_text: Then the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Samantaraśmi</s>, having received from the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnākara</s> those thousand-petaled lotuses made of various jewels, shining with golden radiance, together with many hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>niyutas</s> of <s>bodhisattvas</s>, householders and renunciants, boys and girls — surrounded and attended by them — in the eastern direction, in those world-realms as numerous as the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, honoring, venerating, respecting, and worshiping the <s>Buddhas</s>, Blessed Ones, with flowers, incense, fragrances, garlands, unguents, powders, robes, parasols, banners, flags, and victory-standards, he arrived at this <s>Sahā</s> world-realm. And he approached <s>Śākyamuni</s> <s>Tathāgata</s>. Having approached, he bowed down with his head at the feet of the Blessed One and stood to one side. Standing to one side, the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Samantaraśmi</s> addressed the Blessed One <s>Śākyamuni</s> thus: 'The Blessed One <s>Ratnākara</s> inquires of the Blessed One about his health, whether he has few ailments, few troubles, lightness in rising, comfort in his activities, strength, and pleasant abiding. And these thousand-petaled lotuses made of various jewels, shining with golden radiance, have been sent by that Blessed One, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnākara</s>, for the Blessed One.' Then the Blessed One <s>Śākyamuni</s> <s>Tathāgata</s>, having received those lotuses, cast them toward those world-realms as numerous as the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> in the eastern direction. And those world-realms were fully covered with those lotuses. Upon those lotuses sat figures of <s>Buddhas</s>, and in those <s>buddhakṣetras</s> they taught the <s>Dharma</s> — namely, this very teaching of the <s>Dharma</s> connected with the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> (Perfection of Wisdom). And whatever beings heard that <s>Dharma</s>, they became destined for the supreme, perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>). Then those <s>bodhisattvas</s>, those householders, those renunciants, those boys and girls who had come from the world-realm <s>Ratnāvatī</s> together with the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Samantaraśmi</s>, each with their own roots of merit, having honored, venerated, esteemed, and worshiped the Blessed One <s>Śākyamuni</s>, sat down to one side.

<s>Śākyamuni</s> the <s>Tathāgata</s>, having taken those lotuses, cast them toward the world-realms in the northern direction, as numerous as the sands of the river <s>Gaṅgā</s>. By those lotuses, those world-realms were covered. On those lotuses sat Buddha-forms, and in those <s>buddhakṣetras</s> (buddha-fields) they taught the <s>Dharma</s>—namely, this very <s>Dharma</s>-teaching connected with the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> (Perfection of Wisdom). And those beings who heard that <s>Dharma</s> became destined for unsurpassed perfect awakening. Then those <s>bodhisattvas</s>, those householders, those renunciants, those boys and those girls, having come from the world-realm <s>Ratnāvatī</s> together with the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Samantaraśmi</s>, having honored, respected, esteemed, and worshipped the Blessed One <s>Śākyamuni</s> with their respective roots of merit, sat down to one side.
Then in the northeastern direction, having passed beyond world-realms as numerous as the sands of the river <s>Gaṅgā</s>, beyond them all, there was the final world-realm called <s>Samādhyalaṅkṛtā</s> (Adorned with Concentration). There dwelt, abided, and lived the <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Samādhihastyuttaraśrī</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Enlightened One. He was teaching the <s>Dharma</s> of this very <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> to the <s>bodhisattvas</s>.
Then in that world-realm, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> named <s>Vijayavikrāmin</s>, having seen that great radiance, that great earthquake, and that incomparably beautiful form of the Blessed One, approached the Blessed One <s>Ratnākara</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Enlightened One. Having approached and bowed at the feet of the Blessed One, he spoke thus to the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnākara</s>: 'What, Blessed One, is the cause, what is the condition for the appearance of this great radiance in the world, and of this great earthquake, and of the display of such an incomparably beautiful form of a <s>Tathāgata</s>?' When this was said, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnākara</s> spoke thus to the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Samantaraśmi</s>:
'There is, noble son, in the south-southwestern direction from here, having passed beyond world-realms as numerous as the sands of the river <s>Gaṅgā</s>, a world-realm called <s>Sahā</s>. There dwells, abides, and lives the <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Śākyamuni</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Enlightened One. He is illuminating the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> for the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s>, and this is its miraculous power.' Then the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Samantaraśmi</s> spoke thus to the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnākara</s>: 'I shall go, Blessed One, to that <s>Sahā</s> world-realm, to see, worship, and attend upon that <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Śākyamuni</s>, and those <s>bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s>, who are for the most part youthful princes, who have attained <s>dhāraṇī</s>, who are skilled in producing <s>samādhis</s>, and who have reached the supreme perfection of mastery over all <s>samādhis</s>.' The Blessed One said: 'Go, noble son, whenever you think the time is right.' Then the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnākara</s> gave to the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Samantaraśmi</s> thousand-petaled lotuses made of various jewels with a golden radiance. 'With these lotuses, noble son, you shall shower that <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Śākyamuni</s>. And you shall say thus: "The Blessed One <s>Ratnākara</s> inquires of the Blessed One about his health, whether he is free from illness, free from affliction, light in rising, comfortable in his journeys, strong, and dwelling in pleasant contact. And these lotuses have been sent by that Blessed One <s>Ratnākara</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Enlightened One, for the Blessed One." And may you be mindful and self-possessed in that <s>buddhakṣetra</s>, noble son. For what reason? Because the <s>bodhisattvas</s> who are born in that <s>Sahā</s> world-realm are hard to approach.' Then the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Samantaraśmi</s>, having taken from the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnākara</s> those thousand-petaled lotuses made of various jewels with a golden radiance, surrounded and attended by many hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭi-niyutas</s> of <s>bodhisattvas</s>, householders, renunciants, boys, and girls, honoring, respecting, esteeming, and worshipping the Blessed <s>Buddhas</s> in those world-realms as numerous as the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> in the eastern direction, with flowers, incense, fragrances, garlands, unguents, powders, garments, parasols, banners, flags, and victory standards, arrived at this <s>Sahā</s> world-realm. He approached the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Śākyamuni</s>, bowed his head at the feet of the Blessed One, and stood to one side. Standing to one side, the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Samantaraśmi</s> spoke thus to the Blessed One <s>Śākyamuni</s>: 'The Blessed One <s>Ratnākara</s> inquires of the Blessed One about his health, whether he is free from illness, free from affliction, light in rising, comfortable in his journeys, strong, and dwelling in pleasant contact. for the Blessed One. Then the Blessed One <s>Śākyamuni</s> the <s>Tathāgata</s>, having taken those lotuses, cast them toward the world-realms in the northeastern direction, as numerous as the sands of the river <s>Gaṅgā</s>. By those lotuses, those world-realms were covered. On those lotuses sat Buddha-forms, and in those <s>buddhakṣetras</s> they taught the <s>Dharma</s>—namely, this very <s>Dharma</s>-teaching connected with the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. And those beings who heard that <s>Dharma</s> became destined for unsurpassed perfect awakening. Then those <s>bodhisattvas</s>, householders, renunciants, boys, and girls, having come from the world-realm <s>Ratnāvatī</s> together with the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Samantaraśmi</s>, having honored, respected, esteemed, and worshipped the Blessed One <s>Śākyamuni</s> with their respective roots of merit, sat down to one side.

There dwelt the <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Padmottaraśrī</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Enlightened One. He was teaching the <s>Dharma</s> of this very <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> to the <s>bodhisattvas</s>.
Then in that world-realm, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> named <s>Padmahasta</s>, having seen that great radiance, earthquake, and incomparably beautiful form of the Blessed One, approached the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnākara</s> and asked about the cause. The <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnākara</s> spoke to the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Samantaraśmi</s>:
'There is, noble son, in the northwestern direction from here, having passed beyond world-realms as numerous as the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, a world-realm called <s>Sahā</s>. There the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Śākyamuni</s> dwells, abides, and lives. He is illuminating the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> for the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s>, and this is its miraculous power.' Then the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Samantaraśmi</s> received permission to go and was given jeweled thousand-petaled golden-radiant lotuses by the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnākara</s> with the same instructions as before. He arrived at the <s>Sahā</s> world-realm, bowed at the feet of the Blessed One <s>Śākyamuni</s>, conveyed <s>Ratnākara</s>'s greetings and presented the lotuses.

By those lotuses those world-realms were covered, Buddha-forms appeared teaching the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, and beings who heard became destined for unsurpassed perfect awakening. The retinue sat down to one side.

From here, in the southeastern direction, having passed beyond world-realms as numerous as the sands of the river <s>Gaṅgā</s>, there is a world-realm called <s>Sahā</s>. There, the <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Śākyamuni</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the perfectly and fully awakened one, abides, endures, and maintains himself. He is illuminating the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> (Perfection of Wisdom) for the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s> (great beings), and such is his majestic power. Then the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Samantaraśmi</s> addressed the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnākara</s> thus: "I wish to go, Blessed One, to that <s>Sahā</s> world-realm, to see, venerate, and attend upon that <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Śākyamuni</s>, and those <s>bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s> who are predominantly in the state of princes (<s>kumārabhūta</s>), who have attained <s>dhāraṇī</s> (power of retention), who are skilled in the exercise of <s>samādhi</s> (concentration), and who have reached the perfection of mastery over all <s>samādhis</s>." The Blessed One said: "Go, son of good family, to whatever you now consider the proper time." Then the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnākara</s> gave to the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Samantaraśmi</s> thousand-petaled lotuses made of various jewels and gleaming with golden luster, [saying:] "With these lotuses, son of good family, scatter them upon the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Śākyamuni</s>. And say thus: 'The Blessed One <s>Ratnākara</s> inquires after the Blessed One's health — whether he is free from illness, free from affliction, light in rising, well in his daily routine, strong, and dwelling in comfort of touch. And these lotuses have been sent by the Blessed One <s>Ratnākara</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the perfectly and fully awakened one, for the Blessed One.' And you, son of good family, should act with full awareness in that <s>buddhakṣetra</s> (buddha-field). For what reason? For those <s>bodhisattvas</s> who have been born in that <s>Sahā</s> world-realm are formidable." Then the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Samantaraśmi</s>, having received those thousand-petaled lotuses made of various jewels and gleaming with golden luster from the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnākara</s>, surrounded and attended by many hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭi-niyutas</s> of <s>bodhisattvas</s>, householders, renunciants, boys, and girls, traveling through the eastern direction, honoring, respecting, revering, and worshiping the <s>Buddhas</s> and Blessed Ones in those <s>Gaṅgā</s>-sand-numerous world-realms with flowers, incense, fragrances, garlands, unguents, powders, robes, parasols, banners, flags, and victory standards, arrived at this <s>Sahā</s> world-realm. He approached the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Śākyamuni</s>, bowed his head at the feet of the Blessed One, and stood to one side. Standing to one side, the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Samantaraśmi</s> addressed the Blessed One <s>Śākyamuni</s> thus: "The Blessed One <s>Ratnākara</s> inquires after the Blessed One's health — whether he is free from illness, free from affliction, light in rising, well in his daily routine, strong, and dwelling in comfort of touch. And these thousand-petaled lotuses made of various jewels and gleaming with golden luster have been sent by the Blessed One <s>Ratnākara</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s>," for the Blessed One. Then the Blessed One <s>Śākyamuni</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, having received those lotuses, cast them toward the northwestern direction, toward those <s>Gaṅgā</s>-sand-numerous world-realms. And by those lotuses, those world-realms became radiant. And on those lotuses, <s>Buddha</s>-forms were seated, and in those <s>buddhakṣetras</s> they taught the <s>Dharma</s> — namely, this very <s>Dharma</s>-teaching connected with the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. And those beings who heard that <s>Dharma</s> became destined for <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> (supreme, perfect awakening). Then those <s>bodhisattvas</s>, householders, renunciants, boys, and girls who had come from the <s>Ratnāvatī</s> world-realm together with the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Samantaraśmi</s>, each with their own roots of merit, having honored, respected, revered, and worshiped the Blessed One <s>Śākyamuni</s>, sat down to one side.
Then, from the direction below, having passed beyond <s>Gaṅgā</s>-sand-numerous world-realms, at the very last world-realm, there is one called <s>Padmā</s>. There, the <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Padmaśrī</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the perfectly and fully awakened one, abides, endures, and maintains himself. He teaches this very <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> as the <s>Dharma</s> for <s>bodhisattvas</s>. Then, in that world-realm, the <s>bodhisattva</s> named <s>Padmottara</s>, the great being, having seen that great flood of light, that great earthquake, and that magnificent body of the Blessed One, approached the Blessed One, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnākara</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the perfectly and fully awakened one. Having approached, he bowed at the feet of that Blessed One and addressed that <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnākara</s> thus: "What, Blessed One, is the cause, what is the condition, for the appearance in the world of this great flood of light, this great earthquake, and the display of this magnificent body of a <s>Tathāgata</s>?" When this was said, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnākara</s> addressed the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Samantaraśmi</s> thus: "There is, son of good family, in the direction above from here, having passed beyond <s>Gaṅgā</s>-sand-numerous world-realms, a world-realm called <s>Sahā</s>. There, the <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Śākyamuni</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the perfectly and fully awakened one, abides, endures, and maintains himself. He is illuminating the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> for the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s>, and such is his majestic power." [The same exchange follows as before.] Then the Blessed One <s>Śākyamuni</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, having received those lotuses, cast them toward the direction below, toward those <s>Gaṅgā</s>-sand-numerous world-realms. And by those lotuses, those world-realms became radiant. And on those lotuses, <s>Buddha</s>-forms were seated, teaching the <s>Dharma</s> connected with the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. And those beings who heard that <s>Dharma</s> became destined for <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>. Then those <s>bodhisattvas</s>, householders, renunciants, boys, and girls who had come from the <s>Ratnāvatī</s> world-realm together with the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Samantaraśmi</s>, each with their own roots of merit, having honored and worshiped the Blessed One <s>Śākyamuni</s>, sat down to one side.
Then, from the direction above, having passed beyond <s>Gaṅgā</s>-sand-numerous world-realms, at the very last world-realm, there is one called <s>Nandā</s>. There, the <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Nandaśrī</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the perfectly and fully awakened one, abides, endures, and maintains himself. He teaches this very <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> as the <s>Dharma</s> for <s>bodhisattvas</s>. Then, in that world-realm, the <s>bodhisattva</s> named <s>Nandadatta</s>, the great being, having seen that great flood of light, that great earthquake, and that magnificent body of the Blessed One, approached the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnākara</s> and asked the same question. The <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Ratnākara</s> replied that in the direction below, in the <s>Sahā</s> world-realm, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Śākyamuni</s> teaches the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> with such majestic power. [The same exchange and journey follows.] Then the Blessed One <s>Śākyamuni</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, having received those lotuses, cast them toward the direction above, toward those <s>Gaṅgā</s>-sand-numerous world-realms. And by those lotuses, those world-realms became radiant. And on those lotuses, <s>Buddha</s>-forms were seated, teaching the <s>Dharma</s> connected with the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. And those beings who heard that <s>Dharma</s> became destined for <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>. Then those visitors from <s>Ratnāvatī</s>, together with the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> <s>Samantaraśmi</s>, having honored and worshiped the Blessed One <s>Śākyamuni</s>, sat down to one side.
Then, in that very instant, this trichiliocosm became made of the seven jewels, strewn with flowers, adorned with hanging garlands of silk and streamers, and beautified with wish-fulfilling trees whose topmost branches bent low with the weight of various ornaments, with flower-trees, fruit-trees, fragrance-trees, and garland-trees — just like the world-realm <s>Padmāvatī</s>, the <s>buddhakṣetra</s> of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Samantakusuma</s>, where <s>Mañjuśrī</s> the prince (<s>kumārabhūta</s>) dwells, together with the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Susthitamati</s> and other <s>bodhisattvas</s> of great power. And the Blessed One beheld the world with its gods, assembled together with <s>Māra</s> and <s>Brahmā</s>, the population including <s>śramaṇas</s> (ascetics) and <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, and those <s>bodhisattvas</s> in the state of princes. [Thus ends the <s>Nidāna</s> (Introduction)].

<s>Śāriputra</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> (great being) who desires to fully awaken to all <s>dharmas</s> should apply himself to the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> (Perfection of Wisdom)." [This is, in brief, the arising of the mind accompanied by the desire for awakening.]
When this was said, the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> said this to the Blessed One: "How, Blessed One, should the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> who desires to fully awaken to all <s>dharmas</s> in every way apply himself to the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>?"
When this was said, the Blessed One said this to the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>: "Here, <s>Śāriputra</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, abiding in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, should perfect the <s>Dānapāramitā</s> (Perfection of Generosity) through the practice of non-attachment, based on the non-apprehension of gift, giver, and recipient. The <s>Śīlapāramitā</s> (Perfection of Morality) should be perfected, based on [the understanding of] the non-existence of offense, non-offense, and transgression. The <s>Kṣāntipāramitā</s> (Perfection of Patience) should be perfected, based on imperturbability. The <s>Vīryapāramitā</s> (Perfection of Vigor) should be perfected, based on the non-relaxation of bodily and mental vigor. The <s>Dhyānapāramitā</s> (Perfection of Meditation) should be perfected, based on non-relishing. The <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> (Perfection of Wisdom) should be perfected, based on the non-apprehension of wisdom and deficient wisdom."

"The <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> who desires, having surveyed <s>sarvajñatā</s> (omniscience) with knowledge and vision, to transcend it — should cultivate the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. The <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> who desires to perfect <s>mārgajñatā</s> (knowledge of the path), to attain <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> (knowledge of all aspects), to perfect the knowledge of the forms of the mental conduct of all beings, and to uproot all latent tendencies, entanglements, and <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) — should apply himself to the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. Thus should the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> train in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. The <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> who desires to enter the <s>bodhisattva-niyāma</s> (fixed course of a bodhisattva), to transcend the stages of <s>śrāvakas</s> (disciples) and <s>pratyekabuddhas</s> (solitary buddhas), to abide on the irreversible stage, to transcend the <s>kumārabhūmi</s> (youth stage), to attain the six <s>abhijñās</s> (supernatural knowledges), to know the dispositions, conduct, and stirrings of the minds of all beings, to surpass the knowledge of all <s>śrāvakas</s> and <s>pratyekabuddhas</s>, and to obtain the bliss of <s>dhāraṇī</s> (power of retention) and <s>samādhi</s> (concentration) — [should train in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>]." [This is, accompanied by practice, the blazing-fire-simile.]
"The <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> who desires to establish the miserly in generosity, and who desires, by a single mental arising accompanied by rejoicing, to surpass all the gifts being given by all <s>śrāvakas</s> and <s>pratyekabuddhas</s> — should train in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>."

children.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Śāriputra</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s>, wishing to establish all beings in the <s>Dānapāramitā</s> (perfection of generosity), the <s>Śīlapāramitā</s> (perfection of moral conduct), the <s>Kṣāntipāramitā</s> (perfection of patience), the <s>Vīryapāramitā</s> (perfection of vigor), the <s>Dhyānapāramitā</s> (perfection of meditation), and the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> (perfection of wisdom), in a world bounded by the <s>Dharmadhātu</s> (realm of phenomena) and extending to the limits of the <s>Ākāśadhātu</s> (realm of space), should train in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. Furthermore, <s>Śāriputra</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s>, wishing to make even a single generation of a wholesome thought inexhaustible until awakening at the seat of enlightenment (<s>Bodhimaṇḍa</s>), should train in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. Furthermore, <s>Śāriputra</s>, [thinking:] 'May the <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones, in the ten directions speak my praise!'—the <s>bodhisattva</s> {<s>mahāsattva</s> should train in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>}. [Thus the <s>Ādityopama</s> (resembling the sun), accompanied by <s>bala</s> (power).] Furthermore, <s>Śāriputra</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s>, wishing to train in <s>adhyātmaśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of the internal), should train in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. Likewise, wishing to train in <s>bahirdhāśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of the external), <s>adhyātmabahirdhāśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of the internal and external), <s>śūnyatāśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of emptiness), <s>mahāśūnyatā</s> (great emptiness), <s>paramārthaśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of the ultimate), <s>saṃskṛtaśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of the conditioned), <s>atyantaśūnyatā</s> (absolute emptiness), <s>anavarāgraśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of beginninglessness and endlessness), <s>anakāraśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of non-rejection), <s>prakṛtiśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of essential nature), <s>sarvadharmaśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of all phenomena), <s>svalakṣaṇaśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of own-characteristics), <s>anupalambhaśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of non-apprehension), <s>abhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of the nature of non-existence), <s>bhāvaśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of existence), <s>abhāvaśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of non-existence), <s>svabhāvaśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of own-nature), and <s>parabhāvaśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of other-nature), the <s>bodhisattva</s> {<s>mahāsattva</s> should train in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>}. Furthermore, <s>Śāriputra</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s>, wishing to comprehend the <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) of all <s>dharmas</s>, should train in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. Likewise, wishing to comprehend the <s>tathatā</s> of the <s>Dharmadhātu</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s> {<s>mahāsattva</s> should train in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>}. Wishing to comprehend the <s>tathatā</s> of the ultimate limit of all existence (<s>sarvabhūtakoṭī</s>), the <s>bodhisattva</s> {<s>mahāsattva</s> should train in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>}.

children.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Śāriputra</s>, a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> who wishes to know the atoms of earth, water, fire, and wind in the great trichiliocosm should train in <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> (the Perfection of Wisdom). Furthermore, <s>Śāriputra</s>, a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> practicing <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> knows: 'When a gift is given in this way, it yields great fruit. When a gift is given in this way, it causes rebirth in the families of great <s>kṣatriya</s> (warrior) clans; it causes rebirth in the families of great <s>brāhmaṇa</s> clans; it causes rebirth in the families of great householder clans. When a gift is given in this way, it causes rebirth among the <s>Cāturmahārājika</s> gods; when a gift is given in this way, it causes rebirth among the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> (Thirty-Three) gods; when a gift is given in this way, among the <s>Yāma</s> gods; among the <s>Tuṣita</s> gods; among the <s>Nirmāṇarati</s> gods; among the <s>Paranirmitavaśavartin</s> gods. When a gift is given in this way, it conduces to the attainment of the first <s>dhyāna</s> (meditative absorption); to the attainment of the second <s>dhyāna</s>; of the third <s>dhyāna</s>; of the fourth <s>dhyāna</s>. It conduces to the attainment of the <s>samāpatti</s> (attainment) of the sphere of infinite space (<s>ākāśānantyāyatana</s>); of the sphere of infinite consciousness (<s>vijñānānantyāyatana</s>); of the sphere of nothingness (<s>ākiñcanyāyatana</s>); of the sphere of neither perception nor non-perception (<s>naivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatana</s>). When a gift is given in this way, it conduces to the attainment of the thirty-seven <s>bodhipakṣya dharmas</s> (qualities conducive to awakening). It conduces to the attainment of the fruit of <s>Srotaāpatti</s> (stream-entry); of the fruit of <s>Sakṛdāgāmin</s> (once-returning); of the fruit of <s>Anāgāmin</s> (non-returning); of the fruit of <s>Arhat</s> (worthy one); to the attainment of <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>-hood (solitary awakening); to the attainment of perfect and complete Buddhahood (<s>samyaksaṃbuddhatva</s>).' Furthermore, <s>Śāriputra</s>, a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> practicing <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> should know: 'When a gift is given with skillful means (<s>upāyakauśalya</s>), it fulfills the perfection of generosity (<s>dānapāramitā</s>). When a gift is given in this way, it fulfills the perfection of morality (<s>śīlapāramitā</s>); the perfection of patience (<s>kṣāntipāramitā</s>); the perfection of vigor (<s>vīryapāramitā</s>); the perfection of meditation (<s>dhyānapāramitā</s>); the perfection of wisdom (<s>prajñāpāramitā</s>).'

children.translated_text: When this was said, the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> addressed the Blessed One thus: 'How, Blessed One, does a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, while giving a gift, fulfill the perfection of generosity (<s>dānapāramitā</s>)? How, while giving a gift, does he fulfill the perfection of morality (<s>śīlapāramitā</s>)? How, the perfection of patience (<s>kṣāntipāramitā</s>)? How, the perfection of vigor (<s>vīryapāramitā</s>)? How, the perfection of meditation (<s>dhyānapāramitā</s>)? How, Blessed One, does a <s>bodhisattva</s>, while giving a gift, fulfill the perfection of wisdom (<s>prajñāpāramitā</s>)?' The Blessed One said: 'Through the non-apprehension (<s>anupalambha</s>) of the gift, the giver, and the recipient, the perfection of generosity (<s>dānapāramitā</s>) is fulfilled. Through the state of non-transgression, non-offense, and non-excessive-offense, the perfection of morality (<s>śīlapāramitā</s>) is fulfilled. Through non-agitation and non-disturbance, the perfection of patience (<s>kṣāntipāramitā</s>) is fulfilled. Through the non-relaxation of bodily and mental vigor, the perfection of vigor (<s>vīryapāramitā</s>) is fulfilled. Through non-distraction and non-conceptualization, the perfection of meditation (<s>dhyānapāramitā</s>) is fulfilled. Through the method of non-apprehension in the discernment of all <s>dharmas</s>, the perfection of wisdom (<s>prajñāpāramitā</s>) is fulfilled. Thus, for a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> giving a gift, the six <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections) are fulfilled. "Furthermore, <s>Śāriputra</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> who desires to pervade with a single cross-legged seat all the space element in the <s>trisāhasramahāsāhasra-lokadhātu</s> (great trichiliocosm) should train in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. Furthermore, <s>Śāriputra</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> who desires, having bound together with a single hair all the mountains in the <s>trisāhasramahāsāhasra-lokadhātu</s> — <s>Sumeru</s>, <s>Mahāsumeru</s>, <s>Cakravāḍa</s>, <s>Mahācakravāḍa</s>, and others — to hurl them across innumerable, immeasurable world-realms, should train in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. Furthermore, <s>Śāriputra</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> who desires to see with the divine eye the <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones, in all <s>buddhakṣetras</s> (buddha-fields) in each of the ten directions, who desires to hear their <s>dharmadeśanā</s> (teaching of the Dharma) with the divine ear, who desires to know the mental conduct of all beings, who desires to recollect their former abodes, who desires to accomplish the <s>abhijñā</s> (supernatural knowledge) of the destruction of the <s>āsravas</s> (defilements), and who desires to directly realize <s>bhūtakoṭi</s> (the limit of reality) — should train in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>." [This is, accompanied by the <s>abhijñās</s> (supernatural knowledges), the great-king-simile.]
"Furthermore, <s>Śāriputra</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> who desires to provide for all the <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones, together with their assemblies of <s>śrāvakas</s> and <s>bodhisattvas</s>, in world-realms as numerous as the sands of the river <s>Gaṅgā</s> in each of the ten directions, with a single alms-bowl, should train in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. Likewise, one who desires to honor, revere, esteem, and worship those <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones with clouds of flowers, incense, fragrance, garlands, ointments, powders, robes, parasols, banners, and flags should train in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.
Furthermore, <s>Śāriputra</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> who desires to establish the beings in world-realms as numerous as the sands of the river <s>Gaṅgā</s> in the eastern direction in the aggregate of <s>śīla</s> (moral conduct), to establish them in the aggregate of <s>samādhi</s> (concentration), to establish them in the aggregate of <s>vimukti-jñāna-darśana</s> (knowledge and vision of liberation), to establish them in the fruit of <s>srotaāpatti</s> (stream-entry), to establish them in the fruit of <s>sakṛdāgāmin</s> (once-returning), to establish them in the fruit of <s>anāgāmin</s> (non-returning), to establish them in <s>arhattva</s> (arhatship), to establish them in <s>pratyekabodhi</s> (solitary awakening), and up to establishing them in the <s>anupadhiśeṣa-nirvāṇadhātu</s> (realm of complete extinction without remainder) — should train in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. Just as in the eastern direction, so too in the southern, western, northern, intermediate directions, below, and above, in world-realms as numerous as the sands of the river <s>Gaṅgā</s> in each direction,

children.translated_text: [Thus the <s>Yānopama</s> (resembling a vehicle), accompanied by <s>śamatha</s> (calm abiding) and <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight).] Furthermore, {<s>Śāriputra</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s>}, wishing to grasp, retain, recite, practice in accordance with its true nature, and extensively illuminate to others whatever has been spoken, is being spoken, and will be spoken by the <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones, in the ten directions—namely, <s>sūtra</s>, <s>geya</s> (songs), <s>vyākaraṇa</s> (prophecies), <s>gāthā</s> (verses), <s>udāna</s> (inspired utterances), <s>nidāna</s> (narratives of origin), <s>itivṛttaka</s> (tales of past events), <s>jātaka</s> (birth stories), <s>vaipulya</s> (extensive discourses), <s>adbhutadharma</s> (accounts of marvels), <s>avadāna</s> (heroic tales), and <s>upadeśa</s> (instructions)—and that which has not been heard by the <s>Śrāvakas</s>, {should train in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>}. Furthermore, {<s>Śāriputra</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s>}, wishing to grasp, retain, recite, practice in accordance with its true nature, and extensively illuminate to others whatever has been spoken, is being spoken, and will be spoken by the <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones, in the eastern direction, {should train in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>}. Whatever has been spoken, is being spoken, and will be spoken by the <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones, in the southern direction—wishing to grasp, retain, recite, practice in accordance with its true nature, and extensively illuminate all of that to others, should train in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. Whatever in the western direction... whatever in the northern direction... whatever in the northeastern direction... whatever in the southeastern direction... whatever in the southwestern direction... whatever in the northwestern direction... whatever in the direction below—wishing to grasp, retain, recite, practice in accordance with its true nature, and extensively illuminate all of that to others, should train in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. Whatever has been spoken, is being spoken, and will be spoken by the <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones, in the direction above—wishing to grasp, retain, recite, practice in accordance with its true nature, and extensively illuminate all of that to others, should train in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. [Thus the <s>Prasnavaṇopama</s> (resembling a flowing stream), accompanied by <s>dhāraṇī</s> (retention) and <s>pratibhāna</s> (eloquence).] Furthermore, {<s>Śāriputra</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s>}, wishing to illuminate all the darkness and gloom in the world-realms as numerous as the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> river in the eastern direction, where not even the radiance of the sun and moon can reach, {should train in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>}. [Likewise for] the darkness and gloom in the world-realms as numerous as the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> river in the southern direction, the western direction, the northern direction, the northeastern direction, the southeastern direction, the southwestern direction, the northwestern direction, and the direction below—where not even the radiance of the sun and moon can reach—wishing to illuminate all of them, should train in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. The darkness and gloom in the world-realms as numerous as the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> river in the direction above—where not even the radiance of the sun and moon can reach—wishing to illuminate all of them, should train in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. Furthermore, {<s>Śāriputra</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s>}, wishing to cause all the beings born in various <s>Buddhakṣetras</s> (Buddha-fields) in the world-realms as numerous as the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> river in the eastern direction to hear the word of the <s>Buddha</s>, the word of the <s>Dharma</s>, and the word of the <s>Saṅgha</s>, and wishing to establish those beings in right view (<s>samyagdṛṣṭi</s>)—

03203 [Thus the simile of the sound of joy, accompanied by the summary of the <s>Dharma</s>.]
03204 Furthermore, <s>Śāriputra</s>, a <s>bodhisattva-mahāsattva</s> [should think]: 'Those beings who are blind in all the <s>buddhakṣetras</s> in world-realms as numerous as the sands of the river <s>Gaṅgā</s> in the eastern direction — they, through my power, shall see forms with their eyes' —
03205-03206 thus one should train in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. Likewise: 'The deaf shall hear sounds with their ears; the mad shall regain
03207 mindfulness; the naked shall obtain garments; the hungry
03208 beings shall have full bowls; those reborn in the lower realms
03209 shall be liberated from all lower realms and shall obtain human existence; I shall establish the immoral in the aggregate of morality (<s>śīlaskandha</s>),
03210 the unconcentrated in the aggregate of <s>samādhi</s>,
03211 the foolish in the aggregate of <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom), the unliberated in the aggregate of liberation (<s>vimuktiskandha</s>),
03212 those lacking liberation-knowledge-and-vision in the aggregate of liberation-knowledge-and-vision (<s>vimuktijñānadarśanaskandha</s>), those who have not realized the noble truths in the fruit of stream-entry (<s>srotāpattiphala</s>),
03213 in the fruit of once-returning (<s>sakṛdāgāmiphala</s>), in the fruit of non-returning (<s>anāgāmiphala</s>), in <s>arhattva</s> (arhatship),
03214 in <s>pratyekabodhi</s> (solitary awakening), in <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> (unsurpassed perfect awakening)' — the <s>bodhisattva</s> should
03215 train in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. [The same formula is repeated for] those beings in the southern direction, [in world-realms as numerous as the sands of the river <s>Gaṅgā</s>, in all <s>buddhakṣetras</s>: the blind shall see, the deaf shall hear, the mad shall regain mindfulness, the naked shall obtain garments, the hungry shall be filled, those in the lower realms shall be liberated and obtain human existence; I shall establish the immoral in morality, the unconcentrated in <s>samādhi</s>, the foolish in wisdom, the unliberated in liberation, those lacking liberation-knowledge in liberation-knowledge-and-vision, those not on the noble truths in stream-entry, once-returning, non-returning, arhatship, solitary awakening, and unsurpassed perfect awakening — the <s>bodhisattva</s> should train in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. The same for] those in the western direction, [the same formula;] those in the northern direction, [the same formula;] those in the northeastern direction, [the same formula;] those in the southeastern direction, [the same formula;] those in the southwestern direction, [the same formula;] those in the northwestern direction, [the same formula;] those in the downward direction, [the same formula;]
03216 those in the upward direction, [in world-realms as numerous as the sands of the river <s>Gaṅgā</s>, in all <s>buddhakṣetras</s>: the blind shall see, the deaf shall hear, the mad shall regain mindfulness, the naked shall obtain garments, the hungry shall be filled, those in the lower realms shall be liberated and obtain human existence; I shall establish the immoral in morality, the unconcentrated in <s>samādhi</s>, the foolish in wisdom, the unliberated in liberation, those lacking liberation-knowledge in liberation-knowledge-and-vision, those not on the noble truths in stream-entry, once-returning, non-returning, arhatship, solitary awakening, and unsurpassed perfect awakening — the <s>bodhisattva</s> should train in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.]
03217 [Thus the simile of the river current, accompanied by the one-way path.]
03218 Furthermore, <s>Śāriputra</s>, a <s>bodhisattva-mahāsattva</s> wishing to train in the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s conduct should train in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. Furthermore,
03219 <s>Śāriputra</s>, a <s>bodhisattva-mahāsattva</s> practicing the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> should investigate thus: 'When shall I, like a <s>nāga</s>—'

Furthermore, <s>Śāriputra</s>, a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> practicing <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> should reflect thus: 'Why should I, surrounded and attended by the <s>Cāturmahārājika</s> gods, the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> (Thirty-Three) gods, the <s>Yāma</s> gods, the <s>Tuṣita</s> gods, the <s>Nirmāṇarati</s> gods, the <s>Paranirmitavaśavartin</s> gods, the <s>Brahmakāyika</s> gods, the <s>Brahmapurohita</s> gods, the <s>Brahmapāriṣadya</s> gods, the <s>Parīttābha</s> gods, the <s>Apramāṇābha</s> gods, the <s>Ābhāsvara</s> (Radiant) gods, the <s>Parīttaśubha</s> gods, the <s>Apramāṇaśubha</s> gods, the <s>Śubhakṛtsna</s> gods, the <s>Anabhraka</s> gods, the <s>Puṇyaprasava</s> gods, the <s>Bṛhatphala</s> gods, the <s>Asaṃjñisattva</s> gods, and the <s>Śuddhāvāsa</s> (Pure Abode) gods — <s>Aspṛha</s>, <s>Atapa</s>, <s>Sadṛśa</s>, <s>Sudarśana</s>, and <s>Akaniṣṭha</s> — attended by many hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>niyutas</s> of divine sons, approach the foot of the <s>Bodhimaṇḍa</s> tree (Tree of Awakening)?' — one should train in <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. Furthermore, (the bodhisattva should reflect): 'Why should the <s>Cāturmahārājika</s> gods, the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods, the <s>Yāma</s> gods, the <s>Tuṣita</s> gods, the <s>Nirmāṇarati</s> gods, the <s>Paranirmitavaśavartin</s> gods, the <s>Brahmakāyika</s> gods, the <s>Brahmapurohita</s> gods, the <s>Brahmapāriṣadya</s> gods, the <s>Parīttābha</s> gods, the <s>Apramāṇābha</s> gods, the <s>Ābhāsvara</s> gods, the <s>Parīttaśubha</s> gods, the <s>Apramāṇaśubha</s> gods, the <s>Śubhakṛtsna</s> gods, the <s>Anabhraka</s> gods, the <s>Puṇyaprasava</s> gods, the <s>Bṛhatphala</s> gods, the <s>Asaṃjñisattva</s> gods, and the <s>Akaniṣṭha</s> gods spread a seat at the foot of the <s>Bodhimaṇḍa</s> tree?' — one should train in <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. Furthermore, (the bodhisattva should reflect): 'Why should the spot of earth (beneath me), whether I am walking, standing, sitting, or lying down when I have fully awakened to the supreme, perfect awakening, become diamond-hard?' — one should train in <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. Furthermore, (the bodhisattva should reflect): 'Why should I, on the very day that I go forth, attain the supreme, perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>) on that very same day?'

children.translated_text: 'On that very day, I should turn the wheel of the <s>Dharma</s>. And as I turn the wheel of the <s>Dharma</s>, the <s>Dharma</s>-eye for all <s>dharmas</s>, long free from dust and stain, should be released for innumerable, immeasurable beings. The minds of innumerable, immeasurable beings should be freed from the <s>āsravas</s> (outflows) without clinging. Innumerable, immeasurable beings should become irreversible (<s>avinivartanīya</s>) from the supreme, perfect awakening' — one should train in <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. Furthermore, (the bodhisattva should reflect): 'Why should I have an immeasurable and incalculable assembly of <s>śrāvakas</s> (disciples)? Immeasurable and incalculable beings should become <s>bodhisattvas</s> seated in one assembly at one <s>Dharma</s>-teaching, irreversible from the supreme, perfect awakening. And there should be an incalculable and immeasurable assembly of <s>bodhisattvas</s>. And there should be an unlimited measure of life-span. And there should be an unlimited splendor of radiance' — one should train in <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. Furthermore, (the bodhisattva should reflect): 'Why should it be that, when I have fully awakened to the supreme, perfect awakening, in that <s>buddhakṣetra</s> (buddha-field) there are utterly and completely no bases of passion, hatred, or delusion whatsoever?' — one should train in <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. Furthermore, (the bodhisattva should reflect): 'Why should it be that, when I have fully awakened to the supreme, perfect awakening, beings would be endowed with such wisdom that the <s>Buddhas</s>, Blessed Ones, abiding in other <s>buddhakṣetras</s> would utter this inspired exclamation (<s>udāna</s>): "Excellent is tranquility! Excellent is restraint! Excellent is self-control! Excellent is the dwelling in the holy life of a hero! Excellent is non-harmfulness toward all living beings!"' — one should train in <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. Furthermore, (the bodhisattva should reflect): 'Why should it be that, even after my <s>Parinirvāṇa</s> (final passing), there would be no disappearance of the true <s>Dharma</s>; and that upon merely hearing my name, beings in world-realms as numerous as the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> in the ten directions would become destined for the supreme, perfect awakening' — one should train in <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.

And some <s>bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s>, through <s>upāyakauśalya</s> (skillful means), having enjoyed the five strands of sensual pleasure, go forth and awaken to <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>.

Just as, <s>Śāriputra</s>, a skilled magician or a magician's apprentice, well-trained in magic, were to conjure the five strands of sensual pleasure and then delight, sport, and amuse himself with those five strands of sensual pleasure — what do you think, <s>Śāriputra</s>, would those five strands of sensual pleasure have been tasted and enjoyed by that magician or his apprentice?' <s>Śāriputra</s> replied: 'No indeed, Blessed One.' The Blessed One said: 'Just so, <s>Śāriputra</s>, a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> enjoys the five strands of sensual pleasure through <s>upāyakauśalya</s> (skillful means) for the purpose of maturing beings. But a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> is not stained by the strands of sensual pleasure. In this manner, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> speaks of the faults of sensual desires: "Desires are on fire! Desires are disgusting! Desires are harmful! Desires are adversarial!" For thus, <s>Śāriputra</s>, a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> takes up the five strands of sensual pleasure for the purpose of maturing beings.' [Thus ends the section on the generation of the thought of awakening, accompanied by the desire for <s>Dharma</s>, like a great cloud.]
When this was said, the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> addressed the Blessed One thus: 'How, Blessed One, should a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> practice the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> (Perfection of Wisdom)?' When this was said, the Blessed One addressed the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> thus: 'Here, <s>Śāriputra</s>, a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, while practicing the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, being a <s>bodhisattva</s>, does not perceive a <s>bodhisattva</s>; he does not perceive even the name "<s>bodhisattva</s>"; he does not perceive the conduct of a <s>bodhisattva</s>; he does not perceive the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>; he does not perceive <s>rūpa</s> (form); likewise, he does not perceive <s>vedanā</s> (feeling), <s>saṃjñā</s> (perception), <s>saṃskāras</s> (formations), or <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness).

children.translated_text: For what reason? For the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> is empty of <s>bodhisattva</s>-nature and empty of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>-nature. For what reason? Because this is its intrinsic nature. For <s>rūpa</s> (form) is not empty through <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness); <s>vedanā</s> (feeling), <s>saṃjñā</s> (perception), <s>saṃskāras</s> (formations), and <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness) are not empty through <s>śūnyatā</s>. <s>Śūnyatā</s> is not other than <s>rūpa</s>; <s>śūnyatā</s> is not other than <s>vedanā</s>; <s>śūnyatā</s> is not other than <s>saṃjñā</s>; <s>śūnyatā</s> is not other than <s>saṃskāras</s>; <s>śūnyatā</s> is not other than <s>vijñāna</s>. For what reason? <s>Rūpa</s> itself is <s>śūnyatā</s>; <s>vedanā</s> itself is <s>śūnyatā</s>; <s>saṃjñā</s> itself is <s>śūnyatā</s>; <s>saṃskāras</s> themselves are <s>śūnyatā</s>; <s>vijñāna</s> itself is <s>śūnyatā</s>. <s>Śūnyatā</s> itself is <s>rūpa</s>; <s>śūnyatā</s> itself is <s>vedanā</s>; <s>śūnyatā</s> itself is <s>saṃjñā</s>; <s>śūnyatā</s> itself is <s>saṃskāras</s>; <s>śūnyatā</s> itself is <s>vijñāna</s>. For what reason? For what is called '<s>bodhisattva</s>' is a mere name; what is called '<s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>' is a mere name; <s>rūpa</s>, <s>vedanā</s>, <s>saṃjñā</s>, <s>saṃskāras</s>, <s>vijñāna</s> — these are mere names. For <s>rūpa</s>, <s>vedanā</s>, <s>saṃjñā</s>, <s>saṃskāras</s>, and <s>vijñāna</s> are like <s>māyā</s> (illusion), and <s>māyā</s> is a mere name — not established in a place, not established in a locale, not occurring together, a false appearance. For what has the nature of the appearance of <s>māyā</s>, there is no arising and no cessation, no defilement and no purification. Thus, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, while practicing the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, does not perceive arising, does not perceive cessation, does not perceive defilement, does not perceive purification. For what reason? For names are fabricated, simulated <s>dharmas</s>; they are conceptually constructed and referred to by adventitious designations. The <s>bodhisattva</s>, while practicing the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, does not perceive all those names; not perceiving them, he does not cling. Furthermore, <s>Śāriputra</s>, a <s>bodhisattva</s> practicing the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> does not examine thus: 'What is called "<s>bodhisattva</s>" is a mere name; what is called "<s>Bodhi</s> (awakening)" is a mere name; what is called "<s>Prajñā</s> (wisdom)" —'

Just as, <s>Śāriputra</s>, one speaks of a 'self' (<s>ātman</s>), yet no self is apprehended, neither is a being, a living soul, a nourisher, a person, an individual, nor a human apprehended — on account of the emptiness of non-apprehension (<s>anupalambhaśūnyatā</s>). Why is that? Because the <s>bodhisattva</s> does not perceive even that by which he might become attached. Practicing in this way, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> practices the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. children.translated_text: The <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) of a <s>srotaāpanna</s> (stream-enterer), the <s>prajñā</s> of a <s>sakṛdāgāmin</s> (once-returner), of an <s>anāgāmin</s> (non-returner), of an <s>arhat</s>, and of a <s>pratyekabuddha</s>; the <s>prajñā</s> of a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>; and the <s>prajñā</s> of a <s>Tathāgata</s>, an <s>Arhat</s>, a Perfectly Enlightened One—all these wisdoms are undifferentiated, isolated, unarisen, without self-nature, and empty. And, Blessed One, in that which is undifferentiated, isolated, unarisen, without self-nature, and empty, no differentiation or distinction can be apprehended. How then, Blessed One, does the <s>prajñā</s> cultivated for even a single day by a <s>bodhisattva</s> practicing the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> surpass the <s>prajñā</s> of all <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>? When this was said, the Blessed One spoke thus to the Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>: What do you think, <s>Śāriputra</s>? The purpose for which the <s>prajñā</s> of a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> practicing the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, cultivated for even a single day, is present—endowed with all aspects, practicing <s>sarvajñatā</s> (omniscience), working for the welfare of all beings, having understood all <s>dharmas</s> in all their aspects, thinking 'All beings are to be led to <s>parinirvāṇa</s>'—is that purpose present for all the <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, <s>Śāriputra</s>? <s>Śāriputra</s> replied: No indeed, Blessed One. The Blessed One said: What do you think, <s>Śāriputra</s>? Do all the <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> think thus: 'Having awakened to unsurpassed perfect <s>bodhi</s>, we shall lead all beings to <s>parinirvāṇa</s> in the <s>nirvāṇadhātu</s> (realm of nirvāṇa) without remainder'? <s>Śāriputra</s> replied: No indeed, Blessed One. The Blessed One said: By this explanation too, <s>Śāriputra</s>, you should understand thus: the <s>prajñā</s> of all <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> does not reach even a hundredth part of the <s>prajñā</s> of a <s>bodhisattva</s> cultivated for a single day, nor a thousandth, nor a hundred-thousandth, nor does it approach any fraction, calculation, comparison, or resemblance whatsoever.
