'we shall lead immeasurable, incalculable, and boundless beings to <s>parinirvāṇa</s>.' <s>Śāriputra</s> replied: No indeed, Blessed One. The Blessed One said: But the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, <s>Śāriputra</s>, thinks thus: 'Having practiced the six <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections), having ripened beings, having purified the <s>buddhakṣetra</s> (buddha-field), having fulfilled the ten <s>Tathāgata</s>-powers, the four <s>vaiśāradyas</s> (fearlessnesses), the four <s>pratisaṃvids</s> (analytical knowledges), and the eighteen <s>āveṇika-buddhadharmas</s> (unique qualities of a Buddha), having awakened to unsurpassed perfect <s>bodhi</s>, I shall lead immeasurable, incalculable, and boundless beings to <s>parinirvāṇa</s>.' Just as, <s>Śāriputra</s>, a firefly does not think: 'By my light, <s>Jambudvīpa</s> shall be illuminated; by my light, <s>Jambudvīpa</s> shall be filled with radiance'—even so, <s>Śāriputra</s>, none among all the <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> thinks: 'Having practiced the six <s>pāramitās</s>, having ripened beings, having purified the <s>buddhakṣetra</s>, having fulfilled the ten <s>Tathāgata</s>-powers, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, having awakened to unsurpassed perfect <s>bodhi</s>, I shall lead immeasurable, incalculable, and boundless beings to <s>parinirvāṇa</s>.' But just as, <s>Śāriputra</s>, the disk of the sun, upon rising, illuminates and fills all of <s>Jambudvīpa</s> with radiance—even so, <s>Śāriputra</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, having practiced the six <s>pāramitās</s>, having ripened beings, having purified the <s>buddhakṣetra</s>, having fulfilled the ten <s>Tathāgata</s>-powers, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, having awakened to unsurpassed perfect <s>bodhi</s>, leads immeasurable, incalculable, and boundless beings to <s>parinirvāṇa</s>.
When this was said, the Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> spoke thus to the Blessed One: How, Blessed One, does a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> transcend the stage of <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, reach the <s>avaivartanīya-bhūmi</s> (irreversible stage), and purify the path to awakening? When this was said, the Blessed One spoke thus to the Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>: Here, <s>Śāriputra</s>, a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, from the first arising of the <s>bodhicitta</s> (thought of awakening) onward, practicing the six <s>pāramitās</s> and abiding in <s>dharmas</s> that are empty, signless, and wishless, transcends the stage of <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, reaches the irreversible stage, and purifies the path to awakening.
When this was said, the Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> spoke thus to the Blessed One: On which stage, Blessed One, does a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, abiding, constantly and continuously surpass all <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>?

When this was said, the Blessed One addressed the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> thus: From the first arising of the thought of awakening (<s>prathamacittotpāda</s>), <s>Śāriputra</s>, a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> practicing the six <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections), up until the seat of awakening (<s>bodhimaṇḍa</s>), in the interval, is continuously and constantly worthy of offerings from all <s>śrāvakas</s> and <s>pratyekabuddhas</s>. For what reason? For indeed, <s>Śāriputra</s>, it is thanks to the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> that there is the arising in the world of all wholesome <s>dharmas</s> (qualities) — namely, the ten wholesome paths of action (<s>kuśala karmapatha</s>), the five trainings (<s>śikṣā</s>), the <s>poṣadha</s> (observance day) endowed with eight factors, the four <s>dhyānas</s> (meditative absorptions), the four immeasurables (<s>apramāṇa</s>), the four formless attainments (<s>ārūpyasamāpatti</s>), the five superknowledges (<s>abhijñā</s>), the four noble truths (<s>āryasatya</s>), the four foundations of mindfulness (<s>smṛtyupasthāna</s>), the four right exertions (<s>samyakprahāṇa</s>), the four bases of supernatural power (<s>ṛddhipāda</s>), the five faculties (<s>indriya</s>), the five powers (<s>bala</s>), the seven factors of awakening (<s>bodhyaṅga</s>), and the noble eightfold path (<s>āryāṣṭāṅga mārga</s>) — there is their arising in the world. children.translated_text: the gods of the sphere of nothingness (<s>Ākiñcanyāyatana</s>) come into existence, the gods of the sphere of neither perception nor non-perception (<s>Naivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatana</s>) come into existence. <s>Srotaāpannas</s> (stream-enterers) arise in the world. <s>Sakṛdāgāmins</s> (once-returners) arise in the world. <s>Anāgāmins</s> (non-returners) arise in the world. <s>Arhats</s> (worthy ones) arise in the world. <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> (solitary awakened ones) arise in the world. <s>Bodhisattvas</s> arise in the world. <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, perfectly and fully awakened ones (<s>samyaksaṃbuddha</s>) arise in the world. When this was said, the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> addressed the Blessed One thus: 'Does a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, Blessed One, purify the offering (<s>dakṣiṇā</s>), or not?' The Blessed One said: 'No indeed, <s>Śāriputra</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> does not purify the offering. For what reason? The offering to a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> is utterly pure (<s>atyantaśuddha</s>) in itself. For what reason? The <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, <s>Śāriputra</s>, is a giver (<s>dāyaka</s>). A giver of what? A giver of wholesome <s>dharmas</s> (qualities). Of which wholesome <s>dharmas</s> is he a giver? Namely, of the ten wholesome paths of action (<s>kuśala karmapatha</s>), the five trainings (<s>śikṣā</s>), the <s>poṣadha</s> (observance day) endowed with eight factors, the four <s>dhyānas</s> (meditative absorptions), the four immeasurables (<s>apramāṇa</s>), the four formless attainments (<s>ārūpyasamāpatti</s>), the five superknowledges (<s>abhijñā</s>), the four noble truths (<s>āryasatya</s>), the four foundations of mindfulness (<s>smṛtyupasthāna</s>), the four right exertions (<s>samyakprahāṇa</s>), the four bases of supernatural power (<s>ṛddhipāda</s>), the five faculties (<s>indriya</s>), the five powers (<s>bala</s>), the seven factors of awakening (<s>bodhyaṅga</s>), the noble eightfold path (<s>āryāṣṭāṅga mārga</s>), the four kinds of fearlessness (<s>vaiśāradya</s>), the four analytical knowledges (<s>pratisaṃvid</s>), the six perfections (<s>pāramitā</s>), the ten powers of a <s>Tathāgata</s> (<s>tathāgatabala</s>), and the eighteen distinctive qualities of a <s>Buddha</s> (<s>āveṇika buddhadharma</s>) — he is a giver of these.' [Thus ends the instruction on practice (<s>pratipattyavavāda</s>).] When this was said, the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> addressed the Blessed One thus: 'In what way, Blessed One, is a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> to be called engaged in <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> (the Perfection of Wisdom)?' When this was said, the Blessed One addressed the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> thus: 'Here, <s>Śāriputra</s>, a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> who is engaged in the emptiness of form (<s>rūpaśūnyatā</s>) is to be called engaged.'

One engaged in the emptiness of formations (<s>saṃskāraśūnyatā</s>) is to be called engaged. One engaged in the emptiness of consciousness (<s>vijñānaśūnyatā</s>) is to be called engaged. children.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Śāriputra</s>, a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> practicing <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> does not practice <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> for the sake of the perfection of generosity (<s>dānapāramitā</s>). He does not practice <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> for the sake of the perfection of morality (<s>śīlapāramitā</s>), for the sake of the perfection of patience (<s>kṣāntipāramitā</s>), for the sake of the perfection of vigor (<s>vīryapāramitā</s>), for the sake of the perfection of meditation (<s>dhyānapāramitā</s>), for the sake of the perfection of wisdom (<s>prajñāpāramitā</s>). He does not practice for the sake of the irreversible stage (<s>avinivartanīyabhūmi</s>), for the sake of the ripening of beings, for the sake of the purification of the <s>buddhakṣetra</s> (buddha-field), for the sake of the ten powers of the <s>Tathāgata</s> (<s>tathāgatabala</s>), for the sake of the four fearlessnesses (<s>vaiśāradya</s>), for the sake of the four analytical knowledges (<s>pratisaṃvid</s>), for the sake of the eighteen unique qualities of a <s>Buddha</s> (<s>āveṇika buddhadharma</s>). He does not practice for the sake of the emptiness of the internal (<s>adhyātmaśūnyatā</s>), the emptiness of the external (<s>bahirdhāśūnyatā</s>), the emptiness of both the internal and external (<s>adhyātmabahirdhāśūnyatā</s>), the emptiness of emptiness (<s>śūnyatāśūnyatā</s>), great emptiness (<s>mahāśūnyatā</s>), the emptiness of the ultimate (<s>paramārthaśūnyatā</s>), the emptiness of the conditioned (<s>saṃskṛtaśūnyatā</s>), absolute emptiness (<s>atyantaśūnyatā</s>), the emptiness of what is without beginning or end (<s>anavarāgraśūnyatā</s>), the emptiness of non-rejection (<s>anavakāraśūnyatā</s>), the emptiness of inherent nature (<s>prakṛtiśūnyatā</s>), the emptiness of all <s>dharmas</s> (<s>sarvadharmaśūnyatā</s>), the emptiness of own-characteristics (<s>svalakṣaṇaśūnyatā</s>), the emptiness of non-apprehension (<s>anupalambhaśūnyatā</s>), the emptiness of the non-existence of inherent nature (<s>abhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā</s>), the emptiness of existence (<s>bhāvaśūnyatā</s>), the emptiness of non-existence (<s>abhāvaśūnyatā</s>), the emptiness of own-nature (<s>svabhāvaśūnyatā</s>), or the emptiness of other-nature (<s>parabhāvaśūnyatā</s>). He does not practice for the sake of <s>tathatā</s> (suchness), for the sake of the <s>dharmadhātu</s> (element of reality), for the sake of the <s>bhūtakoṭi</s> (summit of reality). For what reason? Because a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> practicing <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> does not perceive the breaking apart of any <s>dharma</s> whatsoever. Thus, <s>Śāriputra</s>, a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> practicing <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> does not practice <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> for the sake of the divine eye, for the sake of the divine ear, for the sake of the knowledge of others' minds.

children.translated_text: He does not practice the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> (Perfection of Wisdom) on account of the recollection of former lives. He does not practice the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> on account of miraculous powers. For what reason? For while practicing the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, he does not perceive even the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> itself — how much less a <s>bodhisattva</s>, how much less all forms and all <s>abhijñās</s> (supernatural knowledges). Thus, <s>Śāriputra</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> (great being), while practicing the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, is to be called 'properly engaged.' Furthermore, <s>Śāriputra</s>, a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> practicing the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> does not think thus: 'I shall know, with the divine eye, the death and rebirth of beings in <s>Gaṅgā</s>-sand-numerous world-realms in the eastern direction; I shall hear their sounds with the divine ear; I shall know their minds; and having recalled their former lives, I shall go by miraculous power and teach them the <s>Dharma</s>.' Thus, <s>Śāriputra</s>, a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> does not think thus: 'I shall know, with the divine eye, the death and rebirth of beings in <s>Gaṅgā</s>-sand-numerous world-realms in the southern direction; I shall hear their sounds with the divine ear; I shall know their minds; and having recalled their former lives, I shall go by miraculous power and teach them the <s>Dharma</s>.' Likewise in the western direction, the northern direction, the northeastern direction, the southeastern direction, the southwestern direction, the northwestern direction, and below — thus, <s>Śāriputra</s>, a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> does not think thus: 'I shall know, with the divine eye, the death and rebirth of beings in <s>Gaṅgā</s>-sand-numerous world-realms in the direction above; I shall hear their sounds with the divine ear; I shall know their minds; and having recalled their former lives, I shall go by miraculous power and teach them the <s>Dharma</s>.'

children.translated_text: Thus, <s>Śāriputra</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, while practicing the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, leading to final <s>nirvāṇa</s> immeasurable, incalculable, and boundless beings — he is to be called 'properly engaged.' Thus, <s>Śāriputra</s>, when the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> practices the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, <s>Māra</s> the Evil One finds no opening. And all his other worldly <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), whatever they may be, are all crushed. And those <s>Buddhas</s> and Blessed Ones, <s>Śāriputra</s>, who in the eastern direction abide, endure, maintain themselves, and teach the <s>Dharma</s> in <s>Gaṅgā</s>-sand-numerous world-realms, and their <s>śrāvakas</s> (disciples), and their <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, and the <s>Cāturmahārājakāyika</s> gods, the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods, the <s>Yāma</s> gods, the <s>Tuṣita</s> gods, the <s>Nirmāṇarati</s> gods, the <s>Paranirmitavaśavartin</s> gods, the <s>Brahmapārṣadya</s> gods, the <s>Brahmapurohita</s> gods, the <s>Mahābrahmā</s> gods, the <s>Parīttābha</s> gods, the <s>Apramāṇābha</s> gods, the <s>Ābhāsvara</s> (Radiant) gods, the <s>Parīttaśubha</s> gods, the <s>Apramāṇaśubha</s> gods, the <s>Śubhakṛtsnā</s> gods, the <s>Anabhraka</s> gods, the <s>Puṇyaprasava</s> gods, the <s>Bṛhatphala</s> gods, the <s>Asaṃjñisattva</s> gods, the <s>Śuddhāvāsa</s> (Pure Abode) gods, the <s>Avṛha</s> gods, the <s>Atapa</s> gods, the <s>Sudṛśa</s> gods, the <s>Sudarśana</s> gods, and the <s>Akaniṣṭha</s> gods — they all protect that <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>: 'Let no one create an obstacle for this <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>!' Whatever bodily faults may befall him, those all ripen in this very life. For what reason? For he pervades all beings with <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness). And those <s>Buddhas</s> and Blessed Ones, <s>Śāriputra</s>, who in the southern direction abide, endure, maintain themselves, and teach the <s>Dharma</s> in <s>Gaṅgā</s>-sand-numerous world-realms, together with their <s>śrāvakas</s>, <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, and all the gods from <s>Cāturmahārājakāyika</s> up to <s>Akaniṣṭha</s> — they too all protect that <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>: 'Let no one create an obstacle for this <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>!' Whatever bodily faults may befall him, those all ripen in this very life. For what reason? For he pervades all beings with <s>maitrī</s>. [Likewise in all remaining directions.]

children.translated_text: Moreover, <s>Śāriputra</s>, those <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bhagavats</s> who dwell, abide, and carry on in world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river <s>Gaṅgā</s> in the western direction, and who teach the <s>Dharma</s>, and their <s>śrāvakas</s>, and the <s>pratyekabuddhas</s>, and the <s>Cāturmahārājakāyika</s> gods, the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s>, <s>Yāma</s>, <s>Tuṣita</s>, <s>Nirmāṇarati</s>, <s>Paranirmitavaśavartin</s>, <s>Brahmapārṣadya</s>, <s>Brahmapurohita</s>, <s>Mahābrahmā</s>, <s>Parīttābha</s>, <s>Apramāṇābha</s>, <s>Ābhāsvara</s>, <s>Parīttaśubha</s>, <s>Apramāṇaśubha</s>, <s>Śubhakṛtsna</s>, <s>Anabhraka</s>, <s>Puṇyaprasava</s>, <s>Bṛhatphala</s>, <s>Asaṃjñisattva</s>, <s>Śuddhāvāsa</s>, <s>Avṛha</s>, <s>Atapa</s>, <s>Sudṛśa</s>, <s>Sudarśana</s>, and <s>Akaniṣṭha</s> gods — they too protect that <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s>: "May no one create an obstacle for this <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s>." Whatever bodily faults he may have, those too become pertaining to the present life for him. For what reason? Because he pervades all beings with <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness). Likewise, <s>Śāriputra</s>, those <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bhagavats</s> in the northern direction, together with their <s>śrāvakas</s>, <s>pratyekabuddhas</s>, and all the gods from the <s>Cāturmahārājakāyikas</s> up to the <s>Akaniṣṭhas</s>, also protect that <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s>, [thinking:] "May no one create an obstacle for this <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s>." Whatever bodily faults he may have, those too become pertaining to the present life for him. For what reason? Because he pervades all beings with <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness). children.translated_text: There are, <s>Śāriputra</s>, <s>bodhisattva-mahāsattvas</s> who, by the very first arising of the mind of awakening, engage in the practice of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. Together with many hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭis</s> and <s>niyutas</s> of <s>bodhisattvas</s>, they travel from <s>buddhakṣetra</s> to <s>buddhakṣetra</s> for the purification of their own <s>buddhakṣetra</s>, and they fully awaken to <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> in various <s>buddhakṣetras</s>. There are, <s>Śāriputra</s>, <s>bodhisattva-mahāsattvas</s> who, while practicing the six <s>pāramitās</s>, become <s>cakravartins</s> (wheel-turning monarchs), and placing the <s>dānapāramitā</s> (perfection of generosity) foremost, they provide all beings with all means of happiness — food to those who need food, drink to those who need drink, likewise fragrances, garlands, ointments, powders, incense, beds, seats, shelters, dwellings, wealth, grain, jewels, pearls, gold, silver, coral, and ornaments, and the necessities of livelihood. Having established beings in the ten <s>kuśalakarmapatha</s> (wholesome courses of action), they are reborn among the <s>Brahmakāyika</s> gods up to the <s>Akaniṣṭha</s> gods, and fully awaken to <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> in various <s>buddhakṣetras</s>. There are, <s>Śāriputra</s>, <s>bodhisattva-mahāsattvas</s> who, having accomplished the four <s>dhyānas</s> and then having fallen away from the <s>dhyānas</s>, attain the first <s>dhyāna</s> and are reborn among the <s>Brahmakāyika</s> gods. Then again, having accomplished the <s>dhyānas</s>, they are reborn in <s>Akaniṣṭha</s> and fully awaken to <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> in various <s>buddhakṣetras</s>.

children.translated_text: There are, <s>Śāriputra</s>, <s>bodhisattva-mahāsattvas</s> who, having passed away from the <s>Brahmaloka</s>, are reborn in the <s>Śuddhāvāsas</s> (Pure Abodes). Having passed through one or two of the <s>Śuddhāvāsa</s> stations, they are reborn among the <s>Akaniṣṭha</s> gods and fully awaken to <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> in various <s>buddhakṣetras</s>. There are, <s>Śāriputra</s>, <s>bodhisattva-mahāsattvas</s> who, having created a body similar to that of a <s>Tathāgata</s>, purify the <s>Tuṣita</s> heaven, and are reborn among the <s>Brahmakāyika</s> gods up to the <s>Akaniṣṭha</s> gods. Through <s>upāyakauśalya</s> (skillful means) they teach the <s>Dharma</s> to beings in the hells, they teach the <s>Dharma</s> to beings born in animal realms, they teach the <s>Dharma</s> to beings in the world of <s>Yama</s>. There are, <s>Śāriputra</s>, <s>bodhisattva-mahāsattvas</s> who, abiding in the six <s>pāramitās</s>, create a body similar to the body of a <s>Tathāgata</s>, and traveling to <s>buddhakṣetras</s> as numerous as the sands of the river <s>Gaṅgā</s>, they teach the <s>Dharma</s> to beings, attend upon the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, accomplish the <s>buddhakṣetra</s>, and hear the <s>Dharma</s>. Thus in the eastern direction, the southern, western, northern, northeastern, southeastern, southwestern, northwestern, upward, and downward — in all ten directions, in each direction, having gone to world-realms as numerous as the sands of the river <s>Gaṅgā</s>, they teach the <s>Dharma</s> to beings, accomplish <s>buddhakṣetras</s>, attend upon the <s>Buddhas</s>, and hear the <s>Dharma</s>. From those <s>buddhakṣetras</s>, creating emanations, they accomplish the most excellent, supreme, unsurpassed <s>buddhakṣetras</s>,

Rising from that, they enter the sphere of infinite consciousness (<s>vijñānānantyāyatana</s>). Rising from that, they enter the attainment of cessation. There are, <s>Śāriputra</s>, <s>bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s> who, abiding in the six <s>pāramitās</s>, illuminate the <s>Buddha-dharmas</s> for beings. There are, <s>Śāriputra</s>, <s>bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s> who, in buddha-less world-systems devoid of <s>śrāvakas</s> (hearers), fully awaken to <s>pratyekabodhi</s> (solitary awakening). [Thus, the fruits attainable through the <s>śrāvaka</s> (hearer) and <s>pratyekabuddha</s> (solitary awakened one) paths.]
<s>Śāriputra</s>, the knowledge and radiance of all <s>śrāvakas</s> and <s>pratyekabuddhas</s> is the patience of a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> who has attained the acceptance of the non-arising of dharmas (<s>anutpattikadharmakṣānti</s>). Thus, the establishment of others in a dharma not yet attained by oneself. These, <s>Śāriputra</s>, should be known as irreversible (<s>avinivartanīya</s>) <s>bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s> who abide in this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. There are, <s>Śāriputra</s>, <s>bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s> who, abiding in the six <s>pāramitās</s>, purify the <s>Tuṣita</s> heaven. Those <s>bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s> should indeed be known as belonging to the Fortunate Aeon (<s>Bhadrakalpa</s>). These, <s>Śāriputra</s>, are irreversible (<s>vaivartika</s>) <s>bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s> whose arising is in the <s>Buddha-dharmas</s>. Therefore, <s>Śāriputra</s>, a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> practicing the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> should give no occasion to blameworthy actions of body, speech, and mind, and should train for the purification of actions of body, speech, and mind. [Thus, the illumination of the community of irreversible bodhisattvas.] [Thus, the instruction on the jewel of the <s>Saṃgha</s>.]

children.translated_text: When this was said, the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> addressed the Blessed One thus: 'What, Blessed One, is blameworthy bodily action, blameworthy verbal action, blameworthy mental action?' When this was said, the Blessed One addressed the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> thus: 'Here, <s>Śāriputra</s>, when a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> thinks thus: "What is that body with which I might undertake bodily action? What is that speech with which I might undertake verbal action? What is that mind with which I might undertake mental action?" — while examining thus, he apprehends body, he apprehends speech, he apprehends mind. This, <s>Śāriputra</s>, is the blameworthy undertaking of bodily, verbal, and mental action of a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>. But indeed, <s>Śāriputra</s>, a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> practicing <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> does not apprehend body, does not apprehend speech, does not apprehend mind — by which body, speech, and mind he might produce a thought of miserliness, ill-conduct, malice, laziness, distraction, or faulty wisdom. It is impossible, <s>Śāriputra</s>, there is no occasion that a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> practicing <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> would produce coarseness of body, speech, or mind. This situation does not exist. For what reason? For indeed, <s>Śāriputra</s>, a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> practicing the six <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections) purifies the coarseness of body, purifies the coarseness of speech, purifies the coarseness of mind.' <s>Śāriputra</s> asked: 'How, Blessed One, does a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> purify the coarseness of body, speech, and mind?' The Blessed One said: 'Because, <s>Śāriputra</s>, a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> does not apprehend body, does not apprehend speech, does not apprehend mind.'

children.translated_text: 'Thus indeed, <s>Śāriputra</s>, a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> purifies the coarseness of body, speech, and mind. Moreover, <s>Śāriputra</s>, when the ten wholesome paths of action follow upon a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> from the first arising of the thought (of awakening), and he does not produce a <s>śrāvaka</s>-thought or a <s>pratyekabuddha</s>-thought, and when the thought of great compassion (<s>mahākaruṇā</s>) is constantly and continuously present toward all beings — thus indeed, <s>Śāriputra</s>, I declare that the coarseness of body, speech, and mind of a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> is purified. There are, <s>Śāriputra</s>, <s>bodhisattvas</s> <s>mahāsattvas</s> who, while practicing <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> and purifying the path of awakening (<s>bodhimārga</s>), practice the perfection of generosity (<s>dānapāramitā</s>), the perfection of morality (<s>śīlapāramitā</s>), the perfection of patience (<s>kṣāntipāramitā</s>), the perfection of vigor (<s>vīryapāramitā</s>), the perfection of meditation (<s>dhyānapāramitā</s>), and the perfection of wisdom (<s>prajñāpāramitā</s>).' <s>Śāriputra</s> asked: 'What, Blessed One, is the path of awakening (<s>bodhimārga</s>) of <s>bodhisattvas</s> <s>mahāsattvas</s>?' The Blessed One said: 'When, <s>Śāriputra</s>, a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> practicing <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> does not apprehend body, does not apprehend speech, does not apprehend mind, does not apprehend the perfection of generosity, does not apprehend the perfection of morality, does not apprehend the perfection of patience, does not apprehend the perfection of vigor, does not apprehend the perfection of meditation, does not apprehend the perfection of wisdom, does not apprehend a <s>śrāvaka</s>, does not apprehend a <s>pratyekabuddha</s>, does not apprehend a <s>bodhisattva</s>, does not apprehend a <s>Buddha</s> — this, <s>Śāriputra</s>, is the path of awakening (<s>bodhimārga</s>) of a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, namely, the non-apprehension of all <s>dharmas</s> (<s>sarvadharmānupalambha</s>). Proceeding by this path, a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> practicing the six <s>pāramitās</s> cannot be crushed.'

07701 There are, <s>Śāriputra</s>, <s>bodhisattva-mahāsattvas</s> who attain and purify the five eyes.

07703 the <s>Dharma</s> eye (<s>dharmacakṣus</s>), and the <s>Buddha</s> eye (<s>buddhacakṣus</s>).
07704 <s>Śāriputra</s> said: What, <s>Bhagavān</s>, is the purified fleshly eye of a <s>bodhisattva-mahāsattva</s>?
07705 The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: There is, <s>Śāriputra</s>, a fleshly eye of a <s>bodhisattva-mahāsattva</s>
07706 that sees a hundred <s>yojanas</s>. There is a fleshly eye of a <s>bodhisattva-mahāsattva</s>
07707 that sees two hundred <s>yojanas</s>. There is [a fleshly eye] that sees [all of] <s>Jambudvīpa</s>. There is [one] that
07708 sees a four-continent world-realm. There is [one] that sees a thousandfold world-realm.
07709 There is [one] that sees a twofold-thousand world-realm. There is [one] that sees the <s>trisāhasramahā</s>-
07710 <s>sāhasra</s> (great trichiliocosm) world-realm. This, <s>Śāriputra</s>, is the purified
07711 fleshly eye of a <s>bodhisattva-mahāsattva</s>.
07712 <s>Śāriputra</s> said: What, <s>Bhagavān</s>, is the purified divine eye of a <s>bodhisattva-mahāsattva</s>?

07714 that, the <s>bodhisattva</s> knows. The divine eye of the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> <s>devas</s> —
07715 that, the <s>bodhisattva</s> knows. The divine eye of the <s>Yāma</s> <s>devas</s> —
07716 that, the <s>bodhisattva</s> knows. [The divine eye of the <s>Tuṣita</s> <s>devas</s> — that, the <s>bodhisattva</s> knows. The divine eye of the <s>Nirmāṇarati</s> <s>devas</s> — that, the <s>bodhisattva</s> knows. The divine eye of the <s>Paranirmitavaśavartin</s> <s>devas</s> — that, the <s>bodhisattva</s> knows. children.translated_text: <s>Śāriputra</s> said: What, <s>Bhagavan</s>, is the completely pure wisdom eye of the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>? The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: The wisdom eye with which the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> is endowed, <s>Śāriputra</s>, does not cognize any <s>dharma</s> whatsoever — whether conditioned or unconditioned, wholesome or unwholesome, blameworthy or blameless, with outflows or without outflows, defiled or undefiled, worldly or supramundane, afflicted or purified. With this wisdom eye, no <s>dharma</s> whatsoever has been seen, heard, thought, or cognized by the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>. This, <s>Śāriputra</s>, is the completely pure wisdom eye of the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>.

children.translated_text: <s>Śāriputra</s> said: What, <s>Bhagavan</s>, is the completely pure <s>Dharma</s>-eye of the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>? The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: Here, <s>Śāriputra</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> knows by means of the <s>Dharma</s>-eye alone: 'This person is a faith-follower. This person is a <s>Dharma</s>-follower. This person abides in <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness). This person abides in the signless. This person abides in the wishless. This person abides in <s>śūnyatā</s>. Through the gateway of liberation of <s>śūnyatā</s>, the five faculties will arise for this person. Through the five faculties, he attains the uninterrupted <s>samādhi</s>. Through the uninterrupted <s>samādhi</s>, he will produce the knowledge and vision of liberation. Through the knowledge and vision of liberation, he will abandon the three fetters — the view of a self-existing body, attachment to rules and rituals, and doubt. This person is called a stream-enterer. Having attained the path of cultivation, because of the attenuation of sensual desire and ill-will, this person is called a once-returner. Through that very path of cultivation, intensively developed, because of the abandonment of sensual desire and ill-will, this person is called a non-returner. Through that very path of cultivation, intensively developed, having abandoned desire for form, desire for the formless, ignorance, pride, and restlessness, this person is called an <s>arhat</s>.' Through the five faculties, he attains the uninterrupted <s>samādhi</s>. Through the uninterrupted <s>samādhi</s>, he will produce the knowledge and vision of liberation. Through the knowledge and vision of liberation, he will abandon the three fetters — the view of a self-existing body, attachment to rules and rituals, and doubt. This person is called a stream-enterer. Having attained the path of cultivation, because of the attenuation of sensual desire and ill-will, this person is called a once-returner. Through that very path of cultivation, intensively developed, because of the abandonment of sensual desire and ill-will, this person is called a non-returner. Through that very path of cultivation, intensively developed, having abandoned desire for form, desire for the formless, ignorance, pride, and restlessness, this person is called an <s>arhat</s>.' 'This person abides in the wishless. Through the gateway of liberation of the wishless, the five faculties will arise for this person. Through the five faculties, he attains the uninterrupted <s>samādhi</s>. Through the uninterrupted <s>samādhi</s>, he will produce the knowledge and vision of liberation. Through the knowledge and vision of liberation, he will abandon the three fetters — the view of a self-existing body, attachment to rules and rituals, and doubt. This person is called a stream-enterer. Having attained the path of cultivation, because of the attenuation of sensual desire and ill-will, this person is called a once-returner. Through that very path of cultivation, intensively developed, because of the abandonment of sensual desire and ill-will, this person is called a non-returner. Through that very path of cultivation, intensively developed, having abandoned desire for form, desire for the formless, ignorance, pride, and restlessness, this person is called an <s>arhat</s>.' This, <s>Śāriputra</s>, is the completely pure <s>Dharma</s>-eye of the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>.

children.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Śāriputra</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> knows thus: 'Whatever has the nature of arising (<s>samudayadharmin</s>), all that has the nature of cessation (<s>nirodhadharmin</s>).' Furthermore, <s>Śāriputra</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> knows thus: 'This <s>bodhisattva</s> has just produced the initial aspiration (<s>prathamacittotpādika</s>), who practices either the perfection of generosity (<s>dānapāramitā</s>) or the perfection of morality (<s>śīlapāramitā</s>) — he thereby obtains the faculty of faith (<s>śraddhendriya</s>) and the faculty of vigor (<s>vīryendriya</s>). Endowed with <s>upāyakauśalya</s> (skillful means), he deliberately takes on a physical existence and becomes one who apprehends wholesome roots (<s>kuśalamūla</s>). This <s>bodhisattva</s> will be reborn in great <s>brāhmaṇa</s> families. This one will be reborn in great <s>kṣatriya</s> families. This one will be reborn in great householder (<s>gṛhapati</s>) families. This one will be reborn among the <s>Cāturmahārājakāyika</s> gods. This one will be reborn among the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods. This one will be reborn among the <s>Yāma</s> gods. This one will be reborn among the <s>Tuṣita</s> gods. This one will be reborn among the <s>Nirmāṇarati</s> gods. This one will be reborn among the <s>Paranirmitavaśavartin</s> gods. This one will be reborn even up to the <s>Akaniṣṭha</s> gods. Having established himself there, he will ripen beings, serve beings by every possible means, purify the <s>buddhakṣetra</s> (buddha-field), and please the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, the <s>Arhats</s>, the perfectly enlightened ones — he will honor, revere, and respect them, and will not fall into the level of the <s>Śrāvaka</s> or the level of the <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>. This <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> does not turn back until he has fully awakened to <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> (unsurpassed perfect enlightenment).' This, <s>Śāriputra</s>, is the purified <s>dharmacakṣus</s> (dharma-eye) of the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>.

children.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Śāriputra</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> knows thus: 'These <s>bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s> have received a prediction (<s>vyākaraṇa</s>) regarding <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> (unsurpassed perfect enlightenment); these <s>bodhisattvas</s> have not received a prediction. These <s>bodhisattvas</s> have perfected their <s>abhijñās</s> (superknowledges); these <s>bodhisattvas</s> have not perfected them. This <s>bodhisattva</s>, having perfected the <s>abhijñās</s>, goes to world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river <s>Gaṅgā</s> in the eastern direction and even up to the zenith, and honors, reveres, respects, and worships the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, the <s>Arhats</s>, the perfectly enlightened ones. This <s>bodhisattva</s> has not perfected the <s>abhijñās</s> and does not worship them. This <s>bodhisattva</s> will obtain the <s>abhijñās</s>; this <s>bodhisattva</s> will not obtain the <s>abhijñās</s>. This <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> will have a purified <s>buddhakṣetra</s> (buddha-field); this <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> will have an unpurified <s>buddhakṣetra</s>. By this <s>bodhisattva</s>, beings have been purified; by this <s>bodhisattva</s>, beings have not been purified. The <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones, speak the praise of this <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>; of this one they do not speak the praise. These <s>bodhisattvas</s> will abide near the <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones; these <s>bodhisattvas</s> will not abide near them. This <s>bodhisattva</s> will have a limited lifespan; this <s>bodhisattva</s> will have an unlimited lifespan. This <s>bodhisattva</s> will have a limited <s>saṃgha</s>; this <s>bodhisattva</s> will have an unlimited <s>saṃgha</s>. This <s>bodhisattva</s>, having fully awakened to <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>, will have a <s>bodhisattvasaṃgha</s>; this one will not have a <s>bodhisattvasaṃgha</s>.'

children.translated_text: 'This <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> will practice austerities (<s>duṣkaracaryā</s>); this one will not practice austerities. This <s>bodhisattva</s> is in his last existence (<s>caramabhavika</s>); this one is not in his last existence. This <s>bodhisattva</s> will sit at the seat of enlightenment (<s>bodhimaṇḍa</s>); this one will not sit at the seat of enlightenment. This <s>bodhisattva</s> will have a <s>Māra</s>; this one will not have a <s>Māra</s>.' Thus indeed, <s>Śāriputra</s>, is the purified <s>dharmacakṣus</s> (dharma-eye) of the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>. <s>Śāriputra</s> said: 'What, Blessed One, is the purified <s>buddhacakṣus</s> (buddha-eye) of the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>?' The Blessed One said: '<s>Śāriputra</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, immediately after producing the thought of enlightenment (<s>bodhicitta</s>), enters the diamond-like <s>samādhi</s> (<s>vajropamasamādhi</s>) and with wisdom conjoined in a single moment of mind (<s>ekacittakṣaṇasamāyukta</s>) attains <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> (omniscience of all aspects). He is endowed with the ten powers of the <s>Tathāgata</s> (<s>tathāgatabala</s>), the four confidences (<s>vaiśāradya</s>), the four analytical knowledges (<s>pratisaṃvid</s>), and the eighteen special qualities of a <s>Buddha</s> (<s>āveṇikabuddhadharma</s>), and is endowed with great loving-kindness (<s>mahāmaitrī</s>) and great compassion (<s>mahākaruṇā</s>). With this eye, there is nothing that the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> has not seen, not heard, not cognized, or not known, in all aspects.' Thus indeed, <s>Śāriputra</s>, is the purified <s>buddhacakṣus</s> (buddha-eye) of the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>.

children.translated_text: Thus, <s>Śāriputra</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> who wishes to purify the five eyes (<s>pañcacakṣus</s>) should practice the six <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections). For what reason? Because, <s>Śāriputra</s>, all wholesome <s>dharmas</s> are included within the six <s>pāramitās</s> — all <s>Śrāvaka</s>-dharmas, all <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>-dharmas, and all <s>bodhisattva</s>-dharmas. Indeed, <s>Śāriputra</s>, those who speak correctly would say that the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is the collection of all wholesome <s>dharmas</s>. For what reason? Because, <s>Śāriputra</s>, the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is the mother that gives birth to all the <s>pāramitās</s> and to these five eyes of the <s>bodhisattva</s>. Having trained in these five eyes of the <s>bodhisattva</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s> fully awaken to <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> (unsurpassed perfect enlightenment). [Thus ends the teaching on the five eyes.] Herein, <s>Śāriputra</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, while practicing the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, cultivates the perfection of superknowledges (<s>abhijñāpāramitā</s>). He experiences manifold forms of miraculous powers (<s>ṛddhividhi</s>): he causes the earth to quake; having been one, he becomes many; having been many, he becomes one. He experiences both appearance and disappearance. He passes unobstructed through walls, through ramparts, through mountains, just as a bird passes through the sky. He dives in and out of the earth just as if it were water. He walks upon water without breaking through, just as upon earth. He smokes and blazes like a great mass of fire. He releases water from his body like a great rain cloud. Even these

children.translated_text: he touches and strokes the sun and moon, so great in supernatural power and majesty, with his hand; he controls his body at will even up to the <s>Brahmaloka</s> (world of Brahmā). Yet he does not conceive of that <s>ṛddhi</s> (supernatural power). For indeed, he does not apprehend that supernatural power by which he might conceive; and that too he does not conceive, on account of the emptiness of intrinsic nature (<s>svabhāvaśūnyatā</s>), on account of the separation of intrinsic nature (<s>svabhāvaviviktatā</s>), on account of the non-apprehension of intrinsic nature (<s>svabhāvānupalabdhitā</s>). He does not even produce the volition for supernatural power, nor the volition for the accomplishment of supernatural power, except through attention to <s>sarvajñatā</s> (omniscience). In this way, <s>Śāriputra</s>, a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> practicing <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> accomplishes the knowledge of the direct realization of the <s>abhijñā</s> (superknowledge) of the varieties of supernatural power (<s>ṛddhividhi</s>). With the divine ear-element (<s>divyaśrotradhātu</s>), purified and surpassing the human, he hears sounds both divine and human. Yet he does not conceive with that divine ear, 'I hear sounds.' For indeed, he does not apprehend that very sound, on account of the emptiness of intrinsic nature, on account of the separation of intrinsic nature, on account of the non-apprehension of intrinsic nature. He does not even produce the volition for the divine ear, nor the volition for the accomplishment of the divine ear, except through attention to <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> (knowledge of all aspects). In this way, <s>Śāriputra</s>, a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> practicing <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> accomplishes the knowledge of the direct realization of the <s>abhijñā</s> of the divine ear.

children.translated_text: With his mind he knows as it truly is the minds of other beings and other persons. He knows as it truly is a mind with passion as 'a mind with passion,' a mind free from passion as 'a mind free from passion,' a mind with aversion as 'a mind with aversion,' a mind free from aversion, a mind with delusion, a mind free from delusion, a mind with craving, a mind free from craving, a mind with clinging, a mind without clinging, a contracted mind, a distracted mind, a limited mind, an expansive mind, an exalted mind, a concentrated mind, an unconcentrated mind, a liberated mind, an unliberated mind, a mind with outflows (<s>sāsrava</s>), a mind without outflows (<s>anāsrava</s>), a mind with defilements, a mind without defilements, a surpassable mind, an unsurpassable mind. Yet he does not conceive of this. For indeed, that mind is non-mind (<s>acitta</s>), on account of its inconceivability (<s>acintyatā</s>). He does not conceive, 'I know.' He does not apprehend that very mind, on account of the emptiness of intrinsic nature, on account of the separation of intrinsic nature, on account of the non-apprehension of intrinsic nature. He does not even produce the volition for knowledge of others' minds, nor the volition for the accomplishment of knowledge of others' minds, except through attention to <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> (knowledge of all aspects). In this way, <s>Śāriputra</s>, a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> practicing <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> accomplishes the knowledge of the direct realization of the <s>abhijñā</s> of knowing the conduct and thoughts of all beings.

children.translated_text: With the knowledge of the recollection of former abodes (<s>pūrvanivāsānusmṛtijñāna</s>), he recollects one birth, two, three, up to hundreds of thousands of births. He recollects one mind-moment, up to a hundred mind-moments; one day, up to a hundred days; one month, up to a hundred months; one year, up to a hundred years; one <s>kalpa</s> (aeon), up to a hundred <s>kalpas</s>; many hundreds of <s>kalpas</s>, many thousands of <s>kalpas</s>, many hundreds of thousands of <s>kalpas</s>, many <s>koṭi-niyuta</s>-hundreds of thousands of <s>kalpas</s> — he recollects up to the furthest limit of the past. 'In such a place I was, with such a name, such a lineage, such a birth, such food, such a lifespan, such a length of life. Passing away from there, I was reborn in such a place; passing away from there, I was reborn here.' Thus he recollects his manifold former abodes with their aspects, their appearances, and their details. Yet he does not conceive of that <s>abhijñā</s> of recollection of former abodes. For indeed, that knowledge is non-knowledge (<s>ajñāna</s>), on account of its inconceivability. He does not conceive, 'I know.' He does not apprehend that very knowledge, on account of the emptiness of intrinsic nature, on account of the separation of intrinsic nature, on account of the non-apprehension of intrinsic nature. children.translated_text: practicing <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> accomplishes the knowledge of the direct realization of the recollection of former abodes. With the divine eye (<s>divyacakṣus</s>), purified and surpassing the human, he sees beings dying and being reborn — fair-complexioned and ill-complexioned, in good destinies and bad destinies. He knows beings as they fare according to their <s>karma</s>: 'These beings, endowed with good conduct of body, endowed with good conduct of speech, endowed with good conduct of mind, not reviling the noble ones (<s>āryas</s>), possessed of right views — by reason of their good conduct of body, speech, and mind, they are reborn in a good destiny, in a heavenly world. But these beings, endowed with misconduct of body, endowed with misconduct of speech, endowed with misconduct of mind, reviling the noble ones, possessed of wrong views — by reason of undertaking the <s>karma</s> of wrong views, upon the breaking up of the body, after death, they are reborn in a state of deprivation (<s>apāya</s>), in a bad destiny, in perdition, in the hells.' Thus with the divine eye, purified and surpassing the human, in the world of the ten directions, in all world-realms, ending at the limit of the <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of reality), reaching the boundary of the <s>ākāśadhātu</s> (realm of space), he knows as it truly is the death and rebirth of beings in the six destinies. children.translated_text: Thus again, <s>Śāriputra</s>, when the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> (great being) practices the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> (Perfection of Wisdom), the six <s>abhijñās</s> (supernatural knowledges) are fulfilled and purified. The purified <s>abhijñās</s>, <s>Śāriputra</s>, lead to <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> (omniscience). There are, <s>Śāriputra</s>, <s>bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s> who, while practicing the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, established in the <s>dānapāramitā</s> (perfection of generosity), purify the path to <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> through <s>atyantaśūnyatā</s> (ultimate emptiness), not through the concept of grasping. There are those who, established in <s>śīlapāramitā</s> (perfection of morality), purify the path to <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> through <s>atyantaśūnyatā</s>, through the concept of non-transgression. There are those who, established in <s>kṣāntipāramitā</s> (perfection of patience), purify the path through <s>atyantaśūnyatā</s>, through the concept of imperturbability. There are those who, established in <s>vīryapāramitā</s> (perfection of vigor), purify the path through <s>atyantaśūnyatā</s>, through the concept of non-relaxation of bodily and mental energy. There are those who, established in <s>dhyānapāramitā</s> (perfection of meditation), purify the path through <s>atyantaśūnyatā</s>, through the concept of an undistracted mind. There are those who, established in <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> (perfection of wisdom), purify the path through <s>atyantaśūnyatā</s>, through the concept of abandoning an unwise mind. Thus indeed, <s>Śāriputra</s>, <s>bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s>, while practicing the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, established in the six <s>pāramitās</s>, purify the path to <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> through <s>atyantaśūnyatā</s>. <s>Dāna</s> (generosity) is designated in dependence on grasping; <s>śīla</s> (morality) is designated in dependence on immorality; <s>kṣānti</s> (patience) is designated in dependence on impatience; <s>vīrya</s> (vigor) is designated in dependence on laziness; <s>samādhi</s> (concentration) is designated in dependence on non-concentration; <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) is designated in dependence on folly. He does not think 'I have crossed over.' He does not think 'I have not crossed over.' He does not think '<s>dāna</s> [is one thing and] grasping [another].' He does not think '<s>śīla</s> [is one thing and] immorality [another].' He does not think '<s>kṣānti</s> [is one thing and] agitation [another].' He does not think '<s>vīrya</s> [is one thing and] laziness —'

children.translated_text: He does not think '<s>samādhi</s> [is one thing and] non-concentration [another].' He does not think '<s>prajñā</s> [is one thing and] folly [another].' He does not think 'I have been reviled.' He does not think 'I have been honored.' He does not think 'I have been respected.' He does not think 'I have been disrespected.' For what reason? For indeed, <s>Śāriputra</s>, the unborn (<s>anutpāda</s>) does not think 'I have been reviled,' nor 'I have been honored,' nor 'I have been respected,' nor 'I have been disrespected.' For what reason? For the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> cuts off all thinking. Here, <s>Śāriputra</s>, when a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> practices the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, the virtues that arise in him are not found among <s>śrāvakas</s> (disciples) and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>. Fulfilling these virtues, he matures beings, purifies the <s>buddhakṣetra</s> (buddha-field), and attains <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> (omniscience). Furthermore, <s>Śāriputra</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> generates equal-mindedness toward all beings; having generated equal-mindedness toward all beings, he attains the equality of all <s>dharmas</s>; having attained the equality of all <s>dharmas</s>, he establishes all beings in the equality of all <s>dharmas</s>. In this very life he becomes dear and pleasing to the <s>Buddhas</s> and Blessed Ones, to all <s>bodhisattvas</s>, all <s>śrāvakas</s>, and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>. Wherever he is reborn, there he never sees unpleasant forms with his eyes, never hears unpleasant sounds with his ears, never smells unpleasant scents with his nose —

While this teaching of the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> was being expounded, three hundred <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s> (nuns) covered the Blessed One with their robes as they were and generated the thought of <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>. Then the Blessed One, at that moment, produced a smile. Then the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, rising from his seat, arranging his upper robe over one shoulder, placing his right knee on the ground, and extending his palms joined together toward the Blessed One, addressed the Blessed One thus: 'What, Blessed One, is the cause, what is the condition, for the appearance of this smile? For <s>Buddhas</s> and Blessed Ones do not produce a smile without cause or condition.' The Blessed One said: 'These three hundred <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s>, <s>Ānanda</s>, in the sixty-first <s>kalpa</s> (aeon) from now, will arise in the world as <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, perfectly and fully awakened ones, named <s>Mahāketu</s> (Great Banner), in the <s>kalpa</s> called <s>Tārakopama</s> (Star-like). Then the Blessed One, knowing the disposition of those sons and daughters of good family, at that moment produced a smile. <s>Ānanda</s> asked: 'What, Blessed One, is the cause, what is the condition, for the appearance of this smile?' The Blessed One said: 'Do you see, <s>Ānanda</s>, these ten thousand beings?' <s>Ānanda</s> said: 'I see them, Blessed One.' The Blessed One said: 'These ten thousand beings, <s>Ānanda</s>, having passed away from here, will be reborn in those thousands of <s>buddhakṣetras</s> in the ten directions. children.translated_text: meditation (<s>dhyāna</s>) has been produced, by them the incomparable <s>dhyānapāramitā</s> (perfection of meditation) has been fulfilled. By them incomparable wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>) has been cultivated, by them the incomparable <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> (perfection of wisdom) has been fulfilled. And you yourself, Blessed One, practicing in this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, became a gainer of incomparable form (<s>rūpa</s>), a gainer of incomparable feeling (<s>vedanā</s>), perception (<s>saṃjñā</s>), formations (<s>saṃskāras</s>), and incomparable consciousness (<s>vijñāna</s>); you awakened to incomparable awakening (<s>bodhi</s>), and the incomparable wheel of the <s>Dharma</s> (<s>dharmacakra</s>) was set in motion. Thus the <s>Buddhas</s> and Blessed Ones of the past, future, and present, practicing in this very <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, have awakened, will awaken, and are awakening to unsurpassed perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>). Therefore, Blessed One, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> who wishes to go to the far shore of all <s>dharmas</s> should exert effort in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. Those <s>bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s> who practice this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> are worthy of homage, Blessed One, by the world with its <s>devas</s>, humans, and <s>asuras</s>." When this was said, the Blessed One said to those many <s>śrāvakas</s> (disciples) and those <s>bodhisattvas</s>: "So it is, sons of good family, so it is. Those <s>bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s> who practice this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> are worthy of homage by the world with its <s>devas</s>, humans, and <s>asuras</s>. What is the reason? children.translated_text: It is through the <s>bodhisattva</s> that there arises in the world the manifestation of stream-enterers (<s>srotaāpannas</s>), once-returners (<s>sakṛdāgāmins</s>), non-returners (<s>anāgāmins</s>), <s>arhats</s>, <s>pratyekabuddhas</s>, <s>bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s>, and <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>arhats</s>, perfectly and fully awakened ones (<s>samyaksaṃbuddhas</s>). For, <s>Śāriputra</s>, it is through the <s>bodhisattva</s> that there arises in the world the manifestation of the Three Jewels (<s>triratna</s>). And there arises in the world the manifestation of all worldly means of livelihood — food, drink, clothing, beds, seats, medicines and provisions for the sick — and of gems, pearls, <s>vaiḍūrya</s> (lapis lazuli), conch, crystal, coral, gold, and silver. Indeed, <s>Śāriputra</s>, through the <s>bodhisattva</s> there arises in the world the manifestation of all provisions of happiness, both divine and human, and of the gateways to existence and the gateways to <s>nirvāṇa</s> — in every way, <s>Śāriputra</s>, through the <s>bodhisattva</s>. What is the reason? For, <s>Śāriputra</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s>, while practicing his course, engages beings in the six <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections): he causes them to give gifts, he causes them to undertake morality (<s>śīla</s>), he establishes them in patience (<s>kṣānti</s>), he engages them in vigor (<s>vīrya</s>), he establishes them in meditation (<s>dhyāna</s>), and he engages them in wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>). And all beings, through the <s>bodhisattva</s>, practice the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. Therefore, <s>Śāriputra</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> has set out for the welfare of all beings. Then the Blessed One, at that time, extended his tongue faculty and covered this <s>trisāhasramahāsāhasra lokadhātu</s> (great trichiliocosm) with his tongue faculty. Then from that tongue faculty there issued forth rays of many colors, of various hues, and they illuminated world-realms as numerous as the sands of the river <s>Gaṅgā</s> in the eastern direction. children.translated_text: illuminated [world-realms] with fearlessness. They illuminated world-realms as numerous as the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> river in the western direction with fearlessness. Likewise in the northern direction, the northeastern, southeastern, southwestern, northwestern, and the direction below—they illuminated world-realms as numerous as the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> in each direction with fearlessness. They illuminated world-realms as numerous as the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> river in the direction above with fearlessness. Then, from the <s>Buddhakṣetras</s> as numerous as the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> river in the eastern direction and so on up to the direction above, immeasurable and innumerable <s>bodhisattvas</s>, having seen those arrays of radiance, inquired of the <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones, in their respective <s>Buddhakṣetras</s>: 'Blessed One, by whose power is this display of brilliant radiance seen?' Those <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones, said to those <s>bodhisattvas</s> <s>mahāsattvas</s>: 'Sons of good family, in the western direction and so on down to the lower region, in the <s>Sahā</s> world-realm, a <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, fully awakened <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s> named <s>Śākyamuni</s> lives, endures, and sustains [himself]. Having extended his tongue faculty, he has made world-realms as numerous as the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> river in every direction shine brightly with radiance, and so on up to the direction above—thus in the ten directions, world-realms as numerous as the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> river have been made to shine brightly with radiance, for the purpose of teaching and illuminating the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> to the {<s>bodhisattvas</s>} <s>mahāsattvas</s>.' Those <s>bodhisattvas</s> said to those <s>Tathāgatas</s>: 'We wish to go, Blessed One, to that <s>Sahā</s> world-realm, to see, pay homage to, and attend upon that Blessed One, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Śākyamuni</s>, and to see those {<s>bodhisattvas</s>} <s>mahāsattvas</s> assembled from the ten directions, and to hear that <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.' Those <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones, said: 'Go, sons of good family, if you consider this the right time.' Then those {<s>bodhisattvas</s>} <s>mahāsattvas</s> from the ten directions, having taken flowers, incense, fragrance, garlands, unguents, powders, robes, parasols, banners, flags, and victory standards, and having taken baskets of various jewels, gold, silver, and flowers, with great music, drumming, and singing, approached the Blessed One <s>Śākyamuni</s>. Then the gods of the <s>Cāturmahārājakāyika</s> realm, the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods, the <s>Yāma</s> gods, the <s>Tuṣita</s> gods, the <s>Nirmāṇarati</s> gods, the <s>Paranirmitavaśavartin</s> gods, the <s>Brahmakāyika</s> gods, the <s>Brahmapurohita</s> gods, the <s>Brahmapāriṣadya</s> gods, the <s>Parīttābha</s> gods, the <s>Apramāṇābha</s> gods, the <s>Ābhāsvara</s> gods, the <s>Parīttaśubha</s> gods, the <s>Apramāṇaśubha</s> gods, the <s>Śubhakṛtsna</s> gods, the <s>Anabhraka</s> gods, the <s>Puṇyaprasava</s> gods, the <s>Bṛhatphala</s> gods, the <s>Asaṃjñisattva</s> gods, the <s>Śuddhāvāsa</s> gods, the <s>Aspṛha</s> gods, the <s>Atapa</s> gods, the <s>Sadṛśa</s> gods, the <s>Sudarśana</s> gods, and the <s>Akaniṣṭha</s> gods, having taken divine flowers, incense, fragrance, garlands, unguents, powders, robes, parasols, banners, flags, <s>utpala</s> lotuses, <s>kumuda</s> lotuses, white lotuses, <s>mandārava</s> flowers, and <s>kesaratamāla</s> leaves, approached the Blessed One. Then those <s>bodhisattvas</s> and those gods showered the <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, fully awakened <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s> with those flowers, incense, fragrance, garlands, and unguents. Then those flowers, having risen up and leaving [their hands], stationed themselves above this great trichiliocosm as a pavilion of flowers—four-pillared, four-cornered, well-proportioned on each side, delightful, and pleasing to the heart. Then from that assembly, hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>niyutas</s> of living beings rose from their seats, arranged their upper robes over one shoulder, placed their right knee on the ground, and joining their palms toward the Blessed One, said to the Blessed One: 'Blessed One, may we in the future obtain such <s>dharmas</s> as the <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, fully awakened <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s> [teaches], and may we lead such an assembly of <s>Śrāvakas</s>, and may we teach the <s>Dharma</s> in such an assembly, just as the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the Blessed One, now teaches the <s>Dharma</s>.' Then the Blessed One, knowing the dispositions of those sons of good family, and knowing their acceptance of the non-arising, non-ceasing, non-production, and non-appearance of all <s>dharmas</s>, smiled. Then rays of many colors issued forth from the mouth of the Blessed One, circumambulated the entire world, and returning, disappeared into the crown of the Blessed One's head. Having directly realized [the truth], whatever they speak, teach, and instruct—none of that contradicts <s>dharmatā</s> (the nature of reality). It is the <s>Tathāgata</s> alone, <s>Śāriputra</s>, who through the application of skillful means will instruct the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s> in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. It is beyond the scope of all <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, <s>Śāriputra</s>, to instruct the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s> in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. [Thus the introduction of instruction on the path of seeing.]
Then the Venerable <s>Subhūti</s> spoke thus to the Blessed One: '<s>Bodhisattva</s>'—so it is said, Blessed One. Of which <s>dharma</s> is this a designation, Blessed One, namely '<s>bodhisattva</s>'? I do not perceive, Blessed One, any <s>dharma</s> called '<s>bodhisattva</s>.' Since I do not perceive a <s>bodhisattva</s> and do not apprehend even the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, which <s>bodhisattva</s> shall I instruct in which <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>?' The Blessed One said: This is a mere name, <s>Subhūti</s>, namely '<s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>' and '<s>bodhisattva</s>.' Moreover, that name '<s>bodhisattva</s>' is not apprehended internally, nor externally, nor in between. Just as, <s>Subhūti</s>, 'being' is what it is called—yet no being whatsoever is apprehended. And that name is merely a designation, a <s>dharma</s> of designation, a designation-entity. [Thus the patience of <s>dharmajñāna</s> regarding suffering.]

children.translated_text: knower, seer—all of these are <s>dharmas</s> of designation, all are without arising, without cessation; they are employed solely by mere names. Even so, <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, and the name '<s>bodhisattva</s>'—all of these are <s>dharmas</s> of designation, all are without arising, without cessation; they are employed solely by mere names. Just as, <s>Subhūti</s>, 'this is internal form'—that is merely a designation of a <s>dharma</s>. Of that <s>dharma</s>-designation there is neither arising nor cessation; it is employed solely by the convention of names. '<s>Vedanā</s>' (feeling), <s>Subhūti</s>, is merely a designation of a <s>dharma</s>; of that designation there is neither arising nor cessation; it is employed solely by convention of names. '<s>Saṃjñā</s>' (perception), <s>Subhūti</s>, is merely a designation of a <s>dharma</s>; of that designation there is neither arising nor cessation. '<s>Saṃskāras</s>' (formations), <s>Subhūti</s>, are merely a designation of a <s>dharma</s>; of that designation there is neither arising nor cessation. '<s>Vijñāna</s>' (consciousness), <s>Subhūti</s>, is merely a designation of a <s>dharma</s>; of that designation there is neither arising nor cessation; it is employed solely by convention of names. Even so, <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s>, and the name '<s>bodhisattva</s>'—all are <s>dharmas</s> of designation, and of those <s>dharmas</s> of designation there is neither arising nor cessation; they are employed solely by the convention of names. 'The eye,' <s>Subhūti</s>, is merely a designation of a <s>dharma</s>; of that designation there is neither arising nor cessation; it is employed solely by convention of names. That which is called 'the eye'—that eye is not apprehended internally, nor externally, nor in between. 'The ear,' <s>Subhūti</s>, is merely a designation; of that designation there is neither arising nor cessation. That ear is not apprehended internally, nor externally, nor in between. 'Smell,' <s>Subhūti</s>, is merely a designation. 'Taste,' <s>Subhūti</s>, is merely a designation. 'Touch,' <s>Subhūti</s>, is merely a designation. '<s>Dharmas</s>' (mental objects), <s>Subhūti</s>, are merely a designation. Of all these designations there is neither arising nor cessation; they are employed solely by convention of names. 'The eye-element, the form-element, and the eye-consciousness-element,' <s>Subhūti</s>, are merely designations; of those designations there is neither arising nor cessation. And they are not apprehended internally, nor externally, nor in between. 'The ear-element, the sound-element, and the ear-consciousness-element,' <s>Subhūti</s>, are merely designations; they are not apprehended internally, nor externally, nor in between. children.translated_text: the body element (<s>kāyadhātu</s>), the tangible element (<s>spraṣṭavyadhātu</s>), and the body-consciousness element (<s>kāyavijñānadhātu</s>) — <s>Subhūti</s>, this is a mere designation of dharmas (<s>dharmaprajñaptimātra</s>). And of that designation of dharmas there is no arising (<s>utpāda</s>) and no cessation (<s>nirodha</s>); it is spoken of only through the convention of names (<s>nāmasaṅketamātra</s>). And they are not found internally (<s>adhyātma</s>), nor externally (<s>bahirdhā</s>), nor in between. The mind element (<s>manodhātu</s>), the dharma element (<s>dharmadhātu</s>), and the mind-consciousness element (<s>manovijñānadhātu</s>) — <s>Subhūti</s>, this is a mere designation of dharmas. And of that designation of dharmas there is no arising and no cessation; it is spoken of only through the convention of names. And they are not found internally, nor externally, nor in between. In just the same way, <s>Subhūti</s>, what is called '<s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>,' what is called '<s>bodhisattva</s>,' what is called 'the name of a <s>bodhisattva</s>' — this is a mere designation of dharmas. And of that designation of dharmas there is no arising and no cessation; it is spoken of only through the convention of names. And that name is not found internally, nor externally, nor in between. Just as, <s>Subhūti</s>, this internal body is spoken of as 'body,' and head, neck, belly, shoulders, arms, back, sides, hips, thighs, calves, feet, and bones are spoken of — these are designated dharmas (<s>prajñaptidharmās</s>), and of them there is no arising and no cessation; they are spoken of only through the convention of names. In just the same way, <s>Subhūti</s>, what is called '<s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>,' what is called '<s>bodhisattva</s>,' what is called 'the name of a <s>bodhisattva</s>' — all these are designated dharmas, and of them there is no arising and no cessation; they are spoken of only through the convention of names. Just as, <s>Subhūti</s>, external grass and wood, branches, leaves, and foliage — all of that is designated by various names, and of those names there is no arising and no cessation; they are spoken of only through the convention of names. And those names are not found internally, nor externally, nor in between. In just the same way, <s>Subhūti</s>, what is called '<s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>,' what is called '<s>bodhisattva</s>,' what is called 'the name of a <s>bodhisattva</s>' — all these are designated dharmas, and they are designated by names, and of them there is no arising and no cessation; they are spoken of only through the convention of names. And those names are not found internally, nor externally, nor in between. Thus indeed, <s>Subhūti</s>, a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> should train in <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. Furthermore, <s>Subhūti</s>, just as dreams, echoes, mirages, reflections, and magical illusions, and emanations created by a <s>Tathāgata</s> — all these are mere designations of dharmas, and of them there is no arising and no cessation; they are spoken of only through the convention of names.

children.translated_text: He does not regard perception (<s>saṃjñā</s>) as pleasant, nor does he regard perception as painful. He does not regard perception as self, nor as non-self. He does not regard perception as peaceful, nor as not peaceful. He does not regard perception as empty, nor as not empty. He does not regard perception as having marks (<s>nimitta</s>), nor as without marks. He does not regard perception as having aspiration (<s>praṇihita</s>), nor as without aspiration. He does not regard perception as conditioned (<s>saṃskṛta</s>), nor as unconditioned. He does not regard perception as arisen, nor as unarisen. He does not regard perception as ceased, nor as unceased. He does not regard perception as detached, nor as not detached. He does not regard perception as wholesome (<s>kuśala</s>), nor as unwholesome. He does not regard perception as blameworthy (<s>sāvadya</s>), nor as blameless. He does not regard perception as with outflows (<s>sāsrava</s>), nor as without outflows. He does not regard perception as defilement (<s>saṃkleśa</s>), nor as free from defilement. He does not regard perception as worldly (<s>laukika</s>), nor as transcendent (<s>lokottara</s>). He does not regard perception as defilement, nor as purification (<s>vyavadāna</s>). He does not regard perception as <s>saṃsāra</s>, nor as <s>nirvāṇa</s>. He does not regard volitional formations (<s>saṃskāras</s>) as permanent, nor does he regard volitional formations as pleasant, nor as painful, nor as self, nor as non-self, nor as peaceful, nor as not peaceful, nor as empty, nor as not empty, nor as having marks, nor as without marks, nor as having aspiration, nor as without aspiration, nor as conditioned, nor as unconditioned, nor as arisen, nor as unarisen, nor as ceased, nor as unceased, nor as detached, nor as not detached, nor as wholesome, nor as unwholesome, nor as blameworthy, nor as blameless, nor as with outflows, nor as without outflows, nor as defilement, nor as free from defilement, nor as worldly, nor as transcendent, nor as defilement, nor as purification, nor as <s>saṃsāra</s>, nor as <s>nirvāṇa</s>. He does not regard consciousness (<s>vijñāna</s>) as permanent, nor as impermanent, nor as pleasant, nor as painful, nor as self, nor as non-self, nor as peaceful, nor as not peaceful, nor as empty, nor as not empty, nor as having marks, nor as without marks, nor as having aspiration, nor as without aspiration, nor as conditioned, nor as unconditioned, nor as arisen, nor as unarisen, nor as ceased, nor as unceased, nor as detached, nor as not detached, nor as wholesome, nor as unwholesome, nor as blameworthy, nor as blameless, nor as with outflows, nor as without outflows, nor as defilement, nor as free from defilement, nor as worldly, nor as transcendent, nor as defilement, nor as purification, nor as <s>saṃsāra</s>, nor as <s>nirvāṇa</s>. For what reason? Because, <s>Śāriputra</s>, a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> practicing <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> does not apprehend form (<s>rūpa</s>); he does not apprehend feeling, perception, volitional formations, or consciousness. <s>Śāriputra</s>, form is neither bound nor liberated; feeling is neither bound nor liberated; perception is neither bound nor liberated; volitional formations are neither bound nor liberated; consciousness is neither bound nor liberated. For what reason? Because, <s>Śāriputra</s>, their nature is such. Thus indeed, <s>Śāriputra</s>, a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> practicing <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> does not regard form as 'I,' nor as 'mine,' nor as 'of the nature of self.' He does not regard feeling, perception, volitional formations, or consciousness as 'I,' nor as 'mine,' nor as 'of the nature of self.' For what reason? Because, <s>Śāriputra</s>, it is the nature of form that it is not self; it is the nature of feeling, perception, volitional formations, and consciousness that they are not self. For, <s>Śāriputra</s>, form is empty of own-nature; feeling, perception, volitional formations, and consciousness are empty of own-nature. And whatever is empty is not form; form is not other than emptiness; emptiness is not other than form; form is itself emptiness; emptiness is itself form. Feeling, perception, volitional formations, and consciousness are themselves emptiness; emptiness is itself consciousness. For what reason? <s>Śāriputra</s>, these are mere names (<s>nāmamātra</s>). And all <s>dharmas</s> are mere names. And <s>dharmas</s> that are mere names do not dwell in names, and names do not dwell in <s>dharmas</s>. Thus, <s>Śāriputra</s>, a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> practicing <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, since all <s>dharmas</s> are mere names, does not give rise to two things. Not giving rise to two things, he generates neither attachment nor obstruction. Generating neither attachment nor obstruction, he courses without obstructing <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. Furthermore, <s>Śāriputra</s>, a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> practicing <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> does not regard the eye (<s>cakṣus</s>) as permanent or impermanent. Likewise the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind — he does not regard them as permanent or impermanent. He does not regard form, sound, smell, taste, tangible objects, or <s>dharmas</s> as permanent or impermanent.
