10412 vā aduḥkhāsukhaṃ vā tad api na nityam iti vā nānitaym iti vā {{samanupaśyati na śāntam iti vā nāśāntam iti vā samanupaśyati/ na śūnyam iti vā nāśūnyam iti vā samanupaśyati/ na nimittam iti vā nānimittam iti vā samanupaśyati/ na praṇihitam iti vā nāpraṇihitam iti vā samanupaśyati/ na saṃskṛtam iti vā nāsaṃskṛtam iti vā samanupaśyati/ notpannam iti vā nānutpannam iti vā samanupaśyati/ na niruddham iti vā nāniruddham iti vā samanupaśyati/ na viviktam iti vā nāviviktam iti vā samanupaśyati/ na kuśalam iti vā nākuśalam iti vā samanupaśyati/ na sāvadyam iti vā nānavadyam iti vā samanupaśyati/ na sāsravam iti vā nānāsravam iti vā samanupaśyati/ na saṃkleśam iti vā na niḥkleśam iti vā samanupaśyati/ na laukikam iti vā na lokottaram iti vā samanupaśyati/ na saṃkleśam iti vā na vyavadāṇam iti vā samanupaśyati/ na saṃsāram iti vā na nirvānam iti vā samanupaśyati/}}
10413 yad api kāyaspraṣṭavyakāyavijñānasaṃsparśapratyayād utpadyate vedayitaṃ sukhaṃ vā
10414 duḥkhaṃ vā aduḥkhāsukhaṃ vā tad api na nityam iti vā nānityam iti
10415 vā samanupaśyati/ na sukham iti na duḥkham iti nātmeti nānātmeti
10416 {{samanupaśyati na śāntam iti vā nāśāntam iti vā samanupaśyati/ na śūnyam iti vā nāśūnyam iti vā samanupaśyati/ na nimittam iti vā nānimittam iti vā samanupaśyati/ na praṇihitam iti vā nāpraṇihitam iti vā samanupaśyati/ na saṃskṛtam iti vā nāsaṃskṛtam iti vā samanupaśyati/ notpannam iti vā nānutpannam iti vā samanupaśyati/ na niruddham iti vā nāniruddham iti vā samanupaśyati/ na viviktam iti vā nāviviktam iti vā samanupaśyati/ na kuśalam iti vā nākuśalam iti vā samanupaśyati/ na sāvadyam iti vā nānavadyam iti vā samanupaśyati/ na sāsravam iti vā nānāsravam iti vā samanupaśyati/ na saṃkleśam iti vā na niḥkleśam iti vā samanupaśyati/ na laukikam iti vā na lokottaram iti vā samanupaśyati/ na saṃkleśam iti vā na vyavadāṇam iti vā samanupaśyati/ na saṃsāram iti vā na nirvānam iti vā samanupaśyati/}} yad api kāyaspraṣṭavyakāyavijñānasaṃsparśapratyayād utpadyate vedayitaṃ
10417 sukhaṃ vā duḥkhaṃ vā aduḥkhāsukhaṃ vā/ tad api na saṃsāram iti vā na
10418 nirvāṇam iti vā samanupaśyati/ yad api manodharmamanovijñānasaṃsparśa-
10419 pratyayād utpadyate vedayitaṃ sukhaṃ vā duḥkhaṃ vā aduḥkhāsukhaṃ vā tad api
10420 na nityam iti vā nānityam iti vā samanupaśyati/ na sukham iti
10421 na duḥkham iti nātmeti nānātmeti {{samanupaśyati na śāntam iti vā nāśāntam iti vā samanupaśyati/ na śūnyam iti vā nāśūnyam iti vā samanupaśyati/ na nimittam iti vā nānimittam iti vā samanupaśyati/ na praṇihitam iti vā nāpraṇihitam iti vā samanupaśyati/ na saṃskṛtam iti vā nāsaṃskṛtam iti vā samanupaśyati/ notpannam iti vā nānutpannam iti vā samanupaśyati/ na niruddham iti vā nāniruddham iti vā samanupaśyati/ na viviktam iti vā nāviviktam iti vā samanupaśyati/ na kuśalam iti vā nākuśalam iti vā samanupaśyati/ na sāvadyam iti vā nānavadyam iti vā samanupaśyati/ na sāsravam iti vā nānāsravam iti vā samanupaśyati/ na saṃkleśam iti vā na niḥkleśam iti vā samanupaśyati/ na laukikam iti vā na lokottaram iti vā samanupaśyati/ na saṃkleśam iti vā na vyavadāṇam iti vā samanupaśyati/ na saṃsāram iti vā na nirvānam iti vā samanupaśyati/}}// [iti
10422 duḥkhe 'nvayajñānakṣāntiḥ//]
children.translated_text: [He] does not regard the <s>manodhātu</s> (mind element), the <s>dharmadhātu</s> (element of mental objects), or the <s>manovijñānadhātu</s> (mind-consciousness element) as happiness or as suffering. He does not regard the <s>manodhātu</s> as self or as non-self; he does not regard the <s>dharmadhātu</s> as self or as non-self; he does not regard the <s>manovijñānadhātu</s> as self or as non-self. He does not regard the <s>manodhātu</s> as peaceful or as non-peaceful; [likewise for <s>dharmadhātu</s> and <s>manovijñānadhātu</s>]. He does not regard the <s>manodhātu</s> as empty or as non-empty; [likewise for <s>dharmadhātu</s> and <s>manovijñānadhātu</s>]. [Likewise, he does not regard the <s>manodhātu</s>, <s>dharmadhātu</s>, or <s>manovijñānadhātu</s> as:] with signs or signless, directed or undirected, conditioned or unconditioned, arisen or unarisen, ceased or unceased, secluded or unsecluded, wholesome or unwholesome, blameworthy or blameless, with outflows or without outflows, defiled or undefiled, mundane or supramundane, defilement or purification, <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence) or <s>nirvāṇa</s>. Moreover, the feeling (<s>vedayita</s>) that arises conditioned by the contact of eye, form, and eye-consciousness — whether pleasant, painful, or neither-pleasant-nor-painful — that too he does not regard as permanent or as impermanent. Likewise, he does not regard it as happiness or as suffering, as self or as non-self, as peaceful or as non-peaceful, as empty or as non-empty, as with signs or as signless, as directed or as undirected, as conditioned or as unconditioned, as arisen or as unarisen, as ceased or as unceased, as secluded or as unsecluded, as wholesome or as unwholesome, as blameworthy or as blameless, as with outflows or as without outflows, as defiled or as undefiled, as mundane or as supramundane, as defilement or as purification, as <s>saṃsāra</s> or as <s>nirvāṇa</s>. [Likewise for the feeling arising from the contact of:] ear, sound, and ear-consciousness; [likewise for] nose, smell, and nose-consciousness; [likewise for] tongue, taste, and tongue-consciousness; [likewise for] body, tangibles, and body-consciousness — he does not regard that feeling as permanent or as impermanent, as happiness or as suffering, as self or as non-self, as peaceful or as non-peaceful, as empty or as non-empty, as with signs or as signless, as directed or as undirected, as conditioned or as unconditioned, as arisen or as unarisen, as ceased or as unceased, as secluded or as unsecluded, as wholesome or as unwholesome, as blameworthy or as blameless, as with outflows or as without outflows, as defiled or as undefiled, as mundane or as supramundane, as defilement or as purification, as <s>saṃsāra</s> or as <s>nirvāṇa</s>. Moreover, the feeling that arises conditioned by the contact of body, tangibles, and body-consciousness — whether pleasant, painful, or neither-pleasant-nor-painful — that too he does not regard as <s>saṃsāra</s> or as <s>nirvāṇa</s>. Moreover, the feeling that arises conditioned by the contact of mind, mental objects (<s>dharma</s>), and mind-consciousness — whether pleasant, painful, or neither-pleasant-nor-painful — that too he does not regard as permanent or as impermanent, as happiness or as suffering, as self or as non-self, as peaceful or as non-peaceful, as empty or as non-empty, as with signs or as signless, as directed or as undirected, as conditioned or as unconditioned, as arisen or as unarisen, as ceased or as unceased, as secluded or as unsecluded, as wholesome or as unwholesome, as blameworthy or as blameless, as with outflows or as without outflows, as defiled or as undefiled, as mundane or as supramundane, as defilement or as purification, as <s>saṃsāra</s> or as <s>nirvāṇa</s>. [Thus ends the <s>anvayajñānakṣānti</s> (subsequent knowledge-patience) regarding suffering.]

children.text:
10501 tat kasya hetoḥ/ tathā hi bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ prajñāpāramitāyāṃ
10502 caran prajñāpāramitāṃ prajñāpāramitānāma taṃ ca bodhisattvaṃ tat ca
10503 bodhisattvanāma na samanupaśyati/ saṃskṛte vā dhātāv asaṃskṛte vā dhātau
10504 tathā hi subhūte bodhisattvaḥ prajñāpāramitāyāṃ caran naitān sarvadharmān
10505 kalpayati na vikalpayati/ so 'vikalpe dharme sthitvā smṛtyupasthānāni
10506 bhāvayati/ prajñāpāramitāyāṃ caran na prajñāpāramitāṃ nāpi prajñāpāra-
10507 mitānāma samanupaśyati/ na bodhisattvaṃ nāpi bodhisattvanāma samanu-
10508 paśyati/ evaṃ samyakprahāṇarddhipādendriyabalabodhyaṅgamārgapāramitā-
10509 tathāgatabalavaiśāradyapratisaṃvidaṣṭādaśāveṇikān buddhadharmān bhāvayati
10510 {{prajñāpāramitāyāṃ caran na prajñāpāramitāṃ nāpi prajñāpāramitānāma samanupaśyati/ na bodhisattvaṃ nāpi bodhisattvanāma}} samanupaśyati anyatra sarvākārajñatā
10511 manasikārāt// [iti duḥkhe 'nvayajñānam//]
10512 tathā hi tena prajñāpāramitāyāṃ caratā dharmalakṣaṇaṃ pratividdhaṃ bhavati/
10513 yac ca dharmāṇāṃ lakṣaṇaṃ tan na saṃkliśyate na vyavadāyate/ evaṃ hi subhūte
10514 {bodhisattvena} mahāsattvena prajñāpāramitāyāṃ caratā nāmasāṃketikī dharmaprajñapti-
10515 r anuboddhavyā// [iti samudaye dharmakṣāntiḥ//]
10516 sa nāmasāṃketikyā dharmaprajñaptyā avabudhya na rūpam abhinivekṣyate na
10517 vedanām {abhinivekṣyate}/ na saṃjñām {abhinivekyate}/ na saṃskārān {abhinivekṣyate}/ na vijñānam {abhinivekṣyate}/
children.translated_text:
10501 For what reason? For a <s>bodhisattva-mahāsattva</s> practicing the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>
10502 does not perceive the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, nor the name '<s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>,' nor that <s>bodhisattva</s>, nor that
10503 name '<s>bodhisattva</s>' — whether in the conditioned realm or the unconditioned realm.
10504 For, <s>Subhūti</s>, a <s>bodhisattva</s> practicing the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> does not construct or discriminate these
10505 <s>dharmas</s>. Having stood in the non-discriminative <s>dharma</s>, he cultivates the <s>smṛtyupasthānas</s> (foundations of mindfulness).
10506-10507 Practicing the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, he does not perceive the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> nor its name; he does not perceive the <s>bodhisattva</s> nor the name '<s>bodhisattva</s>.'
10508-10509 Thus he cultivates the <s>samyakprahāṇas</s>, <s>ṛddhipādas</s>, <s>indriyas</s>, <s>balas</s>, <s>bodhyaṅgas</s>, <s>mārgas</s>, <s>pāramitās</s>, <s>Tathāgata</s> powers, fearlessnesses, analytical knowledges, and eighteen unique <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>,
10510 [practicing the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, not perceiving the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> nor its name, not perceiving the <s>bodhisattva</s> nor the name '<s>bodhisattva</s>'] — except through the mental attention directed to <s>sarvākārajñatā</s>
10511 (knowledge of all aspects). [Thus the subsequent knowledge regarding suffering.]
10512 For, having practiced the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, he penetrates the characteristic of <s>dharmas</s>.
10513 And the characteristic of <s>dharmas</s> is neither defiled nor purified. Thus, <s>Subhūti</s>,
10514 a <s>bodhisattva-mahāsattva</s> practicing the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> should understand the designation of <s>dharmas</s>
10515 as merely conventional names. [Thus the acceptance regarding the origin.]
10516 Having understood through the conventional name-designation of <s>dharmas</s>, he does not cling to <s>rūpa</s> (form),
10517 does not cling to <s>vedanā</s> (feeling), does not cling to <s>saṃjñā</s> (perception), does not cling to <s>saṃskāras</s> (formations), does not cling to <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness).

children.text:

10602 m {abhinivekṣyate}/ yad api cakṣuḥsaṃsparśapratyayotpannaṃ vedayitaṃ sukhaṃ vā duḥkhaṃ vā a-
10603 duḥkhāsukhaṃ vā tad api {nābhinivekṣyate}/ na śrotram {abhinivekṣyate} na śabdaṃ na śrotravijñānaṃ na
10604 śrotrasaṃsparśaṃ yad api śrotrasaṃsparśapratyayotpannaṃ vedayitaṃ sukhaṃ vā duḥkhaṃ vā
10605 aduḥkhāsukhaṃ vā tad api {nābhinivekṣyate}/ {{na ghrāṇam abhinivekṣyate na gandhaṃ na ghrāṇavijñānaṃ na ghrāṇasaṃsparśaṃ yad api ghrāṇasaṃsparśapratyayotpannaṃ vedayitaṃ sukhaṃ vā duḥkhaṃ vā aduḥkhāsukhaṃ vā tad api nābhinivekṣyate/ na jihvām abhinivekṣyate na rasaṃ na jihvāvijñānaṃ na jihvāsaṃsparśaṃ yad api jihvāsaṃsparśapratyayotpannaṃ vedayitaṃ sukhaṃ vā duḥkhaṃ vā aduḥkhāsukhaṃ vā tad api nābhinivekṣyate/}}
10606 {{na kāyam abhinivekṣyate na spraṣṭavyaṃ na kāyaṃ na kāyavijñānaṃ na kāyasaṃsparśaṃ yad api kāyasaṃsparśapratyayotpannaṃ vedayitaṃ sukhaṃ vā duḥkhaṃ vā aduḥkhāsukhaṃ vā tad api nābhinivekṣyate/ na mano abhinivekṣyate na dharmam na manovijñānaṃ na manaḥsaṃsparśaṃ yad api manaḥsaṃsparśapratyayotpannaṃ vedayitaṃ sukhaṃ vā duḥkhaṃ vā aduḥkhāsukhaṃ vā tad api nābhinivekṣyate/}}/ nāpi saṃskṛtadhātum {abhinivekṣyate}/ nāpy asaṃskṛtadhātum {abhinivekṣyate}//
children.translated_text:
10601 He does not cling to the eye, does not cling to form [as object], does not cling to eye-consciousness, does not cling to eye-
10602 contact. Whatever feeling — pleasant, painful, or
10603 neither-pleasant-nor-painful — arises conditioned by eye-contact, he does not cling to that either. He does not cling to the ear, to sound, to ear-consciousness, to
10604 ear-contact. Whatever feeling — pleasant, painful, or
10605 neither-pleasant-nor-painful — arises conditioned by ear-contact, he does not cling to that either. [He does not cling to the nose, to smell, to nose-consciousness, to nose-contact. Whatever feeling — pleasant, painful, or neither-pleasant-nor-painful — arises conditioned by nose-contact, he does not cling to that either. He does not cling to the tongue, to taste, to tongue-consciousness, to tongue-contact. Whatever feeling — pleasant, painful, or neither-pleasant-nor-painful — arises conditioned by tongue-contact, he does not cling to that either.]
10606 [He does not cling to the body, to tangibles, to body-consciousness, to body-contact. Whatever feeling — pleasant, painful, or neither-pleasant-nor-painful — arises conditioned by body-contact, he does not cling to that either. He does not cling to the mind, to mental objects, to mind-consciousness, to mind-contact. Whatever feeling — pleasant, painful, or neither-pleasant-nor-painful — arises conditioned by mind-contact, he does not cling to that either.] He does not cling to the conditioned realm. He does not cling to the unconditioned realm.

children.text:
10607 [iti samudaye dharamjñānam//]
10608 sa na dānapāramitām abhinivekṣyate/ na śīla{pāramitām abhinivekṣyate}/ na kṣānti-
10609 {pāramitām abhinivekṣyate}/ na vīrya{pāramitām abhinivekṣyate}/ na dhyāna{pāramitām abhinivekṣyate}/ na prajñā{pāramitām abhinivekṣyate}/ na nāmāpi

10612 ṣy {abhinivekṣyate}/ na buddhacakṣuṣy {abhinivekṣyate}/ nābhijñāsv {abhinivekṣyate}/ nādhyātmaśūnyatāyā-
10613 m {abhinivekṣyate}/ na bahirdhāśūnyatāyām {abhinivekṣyate}/ nādhyātmabahirdhāśūnyatāyām {abhinivekṣyate}/
10614 na śūnyatāśūnyatāyāṃ na mahāśūnyatāyāṃ na paramārthaśūnyatāyāṃ na saṃskṛta-

children.translated_text:
10607 [Thus the knowledge regarding the origin.]
10608 He does not cling to <s>dānapāramitā</s>, does not cling to <s>śīlapāramitā</s>, does not cling to <s>kṣānti</s>-
10609 <s>pāramitā</s>, does not cling to <s>vīryapāramitā</s>, does not cling to <s>dhyānapāramitā</s>, does not cling to <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. He does not
10610 cling to their name or to their characteristic. He does not cling to the body, nor to the fleshly
10611 eye, nor to the divine eye, nor to the wisdom eye, nor to the <s>Dharma</s>
10612 eye, nor to the <s>Buddha</s> eye, nor to the <s>abhijñās</s> (superknowledges). He does not cling to <s>adhyātmaśūnyatā</s> (internal emptiness),
10613 nor to <s>bahirdhāśūnyatā</s> (external emptiness), nor to <s>adhyātmabahirdhāśūnyatā</s> (internal-external emptiness),
10614 nor to <s>śūnyatāśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of emptiness), nor to <s>mahāśūnyatā</s> (great emptiness), nor to <s>paramārthaśūnyatā</s> (ultimate emptiness), nor to <s>saṃskṛta</s>-
10615 <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness of the conditioned), nor to <s>asaṃskṛtaśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of the unconditioned), nor to <s>atyantaśūnyatā</s> (absolute emptiness), nor to <s>anavarāgraśūnyatā</s> (emptiness without beginning or end),
10616 nor to <s>anavakāraśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of non-rejection), nor to <s>prakṛtiśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of intrinsic nature), nor to <s>sarvadharmaśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of all <s>dharmas</s>), nor to <s>sva</s>-
10617 <s>lakṣaṇaśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of own-characteristic), nor to <s>anupalambhaśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of non-apprehension), nor to <s>abhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of the nature of non-existence), nor to <s>bhāvaśūnya</s>-

10701 <s>tā</s> (emptiness of existence), nor to <s>abhāvaśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of non-existence), nor to <s>svabhāvaśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of own-nature), nor to <s>parabhāvaśūnya</s>-
10702 <s>tā</s> (emptiness of other-nature). He does not cling to <s>tathatā</s> (suchness), nor to <s>bhūtakoṭi</s> (the limit of reality), nor to <s>dharmadhātu</s> (the realm of <s>dharmas</s>), nor to the maturation of beings,
10703 nor to the purification of <s>buddhakṣetras</s>, nor to skill in means (<s>upāyakauśalya</s>). For
10704 what reason? For all those <s>dharmas</s> are not found — neither [the one] who would cling, nor
10705 [that] by which one would cling, nor [that] to which one would cling. [Thus the acceptance of subsequent knowledge regarding the origin.]
10706 For thus, <s>Subhūti</s>, a <s>bodhisattva-mahāsattva</s> practicing the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, not clinging
10707 to any <s>dharmas</s>, grows through <s>dānapāramitā</s>, through <s>śīlapāramitā</s>, through <s>kṣāntipāramitā</s>,
10708 through <s>vīryapāramitā</s>, through <s>dhyānapāramitā</s>, through <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. He enters the <s>bodhisattvaniyāma</s> (certainty of the <s>bodhisattva</s>).

10709 [iti samudaye 'nvayajñānam//]
10710 evaṃ hi subhūte bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ prajñāpāramitāyāṃ carann avinivarta-
10711 nīyāṃ bhūmim avakrāmati// [iti nirodhe dharamjñānakṣāntiḥ//]
10712 evaṃ caran subhūte bodhisattvo mahāsattvo 'bhijñāḥ paripūrayati/
10713 abhijñāḥ paripūrya buddhakṣetreṇa buddhakṣetraṃ saṃkrāmati satvāṃś ca paripācayati
10714 buddhāṃś ca bhagavataḥ satkaroti gurūkaroti mānayati tenaiva kuśalamūlena
10715 teṣāṃ buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ cāntika upapadyate dharmaṃ ca śṛṇoti śrutāś cāsya
10716 dharmā na jātūcchetsyante yāvad ā bodhimaṇḍād iti dhāraṇīmukhāni
10717 pratilapsyate samādhimukhāni pratilapsyate/ evaṃ hi subhūte {bodhisattvena}
10718 mahāsattvena rpajñāpāramitāyāṃ caratā nāmasāṃketikī dharmaprajñaptir anu-
10719 boddhavyā// [iti nirodhe dharmajñānam//]
children.translated_text:
10709 [Thus the subsequent knowledge regarding the origin.]
10710 For thus, <s>Subhūti</s>, a <s>bodhisattva-mahāsattva</s> practicing the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> enters
10711 the stage of non-retrogression (<s>avaivartikabhūmi</s>). [Thus the acceptance of knowledge regarding cessation.]
10712 Practicing thus, <s>Subhūti</s>, a <s>bodhisattva-mahāsattva</s> fulfills the <s>abhijñās</s> (superknowledges).
10713 Having fulfilled the <s>abhijñās</s>, he travels from <s>buddhakṣetra</s> to <s>buddhakṣetra</s>, matures beings,
10714 and honors, reveres, and esteems the <s>Buddhas</s>, the <s>Bhagavants</s>. With those very roots of merit,
10715 he is reborn in the presence of those <s>Buddhas</s>, <s>Bhagavants</s>, and hears the <s>Dharma</s>; and the <s>dharmas</s> he has heard
10716 will never be cut off, all the way to the seat of awakening (<s>bodhimaṇḍa</s>). He will attain
10717 <s>dhāraṇīmukhas</s> (gateways of retention) and <s>samādhimukhas</s> (gateways of concentration). Thus, <s>Subhūti</s>,
10718 a <s>bodhisattva-mahāsattva</s> practicing the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> should understand the designation of <s>dharmas</s>
10719 as merely conventional names. [Thus the knowledge regarding cessation.]

children.translated_text: <s>Subhūti</s>, are the ear, sound, and ear-consciousness the <s>bodhisattva</s>? Is he other than these? Are these in him? Is there a <s>bodhisattva</s> apart from ear, sound, and ear-consciousness? What do you think, <s>Subhūti</s>, are the nose, smell, and nose-consciousness the <s>bodhisattva</s>? Is he other than these? Are these in him? Is there a <s>bodhisattva</s> apart from nose, smell, and nose-consciousness? What do you think, <s>Subhūti</s>, are the tongue, taste, and tongue-consciousness the <s>bodhisattva</s>? Is he other than these? Are these in him? Is there a <s>bodhisattva</s> apart from tongue, taste, and tongue-consciousness? What do you think, <s>Subhūti</s>, are the body, tangible objects, and body-consciousness the <s>bodhisattva</s>? Is he other than these? Are these in him? Is there a <s>bodhisattva</s> apart from body, tangible objects, and body-consciousness? What do you think, <s>Subhūti</s>, are the mind, <s>dharmas</s> (mental objects), and mind-consciousness the <s>bodhisattva</s>? Is he other than these? Are these in him? Is there a <s>bodhisattva</s> apart from mind, <s>dharmas</s>, and mind-consciousness? <s>Subhūti</s> said: No indeed, Blessed One. The Blessed One said: What do you think, <s>Subhūti</s>, is the earth element (<s>pṛthivīdhātu</s>) the <s>bodhisattva</s>? Is the <s>bodhisattva</s> other than the earth element? Is there a <s>bodhisattva</s> in the earth element? Is the earth element in the <s>bodhisattva</s>? Is the earth element a non-earth-element <s>bodhisattva</s>? What do you think, <s>Subhūti</s>, is the water element (<s>abdhātu</s>) the <s>bodhisattva</s>? Is the <s>bodhisattva</s> other than the water element? Is there a <s>bodhisattva</s> in the water element? Is the water element in the <s>bodhisattva</s>? Is the water element a non-water-element <s>bodhisattva</s>? What do you think, <s>Subhūti</s>, is the fire element (<s>tejodhātu</s>) the <s>bodhisattva</s>? Is the <s>bodhisattva</s> other than the fire element? Is there a <s>bodhisattva</s> in the fire element? Is the fire element in the <s>bodhisattva</s>? Is the fire element a non-fire-element <s>bodhisattva</s>? What do you think, <s>Subhūti</s>, is the wind element (<s>vāyudhātu</s>) the <s>bodhisattva</s>? Is the <s>bodhisattva</s> other than the wind element? Is there a <s>bodhisattva</s> in the wind element? Is the wind element in the <s>bodhisattva</s>? Is the wind element a non-wind-element <s>bodhisattva</s>? What do you think, <s>Subhūti</s>, is the space element (<s>ākāśadhātu</s>) the <s>bodhisattva</s>? Is the <s>bodhisattva</s> other than the space element? Is there a <s>bodhisattva</s> in the space element? Is the space element in the <s>bodhisattva</s>? Is the space element a non-space-element <s>bodhisattva</s>? What do you think, <s>Subhūti</s>, is the consciousness element (<s>vijñānadhātu</s>) the <s>bodhisattva</s>? Is the <s>bodhisattva</s> other than the consciousness element? Is there a <s>bodhisattva</s> in the consciousness element? Is the consciousness element in the <s>bodhisattva</s>? Is the consciousness element a non-consciousness-element <s>bodhisattva</s>? <s>Subhūti</s> said: No indeed, Blessed One. The Blessed One said: What do you think, <s>Subhūti</s>, is <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) the <s>bodhisattva</s>? Is the <s>bodhisattva</s> other than ignorance? Is ignorance in the <s>bodhisattva</s>? Is the <s>bodhisattva</s> in ignorance? Is ignorance a non-ignorance <s>bodhisattva</s>? What do you think, <s>Subhūti</s>, are the <s>saṃskāras</s> (formations) the <s>bodhisattva</s>? Is the <s>bodhisattva</s> other than formations? Is the <s>bodhisattva</s> in formations? Are formations in the <s>bodhisattva</s>? Are formations non-formations in the <s>bodhisattva</s>? What do you think, <s>Subhūti</s>, is <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness) the <s>bodhisattva</s>? Is the <s>bodhisattva</s> other than consciousness? Is the <s>bodhisattva</s> in consciousness? children.translated_text: Is the non-<s>tathatā</s> of the mind the <s>bodhisattva</s>? [Likewise for the <s>tathatā</s> of form, sound, smell, taste, tangibles, and <s>dharmas</s>.] If, <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s> is not [found] in the sense-bases individually, could it be that in their totality the <s>tathatā</s> of the sense-bases is the <s>bodhisattva</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s> is other than the <s>tathatā</s> of the sense-bases, the <s>bodhisattva</s> is in the <s>tathatā</s> of the sense-bases, the <s>tathatā</s> of the sense-bases is in the <s>bodhisattva</s>, [or] the non-<s>tathatā</s> of the sense-bases is the <s>bodhisattva</s>? <s>Subhūti</s> said: No indeed, Blessed One. The Blessed One said: What do you think, <s>Subhūti</s>? Is the <s>tathatā</s> of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) the <s>bodhisattva</s>? Is the <s>bodhisattva</s> other than the <s>tathatā</s> of <s>avidyā</s>? Is the <s>bodhisattva</s> in the <s>tathatā</s> of <s>avidyā</s>? Is the <s>tathatā</s> of <s>avidyā</s> in the <s>bodhisattva</s>? Is the non-<s>tathatā</s> of <s>avidyā</s> the <s>bodhisattva</s>? [Likewise for the <s>tathatā</s> of <s>saṃskāras</s> (formations), <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness), <s>nāmarūpa</s> (name-and-form), the six sense-bases, contact, feeling, craving, clinging, becoming, birth, and aging-and-death.] If the <s>bodhisattva</s> is not [found] in the links of <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination) individually, could it be that in their totality the <s>tathatā</s> of <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> is the <s>bodhisattva</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s> is other than the <s>tathatā</s> of <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s> is in the <s>tathatā</s> of <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s>, the <s>tathatā</s> of <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> is in the <s>bodhisattva</s>, [or] the non-<s>tathatā</s> of <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> is the <s>bodhisattva</s>? <s>Subhūti</s> said: No indeed, Blessed One. Moreover, <s>Subhūti</s>, considering what meaning do you speak thus: 'Form is not the <s>bodhisattva</s>, feeling is not, perception is not, formations are not, consciousness is not; the earth-element is not, the water-element is not, the fire-element is not, the wind-element is not, the space-element is not, the consciousness-element is not; forms are not, sounds are not, smells are not, tastes are not, tangibles are not, <s>dharmas</s> are not; the eye is not, the ear is not, the nose is not, the tongue is not, the body is not, the mind is not; eye-form-eye-consciousness is not, ear-sound-ear-consciousness is not, nose-smell-nose-consciousness is not, tongue-taste-tongue-consciousness is not, body-tangible-body-consciousness is not, mind-<s>dharma</s>-mind-consciousness is not, <s>avidyā</s> is not, likewise formations-consciousness-name-and-form-six-sense-bases-contact-feeling-craving-clinging-becoming-birth-aging-and-death is not the <s>bodhisattva</s>' — and even 'the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), <s>dhātus</s> (elements), <s>āyatanas</s> (sense-bases), and <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination) are not the <s>bodhisattva</s>'? Not form—

In the ultimate sense, Blessed One, a <s>bodhisattva</s> is not found and is not apprehended. How then could the <s>tathatā</s> of <s>avidyā</s>, of <s>saṃskāras</s>, <s>vijñāna</s>, <s>nāmarūpa</s>, the six <s>āyatanas</s>, <s>sparśa</s>, <s>vedanā</s>, <s>tṛṣṇā</s>, <s>upādāna</s>, <s>bhava</s>, <s>jāti</s>, and <s>jarāmaraṇa</s> be apprehended? Thus, taking the <s>skandhas</s>, <s>dhātus</s>, <s>āyatanas</s>, and links of <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> singly and collectively—in the ultimate sense, Blessed One, a <s>bodhisattva</s> is not found and is not apprehended. How then could the <s>tathatā</s> of the <s>skandhas</s>, <s>dhātus</s>, <s>āyatanas</s>, and <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> be apprehended? There is no such ground. The Blessed One said: Well said, well said, <s>Subhūti</s>! Indeed, <s>Subhūti</s>, a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> should train in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> through the non-apprehension of beings and the non-apprehension of the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. [Thus the knowledge of succession regarding cessation.]
The Blessed One said: What do you think, <s>Subhūti</s>? Is it form that is designated as '<s>bodhisattva</s>'? Is it <s>vedanā</s>, <s>saṃjñā</s>, <s>saṃskāras</s>, or <s>vijñāna</s> that is designated as '<s>bodhisattva</s>'? <s>Subhūti</s> replied: No indeed, Blessed One. The Blessed One said: What do you think, <s>Subhūti</s>? Is it the permanence of form or the impermanence of form that is designated as '<s>bodhisattva</s>'? Is it the pleasure of form, the suffering of form, the selfhood of form, the non-selfhood of form, the peace of form, or the non-peace of form that is designated as '<s>bodhisattva</s>'? What do you think, <s>Subhūti</s>? Is it the impermanence or non-impermanence of <s>vedanā</s> that is designated as '<s>bodhisattva</s>'? Is it the pleasure, suffering, selfhood, non-selfhood, peace, or non-peace of <s>vedanā</s> that is designated as '<s>bodhisattva</s>'? Likewise for <s>saṃjñā</s>, <s>saṃskāras</s>, and <s>vijñāna</s>—is the pleasure, suffering, selfhood, non-selfhood, peace, or non-peace of each designated as '<s>bodhisattva</s>'? What do you think, <s>Subhūti</s>? Is it the <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness) of form, or the non-emptiness of form, the signfulness of form, the signlessness of form, the wishfulness of form, or the wishlessness of form that is designated as '<s>bodhisattva</s>'? Likewise for <s>vedanā</s>, <s>saṃjñā</s>, and <s>saṃskāras</s>. What do you think, <s>Subhūti</s>? Is it the emptiness or non-emptiness, the signfulness or signlessness, the wishfulness or wishlessness of <s>vijñāna</s> that is designated as '<s>bodhisattva</s>'? <s>Subhūti</s> replied: No indeed, Blessed One. The Blessed One said: For what reason, <s>Subhūti</s>, do you speak thus: 'Neither the permanence nor the impermanence of form is designated as "<s>bodhisattva</s>."' Likewise, neither pleasure nor suffering

'<s>Bodhisattva</s>' is not a designation of self, not a designation of non-self, not a designation of peace, not a designation of <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness), not a designation of non-emptiness, not a designation of signs, not a designation of signlessness, not a designation of directed intention toward <s>rūpa</s> (form), not a designation of non-directed intention. '<s>Bodhisattva</s>' is not a designation of the permanence of <s>vedanā</s> (feeling), nor of impermanence — likewise not a designation of pleasure, nor of pain, nor of self, nor of non-self, nor of peace, nor of <s>śūnyatā</s>, nor of non-emptiness, nor of signs, nor of signlessness, nor of directed intention toward <s>vedanā</s>, nor of non-directed intention. [The same applies to <s>saṃjñā</s> (perception), <s>saṃskāras</s> (formations), and <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness) — each is not a designation of permanence, impermanence, pleasure, pain, self, non-self, peace, emptiness, non-emptiness, signs, signlessness, directed intention, or non-directed intention.]
<s>Subhūti</s> said: 'Ultimately, <s>rūpa</s> is not found and is not apprehended — whence could "<s>bodhisattva</s>" be a designation of <s>rūpa</s>? Ultimately, Blessed One, impermanence is not found and is not apprehended — whence could "<s>bodhisattva</s>" be a designation of <s>vedanā</s>?' [Likewise for <s>saṃjñā</s>, <s>saṃskāras</s>, and <s>vijñāna</s>: ultimately none of these — nor their permanence, impermanence, pleasure, pain, self, non-self, peace, emptiness, signs, signlessness, directed intention, or non-directed intention — are found or apprehended. Whence then could "<s>bodhisattva</s>" be a designation of any of them?]
'Blessed One, since ultimately a <s>bodhisattva</s> is not found and is not apprehended, and <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is not found and is not apprehended, and <s>rūpa</s> is not found and is not apprehended — likewise <s>vedanā</s>, <s>saṃjñā</s>, <s>saṃskāras</s>, and <s>vijñāna</s> are not found and not apprehended — which <s>bodhisattva</s> should be instructed in which <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>?'
The Blessed One said: 'Well done, well done, <s>Subhūti</s>! It is so, <s>Subhūti</s>, it is so. A <s>bodhisattva</s> is ultimately not found and not apprehended. <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is not found and not apprehended. <s>Rūpa</s>, <s>vedanā</s>, <s>saṃjñā</s>, <s>saṃskāras</s>, and <s>vijñāna</s> are not found and not apprehended. Therefore, <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> should train in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> — not apprehending a <s>bodhisattva</s>, not apprehending <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, not apprehending the designation of <s>rūpa</s>, not apprehending the designation of <s>vedanā</s>, <s>saṃjñā</s>, <s>saṃskāras</s>, or <s>vijñāna</s>; not apprehending the designation of permanence or impermanence of <s>rūpa</s>, nor the designation of pleasure or pain, nor the designation of peace or non-peace, nor the designation of emptiness or non-emptiness, nor the designation of signs or signlessness, nor the designation of directed or non-directed intention. [Likewise for <s>vedanā</s>, <s>saṃjñā</s>, <s>saṃskāras</s>, and <s>vijñāna</s> — not apprehending the designation of permanence or impermanence, pleasure or pain, peace or non-peace, emptiness or non-emptiness, signs or signlessness, directed or non-directed intention.] Thus should one train in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.' [Thus ends the <s>dharmajñānakṣānti</s> (patience of <s>Dharma</s>-knowledge) on the Path.]

children.translated_text: And as to what you say, <s>Subhūti</s>: 'I do not perceive any <s>dharma</s> called <s>bodhisattva</s>' — indeed, <s>Subhūti</s>, a <s>dharma</s> does not perceive <s>dharmadhātu</s> (the realm of dharmas), nor does <s>dharmadhātu</s> perceive a <s>dharma</s>. [Thus is the knowledge of dharmas on the path.] <s>Subhūti</s>, the element of form (<s>rūpadhātu</s>) does not perceive <s>dharmadhātu</s>, nor does <s>dharmadhātu</s> perceive the element of form. The element of feeling (<s>vedanādhātu</s>) does not perceive <s>dharmadhātu</s>, nor does <s>dharmadhātu</s> perceive the element of feeling. The nose-element (<s>ghrāṇadhātu</s>) does not perceive <s>dharmadhātu</s>, nor does <s>dharmadhātu</s> perceive the nose-element. The tongue-element (<s>jihvādhātu</s>) does not perceive <s>dharmadhātu</s>, nor does <s>dharmadhātu</s> perceive the tongue-element. The body-element (<s>kāyadhātu</s>) does not perceive <s>dharmadhātu</s>, nor does <s>dharmadhātu</s> perceive the body-element. The mind-element (<s>manodhātu</s>) does not perceive <s>dharmadhātu</s>, nor does <s>dharmadhātu</s> perceive the mind-element. The element of visible form does not perceive <s>dharmadhātu</s>, nor does <s>dharmadhātu</s> perceive the element of visible form. The sound-element (<s>śabdadhātu</s>) does not perceive <s>dharmadhātu</s>, nor does <s>dharmadhātu</s> perceive the sound-element. The smell-element (<s>gandhadhātu</s>) does not perceive <s>dharmadhātu</s>, nor does <s>dharmadhātu</s> perceive the smell-element. [Thus is the conformity-knowledge-patience on the path.] <s>Subhūti</s>, the conditioned element (<s>saṃskṛtadhātu</s>) does not perceive the unconditioned element (<s>asaṃskṛtadhātu</s>), nor does the unconditioned element perceive the conditioned element. [Thus is the conformity-knowledge on the path.] [Thus ends the teaching on the path of seeing.] Moreover, <s>Subhūti</s>, the unconditioned cannot be designated apart from the conditioned, nor can the conditioned be designated apart from the unconditioned. children.translated_text: A <s>bodhisattva</s> who wishes to fully comprehend (the eye), Blessed One, should train in <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. A <s>bodhisattva</s> who wishes to fully comprehend the ear should train in <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. The nose, the tongue, the body — a <s>bodhisattva</s> who wishes to fully comprehend (each of these) should train in <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. A <s>bodhisattva</s> who wishes to fully comprehend the mind should train in <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. A <s>bodhisattva</s> who wishes to fully comprehend form should train in <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. Sound, smell, taste, tangible objects — a <s>bodhisattva</s> who wishes to fully comprehend (each of these) should train in <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. A <s>bodhisattva</s> who wishes to fully comprehend <s>dharmas</s> should train in <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. A <s>bodhisattva</s> who wishes to fully comprehend eye-consciousness should train in <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. Ear-consciousness, nose-consciousness, tongue-consciousness, body-consciousness — likewise. A <s>bodhisattva</s> who wishes to fully comprehend mind-consciousness should train in <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. A <s>bodhisattva</s> who wishes to fully comprehend eye-contact and the feeling born of eye-contact should train in <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. Ear-contact, nose-contact, tongue-contact, body-contact and the feelings born of each — likewise. A <s>bodhisattva</s> who wishes to fully comprehend mind-contact and the feeling born of mind-contact should train in <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. A <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> who wishes to abandon passion (<s>rāga</s>), hatred (<s>dveṣa</s>), and delusion (<s>moha</s>), Blessed One, should train in <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. Likewise, a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> who wishes to abandon the view of the transient collection (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>), attachment to rules and vows (<s>śīlavrataparāmarśa</s>), doubt (<s>vicikitsā</s>), sensual desire (<s>kāmarāga</s>), malice (<s>vyāpāda</s>), desire for the form realm (<s>rūparāga</s>), desire for the formless realm (<s>ārūpyarāga</s>), the fetters (<s>saṃyojana</s>), latent tendencies (<s>anuśaya</s>), and entanglements (<s>paryutthāna</s>) should train in <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. Furthermore, a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> who wishes to abandon the four bonds (<s>yoga</s>), the four floods (<s>ogha</s>), the four knots (<s>grantha</s>), the four clingings (<s>upādāna</s>), and the four distortions (<s>viparyāsa</s>) should train in <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. This is called non-mind-ness.' <s>Śāriputra</s> asked: 'Venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, just as that mind is without change and without conceptualization, is <s>rūpa</s> also without change and without conceptualization? Are <s>vedanā</s>, <s>saṃjñā</s>, <s>saṃskāras</s>, and <s>vijñāna</s> also without change and without conceptualization? Likewise, is the eye element, the form element, and the eye-consciousness element without change and without conceptualization? Are the ear element, sound element, and ear-consciousness element without change and without conceptualization? The nose element, smell element, and nose-consciousness element? The tongue element, taste element, and tongue-consciousness element? The body element, tangible element, and body-consciousness element? The mind element, <s>dharma</s> element, and mind-consciousness element—are they without change and without conceptualization? Likewise, the sense-bases, dependent origination, the perfections, the superknowledges, the foundations of mindfulness, right efforts, bases of supernatural power, faculties, powers, factors of awakening, the path, the confidences, the analytical knowledges, the unique <s>Buddha</s>-qualities, up to unsurpassed perfect awakening—are all without change and without conceptualization?' <s>Subhūti</s> said: 'Just so, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>. Just as the mind is without change and without conceptualization, so too the aggregates, elements, sense-bases, dependent origination, perfections, superknowledges, foundations of mindfulness, right efforts, bases of supernatural power, faculties, powers, factors of awakening, the path, the confidences, the analytical knowledges, the unique <s>Buddha</s>-qualities, up to unsurpassed perfect awakening [are without change and without conceptualization].' <s>Śāriputra</s> said: 'Excellent, excellent, venerable <s>Subhūti</s>! It is as though the Blessed One's own son, born from his breast, born from his mouth, born of the <s>Dharma</s>, created by the <s>Dharma</s>, heir to the <s>Dharma</s> and not heir to material things, one who sees the <s>dharmas</s> face to face, a witness in body—as though the one declared by the Blessed One to be foremost among those dwelling in the wilderness—this is his instruction. Thus, venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, the {<s>bodhisattva</s>} <s>mahāsattva</s> should train in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. And thereby the {<s>bodhisattva</s>} <s>mahāsattva</s> is to be examined as non-regressing (<s>avinivartanīya</s>) and is to be understood as not separated from the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.'

12701 nor even by a unique <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharma</s> — it extends only so far as this designation of <s>dharmas</s>. Just as,
12702 <s>Bhagavān</s>, a dream is not to be expressed by anything; an echo, a mirage,
12703 a reflection, a magical creation are not to be expressed by anything. Just as,
12704 <s>Bhagavān</s>, the names 'earth,' 'water,' 'fire,' 'wind,' 'space' are not to be expressed by anything. Just as,
12705 <s>Bhagavān</s>, the names 'morality,' 'concentration,' 'wisdom,' 'liberation,' 'liberation-knowledge-and-vision' are not to be expressed by anything. [So too] the name 'stream-enterer'
12706 is not to be expressed by anything; 'once-returner,' 'non-returner,' '<s>arhat</s>,' '<s>pratyekabuddha</s>,' and
12707 up to '<s>bodhisattva</s>-<s>dharma</s>,' '<s>Tathāgata</s>,' '<s>Buddha</s>,' '<s>tathatā</s>,' '<s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharma</s>' —
12708 the name is not to be expressed by anything: neither by wholesome nor unwholesome, neither by blameworthy nor blameless, neither by pleasant nor
12709 painful, neither by self nor non-self, neither by peaceful nor non-peaceful, neither by isolated nor
12710 non-isolated, neither by sign nor signless, neither by existence nor non-existence.
12711 I, <s>Bhagavān</s>, dependent on this sense, speak thus. This indeed would be, <s>Bhagavān</s>,
12712 my remorse — that I, not apprehending the arising and passing away of all <s>dharmas</s>, not perceiving [them],
12713 would make arising and passing away by a mere name, [saying] '<s>bodhisattva</s>.' Moreover,
12714 <s>Bhagavān</s>, that very name is neither established nor unestablished, neither standing still nor not standing still. For
12715 what reason? Because of the non-existence of that name. Thus that name
12716 is neither established nor unestablished, neither standing still nor not standing still. And here, <s>Bhagavān</s>, when the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is being spoken of for a <s>bodhisattva-mahāsattva</s>,
12717 his mind does not shrink back, does not collapse,
12718 does not become regretful; his thought is not terrified, does not tremble, does not fall into terror.

children.translated_text: he is certainly to be understood as a <s>mahāsattva</s> (great being) established on the irreversible (<s>avinivartanīya</s>) stage of a <s>bodhisattva</s>, well-established through the method of non-abiding. [Thus the distinguishing feature of the object and aspect of the intense heat stage.] Furthermore, Blessed One, a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> practicing <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> should not abide in <s>rūpa</s> (form), should not abide in <s>vedanā</s> (feeling), should not abide in <s>saṃjñā</s> (perception), should not abide in <s>saṃskāras</s> (formations), should not abide in <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness). He should not abide in the eye, should not abide in the ear, should not abide in the nose, should not abide in the tongue, should not abide in the body, should not abide in the mind. He should not abide in visible form, should not abide in sound, should not abide in smell, should not abide in taste, should not abide in tangible objects, should not abide in mental objects (<s>dharma</s>). He should not abide in eye-consciousness, should not abide in ear-consciousness, should not abide in nose-consciousness, should not abide in tongue-consciousness, should not abide in body-consciousness, should not abide in mind-consciousness. He should not abide in eye-contact, should not abide in the feeling conditioned by eye-contact, should not abide in ear-contact, should not abide in the feeling conditioned by ear-contact, should not abide in nose-contact, should not abide in the feeling conditioned by nose-contact, should not abide in tongue-contact, should not abide in the feeling conditioned by tongue-contact, should not abide in body-contact, should not abide in the feeling conditioned by body-contact, should not abide in mind-contact, should not abide in the feeling conditioned by mind-contact. He should not abide in the earth element (<s>pṛthivīdhātu</s>), should not abide in the water element (<s>abdhātu</s>), should not abide in the fire element (<s>tejodhātu</s>), should not abide in the wind element (<s>vāyudhātu</s>), should not abide in the space element (<s>ākāśadhātu</s>), should not abide in the consciousness element (<s>vijñānadhātu</s>). He should not abide in <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), should not abide in <s>saṃskāras</s> (formations), should not abide in consciousness, should not abide in <s>nāmarūpa</s> (name-and-form), should not abide in the six <s>āyatanas</s> (sense-bases), should not abide in <s>sparśa</s> (contact), should not abide in <s>vedanā</s> (feeling), should not abide in <s>tṛṣṇā</s> (craving), should not abide in <s>upādāna</s> (clinging), should not abide in <s>bhava</s> (becoming), should not abide in <s>jāti</s> (birth), should not abide in <s>jarāmaraṇa</s> (aging-and-death), should not abide in <s>śoka</s> (grief), should not abide in <s>parideva</s> (lamentation), should not abide in <s>duḥkha</s> (suffering), should not abide in <s>daurmanasya</s> (despair) and <s>upāyāsa</s> (distress). What is the reason? For indeed, Blessed One, form is empty of form-ness; feeling is empty of feeling-ness; perception is empty of perception-ness; formations are empty of formation-ness; consciousness is empty of consciousness-ness. And, Blessed One, the emptiness of form is not form, nor is form other than emptiness — form itself is emptiness, emptiness itself is form. The emptiness of feeling is not feeling, nor is feeling other than emptiness — feeling itself is emptiness, emptiness itself is feeling. The emptiness of perception is not perception, nor is perception other than emptiness — perception itself is emptiness, emptiness itself is perception. The emptiness of formations is not formations, nor are formations other than emptiness — formations themselves are emptiness, emptiness itself is formations. And, Blessed One, the emptiness of consciousness is not consciousness, nor is consciousness other than emptiness — consciousness itself is emptiness, emptiness itself is consciousness. By this method, Blessed One, a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> practicing <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> should not abide in form, should not abide in feeling, should not abide in perception, should not abide in formations, should not abide in consciousness. He should not abide in the earth element, should not abide in the water element, should not abide in the fire element, should not abide in the wind element, should not abide in the space element, should not abide in the consciousness element. What is the reason? For indeed, Blessed One, the earth element is empty of earth-element-ness. The emptiness of the earth element is not the earth element, nor is the earth element other than emptiness — the earth element itself is emptiness, emptiness itself is the earth element. Likewise the water element, fire element, wind element, and space element. For indeed, Blessed One, the consciousness element is empty of consciousness-element-ness. The emptiness of the consciousness element is not the consciousness element, nor is the consciousness element other than emptiness — the consciousness element itself is emptiness, emptiness itself is the consciousness element. 'Blessed One, by this method, a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> (great being) practicing the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> (Perfection of Wisdom) should not abide in the earth element, nor in the water element, the fire element, the wind element, the space element, nor in the consciousness element. He should not abide in <s>rūpa</s> (form), nor in sound, smell, taste, tangible, nor in <s>dharma</s>. For what reason? For, Blessed One, <s>rūpa</s> is empty of <s>rūpa</s>-ness; sound is empty of sound-ness; smell is empty of smell-ness; taste is empty of taste-ness; tangible is empty of tangible-ness. And, Blessed One, the <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness) of <s>rūpa</s> is not that <s>rūpa</s>, nor is <s>rūpa</s> other than <s>śūnyatā</s> — <s>rūpa</s> itself is <s>śūnyatā</s>, <s>śūnyatā</s> itself is <s>rūpa</s>. [Likewise for sound, smell, taste, tangible, and <s>dharma</s> — the <s>śūnyatā</s> of each is not that thing, nor is that thing other than <s>śūnyatā</s>; each is <s>śūnyatā</s> and <s>śūnyatā</s> is each.]
By this method, Blessed One, a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> practicing the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> should not abide in <s>rūpa</s>, sound, smell, taste, tangible, or <s>dharma</s>; nor in the eye, ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind; nor in eye-consciousness, ear-consciousness, nose-consciousness, tongue-consciousness, body-consciousness, or mind-consciousness. For what reason? For eye-consciousness is empty of eye-consciousness-ness; [likewise ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-consciousness are each empty of their own nature — the <s>śūnyatā</s> of each is not that consciousness, nor is that consciousness other than <s>śūnyatā</s>; each is <s>śūnyatā</s> and <s>śūnyatā</s> is each.]
He should not abide in eye-contact, ear-contact, nose-contact, tongue-contact, body-contact, or mind-contact. For what reason? For eye-contact is empty of eye-contact-ness; [likewise each of the six contacts is empty of its own nature — the <s>śūnyatā</s> of each is not that contact, nor is that contact other than <s>śūnyatā</s>; each is <s>śūnyatā</s> and <s>śūnyatā</s> is each.]
By this method, Blessed One, a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> practicing the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> should not abide in eye-contact, nor in ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, or mind-contact. He should not abide in the feeling arisen from eye-contact, nor in the feeling arisen from ear-contact, nose-contact, tongue-contact, body-contact, or mind-contact. He should not abide in <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), nor in any [of the links of dependent origination] up to old age and death. For what reason? For, Blessed One, <s>avidyā</s> is empty of <s>avidyā</s>-ness; and the <s>śūnyatā</s> of <s>avidyā</s> is not that <s>avidyā</s>, nor is <s>avidyā</s> other than <s>śūnyatā</s> — <s>avidyā</s> itself is <s>śūnyatā</s>, <s>śūnyatā</s> itself is <s>avidyā</s>. Likewise, <s>saṃskāras</s> (formations) are empty of <s>saṃskāra</s>-ness; <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness) is empty of <s>vijñāna</s>-ness; <s>nāmarūpa</s> (name-and-form) is empty of <s>nāmarūpa</s>-ness; the six <s>āyatanas</s> (sense-bases) are empty of <s>āyatana</s>-ness; <s>sparśa</s> (contact) is empty of <s>sparśa</s>-ness; <s>vedanā</s> (feeling) is empty of <s>vedanā</s>-ness; <s>tṛṣṇā</s> (craving) is empty of <s>tṛṣṇā</s>-ness; <s>upādāna</s> (clinging) is empty of <s>upādāna</s>-ness; <s>bhava</s> (becoming) is empty of <s>bhava</s>-ness; <s>jāti</s> (birth) is empty of <s>jāti</s>-ness. For, Blessed One, <s>jarāmaraṇa</s> (old age and death)

13013 tathā hi dānapāramitaiva śūnyā dānapāramitāsvabhāvena/ {{śīlapāramitaiva śūnyā śīlapāramitāsvabhāvena/ kṣātipāramitaiva śūnyā kṣāntipāramitāsvabhāvena/ vīryapāramitaiva śūnyā vīryapāramitāsvabhāvena/ dhyānapāramitaiva śūnyā dhyānapāramitāsvabhāvena/ prajñāpāramitaiva śūnyā prajñāpāramitāsvabhāvena/ yā ca bhagavan dānapāramitāyāḥ śūnyatā na sā dānapāramitā/ na cānyatra dānapāramitāyāḥ dānapāramitā dānapāramitaiva śūnyatā śūnyataiva dānapāramitā/ yā ca bhagavan śīlapāramitāyāḥ śūnyatā na sā śīlapāramitā/ na cānyatra śīlapāramitāyāḥ śīlapāramitā śīlapāramitaiva śūnyatā śūnyataiva śīlapāramitā/ yā ca bhagavan kṣāntipāramitāyāḥ śūnyatā na sā kṣāntipāramitā/ na cānyatra kṣāntipāramitāyāḥ kṣāntipāramitā kṣāntipāramitaiva śūnyatā śūnyataiva kṣāntipāramitā/ yā ca bhagavan vīryapāramitāyāḥ śūnyatā na sā vīryapāramitā/ na cānyatra vīryapāramitāyāḥ vīryapāramitā vīryapāramitaiva śūnyatā śūnyataiva vīryapāramitā/ yā ca bhagavan dhyānapāramitāyāḥ śūnyatā na sā dhyānapāramitā/ na cānyatra dhyānapāramitāyāḥ dhyānapāramitā dhyānapāramitaiva śūnyatā śūnyataiva dhyānapāramitā/ yā ca bhagavan prajñāpāramitāyāḥ śūnyatā na sā prajñāpāramitā/ na cānyatra prajñāpāramitāyāḥ prajñāpāramitā prajñāpāramitaiva śūnyatā śūnyataiva prajñāpāramitā/}}
13014 tad anenāpi bhagavan paryāyeṇa {bodhisattvena mahāsattvena prajñāpāramitāyāṃ caratā}
13015 na dānapāramitāyāṃ {sthātavyaṃ} {{na śīlapāramitāyāṃ sthātavyaṃ na kṣāntipāramitāyāṃ sthātavyaṃ na vīryapāramitāyāṃ sthātavyaṃ na dhyānapāramitāyāṃ sthātavyaṃ}} na prajñāpāramitāyāṃ {sthātavyam}/

children.translated_text: [Aging-and-death] is empty of <s>jarāmaraṇa</s>-ness (aging-and-death-ness). And the emptiness of <s>jarāmaraṇa</s> (aging-and-death) is not <s>jarāmaraṇa</s>; nor is <s>jarāmaraṇa</s> apart from emptiness; <s>jarāmaraṇa</s> itself is <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness), and <s>śūnyatā</s> itself is <s>jarāmaraṇa</s>. By this method, Blessed One, a <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> practicing <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> should not abide in <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), [likewise should not abide in <s>saṃskāras</s> (formations), <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness), <s>nāmarūpa</s> (name-and-form), the six <s>āyatanas</s> (sense-bases), <s>sparśa</s> (contact), <s>vedanā</s> (feeling), <s>tṛṣṇā</s> (craving), <s>upādāna</s> (clinging), <s>bhava</s> (becoming), <s>jāti</s> (birth),] nor in <s>jarāmaraṇa</s> (aging-and-death). Likewise for the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), <s>dhātus</s> (elements), and <s>āyatanas</s> (sense-bases). Furthermore, a <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> practicing <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> should not abide in the <s>smṛtyupasthānas</s> (foundations of mindfulness). Why is that? For indeed, Blessed One, the <s>smṛtyupasthānas</s> are empty of <s>smṛtyupasthāna</s>-ness. And, Blessed One, the emptiness of the <s>smṛtyupasthānas</s> is not the <s>smṛtyupasthānas</s>; nor are the <s>smṛtyupasthānas</s> apart from the <s>smṛtyupasthānas</s>; the <s>smṛtyupasthānas</s> themselves are <s>śūnyatā</s>, and <s>śūnyatā</s> itself is the <s>smṛtyupasthānas</s>. Therefore by this method too, Blessed One, a <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> practicing <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> should not abide in the <s>smṛtyupasthānas</s>. Likewise [one should not abide] in the <s>samyakprahāṇas</s> (right exertions), <s>ṛddhipādas</s> (bases of supernatural power), <s>indriyas</s> (faculties), <s>balas</s> (powers), <s>bodhyaṅgas</s> (factors of awakening), <s>mārgāṅgas</s> (path-factors), the <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections), <s>abhijñās</s> (superknowledges), the ten <s>balas</s> (powers [of a Tathāgata]), the <s>vaiśāradyas</s> (fearlessnesses), the <s>pratisaṃvids</s> (analytical knowledges), and the eighteen <s>āveṇikabuddhadharmas</s> (unique buddha-qualities). Why is that? For indeed, the <s>āveṇikabuddhadharmas</s> are empty of <s>āveṇikabuddhadharma</s>-ness. And, Blessed One, the emptiness of the <s>āveṇikabuddhadharmas</s> is not the <s>āveṇikabuddhadharmas</s>; nor are the <s>āveṇikabuddhadharmas</s> apart from the <s>āveṇikabuddhadharmas</s>; the <s>āveṇikabuddhadharmas</s> themselves are <s>śūnyatā</s>, and <s>śūnyatā</s> itself is the <s>āveṇikabuddhadharmas</s>. Therefore by this method too, Blessed One, a <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> practicing <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> should not abide in the <s>samyakprahāṇas</s>, <s>ṛddhipādas</s>, <s>indriyas</s>, <s>balas</s>, <s>bodhyaṅgas</s>, <s>mārgāṅgas</s>, <s>balas</s> [of a Tathāgata], <s>vaiśāradyas</s>, <s>pratisaṃvids</s>, or <s>āveṇikabuddhadharmas</s>. Furthermore, Blessed One, a <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> practicing <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> should not abide in <s>dānapāramitā</s> (perfection of giving). Why is that? For indeed, <s>dānapāramitā</s> itself is empty of <s>dānapāramitā</s>-nature; [likewise <s>śīlapāramitā</s> (perfection of morality) is empty of <s>śīlapāramitā</s>-nature, <s>kṣāntipāramitā</s> (perfection of patience) is empty of <s>kṣāntipāramitā</s>-nature, <s>vīryapāramitā</s> (perfection of vigor) is empty of <s>vīryapāramitā</s>-nature, <s>dhyānapāramitā</s> (perfection of meditation) is empty of <s>dhyānapāramitā</s>-nature, <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> (perfection of wisdom) is empty of <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>-nature.] And, Blessed One, the emptiness of <s>dānapāramitā</s> is not <s>dānapāramitā</s>; nor is <s>dānapāramitā</s> apart from <s>dānapāramitā</s>; <s>dānapāramitā</s> itself is <s>śūnyatā</s>, and <s>śūnyatā</s> itself is <s>dānapāramitā</s>. [Likewise for <s>śīlapāramitā</s>, <s>kṣāntipāramitā</s>, <s>vīryapāramitā</s>, <s>dhyānapāramitā</s>, and <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>.] Therefore by this method too, Blessed One, a <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> practicing <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> should not abide in <s>dānapāramitā</s>, [nor in <s>śīlapāramitā</s>, <s>kṣāntipāramitā</s>, <s>vīryapāramitā</s>, <s>dhyānapāramitā</s>,] nor in <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>. Furthermore, Blessed One, a <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> practicing <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> should not abide in syllables, nor in the production of syllables, nor in single utterance, double utterance, or triple utterance. Why is that? For indeed, syllables are empty of syllable-nature. And, Blessed One, the emptiness of syllables is not syllables; nor are syllables apart from emptiness; syllables themselves are <s>śūnyatā</s>, and <s>śūnyatā</s> itself is syllables. Therefore by this method, Blessed One, a <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> practicing <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> should not abide in syllables. Furthermore, Blessed One, a <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> practicing <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>

children.translated_text: Blessed One, by this method, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> practicing the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> should not abide in [the notion that] consciousness (<s>vijñāna</s>) is peaceful. Thus he should not abide in the state of having causes, origination, arising, and conditions. Furthermore, Blessed One, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> practicing the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> should not abide in <s>tathatā</s> (suchness). For what reason? Because <s>tathatā</s> is empty of the own-nature of <s>tathatā</s>. Blessed One, the emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>) of <s>tathatā</s> is not <s>tathatā</s>, nor is emptiness something other than <s>tathatā</s> — <s>tathatā</s> itself is emptiness, emptiness itself is <s>tathatā</s>. By this method too, Blessed One, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> practicing the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> should not abide in <s>tathatā</s>. He should not abide in <s>dharmatā</s> (the nature of dharmas). For what reason? Because <s>dharmatā</s> is empty of the own-nature of <s>dharmatā</s>. The emptiness of <s>dharmatā</s> is not <s>dharmatā</s>, nor is emptiness something other than <s>dharmatā</s> — <s>dharmatā</s> itself is emptiness, emptiness itself is <s>dharmatā</s>. By this method too, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> practicing the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> should not abide in <s>dharmatā</s>. He should not abide in <s>dharmadhātu</s> (the realm of dharmas). For what reason? Because <s>dharmadhātu</s> is empty of the own-nature of <s>dharmadhātu</s>. The emptiness of <s>dharmadhātu</s> is not <s>dharmadhātu</s>, nor is emptiness something other than <s>dharmadhātu</s> — <s>dharmadhātu</s> itself is emptiness, emptiness itself is <s>dharmadhātu</s>. By this method too, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> practicing the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> should not abide in <s>dharmadhātu</s>. He should not abide in <s>dharmaniyāmatā</s> (the fixed order of dharmas). For what reason? Because <s>dharmaniyāmatā</s> is empty of the own-nature of <s>dharmaniyāmatā</s>. The emptiness of <s>dharmaniyāmatā</s> is not <s>dharmaniyāmatā</s>, nor is emptiness something other than <s>dharmaniyāmatā</s> — <s>dharmaniyāmatā</s> itself is emptiness, emptiness itself is <s>dharmaniyāmatā</s>. By this method too, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> practicing the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> should not abide in <s>dharmaniyāmatā</s>. He should not abide in <s>bhūtakoṭi</s> (the limit of reality). For what reason? Because <s>bhūtakoṭi</s> is empty of the own-nature of <s>bhūtakoṭi</s>. The emptiness of <s>bhūtakoṭi</s> is not <s>bhūtakoṭi</s>, nor is emptiness something other than <s>bhūtakoṭi</s> — <s>bhūtakoṭi</s> itself is emptiness, emptiness itself is <s>bhūtakoṭi</s>. By this method too, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> practicing the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> should not abide in <s>bhūtakoṭi</s>. Furthermore, Blessed One, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> practicing the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> should not abide in any of the gateways of <s>dhāraṇī</s>. For what reason? Because the gateways of <s>dhāraṇī</s> are empty of gateways of <s>dhāraṇī</s>. The emptiness of the gateways of <s>dhāraṇī</s> is not the gateways of <s>dhāraṇī</s>, nor is emptiness something other than the gateways of <s>dhāraṇī</s> — the gateways of <s>dhāraṇī</s> themselves are emptiness, emptiness itself is the gateways of <s>dhāraṇī</s>. By this method too, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> practicing the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> should not abide in the gateways of <s>dhāraṇī</s>. Furthermore, Blessed One, a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> practicing the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, if unskillful in means (<s>anupāyakuśala</s>), with a mind fallen into the conceit of 'I' and 'mine' (<s>ahaṅkāramamakāra</s>), should he abide in form and engage in the fabrication of form (<s>rūpābhisaṃskāra</s>), he does not practice the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. Should he abide in feeling, perception, formations, or consciousness and engage in the fabrication of consciousness, he does not practice the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. For what reason? Because one who engages in fabrication does not grasp the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, does not enter into the practice of the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, does not fulfill the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>; and not fulfilling the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, he will not go forth to <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> (omniscience of all aspects).

children.translated_text: They should be examined, and they should be examined in such a way that there is no mental engagement with any <s>dharma</s> whatsoever. This is called the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>'s <s>samādhi</s>-platform of non-grasping of all <s>dharmas</s> (<s>sarvadharmāparigṛhīta</s>), which is vast, preeminent, immeasurable, definite, and unassailable by all <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>. Even <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> (omniscience of all aspects) is ungrasped — based on the emptiness of the internal (<s>adhyātmaśūnyatā</s>), the emptiness of the external (<s>bahirdhāśūnyatā</s>), the emptiness of the internal-and-external (<s>adhyātmabahirdhāśūnyatā</s>), great emptiness (<s>mahāśūnyatā</s>), the emptiness of emptiness (<s>śūnyatāśūnyatā</s>), ultimate emptiness (<s>paramārthaśūnyatā</s>), the emptiness of the conditioned (<s>saṃskṛtaśūnyatā</s>), the emptiness of the unconditioned (<s>asaṃskṛtaśūnyatā</s>), the emptiness of the ultimate (<s>atyantaśūnyatā</s>), the emptiness of that which is without beginning or end (<s>anavarāgraśūnyatā</s>), the emptiness of non-rejection (<s>anavakāraśūnyatā</s>), the emptiness of inherent nature (<s>prakṛtiśūnyatā</s>), the emptiness of all <s>dharmas</s> (<s>sarvadharmaśūnyatā</s>), the emptiness of own-characteristics (<s>svalakṣaṇaśūnyatā</s>), the emptiness of non-apprehension (<s>anupalambhaśūnyatā</s>), the emptiness of the non-existence of own-nature (<s>abhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā</s>), the emptiness of existence (<s>bhāvaśūnyatā</s>), the emptiness of non-existence (<s>abhāvaśūnyatā</s>), the emptiness of own-nature (<s>svabhāvaśūnyatā</s>), and the emptiness of other-nature (<s>parabhāvaśūnyatā</s>). [Thus is the distinction of object and aspect for the gentle summit-level.] For what reason? Because, Blessed One, <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> should not be grasped through signs (<s>nimitta</s>), for signs are defilements (<s>kleśa</s>). What then are signs? Form is a sign, feeling is a sign, perception is a sign, formations are a sign, consciousness is a sign. The eye is a sign, the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are signs. Visible form is a sign, sound, smell, taste, tangibles, and mental objects are signs. The foundations of mindfulness (<s>smṛtyupasthāna</s>), right efforts (<s>samyakprahāṇa</s>), bases of miraculous power (<s>ṛddhipāda</s>), faculties (<s>indriya</s>), powers (<s>bala</s>), factors of enlightenment (<s>bodhyaṅga</s>), path-factors (<s>mārgāṅga</s>), the [ten] powers, the [four] confidences (<s>vaiśāradya</s>), the [four] analytical knowledges (<s>pratisaṃvid</s>), the unique <s>Buddha</s>-dharmas (<s>āveṇikabuddhadharma</s>), emptiness, the signless (<s>ānimitta</s>), the wishless (<s>apraṇihita</s>), the unfabricated (<s>anabhisaṃskāra</s>), <s>dharmadhātu</s>, <s>dharmatā</s>, <s>dharmaniyāmatā</s>, and <s>bhūtakoṭi</s> — these are signs; this is called defilement. If the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> were to be grasped through signs, then the wanderer <s>Śreṇika</s> would not have gained faith in the teaching. And what is this faith in omniscient knowledge? It is the confidence, non-conceptualization, conviction, reflection, weighing, and thorough examination with regard to the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> — and that through the practice of the signless (<s>animitta</s>). Thus it should be grasped through the signless. Herein, moreover,

children.translated_text: <s>Śreṇika</s> the wanderer, having resolved through faith, as a <s>śraddhānusārin</s> (faith-follower), descended with <s>prādeśika jñāna</s> (partial knowledge). Having descended, he did not grasp <s>rūpa</s> (form), nor <s>vedanā</s> (feeling), nor <s>saṃjñā</s> (perception), nor <s>saṃskāras</s> (formations), nor <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness). For what reason? Because in those <s>dharmas</s> that are <s>svalakṣaṇaśūnya</s> (empty of own-characteristics), no <s>dharma</s> whatsoever was grasped by him, on account of the non-attention to signs. For what reason? Because he does not perceive that knowledge from the standpoint of internal (<s>adhyātma</s>) attainment and realization, nor does he perceive that knowledge from the standpoint of external (<s>bahirdhā</s>) attainment and realization, nor from the standpoint of both internal and external attainment and realization, nor from the standpoint of attainment and realization apart from these. For what reason? Because he does not perceive that <s>dharma</s> which would know or by which one would know. For what reason? He does not perceive that knowledge internally in <s>rūpa</s> (form) [likewise for <s>vedanā</s>, <s>saṃjñā</s>, <s>saṃskāras</s>, <s>vijñāna</s>]; nor externally in <s>rūpa</s> [likewise for <s>vedanā</s>, <s>saṃjñā</s>, <s>saṃskāras</s>, <s>vijñāna</s>]; nor both internally and externally in <s>rūpa</s> [likewise for <s>vedanā</s>, <s>saṃjñā</s>, <s>saṃskāras</s>, <s>vijñāna</s>]; nor apart from <s>rūpa</s> [likewise for <s>vedanā</s>, <s>saṃjñā</s>, <s>saṃskāras</s>, <s>vijñāna</s>] — on account of the emptiness of internal and external (<s>adhyātmabahirdhāśūnyatā</s>). In this word-sequence, <s>Śreṇika</s> the wanderer was resolved. Having thus resolved, as a <s>śraddhānusārin</s> (faith-follower), he descended with <s>prādeśika jñāna</s> (partial knowledge), having taken as authoritative the nature of omniscient knowledge (<s>sarvajñajñānadharmatā</s>), on account of the non-apprehension of all <s>dharmas</s>. Thus resolved, no <s>dharma</s> whatsoever was grasped by him on account of the non-attention to signs, nor was any <s>dharma</s> apprehended by him that he might grasp or release, on account of the non-grasping and non-releasing of all <s>dharmas</s>,

For what reason? Because all <s>dharmas</s> are non-<s>dharmas</s>, up to the <s>smṛtyupasthānas</s> [likewise for <s>samyakprahāṇas</s>, <s>ṛddhipādas</s>, <s>indriyas</s>, <s>balas</s>, <s>bodhyaṅgas</s>, <s>mārgāṅgas</s>, <s>balas</s>, <s>vaiśāradyas</s>, <s>pratisaṃvids</s>, <s>āveṇika buddhadharmas</s>] are non-<s>dharmas</s>, nor are those <s>dharmas</s> non-<s>dharmas</s>. If, however, the {<s>bodhisattva</s>} <s>mahāsattva</s> practicing <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> reflects thus — 'How can that <s>dharma</s> which is not found and not apprehended be <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>?' — then he does not practice <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. children.translated_text: <s>Śāriputra</s>, [the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>] is not found and not apprehended; [likewise] the <s>Dhyānapāramitā</s> is not found and not apprehended, the <s>Vīryapāramitā</s>, the <s>Kṣāntipāramitā</s>, the <s>Śīlapāramitā</s>, and the <s>Dānapāramitā</s> are not found and not apprehended — based on <s>adhyātmaśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of the internal), based on <s>bahirdhāśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of the external), [likewise based on the remaining <s>śūnyatās</s>: emptiness of the internal-and-external, great emptiness, emptiness of emptiness, emptiness of the ultimate, emptiness of the conditioned, emptiness of the unconditioned, emptiness of the limitless, emptiness of the beginningless-and-endless, emptiness of non-rejection, emptiness of intrinsic nature, emptiness of all <s>dharmas</s>, emptiness of specific characteristics, emptiness of the unapprehensible, emptiness of the non-existence of inherent nature, emptiness of existence, emptiness of non-existence, emptiness of own-nature,] and based on <s>parabhāvaśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of other-nature) — form, Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, is not found and not apprehended; [likewise feeling, perception, and formations are not found and not apprehended;] consciousness, Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, is not found and not apprehended. <s>Adhyātmaśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of the internal), Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, is not found and not apprehended; <s>bahirdhāśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of the external) is not found and not apprehended; [likewise the remaining <s>śūnyatās</s> from emptiness of the internal-and-external through emptiness of own-nature are not found and not apprehended;] <s>parabhāvaśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of other-nature) is not found and not apprehended. Up to the thirty-seven <s>bodhipakṣyā dharmāḥ</s> (factors conducive to awakening) are not found and not apprehended. <s>Abhijñā</s> (superknowledge) is not found and not apprehended; the ten powers, the fearlessnesses, the analytical knowledges, and the eighteen exclusive <s>Buddha-dharmas</s> are not found and not apprehended. <s>Tathatā</s> (suchness) is not found and not apprehended; <s>dharmatā</s> (the nature of reality) is not found and not apprehended; <s>dharmasthititā</s> (the stability of reality) is not found and not apprehended; <s>dharmaniyāmatā</s> (the fixed order of reality) is not found and not apprehended; <s>bhūtakoṭi</s> (the limit of reality) is not found and not apprehended. The <s>Buddha</s> also, Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, is not found and not apprehended; <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> (omniscience in all aspects) also, Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, is not found and not apprehended — based on <s>adhyātmaśūnyatā</s> through <s>parabhāvaśūnyatā</s>. Moreover, <s>Śāriputra</s>, if a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, while practicing the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, examines thus and reflects thus, and while so examining and so reflecting, his mind does not shrink, does not collapse, is not terrified, does not become frightened, does not fall into alarm — that <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> should be known as not separated from the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. [This concludes the section on the special object-aspect of the supreme ascending stage.] Then the Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> said to the Venerable <s>Subhūti</s>: For what reason, Venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, should the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> be known as not separated from the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>? <s>Subhūti</s> said: Form, Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, is devoid of the inherent nature of form; likewise feeling, perception, and formations [are devoid of their inherent natures]; consciousness, Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, is devoid of the inherent nature of consciousness. The <s>Dānapāramitā</s> also, Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, is devoid of the inherent nature of the <s>Dānapāramitā</s>; [likewise the <s>Śīlapāramitā</s>, <s>Kṣāntipāramitā</s>, <s>Vīryapāramitā</s>, <s>Dhyānapāramitā</s>, and <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> are each devoid of their own inherent natures.] [Likewise the foundations of mindfulness, right exertions, bases of supernatural power, faculties, powers, factors of awakening, path factors, immeasurable meditations, formless attainments, ten powers, fearlessnesses, analytical knowledges, and eighteen exclusive] <s>Buddha-dharmas</s> are devoid of the inherent nature of the <s>Buddha-dharmas</s>. <s>Bhūtakoṭi</s> (the limit of reality) also, Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, is devoid of the inherent nature of <s>bhūtakoṭi</s>. <s>Śāriputra</s> said: But how, Venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, is the inherent nature of form? How is [the inherent nature] of feeling, perception, and formations? How is the inherent nature of consciousness? How is [the inherent nature] of [all these] individually and collectively?

children.translated_text: and have not gone forth. <s>Śāriputra</s> said: For what reason, venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, are all <s>dharmas</s> unborn and have not gone forth? <s>Subhūti</s> said: <s>Rūpa</s>, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, is empty of the own-nature of <s>rūpa</s>; neither its birth nor its going forth is apprehended. <s>Vedanā</s>, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, is empty of the own-nature of <s>vedanā</s>; neither its birth nor its going forth is apprehended. <s>Saṃjñā</s>, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, is empty of the own-nature of <s>saṃjñā</s>; neither its birth nor its going forth is apprehended. The <s>saṃskāras</s>, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, are empty of the own-nature of the <s>saṃskāras</s>; neither their birth nor their going forth is apprehended. <s>Vijñāna</s>, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, is empty of the own-nature of <s>vijñāna</s>; neither its birth nor its going forth is apprehended. Thus in detail, the same should be applied to the <s>skandhas</s>, <s>dhātus</s>, <s>āyatanas</s>, and <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s>, both individually and collectively, up to: <s>bhūtakoṭi</s> is empty of the own-nature of <s>bhūtakoṭi</s>; neither its birth nor its going forth is apprehended. Thus indeed, <s>Śāriputra</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> practicing <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> draws near to <s>sarvākārajñatā</s>, and to the extent that he draws near to <s>sarvākārajñatā</s>, to that extent he attains purification of body, purification of mind, and purification of marks. And to the extent that he attains purification of body, purification of mind, and purification of marks, to that extent no mind accompanied by passion arises in the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, no mind accompanied by aversion arises, no mind accompanied by delusion arises, no mind accompanied by pride arises, no mind accompanied by greed arises, no mind accompanied by wrong views arises. Because of the non-arising of mind accompanied by passion, aversion, delusion, pride, and wrong views, he is never reborn in a mother's womb, but is always spontaneously born. He passes from <s>buddhakṣetra</s> (buddha-field) to <s>buddhakṣetra</s>, attends upon the <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bhagavāns</s>, matures beings, and purifies buddha-fields. He is never separated from those <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bhagavāns</s> until he fully awakens to <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> (unsurpassed perfect awakening). Thus indeed, <s>Śāriputra</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> draws near to <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>. children.translated_text: he courses in <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. If he courses in feeling, he courses in marks (<s>nimitta</s>) — he does not course in <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. If he courses in perception, in volitional formations, in consciousness — he courses in marks, he does not course in <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. If he courses (thinking) 'form is permanent,' he courses in marks — he does not course in <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. If he courses (thinking) 'feeling is permanent,' 'perception is permanent,' 'volitional formations are permanent,' 'consciousness is permanent' — he courses in marks, he does not course in <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. If he courses (thinking) 'form is pleasant or painful' — he courses in marks, he does not course in <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. Likewise for feeling, perception, volitional formations, and consciousness (as pleasant or painful). If he courses (thinking) 'form is self or non-self' — he courses in marks, he does not course in <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. Likewise for feeling, perception, volitional formations, and consciousness. If he courses (thinking) 'form is peaceful or not peaceful' — he courses in marks, he does not course in <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. Likewise for all five <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates) through (the pairs): empty or not empty, with marks or without marks, with aspiration or without aspiration, conditioned or unconditioned, arisen or unarisen, ceased or unceased, detached or not detached, wholesome or unwholesome, blameworthy or blameless, with outflows or without outflows, defiled or undefiled, worldly or transcendent, defilement or purification, <s>saṃsāra</s> or <s>nirvāṇa</s>. If he courses in the perfection of generosity (<s>dānapāramitā</s>), he courses in marks — he does not course in <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. Likewise for the perfection of morality (<s>śīlapāramitā</s>), the perfection of patience (<s>kṣāntipāramitā</s>), the perfection of vigor (<s>vīryapāramitā</s>), and the perfection of meditation (<s>dhyānapāramitā</s>). If he courses in <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> (as an apprehended object), he courses in marks — he does not course in <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. If he courses in the internal emptiness (<s>adhyātmaśūnyatā</s>), the external emptiness, the emptiness of both internal and external, the emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, the emptiness of the conditioned, absolute emptiness, the emptiness of what is without beginning or end, the emptiness of non-rejection, the emptiness of inherent nature, the emptiness of all <s>dharmas</s>, the emptiness of own-characteristics, the emptiness of non-apprehension, the emptiness of the non-existence of inherent nature, the emptiness of existence, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of own-nature, or the emptiness of other-nature — he courses in marks, he does not course in <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. If he courses in the foundations of mindfulness (<s>smṛtyupasthāna</s>), the right efforts, the bases of supernatural power, the faculties, the powers, the factors of awakening, or the path — he courses in marks, he does not course in <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. If he courses in the ten powers of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the four fearlessnesses, the four analytical knowledges, or the eighteen unique qualities of a <s>Buddha</s> — he courses in marks, he does not course in <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. If he courses in <s>sarvajñatā</s> (omniscience), he courses in marks — he does not course in <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. For what reason? Because <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is not to be apprehended, and one who courses in it is not to be apprehended, and the <s>dharma</s> in which one courses is not to be apprehended.
