children.translated_text: as with wishes or wishless, as isolated or non-isolated. For what reason? For, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, the <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness) of <s>rūpa</s> is not that <s>rūpa</s>, and apart from <s>śūnyatā</s> there is no <s>rūpa</s>, and apart from <s>rūpa</s> there is no <s>śūnyatā</s>—<s>rūpa</s> itself is <s>śūnyatā</s> and <s>śūnyatā</s> itself is <s>rūpa</s>. The <s>śūnyatā</s> of <s>vedanā</s>, the <s>śūnyatā</s> of <s>saṃjñā</s>, the <s>śūnyatā</s> of <s>saṃskāras</s>, the <s>śūnyatā</s> of <s>vijñāna</s>—that is <s>vijñāna</s>, and apart from <s>śūnyatā</s> there is no <s>vijñāna</s>, and apart from <s>vijñāna</s> there is no <s>śūnyatā</s>—<s>śūnyatā</s> itself is <s>vijñāna</s> and <s>vijñāna</s> itself is <s>śūnyatā</s>. Thus, severally and collectively, in the aggregates, elements, sense-bases, dependent origination, the foundations of mindfulness, the right efforts, the bases of supernatural power, the faculties, the powers, the factors of awakening, the path, the powers, the confidences, the analytical knowledges, and the unique <s>Buddha</s>-qualities—up to: the <s>śūnyatā</s> of the <s>Buddha</s>-qualities is not those <s>Buddha</s>-qualities, and apart from <s>śūnyatā</s> there are no <s>Buddha</s>-qualities, and apart from the <s>Buddha</s>-qualities there is no <s>śūnyatā</s>—<s>śūnyatā</s> itself is the <s>Buddha</s>-qualities and the <s>Buddha</s>-qualities themselves are <s>śūnyatā</s>. Thus, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, the {<s>bodhisattva</s>} <s>mahāsattva</s> practicing the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> should be understood as skillful in means. Thus, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, the {<s>bodhisattva</s>} <s>mahāsattva</s> practicing the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is capable of fully awakening to unsurpassed perfect enlightenment. Furthermore, while practicing the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, if he approaches any <s>dharma</s>, he does not practice the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>; if he does not approach, he does not practice; if he both approaches and does not approach, he does not practice; if he neither approaches nor does not approach, he does not practice the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.' <s>Śāriputra</s> asked: 'For what reason, venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, does the {<s>bodhisattva</s>} <s>mahāsattva</s> practicing the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> not approach?' <s>Subhūti</s> said: 'For, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, the own-nature (<s>svabhāva</s>) of the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is not apprehended. For what reason? For the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is of the nature of non-existence of own-nature (<s>abhāvasvabhāva</s>). By this method, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, the {<s>bodhisattva</s>} <s>mahāsattva</s> does not approach [thinking] "I practice the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>," nor does he approach [thinking] "I do not practice," nor "I both practice and do not practice," nor "I neither practice nor do not practice." For what reason? For all <s>dharmas</s> have been penetrated and realized by him as being of the nature of non-existence of own-nature. If, when the {<s>bodhisattva</s>} <s>mahāsattva</s> practices the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> in this way, his mind does not sink, does not shrink, does not tremble, does not become terrified, and does not fall into fear—it should be understood, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, that this {<s>bodhisattva</s>} <s>mahāsattva</s> is drawing near to <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> (omniscience). [Thus the distinction of object and aspect for one of intense patience (<s>adhimātrakṣānti</s>).]'

That <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> (omniscience of all aspects) too, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, is non-dual and undivided, based on the non-existence of the self-nature of all <s>dharmas</s>. This <s>samādhi</s> (meditative absorption) called <s>Sarvadharmasvabhāvānutpatti</s> (non-arising of the self-nature of all dharmas) of <s>bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s> (great beings) is vast, supreme, immeasurable, definite, and unassailable by all <s>śrāvakas</s> (hearers) and <s>pratyekabuddhas</s> (solitary buddhas). Abiding in this <s>samādhi</s>, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> swiftly awakens to <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> (unsurpassed perfect awakening). <s>Śāriputra</s> said: Abiding in which <s>samādhis</s>, venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, does a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> swiftly awaken to <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>? <s>Subhūti</s> said: There is, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, a <s>samādhi</s> of <s>bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s> called <s>Śūraṅgama</s> (heroic march), abiding in which a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> swiftly awakens to <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>. There is a <s>samādhi</s> called <s>Ratnamudra</s> (jewel seal); <s>Sucandra</s> (beautiful moon); <s>Candradhvajaketu</s> (moon-banner-sign); <s>Sarvadharmamudra</s> (seal of all dharmas); <s>Avalokitamūrdha</s> (surveying summit); <s>Dharmadhātuniyata</s> (determined by the dharma-realm); <s>Niyatadhvajaketu</s> (definite banner-sign); <s>Vajropama</s> (diamond-like); <s>Sarvadharmapraveśamudra</s> (seal of entry into all dharmas); <s>Samāhitāvasthāpratiṣṭhāna</s> (established in the state of concentration); <s>Rājamudra</s> (royal seal); <s>Balavīrya</s> (power and vigor); <s>Sarvadharmasamudgata</s> (arising from all dharmas); <s>Niruktiniyatapraveśa</s> (definite entry into etymological explanation); <s>Āsecanakapraveśa</s> (entry into the inexhaustible); <s>Digavalokana</s> (surveying the directions); <s>Dhāraṇīmudra</s> (seal of retention); <s>Asaṃpramuṣita</s> (unforgotten); <s>Samavasaraṇa</s> (coming together); <s>Ākāśasphāraṇa</s> (pervading space); <s>Vajramaṇḍala</s> (diamond circle); <s>Dhvajāgraketurāja</s> (king of the banner-tip-sign); <s>Indraketu</s> (Indra's sign); <s>Srotoanugata</s> (following the stream); <s>Siṃhavijṛmbhita</s> (lion's yawn); <s>Vyatyastasamāpatti</s> (crossed attainment); <s>Raṇaṃjaha</s> (abandoning battle); <s>Vairocana</s> (illuminating); <s>Nimiṣa</s> (winking); <s>Niketasthita</s> (abiding in a dwelling); <s>Niścita</s> (certainty); <s>Vipulapratipanna</s> (vast attainment); <s>Anantaprabha</s> (infinite light); <s>Prabhākara</s> (light-maker); <s>Varadharmamudra</s> (seal of the excellent dharma); <s>Samantāvabhāsa</s> (universal illumination); <s>Śuddhāvāsa</s> (pure abode); <s>Vimalaprabha</s> (stainless light).

There is the <s>samādhi</s> called <s>Aratikara</s> (producing delight); <s>Ajaya</s> (unconquerable); <s>Tejovatī</s> (possessing splendor); <s>Kṣayāpagata</s> (free from decay); <s>Anirjita</s> (unvanquished); <s>Ratijaha</s> (abandoning delight); <s>Dharmaṅgata</s> (entered into dharma); <s>Vikiraṇa</s> (scattering); <s>Sarvadharmapadaprabheda</s> (analysis of the categories of all dharmas); <s>Samākṣarāvatāra</s> (descent into equal syllables); <s>Ākārānabhiniveśanirhāra</s> (removal of clinging to appearances); <s>Ākārānavakāra</s> (non-depreciation of appearances); <s>Niratiśayasarvabhavatalavikiraṇa</s> (unsurpassed scattering of the grounds of all existences); children.translated_text: the <s>samādhi</s> (concentration) called <s>Mahāvyūha</s> (Great Array); there is the <s>samādhi</s> called <s>Sarvalokaprabhākara</s> (Illuminator of All Worlds); there is the <s>samādhi</s> called <s>Samādhisaratā</s> (Delight in Concentration); there is the <s>samādhi</s> called <s>Anayavinayanayavimukta</s> (Freed from the Method of Disciplining the Undisciplined); there is the <s>samādhi</s> called <s>Anusaraṇasarvasamavasaraṇa</s> (Following All Assemblies); there is the <s>samādhi</s> called <s>Anilaniyata</s> (Determined by the Wind); there is the <s>samādhi</s> called <s>Tathatāsthitaniścita</s> (Certainty Established in Suchness); there is the <s>samādhi</s> called <s>Kāyakalisaṃpramathana</s> (Crushing Bodily Impurity); there is the <s>samādhi</s> called <s>Vākkalividhvaṃsana</s> (Destroying Impurity of Speech); there is the <s>samādhi</s> called <s>Gaganakalpa</s> (Like the Sky); there is the <s>samādhi</s> called <s>Ākāśasaṅgavimuktinirupalepa</s> (Unstained Liberation Free from Attachment to Space). These, Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, are the <s>samādhis</s> by abiding in which a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> quickly awakens to the supreme, perfect awakening. And there are innumerable and immeasurable other <s>samādhimukhas</s> (gateways of concentration) in which <s>bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s>, training, quickly awaken to the supreme, perfect awakening. Among these, what is the <s>samādhi</s> called <s>Śūraṅgama</s> (Heroic March)? The <s>samādhi</s> by which one experiences the range of all <s>samādhis</s> — this is called the <s>Śūraṅgama samādhi</s>. Among these, what is the <s>samādhi</s> called <s>Ratnamudra</s> (Jewel Seal)? The <s>samādhi</s> by which all <s>samādhis</s> are sealed — this is called the <s>Ratnamudra samādhi</s>. And so on, up to: what is the <s>samādhi</s> called <s>Ākāśasaṅgavimuktinirupalepa</s>? The <s>samādhi</s> in which, having abided, one attains the unstained liberation free from attachment to space of all <s>dharmas</s> — this is called the <s>Ākāśasaṅgavimuktinirupalepa samādhi</s>. [Thus the distinguishing feature of the object and aspect of the mild summit dharma.] Then the Venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, through the power of the <s>Buddha</s>, said this to the Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>: This <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, has been predicted by former <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, perfectly and fully awakened ones. Those <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, perfectly and fully awakened ones who presently abide, endure, and live in the ten directions of the world — they too predict that <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>. He who abides in these <s>samādhis</s> does not perceive even the <s>samādhi</s>. He does not conceive through that <s>samādhi</s>: 'I am concentrated,' 'I shall attain concentration,' 'I have attained concentration,' 'I am attaining concentration.' All these conceptualizations do not exist and are not found in the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>. [Thus the distinguishing feature of the object and aspect of the medium summit dharma.]

children.translated_text: <s>Śāriputra</s> said: But, Venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, does a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> abiding in these <s>samādhis</s> receive prediction from the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, perfectly and fully awakened ones? <s>Subhūti</s> said: No indeed, Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>. What is the reason? For indeed, Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is not one thing, <s>samādhi</s> another, and the <s>bodhisattva</s> yet another — the <s>bodhisattva</s> itself is the <s>samādhi</s>, and the <s>samādhi</s> itself is the <s>bodhisattva</s>. <s>Śāriputra</s> said: If, Venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>samādhi</s> is not other and the <s>bodhisattva</s> is not other — the <s>samādhi</s> itself is the <s>bodhisattva</s> and the <s>bodhisattva</s> itself is the <s>samādhi</s>, on account of the equality of all <s>dharmas</s> — can that <s>samādhi</s> then be shown? <s>Subhūti</s> said: No indeed, Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>. <s>Śāriputra</s> said: But, Venerable One, does that son of good family cognize that <s>samādhi</s>? <s>Subhūti</s> said: No, Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, that son of good family does not cognize that <s>samādhi</s>. <s>Śāriputra</s> said: How does he not cognize it? <s>Subhūti</s> said: In the way that he does not conceptualize. <s>Śāriputra</s> said: How does he not conceptualize? <s>Subhūti</s> said: Because all <s>dharmas</s> are non-existent, he does not conceptualize that very <s>samādhi</s>. By this method, Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> does not cognize it. <s>Śāriputra</s> said: How does he not cognize it? <s>Subhūti</s> said: Because of the non-conceptual nature of that <s>samādhi</s>, a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> does not cognize it. [Thus the distinguishing feature of the object and aspect of the intense summit dharma.] Then the Blessed One praised the Venerable <s>Subhūti</s>: Well done, well done, <s>Subhūti</s>! It is just as one who has been declared by me as foremost among those dwelling in the practice of non-conflict (<s>araṇavihārin</s>) would teach. Thus, <s>Subhūti</s>, should a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> train in <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. Thus

children.translated_text: One should train in the <s>dhyānapāramitā</s> (perfection of meditation), the <s>vīryapāramitā</s> (perfection of vigor), the <s>kṣāntipāramitā</s> (perfection of patience), the <s>śīlapāramitā</s> (perfection of morality), and the <s>dānapāramitā</s> (perfection of generosity). Likewise, one should train in the thirty-seven <s>bodhipakṣadharmas</s> (qualities conducive to awakening) up to the eighteen exclusive <s>buddhadharmas</s> (qualities of a Buddha). Then the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> addressed the Blessed One thus: 'Training thus, Blessed One, does the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> train in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>?' The Blessed One said: 'Training thus, <s>Śāriputra</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> trains in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> through the method of non-apprehension (<s>anupalambhayoga</s>). Likewise he trains in the <s>dhyānapāramitā</s> through non-apprehension, the <s>vīryapāramitā</s> through non-apprehension, the <s>kṣāntipāramitā</s> through non-apprehension, the <s>śīlapāramitā</s> through non-apprehension, the <s>dānapāramitā</s> through non-apprehension; and in detail, in the thirty-seven <s>bodhipakṣadharmas</s> he trains through non-apprehension; in the immeasurable <s>dhyānas</s> and formless attainments he trains through non-apprehension; in the ten powers, four fearlessnesses, and eighteen exclusive <s>buddhadharmas</s> he trains through non-apprehension.' <s>Śāriputra</s> asked: 'What is it, Blessed One, that he does not apprehend?' The Blessed One said: 'He does not apprehend a self, <s>Śāriputra</s>, nor a being, a living being, a nourisher, a person, an individual, a human, a youth, a doer, an experiencer, a knower, or a seer — on account of ultimate purity. Likewise, he does not apprehend the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), <s>dhātus</s> (elements), <s>āyatanas</s> (sense bases), and <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination), whether separately or collectively — on account of ultimate purity. He does not apprehend <s>duḥkha</s> (suffering), <s>samudaya</s> (origination), <s>nirodha</s> (cessation), or <s>mārga</s> (the path) — on account of ultimate purity. He does not apprehend the form realm, the formless realm, the immeasurable <s>dhyānas</s> and formless attainments, the <s>smṛtyupasthānas</s> (foundations of mindfulness), <s>samyakprahāṇas</s> (right efforts), <s>ṛddhipādas</s> (bases of power), <s>indriyas</s> (faculties), <s>balas</s> (powers), <s>bodhyaṅgas</s> (factors of awakening), or the <s>mārga</s> (path) — on account of ultimate purity. He does not apprehend the <s>pāramitās</s> — on account of ultimate purity. He does not apprehend a <s>srotaāpanna</s> (stream-enterer), a <s>sakṛdāgāmin</s> (once-returner), an <s>anāgāmin</s> (non-returner), an <s>arhat</s>, a <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>, a <s>bodhisattva</s>, or a <s>Buddha</s> — on account of ultimate purity.' <s>Śāriputra</s> asked: 'What then, Blessed One, is this purity?' The Blessed One said: 'Non-arising, <s>Śāriputra</s>, non-appearance, non-apprehension, non-conditioning — this is called purity.' [Thus ends the section on the general engagement with conceptual analysis.] <s>Śāriputra</s> asked: 'Training thus, Blessed One, in which <s>dharmas</s> does the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> train?' children.translated_text: <s>dharmas</s>. For what reason? For these <s>dharmas</s>, <s>Śāriputra</s>, do not exist as the childish, ordinary persons (<s>bālapṛthagjanas</s>) conceive them.' <s>Śāriputra</s> asked: 'How, Blessed One, do these <s>dharmas</s> not exist?' The Blessed One said: 'They do not exist in the way that childish, ordinary persons conceive them.' <s>Śāriputra</s> asked: 'How, Blessed One, do these <s>dharmas</s> not exist?' The Blessed One said: 'Insofar as they do not exist, thus they exist. Existing thus as non-existent, they are therefore called "<s>avidyā</s>" (ignorance).' [Thus ends the first analysis of <s>avidyā</s>-conceptualization in the section on heat-stage conceptual engagement.] <s>Śāriputra</s> asked: 'For what reason, Blessed One, are they called "<s>avidyā</s>" while being non-existent?' The Blessed One said: '<s>Rūpa</s> (form), <s>Śāriputra</s>, is not found — on account of <s>adhyātmaśūnyatā</s> (internal emptiness), <s>bahirdhāśūnyatā</s> (external emptiness), <s>adhyātmabahirdhāśūnyatā</s> (internal-external emptiness), up to <s>bhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of the intrinsic nature of existence). <s>Vedanā</s> (feeling), <s>saṃjñā</s> (perception), <s>saṃskāras</s> (formations), and <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness), <s>Śāriputra</s>, [are likewise not found — on account of internal emptiness, external emptiness, and internal-external emptiness.] [Thus ends the second analysis of the <s>rūpa</s>-and-other-<s>skandha</s> conceptualization in the same section.] Therein, the childish are attached to <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) and <s>tṛṣṇā</s> (craving). Having constructed <s>avidyā</s> and <s>tṛṣṇā</s>, and clinging through <s>avidyā</s> and <s>tṛṣṇā</s>, being attached to both extremes, they neither know nor see that <s>dharmas</s> do not exist [as conceived]. Having constructed those <s>dharmas</s>, they become attached to <s>nāmarūpa</s> (name-and-form), and so on up to attachment to <s>buddhadharmas</s> (qualities of a Buddha). [Thus ends the third analysis of attachment to <s>nāmarūpa</s> in the same section.] Those attached to <s>dharmas</s> construct both extremes as non-existent, and having constructed them, they neither know nor see. What do they not know and not see? They do not know and do not see <s>rūpa</s>; they do not know and do not see <s>vedanā</s>, <s>saṃjñā</s>, <s>saṃskāras</s>, and <s>vijñāna</s>; they do not know and do not see up to the <s>skandhas</s>, <s>dhātus</s>, <s>āyatanas</s>, and <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination).

14801 ...up to the eighteen unique <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>, they do not know, they do not see. Therefore they are reckoned as foolish.
14802 [Thus the fourth discrimination: attachment to the two extremes, in the same context.] They do not know or see the condition of ignorance and craving. That <s>rūpa</s> (form) is
14803 defiled — they do not know or see. That <s>rūpa</s> is purified — they do not know or see. That <s>vedanā</s>, <s>saṃjñā</s>, and <s>vijñāna</s> are defiled —
14804 they do not know or see. That <s>vijñāna</s> is purified — they do not know or see. They will not emerge. From where will they not

14806 from the <s>dharmas</s> of <s>śrāvakas</s> and <s>pratyekabuddhas</s>. [Thus the fifth discrimination: knowledge of defilement and purification, in the same context.]
14807 They do not have faith. In what do they not have faith? They do not
14808 have faith that <s>rūpa</s> is empty of <s>rūpa</s>; up to: they do not have faith that <s>bodhi</s> is empty of the nature of <s>bodhi</s>. They do not become established.
14809 In what do they not become established? They do not become established in <s>dānapāramitā</s>, [in <s>śīlapāramitā</s>, in <s>kṣāntipāramitā</s>, in <s>vīryapāramitā</s>, in <s>dhyānapāramitā</s>,] in <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>;
14810 they do not become established in the stage of non-retrogression, up to: they do not become established in <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>.
14811 For this reason they are called foolish. They cling. To what do they cling?
14812 They cling to <s>rūpa</s>, [<s>vedanā</s>, <s>saṃjñā</s>, <s>saṃskāras</s>,] and <s>vijñāna</s>. They cling to passion, hatred, and delusion. They cling to views, up to:

14814 train in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> and emerge in <s>sarvākārajñatā</s>? The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: Thus

14816 <s>mahāsattva</s>, unskilled in means, constructs and clings to the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. He constructs and
14817 clings to <s>dhyānapāramitā</s>, [<s>vīryapāramitā</s>, <s>kṣāntipāramitā</s>, <s>śīlapāramitā</s>,] and <s>dānapāramitā</s>. Likewise, he constructs and clings to the immeasurables, <s>dhyānas</s>, and formless attainments.

14901 <s>Śāriputra</s> said: How then, <s>Bhagavān</s>, does a <s>bodhisattva-mahāsattva</s> train in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>
14902 such that, thus training, he will emerge in <s>sarvākārajñatā</s>? The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: When, <s>Śāriputra</s>,
14903 a <s>bodhisattva-mahāsattva</s>, practicing the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, does not apprehend, does not perceive the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> —
14904 thus indeed, <s>Śāriputra</s>, a <s>bodhisattva-mahāsattva</s>, practicing the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>,
14905 training in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, will emerge in <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> through the method of non-apprehension (<s>anupalambhayoga</s>). Likewise, he does not apprehend, does not perceive
14906 <s>dhyānapāramitā</s> [, <s>vīryapāramitā</s>, <s>kṣāntipāramitā</s>, <s>śīlapāramitā</s>,] <s>dānapāramitā</s>, up to <s>bodhi</s> and <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> — he does not apprehend, does not perceive. Thus indeed,
14907 <s>Śāriputra</s>, a <s>bodhisattva-mahāsattva</s>, practicing the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, training in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>,
14908 will emerge in <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> through the method of non-apprehension. [Thus the seventh discrimination: apprehension, in the same context.]
14909 <s>Śāriputra</s> said: Through whose non-apprehension? The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: He does not apprehend, does not perceive,
14910 the self, <s>Śāriputra</s>, based on its absolute purity. [Thus the eighth discrimination: self and the like, in the same context.]
14911 Non-arising, <s>Śāriputra</s>, non-appearance, non-construction — that is purity. [Thus
14912 the ninth discrimination: purity, arising, and the like, in the same context.] [Thus the first discrimination of what is to be grasped.]
14913 That one, unskilled in means, constructs and clings to <s>rūpa</s>, up to <s>vijñāna</s>. [Thus, in the application of discriminations at the summit-level,
14914 the first discrimination: the meaning of the aggregates.] He constructs and clings to the eye, likewise up to the mind. He constructs and clings to form [as object], likewise up to mental objects.

children.translated_text:
14915 [Thus the second discrimination: the meaning of the gateways of entry, in the same context.] He constructs and clings to the eye-form-eye-consciousness elements. Likewise,
14916 up to the mind-<s>dharma</s>-mind-consciousness elements he constructs and clings. [Thus the third discrimination: the meaning of the classes, in the same context.]
14917 He constructs and clings to ignorance, likewise up to old age and death. [Thus the fourth discrimination: the meaning of arising, in the same context.]
14918 He constructs and clings to <s>adhyātmaśūnyatā</s> (internal emptiness), <s>bahirdhāśūnyatā</s> (external emptiness), <s>adhyātmabahirdhāśūnyatā</s> (internal-external emptiness), up to <s>abhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of the nature of non-existence) —
14919 he constructs and clings. [Thus the fifth discrimination: the meaning of emptiness, in the same context.] He constructs and clings to the six <s>pāramitās</s>. [Thus
14920 the sixth discrimination: the meaning of the <s>pāramitās</s>, in the same context.] He constructs and clings to the thirty-seven <s>bodhipakṣa dharmas</s> (factors conducive to awakening). [Thus
14921 the seventh discrimination: the path of seeing, in the same context.] He constructs and clings to <s>dhyānas</s>, <s>abhijñās</s>, <s>apramāṇas</s>, and formless attainments.

children.translated_text:
he constructs and adheres to <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> (omniscience in all aspects). [Thus the ninth conceptual elaboration of the learner's path.] [Thus the second conceptual elaboration of the graspable.]
He does not apprehend a self, <s>Śāriputra</s>. Likewise he does not apprehend a being, a life, a nourisher, a person, an individual, a human, a youth, an agent, an experiencer, a knower, or a seer. For what reason? Because in the ultimate sense, a self is not found and is not apprehended. [Thus the first conceptual elaboration of the independent self in connection with conceptual elaborations accompanied by patience.] Form, <s>Śāriputra</s>, is not apprehended, and so on up to <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness) is not apprehended. [Thus the second, the conceptual elaboration of a unitary self.] The eye, <s>Śāriputra</s>, is not apprehended, and so on up to the mind. Form is not apprehended, and so on up to the <s>buddhadharmas</s> (qualities of a Buddha) are not apprehended. [Thus the third, the conceptual elaboration of a causal self.] Eye-form-consciousness, <s>Śāriputra</s>, is not apprehended, and so on up to mind-dharma-mind-consciousness is not apprehended. [Thus the fourth, the conceptual elaboration of a self as seer etc.] <s>Pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination), <s>Śāriputra</s>, is not apprehended, and so on up to the formless attainments are not apprehended. [Thus the sixth, the conceptual elaboration of a self as basis of dispassion.] The noble truths are not apprehended. [Thus the seventh, conceptual elaboration of a self as basis of seeing.] The eight <s>vimokṣas</s> (liberations) and the nine successive abiding-attainments are not apprehended. [Thus the eighth, conceptual elaboration of a self as basis of cultivation.] The ten powers are not apprehended, and so on up to <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> is not apprehended. How is it not apprehended? As a self. For what reason? Because one takes up the utter purity of the self. [Thus the ninth, conceptual elaboration of a self as basis of accomplishment.] [Thus the first conceptual elaboration of the grasper.]
Then the Venerable <s>Subhūti</s> spoke thus to the Blessed One: If, Blessed One, someone were to ask: 'Will this illusory person, having trained in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, attain <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> (omniscience)?'

children.translated_text:
—to one asking thus, how should the answer be given? Likewise [if asked:] 'Having trained in the <s>dhyānapāramitā</s>, <s>vīryapāramitā</s>, <s>kṣāntipāramitā</s>, <s>śīlapāramitā</s>, and <s>dānapāramitā</s> (perfections of meditation, vigor, patience, morality, and giving), will he attain <s>sarvākārajñatā</s>?'—to one asking thus, how should the answer be given? And so on up to the thirty-seven <s>bodhipakṣa</s> (factors of awakening) <s>dharmas</s> and up to <s>sarvākārajñatā</s>—'Having trained, will he attain <s>sarvākārajñatā</s>?'—to one asking thus, how should the answer be given?
The Blessed One said: Very well, <s>Subhūti</s>, I shall question you in return here. As it seems fit to you, so you may answer. What do you think, <s>Subhūti</s>? Is form one thing and <s>māyā</s> (illusion) another? Is <s>vedanā</s> (feeling) one thing, <s>saṃjñā</s> (perception) another, <s>saṃskāras</s> (formations) another, <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness) another, and <s>māyā</s> another? <s>Subhūti</s> replied: No, Blessed One. [Thus the first conceptual elaboration of <s>skandha</s>-designation in connection with conceptual elaborations of the highest <s>dharma</s> path.]
The Blessed One said: What do you think, <s>Subhūti</s>? Is <s>māyā</s> one thing and the eye another? Is <s>māyā</s> one thing and the ear, nose, tongue, body another? Is <s>māyā</s> one thing and the mind another? Is <s>māyā</s> one thing and form another? Is <s>māyā</s> one thing and sound, smell, taste, touch another? Is <s>māyā</s> one thing and <s>dharmas</s> another? <s>Subhūti</s> replied: No, Blessed One. [Thus the second, the conceptual elaboration of <s>āyatana</s>-designation.]
The Blessed One said: What do you think, <s>Subhūti</s>? Is <s>māyā</s> one thing and eye-consciousness another? Is <s>māyā</s> one thing and ear-consciousness, nose-consciousness, tongue-consciousness, body-consciousness, or mind-consciousness another? <s>Subhūti</s> replied: No, Blessed One. Is <s>māyā</s> one thing, <s>Subhūti</s>, and the feeling that arises conditioned by eye-contact, ear-contact, nose-contact, tongue-contact, body-contact, or mind-contact—whether pleasant, painful, or neutral—another? <s>Subhūti</s> replied: No, Blessed One.
The Blessed One said: What do you think, <s>Subhūti</s>? Is <s>māyā</s> one thing and the earth-element another? Is <s>māyā</s> one thing and the water-element, fire-element, wind-element, space-element, or consciousness-element another? <s>Subhūti</s> replied: No, Blessed One; the earth-element is not one thing and <s>māyā</s> another. The earth-element itself is <s>māyā</s>, and <s>māyā</s> itself is the earth-element.

15205 bhagavann anyaj jarāmaraṇam anyā māyā/ jarāmaraṇam eva māyā māyaiva jarāmaraṇam//
children.translated_text:
No, Blessed One; the water-element is not one thing and <s>māyā</s> another. The water-element itself is <s>māyā</s>, and <s>māyā</s> itself is the water-element. The fire-element itself is <s>māyā</s>, and <s>māyā</s> itself is the fire-element. The wind-element itself is <s>māyā</s>, and <s>māyā</s> itself is the wind-element. The space-element itself is <s>māyā</s>, and <s>māyā</s> itself is the space-element. No, Blessed One; the consciousness-element is not one thing and <s>māyā</s> another. The consciousness-element itself is <s>māyā</s>, and <s>māyā</s> itself is the consciousness-element. [Thus the third, the conceptual elaboration of <s>dhātu</s>-designation.]
The Blessed One said: What do you think, <s>Subhūti</s>? Is <s>māyā</s> one thing and <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination) another? <s>Subhūti</s> replied: No, Blessed One; <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) is not one thing and <s>māyā</s> another. <s>Avidyā</s> itself is <s>māyā</s>, and <s>māyā</s> itself is <s>avidyā</s>. <s>Saṃskāras</s> (formations) themselves are <s>māyā</s>, and <s>māyā</s> itself is <s>saṃskāras</s>. <s>Vijñāna</s> (consciousness) itself is <s>māyā</s>, and <s>māyā</s> itself is <s>vijñāna</s>. <s>Nāmarūpa</s> (name-and-form) itself is <s>māyā</s>, and <s>māyā</s> itself is <s>nāmarūpa</s>. The six <s>āyatanas</s> (sense-bases) themselves are <s>māyā</s>, and <s>māyā</s> itself is the six <s>āyatanas</s>. <s>Sparśa</s> (contact) itself is <s>māyā</s>, and <s>māyā</s> itself is <s>sparśa</s>. <s>Vedanā</s> (feeling) itself is <s>māyā</s>, and <s>māyā</s> itself is <s>vedanā</s>. <s>Tṛṣṇā</s> (craving) itself is <s>māyā</s>, and <s>māyā</s> itself is <s>tṛṣṇā</s>. <s>Upādāna</s> (grasping) itself is <s>māyā</s>, and <s>māyā</s> itself is <s>upādāna</s>. <s>Bhava</s> (becoming) itself is <s>māyā</s>, and <s>māyā</s> itself is <s>bhava</s>. <s>Jāti</s> (birth) itself is <s>māyā</s>, and <s>māyā</s> itself is <s>jāti</s>. No, Blessed One; <s>jarāmaraṇa</s> (aging-and-death) is not one thing and <s>māyā</s> another. <s>Jarāmaraṇa</s> itself is <s>māyā</s>, and <s>māyā</s> itself is <s>jarāmaraṇa</s>.

No, <s>Bhagavān</s>, <s>māyā</s> is not one thing and <s>bodhi</s> (awakening) another; <s>bodhi</s> itself is <s>māyā</s>; <s>māyā</s> itself, <s>Bhagavān</s>, is <s>bodhi</s>. The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: What do you think, <s>Subhūti</s>? Is there arising or cessation of <s>māyā</s>? <s>Subhūti</s> replied: No, <s>Bhagavān</s>. The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: What do you think, <s>Subhūti</s>? Is there defilement or purification of <s>māyā</s>? <s>Subhūti</s> replied: No, <s>Bhagavān</s>. The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: What do you think, <s>Subhūti</s>? That which has no arising, no cessation, no defilement, and no purification — does it train in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> (Perfection of Wisdom)? Does it train in the <s>Dhyānapāramitā</s> (Perfection of Meditation), [the <s>Vīryapāramitā</s> (Perfection of Effort), the <s>Kṣāntipāramitā</s> (Perfection of Patience), the <s>Śīlapāramitā</s> (Perfection of Morality),] and the <s>Dānapāramitā</s> (Perfection of Giving)? Does it train in the immeasurables, <s>dhyānas</s>, formless attainments, the thirty-seven <s>bodhipakṣa dharmas</s>, the <s>abhijñās</s> (supernatural knowledges), the ten powers (<s>daśabala</s>), the confidences (<s>vaiśāradya</s>), the analytical knowledges (<s>pratisaṃvid</s>), and the exclusive Buddha-qualities? Will it go forth to <s>sarvajñatā</s> (omniscience), and will it attain <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> (knowledge of all aspects)? <s>Subhūti</s> replied: No, <s>Bhagavān</s>. The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: What do you think, <s>Subhūti</s>? Is this designation, concept, description, and convention "<s>bodhisattva</s>" [found] in the five <s>upādānaskandhas</s> (aggregates of clinging)? <s>Subhūti</s> replied: No, <s>Bhagavān</s>. The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: What do you think, <s>Subhūti</s>? By means of mere designation, concept, description, and convention, is the arising or cessation or defilement or purification of the five <s>upādānaskandhas</s> apprehended? <s>Subhūti</s> replied: No, <s>Bhagavān</s>. The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: What do you think, <s>Subhūti</s>? That which has no designation, no concept, no description, no convention, no name, no name-designation, no body, no bodily action, no speech, no verbal action, no mind, no mental action, no arising, no cessation, no defilement, and no purification — will it not, having trained in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, go forth to <s>sarvākārajñatā</s>? <s>Subhūti</s> replied: No, <s>Bhagavān</s>. The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: Indeed, <s>Subhūti</s>, a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> (great being), having trained in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, will go forth to <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> by the method of non-apprehension (<s>anupalambhayoga</s>). <s>Subhūti</s> said: Thus, <s>Bhagavān</s>, a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> training in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> should train just like an illusory person (<s>māyāpuruṣa</s>) in the supreme, perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>). For what reason? Because, <s>Bhagavān</s>, that very illusory person is to be understood as being none other than the five <s>upādānaskandhas</s>. The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: What do you think, <s>Subhūti</s>? children.translated_text: For what reason? Because, Blessed One, the five aggregates of clinging (<s>pañcopādānaskandha</s>) are without the own-nature of existence (<s>abhāvasvabhāva</s>). Thus the five aggregates are like a dream (<s>svapna</s>), and a dream, being without the own-nature of existence, is not apprehended — in the same way, the five aggregates, being without the own-nature of existence, are not apprehended. The Blessed One said: 'What do you think, <s>Subhūti</s> — will the five aggregates, being like an echo (<s>pratiśrutkā</s>), like a mirage (<s>pratibhāsa</s>), like a magical creation (<s>nirmitaka</s>), like a reflection (<s>pratibimba</s>), having trained in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, go forth to <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> (omniscience of all aspects)?' <s>Subhūti</s> said: 'No, Blessed One.' For what reason? Because, Blessed One, an echo, a mirage, a magical creation, and a reflection are without the own-nature of existence — in the same way, the five aggregates, being without the own-nature of existence, are not apprehended. For, Blessed One, form is like an illusion (<s>māyā</s>), feeling is like an illusion, perception is like an illusion, formations are like an illusion, consciousness is like an illusion. That which is consciousness is the six faculties (<s>ṣaḍindriya</s>); those five aggregates are not apprehended through the emptiness of the internal (<s>adhyātmaśūnyatā</s>), not apprehended through the emptiness of the external (<s>bahirdhāśūnyatā</s>), not apprehended through the emptiness of the internal-and-external (<s>adhyātmabahirdhāśūnyatā</s>), and so on up to not apprehended through the emptiness of the non-existence of own-nature (<s>abhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā</s>). If, Blessed One, when this is being spoken, a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> does not shrink back, does not withdraw, does not become remorseful, is not frightened, is not terrified, and does not fall into terror — it should be known, Blessed One, that he will go forth to <s>sarvajñatā</s> (omniscience) and will attain <s>sarvākārajñatā</s>. [Thus is the ninth discrimination regarding the designation of the path of no-more-learning at that very point.] [Thus ends the second discrimination regarding the grasper.] Then the venerable <s>Subhūti</s> said this to the Blessed One: 'May it not be, Blessed One, that a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> who has newly set out in the vehicle (<s>navayānasaṃprasthita</s>), upon hearing this exposition, should shrink back, withdraw, become remorseful, be frightened, be terrified, or fall into terror.' The Blessed One said: 'If, <s>Subhūti</s>, a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> who has newly set out in the vehicle, while practicing the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, were unskillful in means and were not in the hands of a spiritual friend (<s>kalyāṇamitra</s>), he would be frightened, terrified, and would fall into terror.' <s>Subhūti</s> said: 'What, Blessed One, is the <s>upāyakauśalya</s> (skillful means) of the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> practicing the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, practicing which the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> is not frightened, not terrified, and does not fall into terror?' The Blessed One said: 'Here, <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, with a mind conjoined with <s>sarvākārajñatā</s>, contemplates form as impermanent yet does not apprehend it. Smell is not empty by the emptiness of smell — smell itself is emptiness, emptiness itself is smell. Taste is not empty by the emptiness of taste — taste itself is emptiness, emptiness itself is taste. Tangible is not empty by the emptiness of tangible — tangible itself is emptiness, emptiness itself is tangible. <s>Dharma</s> is not empty by the emptiness of <s>dharma</s> — <s>dharma</s> itself is emptiness, emptiness itself is <s>dharma</s>. Eye-consciousness is not empty by the emptiness of eye-consciousness — eye-consciousness itself is emptiness, emptiness itself is eye-consciousness. Ear-consciousness is not empty by the emptiness of ear-consciousness — ear-consciousness itself is emptiness, emptiness itself is ear-consciousness. Nose-consciousness is not empty by the emptiness of nose-consciousness — nose-consciousness itself is emptiness, emptiness itself is nose-consciousness. Tongue-consciousness is not empty by the emptiness of tongue-consciousness — tongue-consciousness itself is emptiness, emptiness itself is tongue-consciousness. Body-consciousness is not empty by the emptiness of body-consciousness — body-consciousness itself is emptiness, emptiness itself is body-consciousness. Mind-consciousness is not empty by the emptiness of mind-consciousness — mind-consciousness itself is emptiness, emptiness itself is mind-consciousness. Eye-contact is not empty by the emptiness of eye-contact — eye-contact itself is emptiness, emptiness itself is eye-contact. Ear-contact is not empty by the emptiness of ear-contact — ear-contact itself is emptiness, emptiness itself is ear-contact. Nose-contact is not empty by the emptiness of nose-contact — nose-contact itself is emptiness, emptiness itself is nose-contact. Tongue-contact is not empty by the emptiness of tongue-contact — tongue-contact itself is emptiness, emptiness itself is tongue-contact. Body-contact is not empty by the emptiness of body-contact — body-contact itself is emptiness, emptiness itself is body-contact. Mind-contact is not empty by the emptiness of mind-contact — mind-contact itself is emptiness, emptiness itself is mind-contact. Feeling conditioned by the eye is not empty by the emptiness of feeling conditioned by the eye — feeling conditioned by the eye itself is emptiness, emptiness itself is feeling conditioned by the eye. Feeling conditioned by the ear is not empty by the emptiness of feeling conditioned by the ear — feeling conditioned by the ear itself is emptiness, emptiness itself is feeling conditioned by the ear. Feeling conditioned by the nose is not empty by the emptiness of feeling conditioned by the nose — feeling conditioned by the nose itself is emptiness, emptiness itself is feeling conditioned by the nose. Feeling conditioned by the tongue is not empty by the emptiness of feeling conditioned by the tongue — feeling conditioned by the tongue itself is emptiness, emptiness itself is feeling conditioned by the tongue. Feeling conditioned by the body is not empty by the emptiness of feeling conditioned by the body — feeling conditioned by the body itself is emptiness, emptiness itself is feeling conditioned by the body. Feeling conditioned by the mind is not empty by the emptiness of feeling conditioned by the mind — feeling conditioned by the mind itself is emptiness, emptiness itself is feeling conditioned by the mind. The foundations of mindfulness are not empty by the emptiness of the foundations of mindfulness — the foundations of mindfulness themselves are emptiness, emptiness itself is the foundations of mindfulness. Likewise for the right exertions, the bases of supernatural power, the faculties, the powers, and the factors of awakening. The path is not empty by the emptiness of the path — the path itself is emptiness, emptiness itself is the path. The <s>Buddha</s>-qualities are not empty by the emptiness of the powers, fearlessnesses, and unique <s>Buddha</s>-qualities — the <s>Buddha</s>-qualities themselves are emptiness, emptiness itself is the <s>Buddha</s>-qualities. This, <s>Subhūti</s>, is the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>'s

<s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> (Perfection of Wisdom)—for thus, <s>Subhūti</s>, a <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> practicing in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> does not tremble, does not become terrified, does not fall into dread. [Thus ends the first chapter on <s>upāyakauśalya</s> (skill in means), together with its supplement.] <s>Subhūti</s> said: What, Blessed One, are the spiritual friends (<s>kalyāṇamitra</s>) of a <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s>, supported by whom, upon hearing this exposition of the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, he does not tremble, does not become terrified, does not fall into dread? The Blessed One said: Here, <s>Subhūti</s>, the spiritual friends of a <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> are those who teach him the <s>dharma</s> that form (<s>rūpa</s>) is impermanent, and that through the method of non-apprehension (<s>anupalambhayoga</s>); and they do not dedicate those wholesome roots (<s>kuśalamūla</s>) to the stage of <s>śrāvakas</s> or <s>pratyekabuddhas</s>, but only toward omniscience in all its aspects (<s>sarvākārajñatā</s>). [Likewise for feeling (<s>vedanā</s>), perception (<s>saṃjñā</s>), formations (<s>saṃskāra</s>), and consciousness (<s>vijñāna</s>)—they teach that each is impermanent through the method of non-apprehension, and do not dedicate the wholesome roots to the stage of <s>śrāvakas</s> or <s>pratyekabuddhas</s>, but only toward <s>sarvākārajñatā</s>.] These, <s>Subhūti</s>, are the spiritual friends of a <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s>—those who teach him the <s>dharma</s> that form is suffering (<s>duḥkha</s>), that form is without self (<s>anātman</s>), peaceful (<s>śānta</s>), secluded (<s>vivikta</s>), empty (<s>śūnya</s>), signless (<s>animitta</s>), and wishless (<s>apraṇihita</s>), through the method of non-apprehension, and do not dedicate those wholesome roots to the stage of <s>śrāvakas</s> or <s>pratyekabuddhas</s>, but only toward <s>sarvākārajñatā</s>. [Likewise for feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness—they teach that each is suffering, without self, peaceful, secluded, empty, signless, and wishless, through the method of non-apprehension, dedicating wholesome roots only toward <s>sarvākārajñatā</s>.] These, <s>Subhūti</s>, are the spiritual friends of a <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s>. Furthermore, <s>Subhūti</s>, the spiritual friends of a <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> are those who teach him the <s>dharma</s> that the eye (<s>cakṣus</s>) is impermanent, through the method of non-apprehension, and do not dedicate those wholesome roots to the stage of <s>śrāvakas</s> or <s>pratyekabuddhas</s>, but only toward <s>sarvākārajñatā</s>. [Likewise for the ear (<s>śrotra</s>), nose (<s>ghrāṇa</s>), tongue (<s>jihvā</s>), body (<s>kāya</s>), and mind (<s>manas</s>)—they teach that each is impermanent through non-apprehension, dedicating wholesome roots only toward <s>sarvākārajñatā</s>. Likewise they teach that the eye is suffering, without self, peaceful, secluded, empty, signless, and wishless, through non-apprehension, dedicating only toward <s>sarvākārajñatā</s>; and likewise for ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind. Likewise for eye-consciousness (<s>cakṣurvijñāna</s>), ear-consciousness, nose-consciousness, tongue-consciousness, body-consciousness, and mind-consciousness—they teach that each is impermanent, and that each is suffering, without self, peaceful, secluded, empty, signless, and wishless, through non-apprehension, dedicating only toward <s>sarvākārajñatā</s>. Likewise for eye-contact (<s>cakṣuḥsaṃsparśa</s>), ear-contact, nose-contact, tongue-contact, body-contact, and mind-contact—they teach that each is impermanent, suffering, without self, peaceful, secluded, empty, signless, and wishless, through non-apprehension, dedicating only toward <s>sarvākārajñatā</s>. Likewise for feeling conditioned by eye-contact (<s>cakṣuḥsaṃsparśapratyayavedayita</s>), and for feeling conditioned by ear-contact, nose-contact, tongue-contact, body-contact, and mind-contact—they teach that each is impermanent, suffering, without self, peaceful, secluded, empty, signless, and wishless, through non-apprehension, dedicating only toward <s>sarvākārajñatā</s>. Likewise for the foundations of mindfulness (<s>smṛtyupasthāna</s>)—they teach that they are impermanent, suffering, without self, peaceful, secluded, empty, signless, and wishless, through non-apprehension, dedicating only toward <s>sarvākārajñatā</s>. Likewise for the right exertions (<s>samyakprahāṇa</s>)—they teach that they are impermanent, suffering, without self, peaceful, secluded, empty, signless, and wishless, through non-apprehension, dedicating only toward <s>sarvākārajñatā</s>.] Likewise for the right exertions, bases of supernatural power (<s>ṛddhipāda</s>), faculties (<s>indriya</s>), powers (<s>bala</s>), factors of awakening (<s>bodhyaṅga</s>), and the Noble Eightfold Path (<s>āryāṣṭāṅgamārga</s>)—they teach that each is impermanent, through the method of non-apprehension, and do not dedicate those wholesome roots to the stage of <s>śrāvakas</s> or <s>pratyekabuddhas</s>, but only toward <s>sarvākārajñatā</s>. Likewise for the immeasurables (<s>apramāṇa</s>), <s>dhyānas</s>, formless attainments (<s>ārūpyasamāpatti</s>), and super-knowledges (<s>abhijñā</s>)—they teach that each is impermanent, through the method of non-apprehension, dedicating only toward <s>sarvākārajñatā</s>. Likewise the fearlessnesses (<s>vaiśāradya</s>), analytical knowledges (<s>pratisaṃvid</s>), ten <s>Tathāgata</s> powers (<s>daśa tathāgatabalāni</s>), and eighteen distinctive qualities of a Buddha (<s>aṣṭādaśāveṇika buddhadharma</s>)—they teach that these too are impermanent, and that they are suffering, through the method of non-apprehension, and do not dedicate those wholesome roots to the stage of <s>śrāvakas</s> or <s>pratyekabuddhas</s>, but only toward <s>sarvākārajñatā</s>. These, <s>Subhūti</s>, are the spiritual friends of a <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s>, supported by whom, upon hearing this exposition of the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, he does not tremble, does not become terrified, does not fall into dread.

<s>Subhūti</s> asked: 'How, Blessed One, will the {<s>bodhisattva</s>} <s>mahāsattva</s> be unskillful in means regarding the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> and have fallen into the hands of evil friends, such that upon hearing this exposition of the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> he will tremble, be terrified, and fall into fear?' The Blessed One said: 'Here, <s>Subhūti</s>, the {<s>bodhisattva</s>} <s>mahāsattva</s> cultivates the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> with mental applications devoid of connection to <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> (omniscience), and apprehends it; and he is conceited on account of the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. He cultivates the <s>Dhyānapāramitā</s> and apprehends it, and is conceited on account of the <s>Dhyānapāramitā</s>. He cultivates the <s>Vīryapāramitā</s> and apprehends it, and is conceited on account of the <s>Vīryapāramitā</s>. He cultivates the <s>Kṣāntipāramitā</s> and apprehends it, and is conceited on account of the <s>Kṣāntipāramitā</s>. He cultivates the <s>Śīlapāramitā</s> and apprehends it, and is conceited on account of the <s>Śīlapāramitā</s>. Furthermore, <s>Subhūti</s>, the {<s>bodhisattva</s>} <s>mahāsattva</s> practicing the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, {with mental applications devoid of connection to <s>sarvākārajñatā</s>}, attends to <s>rūpa</s> as internally empty; attends to <s>rūpa</s> as {externally empty}; and so on up to attending to <s>rūpa</s> as {empty of the nature of non-existence of own-nature}. Likewise he attends to <s>vedanā</s> as internally empty, externally empty, and so on up to empty of the nature of non-existence of own-nature. Similarly <s>saṃjñā</s>, <s>saṃskāras</s>, and <s>vijñāna</s>. {With mental applications devoid of connection to <s>sarvākārajñatā</s>}, he apprehends those [forms of] <s>śūnyatā</s>—<s>adhyātmaśūnyatā</s>, <s>bahirdhāśūnyatā</s>, <s>adhyātmabahirdhāśūnyatā</s>, and so on up to <s>abhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā</s>—and is conceited on account of those <s>śūnyatās</s> through the mode of apprehension. He attends to the eye as internally {empty}, externally {empty}, internally-and-externally {empty}, and so on up to {empty of the nature of non-existence of own-nature}; and he apprehends those <s>śūnyatās</s> and is conceited on account of them through the mode of apprehension. Likewise the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind [are attended to] as internally empty, externally empty, and so on up to empty of the nature of non-existence of own-nature. Likewise form, sounds, smells, tastes, tangibles, and <s>dharmas</s>. Likewise eye-consciousness, ear-consciousness, nose-consciousness, tongue-consciousness, body-consciousness, and mind-consciousness—each attended to as internally empty, externally empty, and so on up to empty of the nature of non-existence of own-nature; and he apprehends those <s>śūnyatās</s> and is conceited on account of them through the mode of apprehension. Likewise eye-contact, ear-contact, nose-contact, tongue-contact, body-contact, and mind-contact—each attended to as internally empty, externally empty, and so on up to empty of the nature of non-existence of own-nature; and he apprehends those <s>śūnyatās</s> and is conceited on account of them through the mode of apprehension. Likewise feeling conditioned by eye-contact, feeling conditioned by ear-contact, nose-contact, tongue-contact, body-contact, and mind-contact—each attended to as internally empty, externally empty, and so on up to empty of the nature of non-existence of own-nature. Thus, from ignorance up to aging-and-death, he attends to each as internally {empty}, externally empty, and so on up to empty of the nature of non-existence of own-nature. Furthermore, {<s>Subhūti</s>}, the {<s>bodhisattva</s>} <s>mahāsattva</s> practicing the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, {with mental applications devoid of connection to <s>sarvākārajñatā</s>}, cultivates the foundations of mindfulness and apprehends them, and is conceited on account of them through the mode of apprehension. Likewise the right efforts, the bases of supernatural power, the faculties, the powers, the factors of awakening, the path, the analytical knowledges, the confidences, the superknowledges, the powers of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, and the <s>Buddha</s>-qualities—he cultivates them, apprehends those <s>Buddha</s>-qualities, and is conceited on account of them through the mode of apprehension. Thus indeed, <s>Subhūti</s>, the {<s>bodhisattva</s>} <s>mahāsattva</s> practicing the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> who is unskillful in means, upon hearing this exposition of the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, will tremble, {be terrified, and fall into fear}.' <s>Subhūti</s> asked: 'How, Blessed One, does the {<s>bodhisattva</s>} <s>mahāsattva</s> come to be in the grip of evil friends?'

What will you accomplish by awakening to the supreme, perfect awakening?' One who does not describe and does not point out such deeds of <s>Māra</s> — this, <s>Subhūti</s>, should be understood as an evil friend of a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>. Furthermore, <s>Subhūti</s>, <s>Māra</s> the Evil One, approaching the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> in the guise of a <s>pratyekabuddha</s> (solitary awakened one), will say: 'The eastern direction, son of good family, is empty of <s>Buddhas</s>, Blessed Ones, <s>bodhisattvas</s>, and <s>śrāvakas</s> — there is no <s>Buddha</s>, no <s>bodhi</s> (awakening), no <s>bodhisattva</s>, no <s>śrāvaka</s>. Likewise the ten directions in all quarters are empty of <s>Buddhas</s>, Blessed Ones, <s>bodhisattvas</s>, and <s>śrāvakas</s> — there is no <s>Buddha</s>, no <s>bodhi</s>, no <s>bodhisattva</s>, no <s>śrāvaka</s>.' One who will not point out such deeds of <s>Māra</s> — these, <s>Subhūti</s>, should be understood as evil friends of a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>. Furthermore, <s>Subhūti</s>, <s>Māra</s> the Evil One, approaching in the guise of a <s>śramaṇa</s> (ascetic), having separated the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> from mental attentions connected with <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> (knowledge of all aspects), will instruct and admonish him with mental attentions connected with <s>śrāvaka</s> and <s>pratyekabuddha</s> practices. One who will not point out this kind of deed of <s>Māra</s> — this, <s>Subhūti</s>, should be understood as an evil friend of a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>. Furthermore, <s>Subhūti</s>, <s>Māra</s> the Evil One, approaching in the guise of a preceptor or teacher, will separate the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> from the <s>bodhisattva</s> practice, will separate him from mental attentions connected with <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> (knowledge of all aspects), and will direct him to the <s>smṛtyupasthānas</s> (foundations of mindfulness), the <s>samyakprahāṇas</s> (right exertions), the <s>ṛddhipādas</s> (bases of supernatural power), the <s>indriyas</s> (faculties), the <s>balas</s> (powers), the <s>bodhyaṅgas</s> (limbs of awakening), and the <s>mārgas</s> (path-factors), and will direct him to <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness), <s>animitta</s> (the signless), and <s>apraṇihita</s> (the wishless), (saying): 'Having directly realized these kinds of <s>dharmas</s>, realize the <s>śrāvaka</s> level! What will you accomplish by awakening to the supreme, perfect awakening?' One who does not describe and does not point out such deeds of <s>Māra</s> — this, <s>Subhūti</s>, should be understood as an evil friend of a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>.

Furthermore, <s>Subhūti</s>, <s>Māra</s> the Evil One, approaching in the guise of the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva's</s> (great being's) mother and father, will say thus: 'Come, son of good family, apply yourself to the realization of the fruit of <s>srotaāpatti</s> (stream-entry)! Apply yourself to the realization of the fruit of <s>sakṛdāgāmin</s> (once-returning), <s>anāgāmin</s> (non-returning), and <s>arhat</s>-ship! What use is <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> (supreme, perfect awakening) for you, on account of which you will have to endure the cutting of hands and feet for incalculable and immeasurable <s>kalpas</s> (aeons) while transmigrating in <s>saṃsāra</s>?' Whoever does not point out and declare these to be the deeds of <s>Māra</s> — this, <s>Subhūti</s>, is to be known as an evil friend of the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>.
Furthermore, <s>Subhūti</s>, <s>Māra</s> the Evil One, approaching in the guise of a <s>bhikṣu</s> (monk), will teach the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> that <s>rūpa</s> (form) is impermanent — through the method of apprehension (<s>upalambhayoga</s>). He will teach that <s>rūpa</s> is suffering, selfless, peaceful, secluded, empty, signless, and wishless — through the method of apprehension. [Likewise for <s>vedanā</s> (feeling), <s>saṃjñā</s> (perception), <s>saṃskāras</s> (formations), <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness), and all the sense faculties — the eye, ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind — he will teach each as impermanent, suffering, selfless, peaceful, secluded, empty, signless, and wishless through the method of apprehension. Likewise for forms, sounds, smells, tastes, tangibles, and <s>dharmas</s>; for the six consciousnesses; for the six contacts; for the feelings arisen from the six contacts.] He will teach the twelve links of dependent origination through the method of apprehension. He will teach the <s>smṛtyupasthānas</s> (foundations of mindfulness), the <s>samyakprahāṇas</s> (right efforts), the <s>ṛddhipādas</s> (bases of power), the <s>indriyas</s> (faculties), the <s>balas</s> (powers), the <s>bodhyaṅgas</s> (factors of awakening), and the <s>mārgāṅgas</s> (path factors) through the method of apprehension. He will teach the ten <s>balas</s> (powers), the four <s>vaiśāradyas</s> (fearlessnesses), and the eighteen exclusive <s>buddhadharmas</s> through the method of apprehension. He will teach <s>dānapāramitā</s> (perfection of generosity), <s>śīlapāramitā</s> (perfection of morality), <s>kṣāntipāramitā</s> (perfection of patience), <s>vīryapāramitā</s> (perfection of vigor), <s>dhyānapāramitā</s> (perfection of meditation), and <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> (perfection of wisdom) through the method of apprehension.
Whoever does not point out and declare these to be the deeds of <s>Māra</s> — this, <s>Subhūti</s>, is to be known as an evil friend of the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>.
<s>Subhūti</s> asked: 'How, Blessed One, should a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> be instructed and taught in order to be well-instructed and well-taught in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>?' The Blessed One said: 'A <s>bodhisattva</s>, <s>Subhūti</s>, should be instructed thus: "O son of good family, come, practicing the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, do not abide in <s>rūpa</s>, do not abide in <s>vedanā</s>, <s>saṃjñā</s>, <s>saṃskāras</s>, or <s>vijñāna</s>." For what reason? For <s>rūpa</s> is empty of <s>rūpa</s>-nature — <s>rūpa</s> itself is <s>śūnyatā</s>, <s>śūnyatā</s> itself is <s>rūpa</s>. [Likewise <s>vedanā</s>, <s>saṃjñā</s>, <s>saṃskāras</s>, and <s>vijñāna</s> are each empty of their own nature — each is <s>śūnyatā</s> and <s>śūnyatā</s> is each.] Just as, <s>Subhūti</s>, the footprint of a bird in the sky is not found and not apprehended — just so, <s>Subhūti</s>, the referent of the word '<s>bodhisattva</s>' is not found and not apprehended. Just as the footprint of a dream is not found and not apprehended, so too the referent of '<s>bodhisattva</s>' is not found and not apprehended. Just as the footprint of an illusion (<s>māyā</s>) is not found and not apprehended, so too for '<s>bodhisattva</s>.' Just as the footprint of a mirage (<s>marīci</s>) is not found and not apprehended, so too for '<s>bodhisattva</s>.' Just as the footprint of an echo (<s>pratiśrutkā</s>), an apparition (<s>pratibhāsa</s>), a reflection (<s>pratibimba</s>), a city of <s>gandharvas</s>, and a magical creation (<s>nirmita</s>) is not found and not apprehended — just so, <s>Subhūti</s>, the referent of the word '<s>bodhisattva</s>' is not found and not apprehended.

16101 [This is the support for the stage of heat.] Just as, <s>Subhūti</s>, the ground of <s>bhūtakoṭi</s> (the limit of reality) is not found and not apprehended, in the same way the ground of a <s>bodhisattva</s>'s meaning is not found and not apprehended. Just as, <s>Subhūti</s>, the ground of <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) is not found and not apprehended, in the same way the ground of a <s>bodhisattva</s>'s meaning is not found and not apprehended.
16102 Likewise for <s>avitathatā</s> (non-falseness), <s>ananyatathatā</s> (non-otherness of suchness), <s>dharmatā</s> (the nature of dharmas), <s>dharmadhātu</s> (dharma-realm), <s>dharmasthititā</s> (stability of dharmas),
16103 <s>dharmaniyāmatā</s> (certainty of dharmas), and <s>satyatā</s> (truth) — the ground is not found and not apprehended; in the same way the ground of a <s>bodhisattva</s>'s meaning is not found and not apprehended. [This is the support for the stage of summit.]
16104 Just as, <s>Subhūti</s>, the ground of <s>rūpa</s> (form) of a person created by <s>māyā</s> (illusion) is not found and not apprehended, in the same way, <s>Subhūti</s>, the ground of a <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s>'s
16105 meaning, when practicing <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> (perfection of wisdom), is not found and not apprehended. Likewise for <s>vedanā</s> (feeling), <s>saṃjñā</s> (perception), and <s>saṃskāras</s> (formations).
16106 Just as, <s>Subhūti</s>, the ground of <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness) of a person created by <s>māyā</s> is not found and not apprehended, in the same way, <s>Subhūti</s>, the ground of a <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s>'s meaning, when practicing <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, is not found and not apprehended.
16107 [Likewise for the six sense faculties (<s>cakṣus</s>, <s>śrotra</s>, <s>ghrāṇa</s>, <s>jihvā</s>, <s>kāya</s>, <s>manas</s>), the six sense objects (<s>rūpa</s>, <s>śabda</s>, <s>gandha</s>, <s>rasa</s>, <s>spraṣṭavya</s>, <s>dharma</s>), and the six consciousnesses (<s>cakṣurvijñāna</s>, <s>śrotravijñāna</s>, <s>ghrāṇavijñāna</s>, <s>jihvāvijñāna</s>, <s>kāyavijñāna</s>, <s>manovijñāna</s>) of a person created by <s>māyā</s> — the ground is not found and not apprehended; in the same way the ground of a <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s>'s meaning, when practicing <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, is not found and not apprehended.] [This is the

16110 found and not apprehended, in the same way, <s>Subhūti</s>, the ground of a <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s>'s meaning, when practicing <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, is not found and not apprehended. 16302 and <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination), whether taken separately or together, because of their utter isolation, the ground of characteristics is not found and not apprehended; in the same way, <s>Subhūti</s>, the ground of a <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s>'s meaning, when practicing <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, is not found and not apprehended.
16303 Just as, <s>Subhūti</s>, because of the utter purity of the <s>smṛtyupasthānas</s> (foundations of mindfulness), the ground of characteristics is not found and not apprehended, in the same way,
16304 <s>Subhūti</s>, the ground of a <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s>'s meaning, when practicing <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, is not found and not apprehended. Likewise for the <s>samyakprahāṇas</s> (right exertions), <s>ṛddhipādas</s> (bases of supernatural power), <s>indriyas</s> (faculties), <s>balas</s> (powers), <s>bodhyaṅgas</s> (factors of awakening), <s>mārgas</s> (path factors), <s>balas</s> (powers), <s>vaiśāradyas</s> (confidences), <s>pratisaṃvids</s> (analytical knowledges), and <s>āveṇikabuddhadharmas</s> (unique Buddha-qualities) — because of their utter purity, the ground of characteristics
16305 is not found and not apprehended; in the same way, <s>Subhūti</s>, the ground of a <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s>'s meaning, when practicing <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, is not found and not apprehended. Just as, <s>Subhūti</s>, in the purity of the view of self, being, life-force,
16306 nourisher, person, individual, human, youth, agent, experiencer, knower, and seer — the ground is not found and not apprehended, because self, being, life-force, nourisher, person, individual, human, youth, agent, experiencer, knower, and seer are non-existent; in the same way, <s>Subhūti</s>, the ground of a <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s>'s meaning, when practicing <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, is not found and not apprehended.
16307 [This is the support for the path of meditation.]
16308 Just as, <s>Subhūti</s>, the ground of the radiance of the rising sun is not found and not apprehended, in the same way, <s>Subhūti</s>, the ground of a <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s>'s meaning, when practicing <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, is not found and not apprehended. [This is the
16309 support for the antidote.]
16310 Just as, <s>Subhūti</s>, when the dissolution of a cosmic age (<s>kalpa</s>) is occurring, the ground of all conditioned things (<s>saṃskāras</s>) is not found and not apprehended, in the same way, <s>Subhūti</s>, the ground of a <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s>'s meaning, when practicing <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, is not found and not apprehended.
16311 [This is the support for the abandonment of adversaries.]
16312 Just as, <s>Subhūti</s>, in the <s>śīla</s> (moral discipline) of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One, the ground of <s>dauḥśīlya</s> (immorality) is not found and not apprehended,
16313 in the same way, <s>Subhūti</s>, the ground of a <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s>'s meaning, when practicing <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, is not found and not apprehended. Just as, <s>Subhūti</s>, in the <s>samādhi</s> (concentration) of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One, the ground of <s>vikṣepa</s> (distraction) is not found and not apprehended,
16314 and in the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom), the ground of <s>dauṣprajña</s> (poor wisdom) is not found and not apprehended, and in the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s <s>vimukti</s> (liberation), the ground of <s>avimukti</s> (non-liberation) is not found and not apprehended,
16315 in the same way, <s>Subhūti</s>, the ground of a <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s>'s meaning, when practicing <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, is not found and not apprehended. Just as, <s>Subhūti</s>, the ground of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s, the <s>Arhat</s>'s, the Perfectly Awakened One's <s>vimuktijñānadarśana</s> (knowledge and vision of liberation)
16316 is not found and not apprehended, in the same way, <s>Subhūti</s>, the ground of a <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s>'s meaning, when practicing <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, is not found and not apprehended. [This is the support for the abandonment of the distinction between antidote and adversary.]
16317 Just as, <s>Subhūti</s>, the ground of the radiance of the sun and the moon is not found and not apprehended, in the same way, <s>Subhūti</s>, the ground of a <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s>'s meaning, when practicing <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, is not found and not apprehended. [This is the support for
16318 <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) and <s>karuṇā</s> (compassion).]

16407 Why is that? Because, <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>bodhi</s> (awakening) by which the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s meaning exists, and the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s
16408 meaning itself — all these dharmas are neither conjoined nor disjoined, formless, without indication, without resistance,
16409 of one characteristic, namely without characteristics. For, <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> should train in the non-attachment
16410 and non-real-existence of all dharmas. And, <s>Subhūti</s>, all dharmas should be understood by the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s>
16411 through non-conceptualization, based upon non-conceptualization. [This is the support for knowledge proceeding without appearance.] [Thus the support for practice has been stated.]
16412
16413 <s>Subhūti</s> said: What, Blessed One, are all dharmas? How, Blessed One, should the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> train in the non-real-existence
16414 of all dharmas? How, Blessed One, should the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> understand all dharmas?
16415 The Blessed One said: All dharmas are said to be wholesome and unwholesome,
16416 determined and undetermined, mundane and supramundane, with outflows and without outflows, conditioned and unconditioned,
16417 shared and unshared. These, <s>Subhūti</s>, are called all dharmas, in which the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> should

children.translated_text: 16501 train in non-real-existence. These, <s>Subhūti</s>, are all the dharmas that the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> should understand.

children.translated_text:
16502 [Thus the nature of the object of practice has been stated.]
16503 <s>Subhūti</s> said: What, Blessed One, are the wholesome mundane dharmas? The Blessed One said:
16504 Wholesome mundane dharmas are said to be: respect for one's mother, respect for one's father, the conduct of an ascetic, the conduct of a brahmin,
16505 respect for the eldest in the family, the basis of meritorious action consisting of giving (<s>dānamaya puṇyakriyāvastu</s>), the basis of meritorious action consisting of moral discipline (<s>śīlamaya puṇyakriyāvastu</s>), the basis of meritorious action consisting of meditation (<s>bhāvanāmaya puṇyakriyāvastu</s>),
16506 skillful means accompanied by service (<s>vaiyāvṛtyasahagata upāyakauśala</s>), the ten wholesome courses of action (<s>daśakuśalāḥ karmapathāḥ</s>), and the nine mundane perceptions:
16507 the perception of a bloated corpse (<s>ādhmātakasaṃjñā</s>), the perception of a discolored corpse (<s>vipaṭumakasaṃjñā</s>), [likewise for the perception of a festering corpse, the perception of a blood-smeared corpse, the perception of a bluish corpse, the perception of a gnawed corpse, the perception of a scattered corpse, the perception of bones,] and the perception of a burnt corpse (<s>vidagdhakasaṃjñā</s>);
16508 the four mundane <s>dhyānas</s> (meditations), the four <s>apramāṇas</s> (immeasurables), and the four formless attainments (<s>ārūpyasamāpattis</s>);
16509 the five mundane <s>abhijñās</s> (superknowledges), and the ten mundane <s>anusmṛtis</s> (recollections), namely: recollection of the <s>Buddha</s>,
16510 recollection of the <s>Dharma</s>, [likewise recollection of the <s>Saṃgha</s>, recollection of moral discipline, recollection of generosity, recollection of the gods, recollection of breathing, recollection of death,] recollection of urgency, and recollection directed toward the body.

16516 laukikā akuśalā dharmāḥ//]
children.translated_text:
16511 [These are called the wholesome mundane dharmas.]
16512 <s>Subhūti</s> said: What, Blessed One, are the mundane unwholesome dharmas? The Blessed One said:
16513 Taking life, taking what is not given, sexual misconduct, false speech, slander, harsh speech, idle
16514 talk, covetousness, malice, and wrong views — these are the ten unwholesome courses of action. Anger, resentment,
16515 concealment, spite, harmfulness, jealousy, miserliness, pride, and wrong pride. [These are called
16516 the mundane unwholesome dharmas.]

children.translated_text:
16601 <s>Subhūti</s> said: What, Blessed One, are the undetermined dharmas? The Blessed One said: Undetermined
16602 bodily action, undetermined verbal action, undetermined mental action, the four undetermined great elements,
16603 the five undetermined sense faculties, the six undetermined sense-bases, the undetermined formless
16604 <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), <s>dhātus</s> (elements), and <s>āyatanas</s> (sense-bases), and the undetermined <s>vipākas</s> (results). [All these are called the undetermined dharmas.]
16605 <s>Subhūti</s> said: What, Blessed One, are the mundane wholesome dharmas? The Blessed One said:
16606 The five <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), the twelve <s>āyatanas</s> (sense-bases), the eighteen <s>dhātus</s> (elements), the ten wholesome courses of action, the four
16607 <s>dhyānas</s> (meditations), the four <s>apramāṇas</s> (immeasurables), the four formless attainments, the five <s>abhijñās</s> (superknowledges), and whatever other
16608 mundane dharmas there are. [These are called the mundane wholesome dharmas.]
16609 <s>Subhūti</s> said: What, Blessed One, are the supramundane wholesome dharmas? The Blessed One said:
16610 The four <s>smṛtyupasthānas</s> (foundations of mindfulness), the four <s>samyakprahāṇas</s> (right exertions), the four <s>ṛddhipādas</s> (bases of supernatural power),
16611 the five <s>indriyas</s> (faculties), the five <s>balas</s> (powers), the seven <s>bodhyaṅgas</s> (factors of awakening), the noble eightfold path;
16612 the <s>śūnyatāvimokṣamukha</s> (gate of liberation through emptiness), the <s>animittavimokṣamukha</s> (gate of liberation through signlessness), the <s>apraṇihitavimokṣamukha</s> (gate of liberation through wishlessness), the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown" (<s>anājñātam ājñāsyāmīndriya</s>),
16613 the faculty of perfect knowledge (<s>ājñendriya</s>), and the faculty of one who has fully known (<s>ājñātāvīndriya</s>); <s>samādhi</s> (concentration) with initial and sustained thought;
16614 <s>samādhi</s> without initial or sustained thought; knowledge, liberation, mindfulness, clear comprehension, proper
16615 mental engagement; and the eight liberations (<s>vimokṣas</s>). What are the eight? One who has form sees forms — this is the
16616 first liberation. One who is without the perception of form internally sees forms externally — this is the second
16617 liberation. One abides intent upon purity — this is the third liberation. Through the complete transcendence of
16618 perceptions of form, through the disappearance of perceptions of resistance, through non-attention to perceptions of diversity,
16619 thinking "Space is infinite," one enters and abides in the sphere of infinite space — this is the fourth
16620 liberation. Through the complete transcendence of the sphere of infinite space, thinking "Consciousness is infinite,"
16621 one enters and abides in the sphere of infinite consciousness — this is the fifth liberation. Through the complete
16622 transcendence of the sphere of infinite consciousness, thinking "There is nothing," one enters and abides in the
16623 sphere of nothingness — this is the sixth liberation. Through the complete transcendence of the sphere of nothingness,

16701 one enters and abides in the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception — this is the seventh liberation. Through the complete transcendence of the sphere of
16702 neither-perception-nor-non-perception, one enters and abides in the cessation of perception and feeling — this is the
16703 eighth liberation. These are the eight liberations. The nine successive abiding attainments:
16704 The four <s>dhyānas</s> (meditations) — secluded from sensual desires, secluded from unwholesome dharmas, with initial
16705 and sustained thought, born of seclusion, accompanied by joy and happiness, one enters and abides in the first <s>dhyāna</s>.
16706 Through the stilling of initial and sustained thought, with inner clarity, with unification of mind, without initial
16707 or sustained thought, born of concentration, accompanied by joy and happiness, one enters and abides in the second <s>dhyāna</s>. Through the fading of joy, one abides in equanimity, mindful
16708 and clearly comprehending, experiencing happiness with the body — that which the noble ones declare: "One who is equanimous, mindful,
16709 and abides in happiness" — one enters and abides in the third <s>dhyāna</s>. Through the abandonment of happiness and the abandonment of suffering,
16710 through the prior disappearance of elation and dejection, neither painful nor pleasant, with equanimity-purified mindfulness, one enters and abides in the fourth
16711 <s>dhyāna</s>. Through the complete transcendence of perceptions of form, through the disappearance of perceptions of resistance,
16712 through non-attention to perceptions of diversity, thinking "Space is infinite," one enters and abides in the sphere of infinite space.
16713 Through the complete transcendence of the sphere of infinite space, thinking "Consciousness is infinite," one enters and abides in the sphere of infinite
16714 consciousness. Through the complete transcendence of the sphere of infinite consciousness, thinking "There is nothing," one enters and abides in the sphere
16715 of nothingness. Through the complete transcendence of the sphere of nothingness, one enters and abides in the sphere of neither-perception-
16716 nor-non-perception. Through the complete transcendence of the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, one enters and abides in the cessation of perception and
16717 feeling. These are the nine successive abiding attainments. <s>Adhyātmaśūnyatā</s> (internal emptiness), <s>bahirdhāśūnyatā</s> (external emptiness),
16718 <s>adhyātmabahirdhāśūnyatā</s> (internal-external emptiness), up to <s>abhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of the non-existence of inherent nature). The ten <s>balas</s> (powers), the four

16803 <s>Subhūti</s> said: What, Blessed One, are the dharmas with outflows (<s>sāsrava</s>)? The Blessed One said: The five <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates),

16805 formless attainments. [These are called the dharmas with outflows.]
16806 <s>Subhūti</s> said: What, Blessed One, are the dharmas without outflows (<s>anāsrava</s>)? The Blessed One said: The four
16807 <s>smṛtyupasthānas</s> (foundations of mindfulness), the four <s>samyakprahāṇas</s> (right exertions), the four <s>ṛddhipādas</s> (bases of supernatural power), the five <s>indriyas</s> (faculties),
16808 the five <s>balas</s> (powers), the seven <s>bodhyaṅgas</s> (factors of awakening), the noble eightfold path, the ten <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>balas</s> (powers), the four
16809 <s>vaiśāradyas</s> (confidences), the four <s>pratisaṃvids</s> (analytical knowledges), up to the eighteen <s>āveṇikabuddhadharmas</s> (unique Buddha-qualities). [These are called
16810 the dharmas without outflows.]
16811 <s>Subhūti</s> said: What, Blessed One, are the conditioned dharmas (<s>saṃskṛta</s>)? The Blessed One said: The desire realm (<s>kāmadhātu</s>),
16812 the form realm (<s>rūpadhātu</s>), the formless realm (<s>ārūpyadhātu</s>), and whatever other dharmas are included within the three realms; the thirty-seven
16813 <s>bodhipakṣadharmas</s> (dharmas conducive to awakening) and the rest. [These are called the conditioned dharmas.]
16814 <s>Subhūti</s> said: What, Blessed One, are the unconditioned dharmas (<s>asaṃskṛta</s>)? The Blessed One said: Those
16815 dharmas whose arising, cessation, and change are not discerned — the destruction of passion, the destruction of hatred, and the destruction of delusion;
16816 <s>tathatā</s> (suchness), <s>avitathatā</s> (non-falseness), <s>ananyatathatā</s> (non-otherness of suchness), <s>dharmatā</s> (nature of dharmas), <s>dharmadhātu</s> (dharma-realm), <s>dharmasthititā</s> (stability of dharmas), <s>dharmaniyāmatā</s> (certainty of dharmas),
16817 and <s>bhūtakoṭi</s> (limit of reality). [These are called the unconditioned dharmas.]
16818 <s>Subhūti</s> said: What, Blessed One, are the shared dharmas (<s>sādhāraṇa</s>)? The Blessed One said: The four

16901 Therein, the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> should not form attachment to dharmas that are empty of their own characteristics, and
