16904 <s>Subhūti</s> said: The expression "<s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s>" is used, Blessed One. For what
16905 reason, Blessed One, is one called a <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s>? The Blessed One said: Here, <s>Subhūti</s>, one will bring about leadership for a great
16906 assembly of beings, a great multitude of beings. For that reason, <s>Subhūti</s>, one is called a <s>bodhisattva</s>
16907 <s>mahāsattva</s>.
16908 <s>Subhūti</s> said: What, Blessed One, is the great assembly of beings, the great multitude of beings, for which the
16909 <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> will bring about leadership? The Blessed One said: The great assembly of beings,
16910 the great multitude of beings, <s>Subhūti</s>, is said to be the <s>gotrabhūmi</s> (lineage-stage), the <s>aṣṭamakabhūmi</s> (eighth stage),
16911 the <s>srotaāpanna</s> (stream-enterer), the <s>sakṛdāgāmin</s> (once-returner), the <s>anāgāmin</s> (non-returner), the <s>arhat</s>, the <s>pratyekabuddha</s> (solitary awakened one), and from the first arising of the thought of awakening
16912 up to the <s>avinivartanīya</s> (irreversible stage). This is the great assembly of beings, the great multitude of beings. For this
16913 the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> will bring about leadership. Therein, <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s>, having generated a diamond-like
16914 mind, should bring about leadership for the great assembly of beings, the great multitude of beings.
16915 <s>Subhūti</s> said: What, Blessed One, is this diamond-like generation of the mind? The Blessed One said: Here,
16916 <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> generates the following mind: "Having donned armor in the immeasurable <s>saṃsāra</s> (cycle of existence),
16917 I must become one who does not abandon any being. I must generate
16918 an attitude of equanimity toward all beings. I must bring all beings to <s>parinirvāṇa</s> (final liberation) through the three vehicles."

children.translated_text: The exalted mind of the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> (great being) by which he will bring about the foremost position for all beings; and with that mind he does not conceive. Furthermore, <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> should have an unshakable mind. Therein, this is the unshakable mind of the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s>: that he does not conceive even of mental attention conjoined with <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> (knowledge of all aspects). Furthermore, <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> should have a mind of benevolence and happiness toward all beings. Therein, this is the benevolent mind of the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s>: the protection of all beings, the non-abandonment of all beings, and with that he does not conceive. This, <s>Subhūti</s>, is the benevolent mind of the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s>. Thus indeed, <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s>, practicing <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> (perfection of wisdom), will bring about the foremost position for all beings. Furthermore, <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> should have delight in the <s>Dharma</s>. He should be engaged in the practice of delighting in the <s>Dharma</s>. Therein, what is the <s>Dharma</s>? The non-differentiation of all <s>dharmas</s> — this is called the <s>Dharma</s>. Therein, what is delight in the <s>Dharma</s>? That which is rejoicing in the <s>Dharma</s> — this is called delight in the <s>Dharma</s>. Therein, what is devotion to the <s>Dharma</s>? The cultivation and repeated practice of that <s>Dharma</s> — this is called devotion to the <s>Dharma</s>. Thus indeed, <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s>, practicing <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, should bring about the foremost position for a great mass of beings, a great assemblage of beings, through the method of non-apprehension. children.translated_text: <s>mahāsattva</s>, practicing <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, abiding in the <s>vajropamasamādhi</s> (diamond-like concentration), up to abiding in the <s>ākāśāsaṅgaimuktinirupalepasamādhi</s> (concentration of space-like unattachment, liberation, and unstainedness), should bring about the foremost position for a great mass of beings, a great assemblage of beings, through the method of non-apprehension. Abiding in these <s>dharmas</s>, <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s>, practicing <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, should bring about the foremost position for a great mass of beings, a great assemblage of beings. Therefore he is called <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s>. [Thus ends the greatness of mind regarding the foremost position of all beings.] Then the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> said to the Blessed One: It occurs to me too, Blessed One, the reason why a <s>bodhisattva</s> is called a <s>mahāsattva</s>. The Blessed One said: Speak, <s>Śāriputra</s>, the reason why a <s>bodhisattva</s> is a <s>mahāsattva</s>. <s>Śāriputra</s> said: Blessed One, he teaches the <s>Dharma</s> for the abandonment of all these views — the view of self, the view of a being, the view of a creature, a life, a nurturer, a person, an individual, a human, a mortal, a doer, an experiencer, a knower, a seer; the view of annihilation, the view of eternalism, the view of existence, the view of non-existence; the view of <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), the view of <s>dhātus</s> (elements), the view of <s>āyatanas</s> (sense-bases); the view of <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination); the view of <s>bodhipakṣa dharmas</s>, the view of <s>balas</s> (powers) and <s>vaiśāradyas</s> (fearlessnesses), the view of unique <s>buddhadharmas</s>; the view of maturing beings, the view of purifying buddha-fields; the view of <s>bodhisattvas</s>, the view of <s>Buddhas</s>, the view of turning the <s>dharmacakra</s> (wheel of Dharma) — through the method of non-apprehension. For this reason he is called <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s>. <s>Subhūti</s> said: For what reason, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, does the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> have a view of <s>rūpa</s> (form), [likewise a view of <s>vedanā</s> (feeling), a view of <s>saṃjñā</s> (perception), a view of <s>saṃskāras</s> (formations),] a view of <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness)? <s>Śāriputra</s> said: Here, venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s>, practicing <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, is unskilled in means. He, apprehending <s>rūpa</s> (form), produces a view through the method of apprehension. Thus in detail, apprehending the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), <s>dhātus</s> (elements), and <s>āyatanas</s> (sense-bases) both separately and collectively, and <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination) up to old age, death, grief, lamentation, suffering, dejection, and despair, he produces a view through the method of apprehension. Likewise, apprehending the <s>smṛtyupasthānas</s> (foundations of mindfulness), [likewise for the right efforts, bases of supernormal power, faculties, powers, factors of awakening, path factors, <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections),] <s>abhijñās</s> (superknowledges), syllables, immeasurables, <s>dhyānas</s> (meditations), and formless attainments, he produces a view through the method of apprehension. Likewise, apprehending the ten <s>balas</s> (powers), <s>vaiśāradyas</s> (fearlessnesses), [likewise <s>pratisaṃvids</s> (analytical knowledges) and the eighteen unique] <s>buddhadharmas</s>, he produces a view through the method of apprehension.

For that <s>sarvajñatā</s> (omniscience) mind is undefiled and not included in the three realms; even in that mind he is unattached. For this reason, the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> is so designated. <s>Śāriputra</s> said: What, venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, is the incomparable mind of the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s>, the mind not shared with all <s>śrāvakas</s> and <s>pratyekabuddhas</s>? <s>Subhūti</s> said: Here, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s>, from the first arising of the thought of awakening, does not perceive the arising or cessation of any <s>dharma</s>, nor decrease nor increase, nor coming nor going, nor defilement nor purification. And where, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, there is no defilement and no purification, no going and no coming, no decrease and no increase, no arising and no cessation — that is neither the mind of a <s>śrāvaka</s> nor the mind of a <s>pratyekabuddha</s>. This, <s>Śāriputra</s>, is the incomparable mind of the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s>, the mind not shared with all <s>śrāvakas</s> and <s>pratyekabuddhas</s>.

children.translated_text: Is not the mind of all <s>śrāvakas</s> (hearers), <s>pratyekabuddhas</s> (solitary buddhas), and <s>samyaksaṃbuddhas</s> (perfectly awakened ones) also undefiled and not included, on account of <s>prakṛtiśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of intrinsic nature)? <s>Subhūti</s> said: So it is, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>. <s>Śāriputra</s> said: Is not <s>rūpa</s> (form) also, <s>Subhūti</s>, undefiled and not included, on account of <s>prakṛtiśūnyatā</s>? Are not the thirty-seven <s>bodhipakṣa dharmas</s> (factors of awakening), the ten <s>tathāgatabalas</s> (powers of the Tathāgata), [likewise the four <s>vaiśāradyas</s> (fearlessnesses), the four <s>pratisaṃvids</s> (analytical knowledges), the three <s>vimokṣamukhas</s> (doors of liberation), and the eighteen unique] <s>buddhadharmas</s> also undefiled and not included, on account of <s>prakṛtiśūnyatā</s>? <s>Subhūti</s> said: So it is, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, as you say. The mind of ordinary foolish beings is also undefiled and not included, on account of <s>prakṛtiśūnyatā</s>. Up to the mind of all <s>śrāvakas</s>, <s>pratyekabuddhas</s>, and <s>samyaksaṃbuddhas</s> is also undefiled and not included, on account of <s>prakṛtiśūnyatā</s>. Up to the thirty-seven <s>bodhipakṣa dharmas</s>, the ten <s>tathāgatabalas</s>, [likewise the four <s>vaiśāradyas</s>, the four <s>pratisaṃvids</s>, the three <s>vimokṣamukhas</s>, and the eighteen unique] <s>buddhadharmas</s> are also undefiled and not included, on account of <s>prakṛtiśūnyatā</s>. <s>Śāriputra</s> said: Even though the venerable <s>Subhūti</s> says "because of mindlessness, even in that mind he is unattached" — is not <s>rūpa</s> (form) unattached even in the absence of form? In <s>rūpa</s> (form) also, venerable one, <s>rūpa</s> is unattached; <s>vedanā</s>, <s>saṃjñā</s>, <s>saṃskāras</s> — in <s>vijñāna</s> also, <s>vijñāna</s> is unattached. The Blessed One said: Speak, <s>Pūrṇa</s>. <s>Pūrṇa</s> said: Blessed One, a being who has donned the great armor, who has set out in the <s>mahāyāna</s> (great vehicle), who has mounted the <s>mahāyāna</s> — for that reason, Blessed One, he is called <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s>. <s>Śāriputra</s> said: To what extent, venerable <s>Pūrṇa</s>, is the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> said to have donned the great armor? <s>Pūrṇa</s> said: Here, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s>, seeking awakening not for the sake of a limited number of beings, abides in <s>dānapāramitā</s> (perfection of giving) and gives gifts. Rather, for the sake of all beings, abiding in <s>dānapāramitā</s>, he gives gifts. Likewise for <s>śīlapāramitā</s> (perfection of morality), <s>kṣāntipāramitā</s> (perfection of patience), <s>vīryapāramitā</s> (perfection of vigor), and <s>dhyānapāramitā</s> (perfection of meditation). Not for the sake of a limited number of beings seeking awakening does he abide in <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> (perfection of wisdom) and cultivate <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>. Rather, for the sake of all beings he cultivates <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>. The <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> does not don the great armor with discrimination among beings, thinking: "I will lead this many beings to <s>nirvāṇa</s>, and this many beings I will not lead to <s>nirvāṇa</s>; I will establish this many beings in awakening, and this many beings I will not establish in awakening." Rather, he dons the armor for the sake of all beings, and he thinks thus: "I myself will fulfill <s>dānapāramitā</s> (perfection of giving) and I will engage all beings in <s>dānapāramitā</s>;"

children.translated_text: [Likewise he thinks: "I myself will fulfill <s>śīlapāramitā</s> (perfection of morality) and engage all beings in <s>śīlapāramitā</s>; I myself will fulfill <s>kṣāntipāramitā</s> (perfection of patience) and engage all beings in <s>kṣāntipāramitā</s>; I myself will fulfill <s>dhyānapāramitā</s> (perfection of meditation) and engage all beings in <s>dhyānapāramitā</s>; I myself will fulfill <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> (perfection of wisdom) and engage all beings in <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>." ] Likewise for the immeasurables, <s>dhyānas</s> (meditations), and formless attainments: "I myself will cultivate them and I will establish all beings in them." Up to the thirty-seven <s>bodhipakṣa dharmas</s> (factors of awakening), the ten <s>balas</s> (powers), the <s>vaiśāradyas</s> (fearlessnesses), and the eighteen unique <s>buddhadharmas</s>: "I myself will abide in them and I will establish all beings in them." To this extent, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> is said to have donned the great armor. [Thus ends the nature of the practice.] Furthermore, <s>Śāriputra</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s>, practicing <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, giving gifts with mental attention conjoined with <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> (knowledge of all aspects), that which is the dedication of his giving to <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> (unsurpassed perfect awakening), having made it common to all beings — this is the <s>dānapāramitā</s> (perfection of giving) armor of the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> practicing <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> while giving gifts. Furthermore, [with the same mental attention conjoined with <s>sarvākārajñatā</s>,] that which is the avoidance of mental attention associated with <s>śrāvakas</s> and <s>pratyekabuddhas</s> — this is his <s>śīlapāramitā</s> (perfection of morality) armor. Furthermore, [with the same mental attention,] that which is the acceptance, approval, and examination of those — this is his <s>kṣāntipāramitā</s> (perfection of patience) armor. Furthermore, [with the same mental attention,] that which is the non-slackening of vigor — he dedicates that root of merit to <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>, having made it common to all beings — this is his <s>vīryapāramitā</s> (perfection of vigor) armor. Furthermore, [with the same mental attention,] that which is the one-pointedness of mind with mental attention conjoined with <s>sarvākārajñatā</s>, giving no opportunity to the mind of <s>śrāvakas</s> and <s>pratyekabuddhas</s> — he dedicates that root of merit to <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>, having made it common to all beings — this is his <s>dhyānapāramitā</s> (perfection of meditation) armor. Furthermore,

[with the same mental attention conjoined with <s>sarvākārajñatā</s>,] that which is the perception of all things as being like magical creations — he neither apprehends the giver, nor the recipient, nor the gift. This is the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> (perfection of wisdom) armor of the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> practicing <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>. In that, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s>, with a mind conjoined with <s>sarvākārajñatā</s>, neither makes a sign of those six <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections) nor apprehends them. Thus indeed, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s>, practicing <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, has donned the great armor. [Thus ends the first set of six, the giving-perfection armor.] Furthermore, <s>Śāriputra</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s>, practicing <s>śīlapāramitā</s> (perfection of morality), with mental attention conjoined with <s>sarvākārajñatā</s>, gives gifts, dedicating them to <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> having made them common to all beings, through the method of non-apprehension. This, <s>Subhūti</s>, is the <s>dānapāramitā</s> (perfection of giving) of the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> practicing <s>śīlapāramitā</s>. Furthermore, [with mental attention conjoined with <s>sarvākārajñatā</s>,] that which is the absence of aspiration for the level of <s>śrāvakas</s> and <s>pratyekabuddhas</s>, let alone the level of ordinary beings — this is the <s>śīlapāramitā</s> of the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> practicing <s>śīlapāramitā</s>. [Likewise for <s>kṣāntipāramitā</s>: the acceptance, approval, and examination of those; for <s>vīryapāramitā</s>: the non-slackening of vigor, dedicating that root of merit to <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> having made it common to all beings; for <s>dhyānapāramitā</s>: the one-pointedness of mind giving no opportunity to mental states associated with <s>śrāvakas</s> and <s>pratyekabuddhas</s>, dedicating that root of merit to <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> having made it common to all beings.] [With mental attention conjoined with <s>sarvākārajñatā</s>,] the perception of magical creations arises. He neither conceives of nor apprehends that morality. This, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, is the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> (perfection of wisdom) of the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> practicing <s>śīlapāramitā</s>. Thus indeed, <s>Śāriputra</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s>, practicing <s>śīlapāramitā</s>, encompasses the six <s>pāramitās</s>. Therefore he is designated as one who has donned the great armor. [Thus ends the second set of six, the morality-perfection armor.] Furthermore, <s>Śāriputra</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s>, practicing <s>kṣāntipāramitā</s> (perfection of patience), gives gifts with mental attention conjoined with <s>sarvākārajñatā</s>, not with mental attention associated with <s>śrāvakas</s> and <s>pratyekabuddhas</s>, and dedicates that root of merit to <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> having made it common to all beings.

children.translated_text: This is the <s>dānapāramitā</s> (perfection of giving) of the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> practicing <s>kṣāntipāramitā</s> (perfection of patience). Likewise, while practicing <s>kṣāntipāramitā</s>, there is <s>śīlapāramitā</s> (perfection of morality), <s>kṣāntipāramitā</s>, <s>vīryapāramitā</s> (perfection of vigor), and <s>dhyānapāramitā</s> (perfection of meditation). Furthermore, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s>, practicing <s>kṣāntipāramitā</s>, applies himself to the accumulation of all <s>buddhadharmas</s> and the maturing of all beings, with <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom), with mental attention conjoined with <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> (knowledge of all aspects), not with mental attention associated with <s>śrāvakas</s> and <s>pratyekabuddhas</s>, and dedicates that root of merit to <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> (unsurpassed perfect awakening), having made it common to all beings. Therefore he is designated as one who has donned the great armor. children.translated_text: <s>Śāriputra</s> said: To what extent, venerable <s>Pūrṇa</s>, is the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> established in the <s>mahāyāna</s> (great vehicle) and mounted upon the <s>mahāyāna</s>? <s>Pūrṇa</s> said: Here, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s>, practicing <s>dānapāramitā</s> (perfection of giving), secluded from sensual desires, secluded from unwholesome <s>dharmas</s>, with initial and sustained thought, with joy and happiness born of seclusion, enters and abides in the first <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation). Likewise the second, third, and fourth <s>dhyānas</s>. Likewise he enters and abides in the sphere of infinite space, the sphere of infinite consciousness, the sphere of nothingness, and the sphere of neither perception nor non-perception. These are the <s>dhyānas</s> (meditations) and formless attainments of the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s>. When the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s>, with these <s>dhyānas</s> and formless attainments, practicing <s>dānapāramitā</s>, enters and emerges with signs characterized by the nature of space, he dedicates those roots of merit to <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> (unsurpassed perfect awakening), having made them common to all beings. This is the <s>dānapāramitā</s> of the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s>. Likewise it should be stated for <s>śīlapāramitā</s> (perfection of morality), <s>kṣāntipāramitā</s> (perfection of patience), <s>vīryapāramitā</s> (perfection of vigor), and <s>dhyānapāramitā</s> (perfection of meditation). Furthermore, <s>Śāriputra</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s>, practicing <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, enters the four <s>dhyānas</s> and the four formless attainments. When the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> abides with these <s>dhyānas</s> and formless attainments, entering and emerging from these <s>dhyānas</s> and formless attainments, he applies mental attention to the signs characterized by the nature of space. Practicing <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, he dedicates those roots of merit and other merit to <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>, with mental attention conjoined with <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> (knowledge of all aspects), having made them common to all beings. This is the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> of the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s>. Thus indeed, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s>, practicing the six <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections), has donned the great armor, matures beings, and purifies the <s>buddhakṣetra</s> (buddha-field). [Thus ends the setting forth through emergence from dhyāna and formless attainments.] Furthermore, <s>Śāriputra</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s>, with mental attention conjoined with <s>sarvākārajñatā</s>, having produced the thought for the destruction of the <s>kleśas</s> (defilements) of all beings — "I will teach the <s>Dharma</s> to all beings" — this is the <s>dānapāramitā</s> (perfection of giving) of the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s>. When the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s>, with that same mental attention conjoined with <s>sarvākārajñatā</s>, ascends to the first <s>dhyāna</s>, teaches the <s>Dharma</s>, abides in the first <s>dhyāna</s>, and gives no opportunity to other mental states

18303 knowledge in [each] emptiness, yet not through the method of apprehension — this is a <s>bodhisattva-mahāsattva</s>'s Great Vehicle.
18304 Furthermore, Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, the Great Vehicle of a <s>bodhisattva-mahāsattva</s> [is this]: the knowledge that does not train in any <s>dharmas</s> —

18306 knowledge does not operate as 'permanent' nor as 'impermanent'; not as 'suffering' nor as 'non-suffering';
18307 [not as 'pleasant' nor as 'non-pleasant'; not as 'self' nor as 'non-self'; not as 'peaceful' nor as 'non-peaceful'; not as 'empty' nor as 'non-empty'; not as 'with signs' nor as 'without signs';]

18309 Furthermore, Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, the Great Vehicle of a <s>bodhisattva-mahāsattva</s> [is this]: knowledge does not operate in the past time-period, does not operate in the future time-period,
18310 does not operate in the present time-period. And his knowledge does not operate in the three time-periods — and that through the method of non-apprehension.
18311 This too, <s>Śāriputra</s>, is a <s>bodhisattva-mahāsattva</s>'s Great Vehicle.
18312 Furthermore, Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, the Great Vehicle of a <s>bodhisattva-mahāsattva</s> [is this]: knowledge does not operate in the <s>kāmadhātu</s> (desire realm), does not operate in the <s>rūpadhātu</s> (form realm), does not operate in the <s>ārūpyadhātu</s> (formless realm);

children.translated_text: having donned the armor of the bases of miraculous power (<s>ṛddhipāda</s>), faculties (<s>indriya</s>), powers (<s>bala</s>), factors of enlightenment (<s>bodhyaṅga</s>), and path-factors (<s>mārgāṅga</s>), having donned the armor of attainments (<s>samāpatti</s>), the armor of emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>), the armor of the confidences (<s>vaiśāradya</s>), the armor of the analytical knowledges (<s>pratisaṃvid</s>), the armor of the eighteen unique <s>Buddha</s>-dharmas (<s>āveṇikabuddhadharma</s>), and the armor of <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> (omniscience of all aspects), having donned the form of a <s>Buddha</s> (<s>buddhavigraha</s>), he pervades the great trichiliocosm (<s>trisāhasramahāsāhasra lokadhātu</s>) with radiance, causes it to quake in six ways, and in every hellish realm of existence, having extinguished that mass of fire, having pacified the sufferings of the hell-beings, and knowing them all to be inclined toward <s>nirvāṇa</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> utters this sound and proclaims this cry: 'Homage to the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the perfectly enlightened one!' Then those hell-beings, having heard that cry of the <s>Buddha</s>, obtain happiness. With that very happiness and joy, they arise from those hells and are reborn in that world-system where they see the <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones, and please them, and they take on rebirth among gods and humans. Likewise, having arisen from the animal realm (<s>tiryagyoni</s>) and the realm of <s>Yama</s>, they are reborn in that world-system where they see the <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones, and please them, and take on rebirth among gods and humans. Thus in the eastern direction, he pervades world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river <s>Gaṅgā</s> with radiance, causes them to quake in six ways, extinguishes the fire in every hellish realm, pacifies the sufferings of the hell-beings, and knowing them all to be inclined toward <s>nirvāṇa</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> utters this sound and proclaims this cry: 'Homage to the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the perfectly enlightened one!' Then those hell-beings, having heard that cry of the <s>Buddha</s>, obtain happiness, arise from those hells with that happiness and joy, and are reborn where they see and please the <s>Buddhas</s> and take on rebirth among gods and humans. Likewise in the southern direction, the western direction, the northern direction, the northeastern direction, the southeastern direction, the southwestern direction, the northwestern direction, the downward direction, and the upward direction — in world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river <s>Gaṅgā</s> in each direction, he pervades with radiance, causes them to quake in six ways, extinguishes the fire in every hellish realm, pacifies the sufferings of hell-beings, and knowing them all to be inclined toward <s>nirvāṇa</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> proclaims: 'Homage to the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the perfectly enlightened one!' And those hell-beings, hearing the cry of the <s>Buddha</s>, obtain happiness, arise from those hells, and are reborn where they see and please the <s>Buddhas</s> and take on rebirth among gods and humans. Thus, <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> is said to have donned the great armor (<s>mahāsannāhasannaddha</s>). Just as, <s>Subhūti</s>, a skilled magician or a magician's apprentice might create at a crossroads, before a great assembly of people, hells, the animal realm, and the realm of <s>Yama</s>, and having created them, might proclaim to those beings the sound of the <s>Buddha</s>, the sound of the <s>Dharma</s>, and the sound of the <s>Saṃgha</s> — and by that sound of the <s>Buddha</s>, sound of the <s>Dharma</s>, and sound of the <s>Saṃgha</s>, they might arise from those hells, animal realms, and realms of <s>Yama</s> and be reborn among gods and humans — yet, <s>Subhūti</s>, has any being been caused to arise from the destinations of hells, the animal realm, or the realm of <s>Yama</s> by that magician or his apprentice? <s>Subhūti</s> said: 'No, Blessed One.' The Blessed One said: 'In the same way, <s>Subhūti</s>, though the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> liberates beings from the three lower realms of existence (<s>apāya</s>) in innumerable, immeasurable, and boundless world-systems, no being whatsoever has been liberated. For what reason? Because it is the nature of those <s>dharmas</s>, <s>Subhūti</s>, based on their having the nature of an illusion (<s>māyādharmatā</s>).' Thus, <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> is said to have mounted the great vehicle (<s>mahāyāna</s>) and donned the great armor.

children.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Subhūti</s>, a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, established in the perfection of generosity (<s>dānapāramitā</s>), having girded on the great armor, magically creates a <s>trisāhasramahāsāhasra lokadhātu</s> (billion-world universe) made of <s>vaidūrya</s> (lapis lazuli). Having created it of <s>vaidūrya</s>, he creates a <s>cakravartin</s> (universal monarch) array. Having created the <s>cakravartin</s> array, he gives food to those who seek food. Likewise, he gives clothing, vehicles, fragrances, garlands, flowers, incense, ointments, powders, ornaments, dwellings, bedding, seats, cloaks, requisites for livelihood, medicines, gold, silver, gems, jewels, coral, conch shells, crystal, pearls, and adornments — whatever various requisites he gives. Having given food to those who seek food, and having given whatever various requisites, he teaches the <s>Dharma</s> to those beings, namely that which is connected with the six <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections). And those beings, having heard that <s>Dharma</s> teaching, are never separated from those perfections until they fully awaken to <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> (unsurpassed perfect awakening). Thus, <s>Subhūti</s>, a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> is said to have girded on the great armor. Just as, <s>Subhūti</s>, a skillful magician or magician's apprentice, standing at a crossroads, would magically create a great multitude of people before a great assembly and give food to those who seek food, and give whatever requisites to those who seek them — what do you think, <s>Subhūti</s>, has that magician or magician's apprentice given anything to anyone? <s>Subhūti</s> said: No, Blessed One. The Blessed One said: Just so, <s>Subhūti</s>, when a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, having magically created a <s>cakravartin</s> array, gives food to those who seek food and gives whatever human requisites, nothing whatsoever has been given to any being. For what reason? This is the nature of <s>dharmas</s>, <s>Subhūti</s>, based on the illusion-nature of <s>dharmas</s>. Thus, <s>Subhūti</s>, a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> is said to have girded on the great armor. [Thus ends the accumulation of generosity (<s>dānasambhāra</s>).] Furthermore, <s>Subhūti</s>, a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, through the perfection of morality (<s>śīlapāramitā</s>), by deliberately grasping rebirth, is born in the family of a <s>cakravartin</s> (universal monarch). children.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Subhūti</s>, a <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s>, abiding in the <s>vīryapāramitā</s> (perfection of vigor), encourages, establishes, and settles all beings in the <s>vīryapāramitā</s>. And how, <s>Subhūti</s>, does a <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s>, abiding in the <s>vīryapāramitā</s>, encourage, establish, and settle all beings in the <s>vīryapāramitā</s>? Here, <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s>, established in physical and mental vigor through mental applications connected with the knowledge of all aspects, encourages, establishes, and settles all beings in physical and mental vigor. Just as, <s>Subhūti</s>, a skilled magician or magician's apprentice, having conjured a great multitude of people at a crossroads, might establish them in physical and mental vigor through mental applications connected with the knowledge of all aspects — yet having established that many beings in physical and mental vigor, no being whatsoever has been established in physical and mental vigor. Just so, <s>Subhūti</s>, although the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> has established that many beings in physical and mental vigor, no being whatsoever has been established in physical and mental vigor. Why is that? This is the nature of <s>dharmas</s>, <s>Subhūti</s>, based on their having the nature of <s>māyā</s> (illusion). Thus indeed, <s>Subhūti</s>, is the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> said to be one who has put on the great armor. Here, <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s>, abiding in the equality of all <s>dharmas</s>, does not perceive either distraction or non-distraction of any <s>dharma</s>. children.translated_text: does not apprehend either the near shore or the far shore of any <s>dharma</s>. Thus does the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> abide in the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> (perfection of wisdom). He likewise encourages, establishes, and settles all beings therein. Just as, <s>Subhūti</s>, a skilled magician or magician's apprentice, having conjured a great multitude of people at a crossroads, might establish that multitude in the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> — yet having established that many beings in the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, not even a single being has been established in the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>. Just so, <s>Subhūti</s>, although the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> has established all beings in the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, no being has been established in the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>. Why is that? This is the nature of <s>dharmas</s>, <s>Subhūti</s>, based on their having the nature of <s>māyā</s> (illusion). Thus indeed, <s>Subhūti</s>, is the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> said to be one who has put on the great armor. [Thus the accumulation of wisdom.] Furthermore, <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s>, having put on the great armor, in the eastern direction, in world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river <s>Gaṅgā</s>, however many beings there are, all of them — just as he himself abides in the <s>dānapāramitā</s> (perfection of giving) — he encourages, establishes, and settles them in the <s>dānapāramitā</s>. Likewise in the <s>śīlapāramitā</s> (perfection of morality), <s>kṣāntipāramitā</s> (perfection of patience), <s>vīryapāramitā</s> (perfection of vigor), <s>dhyānapāramitā</s> (perfection of meditation), and <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> (perfection of wisdom) he encourages, establishes, and settles them. And he teaches the <s>Dharma</s>, namely this very teaching connected with the six <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections). And those beings, having heard it, are never again separated from the six <s>pāramitās</s> until they have fully awakened to unsurpassed perfect awakening. [Likewise for the southern, western, northern, northeastern, southeastern, southwestern, northwestern, downward, and upward directions — in world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā in each direction, the bodhisattva establishes all beings in the six pāramitās and teaches them the Dharma connected with the six pāramitās, so that they are never separated from them until full awakening.]

children.translated_text: [Likewise for the upward direction — in world-systems as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā, the bodhisattva establishes all beings in the six pāramitās and teaches them the Dharma, so they are never separated from them until full awakening.] Just as, <s>Subhūti</s>, a skilled magician or magician's apprentice, having conjured a great multitude of people at a crossroads, encourages, establishes, and settles them in the six <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections). What do you think, <s>Subhūti</s>? Has any being been encouraged, established, or settled in the six <s>pāramitās</s> by that magician or magician's apprentice? <s>Subhūti</s> said: No, <s>Bhagavan</s>. The <s>Bhagavan</s> said: Just so, <s>Subhūti</s>, although the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> has established that many beings in the six <s>pāramitās</s>, no being has been established in the six <s>pāramitās</s>. Why is that? This is the nature of <s>dharmas</s>, <s>Subhūti</s>, based on their having the nature of <s>māyā</s> (illusion). Thus indeed, <s>Subhūti</s>, is the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> said to be one who has put on the great armor. Furthermore, <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s>, having put on the great armor, dwelling with a mind connected with the knowledge of all aspects, does not give occasion to other mental productions, thinking: "I must establish this many beings in the <s>dānapāramitā</s> (perfection of giving)." [Likewise: "I must establish this many beings in the <s>śīlapāramitā</s>," "in the <s>kṣāntipāramitā</s>," "in the <s>vīryapāramitā</s>," "in the <s>dhyānapāramitā</s>," "in the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>."] [Likewise: "I must establish this many beings in the <s>bodhipakṣadharmas</s> (factors of awakening)," "in the distinctive <s>Buddha</s>-qualities," "in the fruit of stream-entry," "in the fruit of once-returning," "in the fruit of non-returning," "in <s>arhatship</s>," "in <s>pratyekabuddhahood</s>."] [Likewise: "I must establish this many beings in omniscience."] Rather, innumerable and immeasurable beings are to be established in the six <s>pāramitās</s>. Likewise in the thirty-seven factors of awakening, the ten <s>Tathāgata</s> powers, the four analytical knowledges, and the eighteen distinctive <s>Buddha</s>-qualities they are to be established — innumerable and immeasurable beings are to be established in the fruit of stream-entry, the fruit of once-returning, the fruit of non-returning, <s>arhatship</s>, and <s>Buddhahood</s>. [Thus the accumulation of calm abiding.]

children.translated_text: Just as, <s>Subhūti</s>, a skilled magician or magician's apprentice, having conjured a great multitude of people at a crossroads, might establish them in the six <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections), and even in the knowledge of all aspects endowed with all modes — just so, <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s>, having established that many innumerable and immeasurable beings in the six <s>pāramitās</s> and in the knowledge of all aspects endowed with all modes, no being has been established in the six <s>pāramitās</s>. Why is that? This is the nature of <s>dharmas</s>, <s>Subhūti</s>, based on their having the nature of <s>māyā</s> (illusion). <s>Subhūti</s> said: As I understand the meaning of the <s>Bhagavan</s>'s words, this <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> should be understood as one who has not put on armor, based on the emptiness of own-characteristics. Why is that? For indeed, <s>Bhagavan</s>, <s>rūpa</s> (form) is empty of <s>rūpa</s>; <s>vedanā</s> (feeling) is empty of <s>vedanā</s>; <s>saṃjñā</s> (perception) is empty of <s>saṃjñā</s>; <s>saṃskāras</s> (formations) are empty of <s>saṃskāras</s>; <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness) is empty of <s>vijñāna</s>. The eye is empty of the eye; [likewise the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are each empty of themselves; form, sound, smell, taste, tangible, and dharma are each empty of themselves;] [likewise eye-consciousness through mind-consciousness are each empty of themselves; feeling conditioned by eye-contact through feeling conditioned by mind-contact are each empty of themselves; the <s>dānapāramitā</s> through <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> are each empty of themselves; <s>adhyātmaśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of the internal) through <s>parabhāvaśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of other-nature) — each of the twenty kinds of emptiness is empty of itself; the thirty-seven <s>bodhipakṣadharmas</s> (factors of awakening) are empty of themselves;] [likewise the ten <s>Tathāgata</s> powers, the eighteen distinctive <s>Buddha</s>-qualities are empty of themselves; the <s>bodhisattva</s> is empty of the <s>bodhisattva</s>.] The armor of the <s>Mahāyāna</s> too, <s>Bhagavan</s>, is empty of the armor of the <s>Mahāyāna</s>. By this method, <s>Bhagavan</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s> should be understood as one who has not put on armor. When this was said, the <s>Bhagavan</s> said to venerable <s>Subhūti</s>: So it is, <s>Subhūti</s>, as you say. Why is that? For indeed, <s>Subhūti</s>, the knowledge of all aspects is unmade, unaltered, and unconditioned. Those beings too are unmade, unaltered, and unconditioned, for whose sake the great armor has been put on by the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s>. <s>Subhūti</s> said: For what reason, <s>Bhagavan</s>, is the knowledge of all aspects unmade, unaltered, and unconditioned? And those beings too unmade, unaltered, and unconditioned, for whose sake the great armor has been put on by the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s>? The <s>Bhagavan</s> said: Based on the non-apprehension of a doer, <s>Subhūti</s>, the knowledge of all aspects is unmade, unaltered, and unconditioned. Those beings too are unmade, unaltered, and unconditioned. Why is that? For indeed, <s>Subhūti</s>, <s>rūpa</s> (form) does not make, does not alter, does not condition. [Likewise <s>vedanā</s>, <s>saṃjñā</s>, <s>saṃskāras</s>, <s>vijñāna</s>; the eye, ear, nose, tongue, body, mind do not make, do not alter, do not condition.] [Likewise form, sound, smell, taste, tangible, <s>dharma</s>; eye-consciousness through mind-consciousness; feeling conditioned by eye-contact through feeling conditioned by mind-contact — none of these make, alter, or condition.] Feeling conditioned by mental contact does not make, does not alter, does not condition. Why is that? For in an ultimate sense, they do not exist and are not apprehended. A dream, <s>Subhūti</s>, does not make, does not alter, does not condition. An echo, a reflection, a mirror-image, a mirage, and an apparition do not make, do not alter, do not condition. Why is that? For in an ultimate sense, they do not exist and are not apprehended. For in an ultimate sense, they do not exist and are not apprehended.] The thirty-seven <s>bodhipakṣadharmas</s> (factors of awakening), the ten <s>Tathāgata</s> powers, the four confidences, the four analytical knowledges, the eighteen distinctive <s>Buddha</s>-qualities, <s>tathatā</s> (suchness), [the element of space, the ultimate point, the inconceivable element, awakening,] and the knowledge of all aspects, <s>Subhūti</s>, do not make, do not alter, do not condition. Why is that? For in an ultimate sense, they do not exist and are not apprehended. By this method, <s>Subhūti</s>, the knowledge of all aspects is unmade, unaltered, and unconditioned. Those beings too, for whose sake the great armor has been put on by the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s>, are unmade, unaltered, and unconditioned. Thus indeed, <s>Subhūti</s>, is the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> said to be one who has put on the great armor. Present <s>vedanā</s> (feeling) [is neither bound nor released; present <s>saṃjñā</s> is neither bound nor released; present <s>saṃskāras</s> are neither bound nor released; present <s>vijñāna</s> is neither bound nor released.] Why is that? Because of the non-existence of <s>rūpa</s>, venerable <s>Pūrṇa</s>, thus that <s>rūpa</s> is neither bound nor released. Because of the non-existence of <s>vedanā</s>, <s>saṃjñā</s>, and <s>saṃskāras</s>, venerable <s>Pūrṇa</s> — because of the non-existence of <s>vijñāna</s>, thus that <s>vijñāna</s> is neither bound nor released. Likewise, because of their being isolated, peaceful, empty, signless, wishless, unconditioned, and unproduced — wholesome, unwholesome, defiled, undefiled, blameworthy, blameless, with outflows, without outflows, worldly, supramundane, afflicted, and purified — venerable <s>Pūrṇa</s>, <s>rūpa</s> is neither bound nor released. Why is that? Because of the non-existence of <s>rūpa</s>, thus that <s>rūpa</s> is neither bound nor released. <s>Vedanā</s>, <s>saṃjñā</s>, <s>saṃskāras</s> — afflicted and purified, venerable <s>Pūrṇa</s>, <s>vijñāna</s> is neither bound nor released. Why is that? Because of the non-existence of <s>vijñāna</s>, thus that <s>vijñāna</s> is neither bound nor released. All <s>dharmas</s> too, venerable <s>Pūrṇa</s>, are neither bound nor released. Why is that? Because of their non-existence, they are neither bound nor released. Likewise, because of their being isolated, up to their being unproduced, they are neither bound nor released. [Likewise, <s>adhyātmaśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of the internal) through <s>parabhāvaśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of other-nature) — each of the twenty kinds of emptiness is neither bound nor released, because of non-existence, and because of being isolated up to unproduced.] [Likewise the thirty-seven <s>bodhipakṣadharmas</s> (factors of awakening) are neither bound nor released, because of non-existence, and because of being isolated up to unproduced.] Likewise the ten powers, the four confidences, up to the eighteen distinctive <s>Buddha</s>-qualities, the knowledge of all aspects, <s>tathatā</s> (suchness), [the <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of dharmas),] and the ultimate point. Thus indeed, venerable <s>Pūrṇa</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> is neither bound nor released. Likewise the six <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections) are neither bound nor released. Up to the knowledge of all aspects too is neither bound nor released. The beings whom he will bring to <s>nirvāṇa</s> — they too are neither bound nor released. The <s>Buddha</s>-fields that he will purify — they too are neither bound nor released. The <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bhagavans</s> whom he will attend upon — they too are neither bound nor released. The <s>Dharma</s> that he will hear — that too is neither bound nor released. He will never be separated from the <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bhagavans</s> — neither bound nor released. He will not be separated from the <s>abhijñās</s> (superknowledges) — neither bound nor released. He will not be separated from the five eyes — neither bound nor released. Likewise he will not be separated from other <s>samādhis</s> — neither bound nor released. He will produce the knowledge of the path in all its aspects, which is neither bound nor released. He will realize the knowledge of all aspects, which is neither bound nor released. He will turn the <s>Dharmacakra</s> (wheel of Dharma), which is neither bound nor released. He will bring beings to <s>nirvāṇa</s> by the three vehicles — neither bound nor released — being himself neither bound nor released. [Thus the accumulation of the paired path.] Then venerable <s>Subhūti</s> said to the <s>Bhagavan</s>: What, <s>Bhagavan</s>, is the <s>Mahāyāna</s> (Great Vehicle) of the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s>? How, <s>Bhagavan</s>, should one understand the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> who has set out in the <s>Mahāyāna</s>? From where will that vehicle go forth? Where will that vehicle stand? And who will go forth by that vehicle? When this was said, the <s>Bhagavan</s> said to venerable <s>Subhūti</s>: As to your question, <s>Subhūti</s>, "What is the <s>Mahāyāna</s> of the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s>?" — the six <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections), <s>Subhūti</s>, are the <s>Mahāyāna</s> of the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s>. What are the six <s>pāramitās</s>? <s>Dānapāramitā</s> (perfection of giving), <s>śīlapāramitā</s> (perfection of morality), <s>kṣāntipāramitā</s> (perfection of patience), <s>vīryapāramitā</s> (perfection of vigor), <s>dhyānapāramitā</s> (perfection of meditation), and <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> (perfection of wisdom). <s>Subhūti</s> said: What, <s>Bhagavan</s>, is the <s>dānapāramitā</s> of the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s>? The <s>Bhagavan</s> said: Here, <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s>, with mental productions connected with the knowledge of all aspects, gives gifts — that is, both inner and outer possessions — and making them common to all beings, dedicates them to unsurpassed perfect awakening, and encourages others therein through the method of non-apprehension. This, <s>Subhūti</s>, is the <s>dānapāramitā</s> of the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s>. <s>Subhūti</s> said: What, <s>Bhagavan</s>, is the <s>śīlapāramitā</s> of the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s>? The <s>Bhagavan</s> said: Here, <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s>, with mental productions connected with the knowledge of all aspects, himself undertakes and practices the ten wholesome courses of action, and encourages others in the ten wholesome courses of action through the method of non-apprehension. This, <s>Subhūti</s>, is the unattached <s>śīlapāramitā</s> of the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s>. <s>Subhūti</s> said: What, <s>Bhagavan</s>, is the <s>kṣāntipāramitā</s> of the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s>? The <s>Bhagavan</s> said: Here, <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s>, with mental productions connected with the knowledge of all aspects, is himself endowed with patience, and encourages others in patience through the method of non-apprehension. This, <s>Subhūti</s>, is the <s>kṣāntipāramitā</s> of the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s>. <s>Subhūti</s> said: What, <s>Bhagavan</s>, is the <s>vīryapāramitā</s> of the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s>? The <s>Bhagavan</s> said: Here, <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s>, with mental productions connected with the knowledge of all aspects, dwells without abandoning his duty in the five <s>pāramitās</s>, and encourages others in those five <s>pāramitās</s> through the method of non-apprehension. This, <s>Subhūti</s>, is the <s>vīryapāramitā</s> of the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s>. <s>Subhūti</s> said: What, <s>Bhagavan</s>, is the <s>dhyānapāramitā</s> of the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s>? The <s>Bhagavan</s> said: Here, <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s>, with mental productions connected with the knowledge of all aspects, himself enters the <s>dhyānas</s> (meditations) through skillful means, yet is not reborn through their power, and encourages others in the <s>dhyānas</s> through the method of non-apprehension. This, <s>Subhūti</s>, is the <s>dhyānapāramitā</s> of the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s>. <s>Subhūti</s> said: What, <s>Bhagavan</s>, is the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> of the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s>? The <s>Bhagavan</s> said: Here, <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s>, with mental productions connected with the knowledge of all aspects, penetrates all <s>dharmas</s> and examines the nature of all <s>dharmas</s>, and encourages beings in the examination of the nature of all <s>dharmas</s> through the method of non-apprehension. This, <s>Subhūti</s>, is the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> of the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s>. This, <s>Subhūti</s>, is the <s>Mahāyāna</s> of the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s>. [Thus the accumulation of skillful means.] Furthermore, <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>Mahāyāna</s> of the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> consists of <s>adhyātmaśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of the internal), [<s>bahirdhāśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of the external), <s>adhyātmabahirdhāśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of both internal and external), <s>śūnyatāśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of emptiness), <s>mahāśūnyatā</s> (great emptiness), <s>paramārthaśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of the ultimate), <s>saṃskṛtaśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of the conditioned), <s>atyantaśūnyatā</s> (absolute emptiness), <s>anavarāgraśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of beginninglessness), <s>anavakāraśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of non-rejection), <s>prakṛtiśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of nature), <s>sarvadharmaśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of all dharmas), <s>svalakṣaṇaśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of own-characteristics), <s>anupalambhaśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of non-apprehension), <s>abhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of the non-existence of inherent nature), <s>bhāvaśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of existence), <s>abhāvaśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of non-existence), <s>svabhāvaśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of own-nature),] and <s>parabhāvaśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of other-nature). The eye, ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind, being internal, are empty of form, sound, smell, taste, touch, and mental objects, without implying an immutable or destructible state. What is the reason? This is their intrinsic nature.
Therein, what are the external <s>dharmas</s> (phenomena) that are empty of internal <s>dharmas</s>? Form, sound, smell, taste, touch,
and mental objects are empty of the eye, ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind, without implying an immutable or destructible state. What is the reason? This is their intrinsic nature. This is called the emptiness of the internal and external (<s>adhyātmabahirdhāśūnyatā</s>).
What then is the emptiness of emptiness (<s>śūnyatāśūnyatā</s>)? The emptiness of all <s>dharmas</s>—that emptiness is itself empty,
without implying an immutable or destructible state. What is the reason? This is its intrinsic nature. This is called the emptiness of emptiness.
What then is great emptiness (<s>mahāśūnyatā</s>)? The eastern direction is empty of the eastern direction; likewise the southern, western,
northern, northeastern, southeastern, southwestern, northwestern, and lower directions; the upper direction is empty of the upper direction, without implying an immutable or destructible state. What is the reason? This is its intrinsic nature. This is called great emptiness.
What then is the emptiness of the ultimate (<s>paramārthaśūnyatā</s>)? The ultimate is called <s>Nirvāṇa</s>; and that <s>Nirvāṇa</s> is empty of <s>Nirvāṇa</s>,
without implying an immutable or destructible state. What is the reason? This is its intrinsic nature. This is called the emptiness of the ultimate.
What then is the emptiness of the conditioned (<s>saṃskṛtaśūnyatā</s>)? The conditioned is called the desire realm (<s>kāmadhātu</s>), the form realm (<s>rūpadhātu</s>), and the formless realm (<s>ārūpyadhātu</s>).
Therein, the desire realm is empty of the desire realm, without implying an immutable or destructible state. What is the reason? This is its intrinsic nature. The form realm is empty of the form realm, without implying an immutable or destructible state. What is the reason? This is its intrinsic nature.
The formless realm is empty of the formless realm, without implying an immutable or destructible state. What is the reason? This is its intrinsic nature. This is called the emptiness of the conditioned.
What then is the emptiness of the unconditioned (<s>asaṃskṛtaśūnyatā</s>)? The unconditioned is called that which has no arising, no cessation,
no abiding, and no alteration. This is called the unconditioned. The unconditioned is empty of the unconditioned,
without implying an immutable or destructible state. What is the reason? This is its intrinsic nature. This is called the emptiness of the unconditioned.
What then is the emptiness of the ultimate limit (<s>atyantaśūnyatā</s>)? That whose end is not apprehended—that ultimate limit is empty of the ultimate,
without implying an immutable or destructible state. What is the reason? This is its intrinsic nature. This is called the emptiness of the ultimate limit.
What then is the emptiness of what is without beginning or end (<s>anavarāgraśūnyatā</s>)? That of which neither the beginning nor the end is apprehended—of that there is no middle
state. That of which no beginning, no middle, and no end is apprehended—of that there is neither coming nor going. The beginning,

This non-apprehension of them is due to their primordial purity, without implying an immutable or destructible state. What is the reason? This is their intrinsic nature. This is called the emptiness of the unapprehendable.

empty, without implying an immutable or destructible state. What is the reason? This is its intrinsic nature. This is called the emptiness of non-existence.
What then is the emptiness of inherent nature (<s>svabhāvaśūnyatā</s>)? Inherent nature is intrinsic nature, non-inversion. That which is
its emptiness, without implying an immutable or destructible state. What is the reason? This is its intrinsic nature. That was not produced by knowledge or vision. What is the reason?
This is its intrinsic nature. This is called the emptiness of inherent nature.
What then is the emptiness of other-nature (<s>parabhāvaśūnyatā</s>)? Whether <s>Tathāgatas</s> arise or do not arise, this very
nature of <s>dharmas</s> abides—the <s>dharmatā</s> (true nature), the <s>dharmasthititā</s> (established nature of dharma), the <s>dharmaniyāmatā</s> (fixed order of dharma), the <s>bhūtakoṭi</s> (limit of reality). That which is its emptiness,
without implying an immutable or destructible state. What is the reason? This is its intrinsic nature. That was not produced by another. What is the reason? This is its intrinsic nature.
This is called the emptiness of other-nature. This, <s>Subhūti</s>, is called the great vehicle (<s>Mahāyāna</s>) of the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> (great being).

children.translated_text: The <s>samādhi</s> called <s>Akṣayākāra</s> (Inexhaustible Aspect) — abiding in this <s>samādhi</s>, he does not perceive the exhaustion of any <s>samādhis</s>; therefore it is called the <s>samādhi</s> named <s>Akṣayākāra</s>. What is the <s>samādhi</s> called <s>Dhāraṇīpratipatti</s> (Practice of Retention)? Abiding in this <s>samādhi</s>, he sustains all <s>samādhis</s>; therefore it is called the <s>samādhi</s> named <s>Dhāraṇīpratipatti</s>. What is the <s>samādhi</s> called <s>Sarvasamyaktvamithyātvasaṃgraha</s> (Encompassing All Rightness and Wrongness)? Abiding in this <s>samādhi</s>, he does not perceive rightness or wrongness in any <s>samādhis</s>; therefore it is called the <s>samādhi</s> named <s>Sarvasamyaktvamithyātvasaṃgraha</s>. What is the <s>samādhi</s> called <s>Sarvarodhanirodhapraśamana</s> (Pacification of All Obstruction and Cessation)? Abiding in this <s>samādhi</s>, he does not perceive obstruction or cessation in any <s>samādhis</s>; therefore it is called the <s>samādhi</s> named <s>Sarvarodhanirodhapraśamana</s>. What is the <s>samādhi</s> called <s>Anusārapratisāra</s> (Pursuit and Return)? Abiding in this <s>samādhi</s>, he does not perceive pursuit or return in any <s>samādhis</s>; therefore it is called the <s>samādhi</s> named <s>Anusārapratisāra</s>. What is the <s>samādhi</s> called <s>Vimalaprabha</s> (Stainless Radiance)? Abiding in this <s>samādhi</s>, the halo of radiance of all <s>samādhis</s> is not apprehended; therefore it is called the <s>samādhi</s> named <s>Vimalaprabha</s>. What is the <s>samādhi</s> called <s>Sāravatī</s> (Having Essence)? Abiding in this <s>samādhi</s>, the essencelessness of all <s>samādhis</s> is not apprehended; therefore it is called the <s>samādhi</s> named <s>Sāravatī</s>. What is the <s>samādhi</s> called <s>Paripūrṇacandravimala</s> (Stainless Full Moon)? Abiding in this <s>samādhi</s>, all his <s>samādhis</s> become complete, just as the moon on the full-moon night; therefore it is called the <s>samādhi</s> named <s>Paripūrṇacandravimala</s>. What is the <s>samādhi</s> called <s>Mahāvyūha</s> (Great Array)? Abiding in this <s>samādhi</s>, all his <s>samādhis</s> become endowed with the great array; therefore it is called the <s>samādhi</s> named <s>Mahāvyūha</s>. What is the <s>samādhi</s> called <s>Sarvākāraprabhākara</s> (Producing Radiance of All Aspects)? Abiding in this <s>samādhi</s>, he produces the radiance of all <s>samādhis</s> and all <s>dharmas</s>; therefore it is called the <s>samādhi</s> named <s>Sarvākāraprabhākara</s>. What is the <s>samādhi</s> called <s>Samādhisamatā</s> (Equality of Concentration)? Abiding in this <s>samādhi</s>, he does not perceive distraction or one-pointedness in any <s>samādhis</s>; therefore it is called the <s>samādhi</s> named <s>Samādhisamatā</s>. What is the <s>samādhi</s> called <s>Araṇasamavasaraṇa</s> (Conflict-free Resort)? Abiding in this <s>samādhi</s>, he attains the conflict-free, refuge-free, universal resort of all <s>samādhis</s>; therefore it is called the <s>samādhi</s> named <s>Araṇasamavasaraṇa</s>. What is the <s>samādhi</s> called <s>Anilāniketa</s> (Without Abode or Dwelling)? Abiding in this <s>samādhi</s>, he does not perceive any clinging in all <s>samādhis</s>; therefore it is called the <s>samādhi</s> named <s>Anilāniketa</s>. What is the <s>samādhi</s> called <s>Tathatāsthitaniścita</s> (Certainty Established in Suchness)? Abiding in this <s>samādhi</s>, he does not deviate from the <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) of all <s>samādhis</s>; therefore it is called the <s>samādhi</s> named <s>Tathatāsthitaniścita</s>. What is the <s>samādhi</s> called <s>Kāyakalisaṃpramathana</s> (Crushing Bodily Impurity)? Abiding in this <s>samādhi</s>, he does not apprehend the body of any <s>samādhis</s>; therefore it is called the <s>samādhi</s> named <s>Kāyakalisaṃpramathana</s>. What is the <s>samādhi</s> called <s>Vākkalividhvaṃsana</s> (Destroying Verbal Impurity)? Abiding in this <s>samādhi</s>, he does not apprehend the verbal action of any <s>samādhis</s>; therefore it is called the <s>samādhi</s> named <s>Vākkalividhvaṃsana</s>. What is the <s>samādhi</s> called <s>Gaganakalpa</s> (Like Space)? Abiding in this <s>samādhi</s>, he illuminates like space; therefore it is called the <s>samādhi</s> named <s>Gaganakalpa</s>. What is the <s>samādhi</s> called <s>Ākāśāsaṅgavimuktinirupalepa</s> (Space-unattached Liberation Without Stain)? Abiding in this <s>samādhi</s>, he attains the space-unattached, liberated, unstained nature of all <s>dharmas</s>; therefore it is called the <s>samādhi</s> named <s>Ākāśāsaṅgavimuktinirupalepa</s>. This, <s>Subhūti</s>, is the great vehicle of the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> practicing <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. [Thus ends the accumulation of merit.] Furthermore, <s>Subhūti</s>, the great vehicle of the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> consists of the four foundations of mindfulness. What are the four? Mindfulness of the body, mindfulness of feelings, mindfulness of mind, and mindfulness of <s>dharmas</s>.

He dwells observing the body in both the internal and external body, yet does not entertain thoughts accompanied by the body, and this through the method of non-apprehension — ardent, clearly comprehending, and mindful, having removed longing and dejection regarding the world. having seen [a corpse] bound with sinews, he applies this to his own body: 'This body too is of such a nature, of such a character, has not gone beyond this natural condition.' Thus, <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> dwells contemplating the body in the external body, ardent, clearly comprehending, mindful, having removed covetousness and grief with regard to the world. Furthermore, <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, when he sees in a charnel ground a skeleton detached from its joints and bonds, disjointed, its bones scattered in various places on the ground — he applies this to his own body: 'This body too is of such a nature, of such a character, has not gone beyond this natural condition.' Thus the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> dwells contemplating the body in the external body, ardent, clearly comprehending, mindful. Furthermore, <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, when he sees in a charnel ground bones scattered in various directions — foot-bones in one place, shin-bones in another, thigh-bones in another, hip-bones in another, spine-bones in another, rib-bones in another, neck-bones in another, arm-bones in another, skull-bones in another — he applies this to his own body: 'This body too is of such a nature, of such a character, has not gone beyond this natural condition.' Furthermore, <s>Subhūti</s>, when the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> sees in a charnel ground bones many years old, hundreds of years old, weathered by wind and sun, white, conch-like — he applies this to his own body in the same manner. Furthermore, <s>Subhūti</s>, when the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> sees in a charnel ground bones more than a year old, bluish, pigeon-colored, putrid, crumbling into dust, he applies this to his own body: 'This body too is of such a nature.' Thus the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> dwells contemplating the body in the external body, ardent, clearly comprehending, mindful, having removed covetousness and grief. And all this through the method of non-apprehension (<s>anupalambhayoga</s>). This too, <s>Subhūti</s>, is the <s>Mahāyāna</s> (Great Vehicle) of the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>.
Furthermore, <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>Mahāyāna</s> of the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> comprises the four <s>samyakprahāṇas</s> (right efforts). What are the four? Here, <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> generates zeal for the non-arising of unwholesome <s>dharmas</s> that have not yet arisen — he makes effort, arouses his mind, and strives rightly. He generates zeal for the abandonment of unwholesome <s>dharmas</s> that have already arisen. He generates zeal for the arising of wholesome <s>dharmas</s> that have not yet arisen. He generates zeal for the maintenance, increase, non-loss, and non-decline of wholesome <s>dharmas</s> that have already arisen — he makes effort, arouses his mind, and strives rightly. And all this through the method of non-apprehension. This too, <s>Subhūti</s>, is the <s>Mahāyāna</s> of the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>.
Furthermore, <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>Mahāyāna</s> of the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> comprises the four <s>ṛddhipādas</s> (bases of supernatural power). What are the four? Here, <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> cultivates the <s>ṛddhipāda</s> endowed with <s>samādhi</s> (concentration) born of <s>chanda</s> (aspiration), together with the abandonment-formations — based on seclusion, based on dispassion, based on cessation, directed toward relinquishment. Likewise the <s>samādhi</s> born of <s>vīrya</s> (vigor), the <s>samādhi</s> born of <s>citta</s> (mind), and the <s>samādhi</s> born of <s>mīmāṃsā</s> (investigation), together with the abandonment-formations — cultivated based on seclusion, dispassion, cessation, and directed toward relinquishment.

This too, <s>Subhūti</s>, is the great vehicle (<s>mahāyāna</s>) of a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>. Furthermore, <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>mahāyāna</s> of a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> consists of the five <s>indriyas</s> (faculties). Which five? The faculty of faith (<s>śraddhendriya</s>), the faculty of vigor (<s>vīryendriya</s>), the faculty of mindfulness (<s>smṛtīndriya</s>), the faculty of concentration (<s>samādhīndriya</s>), and the faculty of wisdom (<s>prajñendriya</s>) — and that through the method of non-apprehension. This too, <s>Subhūti</s>, is the <s>mahāyāna</s> of a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>. Furthermore, <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>mahāyāna</s> of a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> consists of the five <s>balas</s> (powers). Which five? The power of faith (<s>śraddhābala</s>), the power of vigor (<s>vīryabala</s>), the power of mindfulness (<s>smṛtibala</s>), the power of concentration (<s>samādhibala</s>), and the power of wisdom (<s>prajñābala</s>) — and that through the method of non-apprehension. This too, <s>Subhūti</s>, is the <s>mahāyāna</s> of a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>. Furthermore, <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>mahāyāna</s> of a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> consists of the seven <s>bodhyaṅgas</s> (limbs of awakening). Which seven? The awakening-factor of mindfulness (<s>smṛtisaṃbodhyaṅga</s>), the awakening-factor of investigation of <s>dharmas</s> (<s>dharmapravicayasaṃbodhyaṅga</s>), the awakening-factor of vigor (<s>vīryasaṃbodhyaṅga</s>), the awakening-factor of joy (<s>prītisaṃbodhyaṅga</s>), the awakening-factor of tranquility (<s>prasrabdhisaṃbodhyaṅga</s>), the awakening-factor of concentration (<s>samādhisaṃbodhyaṅga</s>), and the awakening-factor of equanimity (<s>upekṣāsaṃbodhyaṅga</s>). Among these, what is the awakening-factor of mindfulness, up to the awakening-factor of equanimity? Here, <s>Subhūti</s>, a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> practicing <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> cultivates the awakening-factor of mindfulness, up to the awakening-factor of equanimity, based on seclusion, based on dispassion, based on cessation, comprehended through relinquishment — and that through the method of non-apprehension. This too, <s>Subhūti</s>, is the <s>mahāyāna</s> of a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>. Furthermore, <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>mahāyāna</s> of a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> is the Noble Eightfold Path (<s>āryāṣṭāṅgamārga</s>). What is the Noble Eightfold Path? Right view (<s>samyagdṛṣṭi</s>), right intention (<s>samyaksaṃkalpa</s>), right action (<s>samyakkarmānta</s>), right livelihood (<s>samyagājīva</s>), right effort (<s>samyagvyāyāma</s>), right mindfulness (<s>samyaksmṛti</s>), and right concentration (<s>samyaksamādhi</s>) — and that through the method of non-apprehension. This too, <s>Subhūti</s>, is the <s>mahāyāna</s> of a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>. Furthermore, <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>mahāyāna</s> of a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> consists of the three <s>samādhis</s> (concentrations). Which three concentrations? <s>Śūnyatā</s> (emptiness), <s>animitta</s> (the signless), and <s>apraṇihita</s> (the wishless). Among these, what is the <s>śūnyatāsamādhi</s> (concentration on emptiness)? The abiding of mind when contemplating all <s>dharmas</s> as empty by their own characteristics — this gateway of liberation (<s>vimokṣamukha</s>) of emptiness is called the <s>śūnyatāsamādhi</s>. The abiding of mind when contemplating all <s>dharmas</s> as signless — this gateway of liberation of the signless is called the <s>animittasamādhi</s>. The abiding of mind when contemplating all <s>dharmas</s> as wishless — this gateway of liberation of the wishless is called the <s>apraṇihitasamādhi</s>. These are the three gateways of liberation, the three concentrations. This too, <s>Subhūti</s>, is the <s>mahāyāna</s> of a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>. One should train in these three gateways of liberation. children.translated_text: and the knowledge of things as they are expressed (<s>yathārutajñāna</s>). Among these, what is the knowledge of suffering? The knowledge of the non-arising of suffering — this is the knowledge of suffering. What is the knowledge of origination? The knowledge of the abandonment of origination. What is the knowledge of cessation? The knowledge of the cessation of suffering. What is the knowledge of the path? The knowledge of directly realizing cessation. What is the knowledge of destruction? The knowledge of the destruction of passion, aversion, and delusion. What is the knowledge of non-arising? The knowledge of non-arising in non-arising. What is the knowledge of <s>dharmas</s>? The knowledge of the cutting off of the <s>dharma</s> of the five <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates). What is the knowledge of subsequent cognition? The eye is impermanent, the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind are impermanent — thus knowledge concerning the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), <s>dhātus</s> (elements), <s>āyatanas</s> (sense-bases), and <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination), both individually and collectively. What is the knowledge of convention? The knowledge of the minds of other beings and other persons through the mind alone. What is the knowledge of proficiency? The knowledge of proficiency in practice. What is the knowledge of things as they are expressed? That is the <s>Tathāgata's</s> knowledge of <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> (knowledge of all aspects) — and that through the method of non-apprehension. This too, <s>Subhūti</s>, is the <s>mahāyāna</s> of a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>. Furthermore, <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>mahāyāna</s> of a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> consists of the three <s>indriyas</s> (faculties). Which three? The faculty of 'I shall come to know the unknown' (<s>anājñātam ājñāsyāmīndriya</s>), the faculty of perfect knowledge (<s>ājñendriya</s>), and the faculty of one who has perfectly known (<s>ājñātāvīndriya</s>). Among these, what is the faculty of 'I shall come to know the unknown'? The faith-faculty, vigor-faculty, mindfulness-faculty, concentration-faculty, and wisdom-faculty of those <s>śaikṣa</s> (learner) persons who have not yet realized, who have not yet illuminated, who have not yet disciplined — this is called the faculty of 'I shall come to know the unknown.' What is the faculty of perfect knowledge? The faith-faculty, vigor-faculty, mindfulness-faculty, concentration-faculty, and wisdom-faculty of those <s>śaikṣa</s> persons who have realized — this is called the faculty of perfect knowledge. What is the faculty of one who has perfectly known? The faith-faculty, vigor-faculty, mindfulness-faculty, concentration-faculty, and wisdom-faculty of those <s>aśaikṣa</s> (beyond-learning) persons — <s>Arhats</s>, <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, and <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, perfectly and fully awakened ones — this is called the faculty of one who has perfectly known. This too, <s>Subhūti</s>, is the <s>mahāyāna</s> of a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, through the method of non-apprehension. Furthermore, <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>mahāyāna</s> of a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> consists of: the concentration with applied and sustained thought (<s>savitarka savicāra samādhi</s>), and the concentration without applied thought but with a measure of sustained thought (<s>avitarko vicāramātra samādhi</s>). Among these, what is the concentration with applied and sustained thought? Here, <s>Subhūti</s>, a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, secluded from sense-desires, secluded from unwholesome, unskillful <s>dharmas</s>, enters and abides in the first <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), which is accompanied by applied and sustained thought, born of seclusion, and filled with joy and happiness. children.translated_text: What is the <s>samādhi</s> without applied thought and with only sustained thought (<s>avitarka avicāramātra</s>)? That which is intermediate between the first <s>dhyāna</s> and the second <s>dhyāna</s> — this is called the <s>samādhi</s> without applied thought and with only sustained thought. Therein, what is the <s>samādhi</s> without applied thought and without sustained thought (<s>avitarka avicāra</s>)? Starting from the second <s>dhyāna</s>, to be elaborated in full, up to the attainment of the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception (<s>naivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatana</s>) — this is called the <s>samādhi</s> without applied thought and without sustained thought. This too, <s>Subhūti</s>, is the great vehicle (<s>mahāyāna</s>) of the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, through the practice of non-apprehension (<s>anupalambhayoga</s>). Furthermore, <s>Subhūti</s>, the great vehicle of the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> is the ten recollections (<s>anusmṛti</s>). Which ten? Namely: recollection of the <s>Buddha</s> (<s>buddhānusmṛti</s>), recollection of the <s>Dharma</s> (<s>dharmānusmṛti</s>), recollection of the <s>Saṃgha</s> (<s>saṃghānusmṛti</s>), recollection of morality (<s>śīlānusmṛti</s>), recollection of generosity (<s>tyāgānusmṛti</s>), recollection of the gods (<s>devatānusmṛti</s>), recollection of going upward (<s>ūrdhvagānusmṛti</s>), recollection of death (<s>maraṇānusmṛti</s>), recollection of the body (<s>kāyānusmṛti</s>), and recollection of breathing in and out (<s>ānāpānānusmṛti</s>). This too, <s>Subhūti</s>, is the great vehicle of the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, through the practice of non-apprehension. Furthermore, <s>Subhūti</s>, the great vehicle of the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> is the four <s>dhyānas</s>, the four immeasurables (<s>apramāṇa</s>), the four formless attainments (<s>ārūpyasamāpatti</s>), the eight liberations (<s>vimokṣa</s>), and the nine successive abiding attainments (<s>anupūrvavihārasamāpatti</s>). This too, <s>Subhūti</s>, is the great vehicle of the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>. Furthermore, <s>Subhūti</s>, the great vehicle of the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> is the ten powers of the <s>Tathāgata</s> (<s>tathāgatabala</s>). Which ten? Here the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> knows as it truly is what is possible as possible and what is impossible as impossible. He knows as it truly is the results of actions and undertakings of actions in the past, future, and present, their locations and causes. He knows as it truly is the manifold elements (<s>nānādhātuka</s>). He knows as it truly is the diverse inclinations (<s>nānādhimuktikatā</s>) of other beings and persons. He knows as it truly is the superior and inferior faculties (<s>indriyaparāparajñānatā</s>) of other beings and persons. He knows as it truly is the path leading everywhere (<s>sarvatragāminī pratipad</s>). He knows as it truly is the defilement, purification, and emergence from <s>dhyāna</s>, liberation, <s>samādhi</s>, and attainments of other beings and persons. He recollects manifold former abodes (<s>pūrvanivāsa</s>). He knows as it truly is, with the divine eye, the passing away and rebirth of beings. Through the destruction of the outflows (<s>āsrava</s>), he realizes by direct knowledge in this very life the outflow-free liberation of mind (<s>cetovimukti</s>) and liberation by wisdom (<s>prajñāvimukti</s>), attaining and abiding in it: 'Birth is exhausted, the holy life has been lived, what had to be done has been done, there is no further existence beyond this' — he knows as it truly is. This too, <s>Subhūti</s>, is the great vehicle of the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, through the practice of non-apprehension.
