children.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Subhūti</s>, the great vehicle (<s>mahāyāna</s>) of the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> is the four confidences (<s>vaiśāradya</s>). Which four? Namely: 'When I, the perfectly enlightened one, declare: "These <s>dharmas</s> have been fully awakened to" — if anyone, whether an ascetic or a god or <s>Māra</s> or <s>Brahmā</s> or anyone else in the world, were to challenge me in accordance with the <s>Dharma</s> — I do not see that basis. Not seeing that basis, I abide having attained security, having attained fearlessness. I know the bull's station, I roar the lion's roar rightly in the assembly, and I turn the <s>Brahma</s>-wheel that has not been turned by any ascetic, <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, god, <s>Māra</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, or anyone else in the world in accordance with the <s>Dharma</s>.' 'When I, whose outflows are destroyed, declare: "These outflows are not yet destroyed" — that basis does not exist. If anyone, whether an ascetic or a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>... [abbreviated]... up to: I turn the <s>Brahma</s>-wheel in accordance with the <s>Dharma</s>.' 'As for those <s>dharmas</s> that I have declared to be obstructive — for one who practices them, they would not suffice as an obstruction — that basis does not exist. If anyone, whether an ascetic or a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>... [abbreviated]... up to: in accordance with the <s>Dharma</s>.' 'The path that I have declared to be noble, leading to liberation — for one who practices it, he would not go forth to the complete destruction of suffering — that basis does not exist. If anyone, whether an ascetic or a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>... [abbreviated]... up to: in accordance with the <s>Dharma</s>.' These are the four confidences. This too, <s>Subhūti</s>, is the great vehicle of the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, through the practice of non-apprehension (<s>anupalambhayoga</s>). Furthermore, <s>Subhūti</s>, the great vehicle of the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> is the four analytical knowledges (<s>pratisaṃvid</s>). Which four? The analytical knowledge of <s>dharmas</s> (<s>dharmapratisaṃvid</s>), the analytical knowledge of meaning (<s>arthapratisaṃvid</s>), the analytical knowledge of etymology (<s>niruktipratisaṃvid</s>), and the analytical knowledge of eloquence (<s>pratibhānapratisaṃvid</s>). This too, <s>Subhūti</s>, is the great vehicle of the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, through the practice of non-apprehension. Furthermore, <s>Subhūti</s>, the great vehicle of the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> is the eighteen unique <s>Buddha</s>-dharmas (<s>āveṇikabuddhadharma</s>). Which eighteen? <s>Subhūti</s>, from the night on which the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, fully awoke to <s>samyaksaṃbodhi</s>, up to the night on which he will enter <s>parinirvāṇa</s> — in this interval, <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> has no stumbling, has no falling, has no lapse of mindfulness, has no perception of diversity, has no mind that is not in <s>samādhi</s>, has no

there is no decline in analytic contemplation and equanimity, no decline in zeal, no decline in vigor, no decline in mindfulness, no decline in <s>samādhi</s> (concentration), no decline in <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom), no decline in liberation. All bodily actions are preceded by knowledge and follow knowledge. All verbal actions are preceded by knowledge and follow knowledge. All mental actions are preceded by knowledge and follow knowledge. In the past period, there is unobstructed, unattached knowledge and vision. In the future period, there is unobstructed, unattached knowledge and vision. In the present period, there is unobstructed, unattached knowledge and vision. These are the eighteen <s>āveṇika-buddhadharmas</s> (unique qualities of a Buddha). This too, <s>Subhūti</s>, is the <s>Mahāyāna</s> of a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>—through the method of non-apprehension. [Thus the accumulation of the path.]
Furthermore, <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>Mahāyāna</s> of a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> includes the <s>dhāraṇī</s>-gates—namely the entry into syllables through the equality of the syllable-method and the syllable-gate. What is this equality of the syllable-method, the syllable-gate, the syllable-entry? The syllable 'a' is a gate, because all <s>dharmas</s> are primordially unarisen (<s>ādyanutpannatvāt</s>). The syllable 'ra' is a gate, because all <s>dharmas</s> are free from impurity (<s>rajoapagatatvāt</s>). The syllable 'pa' is a gate, because all <s>dharmas</s> are taught in the ultimate sense (<s>paramārthanirdeśāt</s>). The syllable 'ca' is a gate, because death and rebirth of all <s>dharmas</s> are not apprehended (<s>cyavanopapattyanupalabdhitvāt</s>). The syllable 'na' is a gate, because names have departed from all <s>dharmas</s>. The syllable 'la' is a gate, because all <s>dharmas</s> transcend the world and the creeping vine of craving with its causes and conditions has been uprooted. The syllable 'da' is a gate, because all <s>dharmas</s> are determined as tamed and subdued. The syllable 'ba' is a gate, because all <s>dharmas</s> are freed from bondage. The syllable 'ḍa' is a gate, because all <s>dharmas</s> are free from tumult. The syllable 'sa' is a gate, because attachment is not apprehended in all <s>dharmas</s>. The syllable 'va' is a gate, because the sound of the path of speech is cut off in all <s>dharmas</s>. The syllable 'ta' is a gate, because the <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) of all <s>dharmas</s> is immovable. The syllable 'ya' is a gate, because all <s>dharmas</s> are truly unarisen. The syllable 'sta' is a gate, because rigidity is not apprehended in all <s>dharmas</s>. The syllable 'ka' is a gate, because an agent is not apprehended in all <s>dharmas</s>. The syllable 'sa' is a gate, because equality is not apprehended in all <s>dharmas</s>. The syllable 'ma' is a gate, because possessiveness is not apprehended in all <s>dharmas</s>. children.translated_text:
the syllable 'jña' is a gate to all <s>dharmas</s>, because omniscient knowledge is not apprehended. The syllable 'ha' is a gate, because a cause is not apprehended. The syllable 'ccha' is a gate, because even a cover is not apprehended. The syllable 'sma' is a gate, because remembrance is not apprehended. The syllable 'ddha' is a gate, because distance has departed. The syllable 'sa' is a gate to all <s>dharmas</s>, because enthusiasm is not apprehended. The syllable 'gha' is a gate, because solidity is not apprehended. The syllable 'ṭha' is a gate, because deception is not apprehended. The syllable 'ṇa' is a gate, because strife has departed. The syllable 'pha' is a gate, because fruit is not apprehended. The syllable 'ska' is a gate, because the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates) are not apprehended. The syllable 'ja' is a gate, because aging is not apprehended. The syllable 'ca' is a gate, because conduct is not apprehended. The syllable 'ṭa' is a gate, because the sound of striking is not apprehended. The syllable 'ḍha' is a gate, because the sound of beating is not apprehended.
There is no further syllabic convention beyond this. For what reason? Because there is no name whatsoever by which one might converse, speak, point out, characterize, or perceive. Just as, <s>Subhūti</s>, space [is without naming], even so should all <s>dharmas</s> be understood. This, <s>Subhūti</s>, is the <s>dhāraṇī</s>-entry, the entry through the teaching of syllables beginning with 'a.' Whatever <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, <s>Subhūti</s>, will know this entry into the skill of syllables beginning with 'a,' that one will not be obstructed by any utterance. He will settle everything according to <s>dharmatā</s> (the nature of reality) and will attain the skill of knowledge of utterances. And whatever <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, <s>Subhūti</s>, will hear this syllable-seal beginning with 'a,' and having heard it, will grasp, retain, recite, and teach it to others, delighting [them] with that continuum—twenty benefits are to be expected for him. What are the twenty? He will be endowed with mindfulness, with understanding, with discernment, with steadfastness, with modesty, with <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom), with ready wit, and will be skilled in truth. He will easily attain this <s>dhāraṇī</s>-gate, and will not be a doubter. He will have no uncertainty. He will not be swayed by others upon hearing smooth speech. He will not be struck down by harsh speech. He will be neither elated nor dejected. He will remain just as established. He will be skilled in utterances, skilled in the <s>skandhas</s>, skilled in the <s>dhātus</s>, skilled in the <s>āyatanas</s>, skilled in the truths, skilled in <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination), skilled in causes, skilled in conditions, skilled in <s>dharmas</s>, and complete in faculties.

children.translated_text:
21401 ...knowledge [of others' minds], he will be skilled in the knowledge of others' minds, skilled in the knowledge of miraculous powers, skilled in the knowledge of the divine ear, skilled in the knowledge of the recollection of
21402 previous lives, skilled in the knowledge of death and rebirth, skilled in the knowledge of the destruction of outflows, skilled in the exposition of
21403 what is possible and impossible, skilled in transcendence, skilled in deportment. He will attain these benefits.
21404 This too, <s>Subhūti</s>, is the <s>dhāraṇīmukha</s> (gateway of retention), the gateway of syllables, the gateway of the letter 'a,' of a <s>bodhisattva-mahāsattva</s>'s
21405 Great Vehicle. [Thus the accumulation of <s>dhāraṇīs</s>.]
21406 And as <s>Subhūti</s> said: 'How does a <s>bodhisattva-mahāsattva</s> set forth on the Great Vehicle?' —
21407 here, <s>Subhūti</s>, a <s>bodhisattva-mahāsattva</s>, practicing the six <s>pāramitās</s>, progresses from stage to stage
21408 (<s>bhūmi</s> to <s>bhūmi</s>). And how, <s>Subhūti</s>, does a <s>bodhisattva-mahāsattva</s> progress from stage to stage? Through the
21409 non-progression of all <s>dharmas</s>. For what reason? For there is no <s>dharma</s> whatsoever that comes
21410 or goes or progresses or approaches. Rather, he does not conceive of the stages of <s>dharmas</s>,
21411 does not think about them, yet performs the preparatory practices for the stages without perceiving the stage.
21412 And what are the preparatory practices of a <s>bodhisattva-mahāsattva</s>'s stages? A <s>bodhisattva-mahāsattva</s> abiding on the first stage
21413 should perform ten stage-preparations. What ten? The preparation of
21414 aspiration — through the method of non-apprehension. The preparation of beneficial action — based on the non-apprehension of signs.
21415 The preparation of equanimity toward all beings — based on the non-apprehension of beings. The preparation of renunciation — based on the non-apprehension of giver, gift, and
21416 recipient. The preparation of attending on spiritual friends — based on not tormenting them. The preparation of
21417 seeking the true <s>Dharma</s> — based on the non-apprehension of all <s>dharmas</s>. The preparation of constant renunciation of household life — based on the non-apprehension of the household. The preparation of yearning for the <s>Buddha</s>-body —
21418 based on the non-apprehension of the signs of the marks and minor marks. The preparation of explaining the <s>Dharma</s> — based on the non-apprehension of divisions of <s>dharmas</s>. The preparation of truthful speech —
21419 based on the non-apprehension of speech. These, <s>Subhūti</s>, are the ten preparations of a <s>bodhisattva-mahāsattva</s>'s first stage, which
21420 a <s>bodhisattva-mahāsattva</s> abiding on the first stage should perform.

children.translated_text:
21501 Furthermore, <s>Subhūti</s>, a <s>bodhisattva-mahāsattva</s> abiding on the second stage gives attention to eight <s>dharmas</s>
21502 and practices them. What eight? Namely: purity of morality, gratitude,
21503 recognition of kindness, establishment in the power of patience, experiencing delight, the undertaking of
21504 great compassion through not abandoning all beings, reverence for teachers through faith, service to the teacher through the perception of him as master,
21505 and seeking the practice of the <s>pāramitās</s>. These, <s>Subhūti</s>, are the eight <s>dharmas</s> that a <s>bodhisattva-mahāsattva</s> abiding on the second
21506 stage should give attention to and practice.
21507 Furthermore, <s>Subhūti</s>, a <s>bodhisattva-mahāsattva</s> abiding on the third stage should stand firm in five <s>dharmas</s>.
21508 In which five? Namely: insatiability in learning, and therein non-attachment to letters;
21509 the exposition of <s>Dharma</s>-giving without material [reward], and therein non-conceit; the dedication of roots of merit to the purification of <s>buddhakṣetras</s>,
21510 and therein non-conceit; unflagging endurance in the limitless <s>saṃsāra</s>,
21511 and therein non-conceit; and establishment in moral shame and dread (<s>hrī</s> and <s>apatrāpya</s>), and therein non-conceit. In these five <s>dharmas</s>, <s>Subhūti</s>, a <s>bodhisattva</s>-
21512 <s>mahāsattva</s> abiding on the third stage should stand firm.
21513 Furthermore, <s>Subhūti</s>, a <s>bodhisattva-mahāsattva</s> abiding on the fourth stage should stand firm in ten <s>dharmas</s>,
21514 and should not abandon them. In which ten? Namely: dwelling in the forest,
21515 having few desires, contentment, not abandoning the <s>dhūtaguṇas</s> (ascetic practices), not abandoning the training, disgust with sensual pleasures,
21516 mental arising accompanied by disenchantment, abandonment of all possessions, mind that does not shrink back,
21517 indifference toward all things. These, <s>Subhūti</s>, are the ten <s>dharmas</s> that a <s>bodhisattva-mahāsattva</s> abiding on the fourth stage
21518 should not abandon and should stand firm in.
21519 Furthermore, <s>Subhūti</s>, a <s>bodhisattva-mahāsattva</s> abiding on the fifth stage should avoid ten <s>dharmas</s>.
21520 Which ten? Namely: association with householders and renunciants should be avoided;
21521 jealousy regarding families should be avoided; frequenting gatherings should be avoided; self-praise should be avoided; disparaging others should be avoided; the ten
21522 unwholesome courses of action should be avoided; pride and obstinacy should be avoided; distorted views should be avoided; doubt
21523 should be avoided; harboring passion, hatred, and delusion should be avoided. These, <s>Subhūti</s>, are the ten <s>dharmas</s> that a <s>bodhisattva-mahāsattva</s>
21524 abiding on the fifth stage should avoid.

children.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Subhūti</s>, a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> abiding on the sixth <s>bhūmi</s> (stage) should fulfill six <s>dharmas</s>. Which six? Namely, the six <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections) should be fulfilled. And another six <s>dharmas</s> should be avoided. Which six? The thought of a <s>śrāvaka</s> (hearer) should be avoided. The thought of a <s>pratyekabuddha</s> (solitary awakened one) should be avoided. The thought of timidity should be avoided. Upon seeing a petitioner, one should not shrink away. All possessions should be relinquished, and no thought of despondency should be produced, nor should a petitioner be rebuffed. These, <s>Subhūti</s>, are the six <s>dharmas</s> that a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> abiding on the sixth <s>bhūmi</s> should fulfill. And another six <s>dharmas</s> should be avoided. Furthermore, <s>Subhūti</s>, for a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> abiding on the seventh <s>bhūmi</s>, twenty <s>dharmas</s> do not arise. Which twenty? Namely, there is no grasping at a self (<s>ātmagrāha</s>), no grasping at a being (<s>sattvagrāha</s>), no grasping at a life-force (<s>jīvagrāha</s>), no grasping at a person (<s>pudgalagrāha</s>), no grasping at annihilation (<s>ucchedagrāha</s>), no grasping at eternalism (<s>śāśvatagrāha</s>), no perception of marks (<s>nimittasaṃjñā</s>), no view of causation (<s>hetudṛṣṭi</s>), no clinging to the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), no clinging to the <s>dhātus</s> (elements), no clinging to the <s>āyatanas</s> (sense-bases), no clinging to supernatural power, no establishment in the three realms, no fixation on the three realms, no attachment to the three realms, no clinging to views relying on the <s>Buddha</s>, no clinging to views relying on the <s>Dharma</s>, no clinging to views relying on the <s>Saṃgha</s>, no clinging to views relying on morality, no disputation that <s>dharmas</s> are empty, and no opposition to emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>). These, <s>Subhūti</s>, are the twenty <s>dharmas</s> that do not arise for a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> abiding on the seventh <s>bhūmi</s>. By that same (bodhisattva) abiding on the seventh <s>bhūmi</s>, twenty <s>dharmas</s> should be fulfilled. Which twenty? Namely, the fulfillment of emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>), the direct realization of the signless (<s>animitta</s>), knowledge of the wishless (<s>apraṇihita</s>), the purification of the three spheres (<s>trimaṇḍalapariśuddhi</s>), compassion and great compassion toward all beings, not despising them, seeing the equality of all <s>dharmas</s> and not clinging to that, penetration of the true method (<s>bhūtanaya</s>) without being conceited about it, acceptance of the non-arising (of <s>dharmas</s>) (<s>anutpādakṣānti</s>), knowledge of non-arising, teaching by the single method, the destruction of conceptual elaboration regarding all <s>dharmas</s>, the turning away from perceptions and views, the turning away from afflictions (<s>kleśa</s>), attainment of calm (<s>śamatha</s>), skill in insight (<s>vipaśyanā</s>), a tamed mind, a mind of unobstructed knowledge everywhere, not being a ground for attachment, going to whatever <s>buddha-kṣetra</s> (buddha-field) one wishes, and there, standing in the assembly of the <s>Buddha</s>, displaying one's own body. These twenty <s>dharmas</s> should be fulfilled by a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> abiding on the seventh <s>bhūmi</s>.

children.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Subhūti</s>, a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> abiding on the eighth <s>bhūmi</s> should fulfill four <s>dharmas</s>. Which four? Namely, penetration into the minds of all beings, sport with superknowledges (<s>abhijñāvikrīḍana</s>), seeing <s>buddha-kṣetras</s> (buddha-fields) and accomplishing them as seen, and attending upon <s>Buddhas</s> and contemplating the <s>Buddha</s>'s body as it truly is. These, <s>Subhūti</s>, are the four <s>dharmas</s> that a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> abiding on the eighth <s>bhūmi</s> should fulfill. Furthermore, <s>Subhūti</s>, a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> abiding on the eighth <s>bhūmi</s> should fulfill (another) four <s>dharmas</s>. Which four? Namely, knowledge of the higher and lower faculties of beings, purification of <s>buddha-kṣetras</s>, frequent attainment of the illusion-like <s>samādhi</s> (concentration), and manifesting a body in accordance with the maturation of beings' wholesome roots through deliberate birth in existence. These, <s>Subhūti</s>, are the four <s>dharmas</s> that a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> abiding on the eighth <s>bhūmi</s> should fulfill. Furthermore, <s>Subhūti</s>, a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> abiding on the ninth <s>bhūmi</s> should fulfill twelve <s>dharmas</s>. Which twelve? Namely, the embrace of infinite aspirations (<s>praṇidhāna</s>) — whatever aspirations he makes, they are all fulfilled; knowledge of the languages of <s>devas</s>, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>gandharvas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, and <s>mahoragas</s>; knowledge of inspired teaching (<s>pratibhānanirdeśa</s>); skill in entry into the womb; excellence of birth; excellence of family; excellence of retinue; excellence of nativity; excellence of renunciation; excellence of the <s>Bodhi</s> tree; and fulfillment of all qualities. These, <s>Subhūti</s>, are the twelve <s>dharmas</s> that a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> abiding on the ninth <s>bhūmi</s> should fulfill. Furthermore, <s>Subhūti</s>, a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> abiding on the tenth <s>bhūmi</s> should be called a <s>Tathāgata</s> indeed. <s>Subhūti</s> said: What, Blessed One, is the cultivation of the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>'s higher intention (<s>adhyāśayaparikarma</s>)? The Blessed One said: That which, through mental engagements connected with <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> (knowledge of all aspects), brings together all wholesome roots — this, <s>Subhūti</s>, is the cultivation of the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>'s higher intention. And what is the cultivation of the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>'s beneficial disposition (<s>hitavastutāparikarma</s>)? That a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> undertakes the pursuit of <s>Mahāyāna</s> knowledge for the benefit of all beings — this is the cultivation of his beneficial disposition. And what is the cultivation of the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>'s equanimity toward all beings (<s>sarvasattvasamacittatāparikarma</s>)? That through mental engagements connected with <s>sarvākārajñatā</s>, one cultivates the four <s>apramāṇas</s> (immeasurables) — loving-kindness (<s>maitrī</s>), compassion (<s>karuṇā</s>), sympathetic joy (<s>muditā</s>), and equanimity (<s>upekṣā</s>) — this is called the cultivation of equanimity toward all beings.

children.translated_text: What is the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>'s preparatory practice of generosity? That he gives undiscriminating gifts to all beings — this is called the preparatory practice of generosity. What is the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>'s preparatory practice of attending virtuous friends? Those virtuous friends of the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> who encourage him toward <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> (omniscience of all aspects) — the attending, serving, waiting upon, and listening to those friends — this is called the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>'s preparatory practice of attending virtuous friends. What is the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>'s preparatory practice of seeking the <s>Dharma</s>? That he seeks the <s>Dharma</s> with mental application conjoined to <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> and does not fall into the level of <s>śrāvakas</s> or <s>pratyekabuddhas</s> — this is called the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>'s preparatory practice of seeking the <s>Dharma</s>. What is the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>'s preparatory practice of constant renunciation? That in all births he goes forth unmixed, takes ordination in the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s teaching, and no obstacle arises for him — this, <s>Subhūti</s>, is called the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>'s preparatory practice of constant renunciation. What is the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>'s preparatory practice of aspiration for the <s>Buddha</s>-body? That having seen the <s>Buddha</s>'s form, he is never without mindfulness of the <s>Buddha</s> until he attains <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> — this, <s>Subhūti</s>, is called the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>'s preparatory practice of aspiration for the <s>Buddha</s>-body. What is the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>'s preparatory practice of explaining the <s>Dharma</s>? That the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, whether in the presence of a <s>Tathāgata</s> or after his <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, teaches the <s>Dharma</s> to beings — good in the beginning, good in the middle, good at the end, with good meaning and good phrasing, complete, perfect, pure, and cleansed — he illuminates the holy life, namely <s>sūtras</s>, verses, prophecies, narratives, birth stories, causes, legends, and also the extensive, marvelous <s>Dharma</s>-instructions. This is called the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>'s preparatory practice of explaining the <s>Dharma</s>. What is the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>'s preparatory practice of truthful speech? That is, acting in accordance with what one has said — this is called the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>'s preparatory practice of truthful speech. These, <s>Subhūti</s>, are the ten preparatory practices of the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> abiding on the first <s>bhūmi</s> (stage). What, <s>Subhūti</s>, are the eight preparatory practices of the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> abiding on the second <s>bhūmi</s>? That the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, while practicing the <s>bodhisattva</s> conduct, does not let even a small deed done for him be forgotten throughout <s>saṃsāra</s>, let alone a great one — this is called the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>'s gratitude and acknowledgment. What is the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>'s establishment in the power of patience? That he has a mind free from ill-will and harmfulness toward all beings — this is called the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>'s establishment in the power of patience. What is the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>'s experience of joyful satisfaction? That he matures all beings — this is called the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>'s experience of joyful satisfaction. What is the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>'s turning toward great compassion? That while practicing the <s>bodhisattva</s> conduct, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> thinks thus: 'For the sake of each single being, I would endure being cooked in hell for <s>kalpas</s> as numerous as the sands of the river <s>Gaṅgā</s>, until that being is established in the <s>Buddha</s>'s knowledge.' Such effort and indefatigability for each and every being — this is called the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>'s turning toward great compassion. What is the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>'s respectful faith? That the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> has faith with humility destroyed everywhere — this is called the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>'s respectful faith. What is the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>'s devoted obedience and faith toward teachers? That in the presence of teachers he has the perception of them as the Teacher — this is called the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>'s devoted obedience and faith toward teachers. What is the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>'s seeking the practice of the <s>pāramitās</s>? That he seeks the <s>pāramitās</s> with single-minded devotion — this is called the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>'s seeking the practice of the <s>pāramitās</s>. What is the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>'s insatiability for learning? Whatever has been spoken by the <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bhagavāns</s>, whether in this world-system or throughout the ten directions of the world — the insatiability in thinking 'I shall master all of it' — this is called the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>'s insatiability for learning. What is the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>'s selfless exposition of the <s>Dharma</s> as a gift? That the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> teaches the <s>Dharma</s>, and through that wholesome act of <s>Dharma</s>-giving, he does not even wish for his own awakening — this is called the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>'s selfless exposition of the <s>Dharma</s> as a gift. What is the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>'s dedication of roots of merit for purifying the <s>buddhakṣetra</s> (buddha-field)? The dedication of those roots of merit by which, while purifying the <s>buddhakṣetra</s>, he purifies his own mind and the minds of others — this is called the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>'s dedication of roots of merit for purifying the <s>buddhakṣetra</s>. What is the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>'s untiring endurance of limitless <s>saṃsāra</s>? is to be abandoned. The non-perception of internal <s>dharmas</s> — this is the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva's</s> abandonment of self-exaltation.
Therein, what is the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva's</s> abandonment of disparaging others? Namely, the non-perception of external <s>dharmas</s>. This is called the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva's</s> abandonment of disparaging others. Therein, how should the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> abandon the ten unwholesome paths of action? For these are obstacles to the noble path and to good rebirth, how much more so to <s>saṃbodhi</s> (awakening). Thus, <s>Subhūti</s>, the ten unwholesome paths of action are to be abandoned by the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>. Therein, how should the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> abandon <s>adhimāna</s> (conceit)? For he does not perceive any <s>dharma</s> — whence then something superior by which he might be conceited? Thus, <s>Subhūti</s>, <s>adhimāna</s> is to be abandoned by the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>.
Therein, how, <s>Subhūti</s>, should the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> abandon <s>stambha</s> (obstinacy)? For he does not perceive the object on the basis of which he might produce obstinacy. Thus, <s>Subhūti</s>, <s>stambha</s> is to be abandoned by the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>. Therein, how, <s>Subhūti</s>, should the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> abandon the <s>viparyāsas</s> (distortions)? Through the non-apprehension of all objects. Thus, <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>viparyāsas</s> are to be abandoned by the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>. Therein, how, <s>Subhūti</s>, should the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> abandon <s>vicikitsā</s> (doubt)? For he perceives all <s>dharmas</s> as free from doubt. Thus, <s>Subhūti</s>, <s>vicikitsā</s> is to be abandoned by the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>. Therein, how, <s>Subhūti</s>, should the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> abandon tolerance of <s>rāga</s> (attachment), <s>dveṣa</s> (aversion), and <s>moha</s> (delusion)? For he does not perceive the object of <s>rāga</s>, <s>dveṣa</s>, and <s>moha</s>. Thus, <s>Subhūti</s>, tolerance of <s>rāga</s>, <s>dveṣa</s>, and <s>moha</s> is to be abandoned by the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>. Therein, how should the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> fulfill six <s>dharmas</s>? Namely, the six <s>pāramitās</s>: <s>dānapāramitā</s> (perfection of generosity), <s>śīlapāramitā</s> (perfection of morality), <s>kṣāntipāramitā</s> (perfection of patience), <s>vīryapāramitā</s> (perfection of vigor), <s>dhyānapāramitā</s> (perfection of meditation), and <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> (perfection of wisdom) — these six <s>pāramitās</s> are to be fulfilled. Therein, how should the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> abandon six <s>dharmas</s>? Namely, the mind of a <s>śrāvaka</s> (hearer) is to be abandoned. For what reason? For this is not the path to awakening. The mind of a <s>pratyekabuddha</s> (solitary buddha) is to be abandoned. For what reason? For this is not the path to awakening. A mind of timidity is not to be produced. For what reason? For this is not the path to awakening. Upon seeing a beggar, a withdrawn mind is not to be produced. For what reason? For this is not the path to awakening. Even after giving away everything, one should not become disheartened. For what reason? For this is not the path to awakening. A beggar is not to be turned away. For what reason? For this is not the path to awakening. Therein, how should the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> not grasp at self? For what reason? For ultimately a self is not found. Thus the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> should not grasp at self. Likewise, grasping at a being (<s>sattva</s>), a life-force (<s>jīva</s>), and a person (<s>pudgala</s>) is not to be done. For what reason? For these ultimately do not exist. Thus grasping at being, life-force, and person is not to be done. Therein, how should the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> not grasp at annihilation (<s>uccheda</s>)? For what reason? Therein, how should the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> not grasp at eternalism (<s>śāśvata</s>)? For what reason? For a <s>dharma</s> that does not arise is not eternal. Thus grasping at eternalism is not to be done. Therein, how should the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> not produce the perception of signs (<s>nimittasaṃjñā</s>)? For what reason? For ultimately defilement is not found. Thus the perception of signs is not to be produced. Therein, how should the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> not hold views about causes (<s>hetudṛṣṭi</s>)? For what reason? For he does not perceive that view. Thus views about causes are not to be held. Likewise, clinging to the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), <s>dhātus</s> (elements), and <s>āyatanas</s> (sense-bases) is not to be done. For what reason? Thus is the purity of the three spheres of the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>. Therein, how should the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> fulfill compassion and mercy (<s>kṛpākaruṇā</s>) toward all beings? Through the attainment of great compassion (<s>mahākaruṇā</s>). Thus should compassion and mercy toward all beings be fulfilled. Therein, how should the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> not look down upon any being? Through the fulfillment of loving-kindness (<s>maitrī</s>). Thus should no being be looked down upon. Therein, what is the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>'s vision of equality (<s>samatādarśana</s>)? The neither-exalting nor denigrating of all <s>dharmas</s> — this is the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>'s vision of equality. Therein, what is the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>'s penetration of the true method (<s>bhūtanayaprativedha</s>)? The non-penetration of all <s>dharmas</s> — this is the penetration of the true method. Therein, what is the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>'s acceptance of the non-arising [of dharmas] (<s>anutpādakṣānti</s>)? The patience toward the non-arising, non-cessation, and non-fabrication of all <s>dharmas</s> — this is the acceptance of non-arising. Therein, what is the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>'s knowledge of non-arising (<s>anutpādajñāna</s>)? The knowledge of the non-arising of name-and-form (<s>nāmarūpa</s>) — this is the knowledge of non-arising. Therein, what is the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>'s exposition of the single approach (<s>ekanayanirdeśa</s>)? The conduct of non-duality (<s>advayasamudacāratā</s>) — this is the exposition of the single approach. Therein, what is the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>'s destruction of conceptual proliferation (<s>kalpanāsamudghāta</s>)? The very conceptualization of all <s>dharmas</s> — this is the destruction of conceptual proliferation. Therein, what is the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>'s turning away from perception and views (<s>saṃjñādṛṣṭivivarta</s>)? The turning away from the perceptions and views of the level of all <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> — this is the turning away from perception and views. Therein, what is the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>'s turning away from defilements (<s>kleśavivarta</s>)? The abandonment of all defilements together with their residual impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>) and connections — this is the turning away from defilements. Therein, what is the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>'s ground of calm and insight (<s>śamathavipaśyanābhūmi</s>)? The knowledge of <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> (omniscience of all aspects) — this is the ground of calm and insight. Therein, what is the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>'s taming of the mind (<s>dāntacittatā</s>)? Non-delight in the triple world (<s>traidhātuka</s>) — this is the taming of the mind. Therein, what is the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>'s unobstructed knowledge (<s>apratihatajñāna</s>)? The attainment of the <s>Buddha</s>-eye (<s>buddhacakṣus</s>) — this is unobstructed knowledge. Therein, what is the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>'s knowledge of neither attachment nor aversion (<s>anunayāpasaraṇajñatā</s>)? The equanimity based on the six sense-bases (<s>ṣaḍāyatanika upekṣā</s>) — this is the knowledge of neither attachment nor aversion. Therein, what is the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>'s going to whichever field he wishes (<s>yatrecchākṣetragamana</s>)? That, without moving from a single <s>buddhakṣetra</s>, he appears in all <s>buddhakṣetras</s>, yet no perception of a <s>buddhakṣetra</s> arises in him — this is going to whichever field he wishes. Therein, what is the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>'s displaying of himself everywhere (<s>sarvatrātmabhāvadarśana</s>)? Displaying his form as appropriate to each assembly — this is displaying himself everywhere. Therein, what is the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>'s entering into the mental conduct of all beings (<s>sarvasattvacittacaritānupraveśa</s>)? Knowing the mental conduct of all beings with a single thought — this is entering into the mental conduct of all beings. Therein, what is the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>'s sporting with superknowledges (<s>abhijñāvikrīḍanā</s>)? Sporting with superknowledges, he traverses from <s>buddhakṣetra</s> to <s>buddhakṣetra</s> to see the <s>Buddhas</s>, yet he does not have the perception of a <s>Buddha</s> — this is sporting with superknowledges. Among these, what is the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva's</s> knowledge of the higher and lower faculties (<s>indriyaparāparajñānatā</s>)? Among these, what is the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva's</s> purification of the <s>buddha-kṣetra</s> (<s>buddhakṣetrapariśodhanatā</s>)? Among these, what is the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva's</s> illusion-like concentration (<s>māyopamasamādhi</s>)? The concentration in which, having abided, he performs all actions yet no mental activity occurs — this is the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva's</s> illusion-like concentration. Among these, what is the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva's</s> continuous attainment (<s>abhīkṣṇasamāpatti</s>)? children.translated_text: That which is the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva's</s> going forth from the household life together with many <s>koṭi-niyuta</s>-hundreds of thousands of beings — this is the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva's</s> excellence of going forth. Among these, what is the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva's</s> excellence of the array of the <s>Bodhi</s> tree (<s>bodhivṛkṣavyūhasampat</s>)? The root of the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva's</s> <s>Bodhi</s> tree is golden, its trunk is made of <s>vaiḍūrya</s> (lapis lazuli), its branches are made of all precious gems, its leaves are made of all precious gems, and the fragrance of its flowers and its radiance pervade infinite world-realms with illumination — this is the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva's</s> excellence of the array of the <s>Bodhi</s> tree. Among these, what is the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva's</s> excellence of the fulfillment of all qualities (<s>sarvaguṇaparipūrisampat</s>)? That which is the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva's</s> purification of the <s>buddha-kṣetra</s> through the maturation of beings — this is the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva's</s> excellence of the fulfillment of all qualities. Among these, how is a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> established on the tenth <s>bhūmi</s> (stage) to be called a <s>Tathāgata</s>? When the ten <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections) of the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> are fulfilled, up to and including the eighteen exclusive <s>buddhadharmas</s> (buddha-qualities) are fulfilled, and the knowledge of <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> (knowledge of all aspects) and the abandonment of all <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) together with their latent tendencies (<s>vāsanā</s>) are accomplished, and great compassion (<s>mahākaruṇā</s>) and all <s>buddhadharmas</s> are fulfilled — in this way, <s>Subhūti</s>, beyond the tenth <s>bodhisattva</s> stage, a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> is to be called a <s>Tathāgata</s>. Among these, what are the ten stages (<s>daśabhūmi</s>) of a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>? The <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, through skillful means (<s>upāyakauśalya</s>), practicing all <s>pāramitās</s>, trained in the thirty-seven factors conducive to awakening (<s>bodhipakṣa dharmas</s>), practicing the immeasurable <s>dhyānas</s> (meditations) and formless attainments (<s>ārūpyasamāpattis</s>), practicing the ten <s>Tathāgata</s> powers (<s>balas</s>), the analytical knowledges (<s>pratisaṃvids</s>), and the eighteen exclusive <s>buddhadharmas</s> — surpasses the <s>gotrabhūmi</s> (lineage stage), the <s>aṣṭamakabhūmi</s> (eighth-person stage), the <s>darśanabhūmi</s> (stage of seeing), the <s>tanubhūmi</s> (stage of thinning), the <s>vītarāgabhūmi</s> (stage of freedom from passion), the <s>kṛtāvibhūmi</s> (stage of accomplishment), the <s>śrāvakabhūmi</s> (disciple stage), the <s>pratyekabuddhabhūmi</s> (solitary awakened one stage), and the <s>bodhisattvabhūmi</s> (bodhisattva stage) — surpassing these nine stages, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> becomes established on the <s>buddhabhūmi</s> (buddha stage). This is the tenth stage of the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>. In this way, <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> has set out in the <s>Mahāyāna</s> (great vehicle). [Thus the accumulation of the stages.] As for <s>Subhūti's</s> statement, 'From where will that vehicle go forth?' — it will go forth from the three realms (<s>traidhātuka</s>). By that through which <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> (knowledge of all aspects) is reached, it will abide there — and that through the method of non-duality (<s>advayayoga</s>). What is the reason? For indeed, the <s>Mahāyāna</s> and <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> — both of these <s>dharmas</s> are neither conjoined nor disjoined, formless, invisible, non-resistant, of one characteristic, namely, the characteristic of being without characteristics. One who would wish to depart from characterless <s>dharmas</s>, <s>Subhūti</s>, would wish to depart from <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) — likewise from <s>bhūtakoṭi</s> (the limit of reality), from the inconceivable realm (<s>acintyadhātu</s>), from the space-realm (<s>ākāśadhātu</s>), from the realm of abandonment (<s>prahāṇadhātu</s>), from the limit of dispassion (<s>virāgakoṭi</s>), from non-arising, non-ceasing, and non-existence — one who would wish to depart from characterless <s>dharmas</s> would wish to depart from these. One who would wish to depart from the emptiness of form (<s>rūpaśūnyatā</s>), <s>Subhūti</s>, would wish to depart from characterless <s>dharmas</s>. Likewise for the emptiness of feeling, the emptiness of perception, the emptiness of volitional formations, and the emptiness of consciousness — one would wish to depart from characterless <s>dharmas</s>. For what reason? Because, <s>Subhūti</s>, the emptiness of form will not depart from the three realms, nor will it abide in <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> (knowledge of all aspects). Likewise the emptiness of feeling, perception, volitional formations, and consciousness will not depart from the three realms nor abide in <s>sarvākārajñatā</s>. For what reason? Because, <s>Subhūti</s>, form is empty of form, feeling is empty of feeling, perception is empty of perception, volitional formations are empty of volitional formations. One who would wish to depart from the emptiness of the eye, <s>Subhūti</s>, would wish to depart from characterless <s>dharmas</s>. Likewise for the emptiness of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind. Likewise for the emptiness of form (visible objects), sound, smell, taste, tangible objects, and <s>dharmas</s> (mental objects). Likewise for the emptiness of eye-consciousness, ear-consciousness, nose-consciousness, tongue-consciousness, body-consciousness, and mind-consciousness; the emptiness of eye-contact, ear-contact, nose-contact, tongue-contact, body-contact, and mind-contact; the emptiness of feeling born of eye-contact, feeling born of ear-contact, nose-contact, tongue-contact, body-contact, and feeling born of mind-contact — one would wish to depart from characterless <s>dharmas</s>. For what reason? Because, <s>Subhūti</s>, the emptiness of the eye will not depart from the three realms nor abide in <s>sarvākārajñatā</s>. Likewise the emptiness of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind will not depart from the three realms nor abide in <s>sarvākārajñatā</s>. Likewise for the emptiness of form, sound, smell, taste, tangible objects, and <s>dharmas</s>; the emptiness of eye-consciousness through mind-consciousness; the emptiness of eye-contact through mind-contact; the emptiness of feeling born of eye-contact through feeling born of body-contact — the emptiness of feeling born of mind-contact will not depart from the three realms nor abide in <s>sarvākārajñatā</s>. For what reason? Because, <s>Subhūti</s>, the eye is empty of the eye, the ear is empty of the ear, the nose is empty of the nose, the tongue is empty of the tongue, the body is empty of the body, the mind is empty of the mind; form is empty of form, sound is empty of sound, smell is empty of smell, taste is empty of taste, tangible objects are empty of tangible objects, <s>dharmas</s> are empty of <s>dharmas</s>; eye-consciousness is empty of eye-consciousness, and so on through mind-consciousness; eye-contact is empty of eye-contact, and so on through mind-contact; feeling born of eye-contact is empty of feeling born of eye-contact, and so on through feeling born of body-contact; feeling born of mind-contact is empty of feeling born of mind-contact. One who would wish to depart from the (emptiness of) a dream, <s>Subhūti</s>, would wish to depart from characterless <s>dharmas</s> — this should be elaborated in full. Likewise for a mirage, an illusion, an echo, a reflection, a mirror-image, a city of <s>gandharvas</s>, and a creation of the <s>Tathāgata</s> — one would wish to depart from characterless <s>dharmas</s>. For what reason? Because, <s>Subhūti</s>, the intrinsic nature of a dream will not depart from the three realms nor abide in <s>sarvākārajñatā</s>. Likewise the intrinsic nature of a mirage, an illusion, an echo, a reflection, a mirror-image, a <s>gandharva</s>'s (city), and the intrinsic nature of a <s>Tathāgata</s>'s creation will not depart from the three realms nor abide in <s>sarvākārajñatā</s>. children.translated_text: the perfection of generosity (<s>dānapāramitā</s>), the perfection of morality (<s>śīlapāramitā</s>), the perfection of patience (<s>kṣāntipāramitā</s>), the perfection of vigor (<s>vīryapāramitā</s>), the perfection of meditation (<s>dhyānapāramitā</s>), and the perfection of wisdom (<s>prajñāpāramitā</s>) — this, <s>Subhūti</s>, is the great vehicle (<s>mahāyāna</s>) of the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>. Furthermore, <s>Subhūti</s>, the great vehicle of the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> is all the gateways of <s>dhāraṇī</s> and all the gateways of <s>samādhi</s> — the <s>Śūraṅgama samādhi</s>, to be elaborated in full, up to the <s>Asaṅgākāśavimuktinirupalepa samādhi</s>. This, <s>Subhūti</s>, is the great vehicle of the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>. Furthermore, <s>Subhūti</s>, the great vehicle of the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> is the emptiness of the internal (<s>adhyātmaśūnyatā</s>), the emptiness of the external (<s>bahirdhāśūnyatā</s>), the emptiness of the internal-and-external (<s>adhyātmabahirdhāśūnyatā</s>), up to the emptiness of the non-existence of own-nature (<s>abhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā</s>). This, <s>Subhūti</s>, is the great vehicle of the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>. Furthermore, <s>Subhūti</s>, the great vehicle of the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> is the four foundations of mindfulness (<s>smṛtyupasthāna</s>), the four right efforts (<s>samyakprahāṇa</s>), the four bases of miraculous power (<s>ṛddhipāda</s>), the five faculties (<s>indriya</s>), the five powers (<s>bala</s>), the seven factors of enlightenment (<s>bodhyaṅga</s>), the noble eightfold path (<s>āryāṣṭāṅgamārga</s>), the four analytical knowledges (<s>pratisaṃvid</s>), the four confidences (<s>vaiśāradya</s>), the six superknowledges (<s>abhijñā</s>), the ten powers of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, and the eighteen unique <s>Buddha</s>-dharmas (<s>āveṇikabuddhadharma</s>). This, <s>Subhūti</s>, is the great vehicle of the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>. As to what <s>Subhūti</s> said — 'That vehicle will go forth having overcome the world with its gods, humans, and <s>asuras</s>' — what then is the world with its gods, humans, and <s>asuras</s>? Namely, the desire-realm (<s>kāmadhātu</s>), the form-realm (<s>rūpadhātu</s>), and the formless realm (<s>ārūpyadhātu</s>). If, <s>Subhūti</s>, the desire-realm were <s>tathatā</s> (suchness), undeviating suchness, non-other suchness, unerring, real, truth, as-it-is, permanent, stable, eternal, of unchanging nature, existent and not non-existent — then this <s>mahāyāna</s> would not go forth having overcome the world with its gods, humans, and <s>asuras</s>. But since, <s>Subhūti</s>, the desire-realm is fabricated, set up, shown to be otherwise than it is, entirely impermanent, unstable, non-eternal, of a nature subject to change, and non-existent — therefore this <s>mahāyāna</s> will go forth having overcome the world with its gods, humans, and <s>asuras</s>. Likewise for the form-realm and the formless realm. If, <s>Subhūti</s>, form were suchness, unerring, real, permanent, stable, eternal, of unchanging nature, existent and not non-existent — then this <s>mahāyāna</s> would not go forth having overcome the world. But since form is fabricated, set up, shown to be otherwise, entirely impermanent, unstable, non-eternal, of a nature subject to change, and non-existent — therefore this <s>mahāyāna</s> will go forth having overcome the world. Likewise for feeling, perception, and formations. If consciousness were [permanent and existent] — the <s>mahāyāna</s> would not go forth. But since consciousness is fabricated and impermanent — therefore the <s>mahāyāna</s> goes forth. Likewise for the eye, ear, nose, tongue, and body. If the mind were [permanent and existent] — the <s>mahāyāna</s> would not go forth. But since the mind is fabricated and impermanent — therefore the <s>mahāyāna</s> goes forth. Likewise for visible form, sound, smell, taste, and tangibles. If mental objects (<s>dharma</s>) were [permanent] — the <s>mahāyāna</s> would not go forth. But since mental objects are fabricated and impermanent — therefore the <s>mahāyāna</s> goes forth. Likewise for eye-consciousness, ear-consciousness, nose-consciousness, tongue-consciousness, and body-consciousness. If mind-consciousness were [permanent] — the <s>mahāyāna</s> would not go forth. But since mind-consciousness is fabricated and impermanent — therefore the <s>mahāyāna</s> goes forth. Likewise for eye-contact, ear-contact, nose-contact, tongue-contact, and body-contact. If mind-contact were [permanent] — the <s>mahāyāna</s> would not go forth. But since mind-contact is fabricated and impermanent — therefore the <s>mahāyāna</s> goes forth. Likewise for feeling born of eye-contact, ear-contact, nose-contact, tongue-contact, and body-contact. If feeling born of mind-contact were [permanent] — the <s>mahāyāna</s> would not go forth. But since feeling born of mind-contact is fabricated and impermanent — therefore the <s>mahāyāna</s> goes forth. If, <s>Subhūti</s>, <s>dharmadhātu</s> were existent and not non-existent, then this <s>mahāyāna</s> would not go forth having overcome the world with its gods, humans, and <s>asuras</s>. But since, <s>Subhūti</s>, <s>dharmadhātu</s> is non-existent and not existent, therefore the <s>mahāyāna</s> will go forth having overcome the world with its gods, humans, and <s>asuras</s>. Likewise for <s>tathatā</s> and <s>bhūtakoṭi</s>. If, <s>Subhūti</s>, the inconceivable element (<s>acintyadhātu</s>) were existent and not non-existent, then this <s>mahāyāna</s> would not go forth having overcome the world. But since the inconceivable element is non-existent and not existent, therefore the <s>mahāyāna</s> will go forth having overcome the world with its gods, humans, and <s>asuras</s>.

children.translated_text: If, <s>Subhūti</s>, the perfection of generosity (<s>dānapāramitā</s>) were an existent and not a non-existent, this <s>Mahāyāna</s> would not go forth surpassing the world with its gods, humans, and <s>asuras</s>. But since, <s>Subhūti</s>, the perfection of generosity is a non-existent and not an existent, therefore the <s>Mahāyāna</s> goes forth surpassing the world with its gods, humans, and <s>asuras</s>. Likewise for the perfection of morality (<s>śīlapāramitā</s>), the perfection of patience (<s>kṣāntipāramitā</s>), the perfection of vigor (<s>vīryapāramitā</s>), the perfection of meditation (<s>dhyānapāramitā</s>), and the perfection of wisdom (<s>prajñāpāramitā</s>) — if each were an existent, the <s>Mahāyāna</s> would not go forth surpassing the world; but since each is a non-existent, therefore the <s>Mahāyāna</s> goes forth. Likewise for the internal emptiness (<s>adhyātmaśūnyatā</s>), the external emptiness (<s>bahirdhāśūnyatā</s>), the emptiness of both internal and external (<s>adhyātmabahirdhāśūnyatā</s>), and so on through the emptiness of the non-existence of inherent nature (<s>abhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā</s>) — since each is a non-existent, the <s>Mahāyāna</s> goes forth surpassing the world. If, <s>Subhūti</s>, the foundations of mindfulness (<s>smṛtyupasthāna</s>) were existents, the <s>Mahāyāna</s> would not go forth; but since they are non-existents, the <s>Mahāyāna</s> goes forth. Likewise for the four right efforts (<s>samyakprahāṇa</s>), the four bases of supernatural power (<s>ṛddhipāda</s>), the five faculties (<s>indriya</s>), the five powers (<s>bala</s>), and the seven factors of awakening (<s>bodhyaṅga</s>). If, <s>Subhūti</s>, the Noble Eightfold Path (<s>āryāṣṭāṅgamārga</s>) were an existent, the <s>Mahāyāna</s> would not go forth; but since it is a non-existent, the <s>Mahāyāna</s> goes forth. If, <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>apramāṇas</s> (immeasurables), <s>dhyānas</s> (meditative absorptions), and formless attainments (<s>ārūpyasamāpatti</s>) were existents, the <s>Mahāyāna</s> would not go forth; but since they are non-existents, the <s>Mahāyāna</s> goes forth. Likewise for the ten powers (<s>daśabala</s>), the four fearlessnesses (<s>vaiśāradya</s>), and the four analytical knowledges (<s>pratisaṃvid</s>). If, <s>Subhūti</s>, the eighteen unique qualities of a <s>Buddha</s> (<s>āveṇika buddhadharma</s>) were existents, the <s>Mahāyāna</s> would not go forth; but since they are non-existents, the <s>Mahāyāna</s> goes forth. [Thus ends the section on non-grasping and going forth (<s>agrahatāniryāṇa</s>).] If, <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>dharmas</s> of the <s>gotrabhū</s> (lineage) stage were existents, the <s>Mahāyāna</s> would not go forth; but since they are non-existents, the <s>Mahāyāna</s> goes forth. If, <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>dharmas</s> of the eighth (person) (<s>aṣṭamaka</s>) were existents, the <s>Mahāyāna</s> would not go forth; but since they are non-existents, the <s>Mahāyāna</s> goes forth. Likewise for the <s>dharmas</s> of the stream-enterer (<s>srotaāpanna</s>), the once-returner (<s>sakṛdāgāmin</s>), the non-returner (<s>anāgāmin</s>), the worthy one (<s>arhat</s>), the solitary awakened one (<s>pratyekabuddha</s>), and the <s>bodhisattva</s>. If, <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>Buddha</s> <s>dharmas</s> were existents, the <s>Mahāyāna</s> would not go forth; but since they are non-existents, the <s>Mahāyāna</s> goes forth. If, <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>gotrabhūmi</s> (lineage stage) were an existent, the <s>Mahāyāna</s> would not go forth; but since it is a non-existent, the <s>Mahāyāna</s> goes forth. Likewise for the eighth (person), the stream-enterer, the once-returner, the non-returner, the worthy one, the solitary awakened one, and the <s>bodhisattva</s>. If, <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>Buddha</s> were an existent, the <s>Mahāyāna</s> would not go forth; but since the <s>Buddha</s> is a non-existent, the <s>Mahāyāna</s> goes forth. If, <s>Subhūti</s>, the world of humans and <s>asuras</s> were an existent, the <s>Mahāyāna</s> would not go forth; but since the world of humans and <s>asuras</s> is a non-existent, the <s>Mahāyāna</s> goes forth. [Thus ends the section on going forth through abandonment (<s>prahāṇaniryāṇa</s>).] If, <s>Subhūti</s>, from the first arising of the thought (of awakening) up to the seat of awakening (<s>bodhimaṇḍa</s>), the thought-arisings (<s>cittotpāda</s>) of the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> during this interval were existents, the <s>Mahāyāna</s> would not go forth; but since, <s>Subhūti</s>, the thought-arisings are non-existents, the <s>Mahāyāna</s> goes forth surpassing the world. If, <s>Subhūti</s>, the diamond-like knowledge (<s>vajropamajñāna</s>) of the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> were an existent and not a non-existent, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> would not, having known all the afflictions (<s>kleśa</s>) together with their latent tendencies (<s>vāsanā</s>) as existents, attain the knowledge of the omniscient one (<s>sarvajñajñāna</s>) endowed with the excellence of all aspects. Thus the <s>Mahāyāna</s> (great vehicle), having overcome the world with its gods, humans, and <s>asuras</s>, will go forth. If, <s>Subhūti</s>, the thirty-two marks of a great person (<s>mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇa</s>) of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the perfectly and fully awakened one, were existence and not non-existence, then the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, perfectly and fully awakened ones, would never have overcome the world with its gods, humans, and <s>asuras</s> with their splendor and glory. Because, <s>Subhūti</s>, the thirty-two marks of a great person of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the perfectly and fully awakened one, are non-existence, not existence — therefore the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, perfectly and fully awakened ones, overcome the world with its gods, humans, and <s>asuras</s> with their splendor and glory. If, <s>Subhūti</s>, the radiance of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the perfectly and fully awakened one, were existence and not non-existence, he would never have pervaded world-realms as numerous as the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> river with his radiance. Because, <s>Subhūti</s>, the radiance of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the perfectly and fully awakened one, is non-existence, not existence — therefore the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the perfectly and fully awakened one, pervades world-realms as numerous as the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> river with his radiance. If, <s>Subhūti</s>, the voice endowed with sixty qualities of the <s>Tathāgata</s> were existence and not non-existence, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the perfectly and fully awakened one, would never make known immeasurable and innumerable world-realms in the ten directions through his voice. Because, <s>Subhūti</s>, the voice endowed with sixty qualities of the <s>Tathāgata</s> is non-existence, not existence — therefore the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the perfectly and fully awakened one, makes known immeasurable and innumerable world-realms in the ten directions through his voice. If, <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>dharmacakra</s> (wheel of the Dharma) of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, with its three turnings and twelve aspects, were existence and not non-existence, then the <s>Tathāgata</s> would never have turned the <s>dharmacakra</s> with its three turnings and twelve aspects, which cannot be turned by any <s>śramaṇa</s> (ascetic), <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, god, <s>Māra</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, or anyone else in the world in accordance with the <s>Dharma</s>. Because, <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>dharmacakra</s> of the <s>Tathāgata</s> with its three turnings and twelve aspects is non-existence, not existence — therefore the <s>dharmacakra</s> with its three turnings and twelve aspects, which cannot be turned by any <s>śramaṇa</s>, <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, god, <s>Māra</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, or anyone else in the world in accordance with the <s>Dharma</s>, has been turned by the <s>Tathāgata</s>. 23601 neither visible nor invisible, neither obstructive nor non-obstructive, neither conjoined nor disjoined. Even so,
23602 <s>Subhūti</s>, that Great Vehicle is neither material nor immaterial, neither visible nor invisible, neither obstructive nor non-obstructive, neither conjoined nor disjoined. Therefore it is said that vehicle is equal to space. Just as, <s>Subhūti</s>, space is neither permanent nor impermanent, neither pleasant nor painful, neither self nor non-self,
23603 neither peaceful nor non-peaceful, even so, <s>Subhūti</s>, that Great Vehicle is neither permanent nor impermanent, neither pleasant nor painful, neither self nor non-self, neither peaceful nor non-peaceful. Therefore it is said that vehicle is equal to space. Just as, <s>Subhūti</s>, space is neither empty nor non-empty, neither
23604 with signs nor without signs, neither with wishes nor without wishes, even so, <s>Subhūti</s>, that Great Vehicle is neither empty nor non-empty, neither with signs nor without signs, neither with wishes nor without wishes. Therefore it is said that vehicle is equal to space. Just as, <s>Subhūti</s>, space
23605 is neither secluded nor not secluded, neither light nor darkness, even so, <s>Subhūti</s>, that Great Vehicle is neither secluded nor not secluded, neither light nor darkness. Therefore it is said that vehicle is equal to space. Just as, <s>Subhūti</s>, space
23606 is neither obtained nor apprehended, even so, <s>Subhūti</s>, that Great Vehicle is neither obtained nor apprehended. Therefore it is said that vehicle is equal to space. Just as, <s>Subhūti</s>, space is neither expression
23607 nor non-expression, even so, <s>Subhūti</s>, that Great Vehicle is neither expression nor non-expression. Therefore it is said that vehicle is equal to space. [Thus the departure through equality.]
23608 As for <s>Subhūti</s>'s statement: 'Just as in space there is room for immeasurable, incalculable, and boundless
23609 beings, even so in that Great Vehicle there is room for immeasurable, incalculable, and
23610 boundless beings' — so it is, <s>Subhūti</s>, so it is. Just as
23611 in space there is room for immeasurable, incalculable, and boundless beings, even so in that Great Vehicle there is room for immeasurable, incalculable, and boundless beings. For what reason?

23701 Furthermore, <s>Subhūti</s>, the non-existence of beings is to be understood as the non-existence of the <s>Tathāgata</s>; from the non-existence of the <s>Tathāgata</s>,
23702 the non-existence of the boundless is to be understood. Thus, <s>Subhūti</s>, in that Great Vehicle there is room for immeasurable, incalculable, and boundless beings. For, <s>Subhūti</s>, those beings, and that space, and that Great Vehicle, and that which is boundless — all of these are not apprehended.
23703 Furthermore, <s>Subhūti</s>, the non-existence of beings is to be understood as the non-existence of space; the non-existence of space is to be understood as the non-existence of the Great
23704 Vehicle; the non-existence of the Great Vehicle is to be understood as the non-existence of the unconditioned; the non-existence of the unconditioned is to be understood as the non-existence of the immeasurable;
23705 the non-existence of the immeasurable is to be understood as the non-existence of the incalculable; the non-existence of the incalculable is to be understood as
23706 the non-existence of the boundless; the non-existence of the boundless is to be understood as the non-existence of all <s>dharmas</s>. Thus,
23707 <s>Subhūti</s>, in that Great Vehicle there is room for immeasurable, incalculable, and boundless beings. For what reason? For, <s>Subhūti</s>, those beings, and that
23708 <s>Tathāgata</s>, and that space, and that Great Vehicle, and that which is unconditioned, and that which is immeasurable, and that which is incalculable,
23709 and that which is boundless, and all those <s>dharmas</s> — all of these are not apprehended.
23710 Furthermore, <s>Subhūti</s>, the non-existence of self and beings is to be understood as the non-existence of beings, living beings, nourishers, persons, individuals, humans, mortals,
23711 agents, experiencers, knowers, and seers; the non-existence of knowers and seers is to be understood as the non-existence of the <s>bhūtakoṭi</s> (limit of reality);
23712 the non-existence of the <s>bhūtakoṭi</s> is to be understood as the non-existence of the immeasurable, incalculable, and boundless;
23713 the non-existence of the immeasurable, incalculable, and boundless is to be understood as the non-existence of all <s>dharmas</s>. Thus, <s>Subhūti</s>, in that
23714 Great Vehicle there is room for immeasurable, incalculable, and boundless beings. For what reason? For, <s>Subhūti</s>, that which is the self, and up to the knower and seer, and that which is
23715 the <s>bhūtakoṭi</s>, and that which is immeasurable, incalculable, and boundless, and all those <s>dharmas</s> — all of these are not apprehended.
23716 Furthermore, <s>Subhūti</s>, the non-existence of self and beings is to be understood as the non-existence of up to the knower and
23717 seer; the non-existence of the knower and seer is to be understood as the non-existence of the inconceivable realm (<s>acintyadhātu</s>); the non-existence of the inconceivable
23718 realm is to be understood as the non-existence of the <s>rūpaskandha</s> (aggregate of form); the non-existence of the <s>rūpaskandha</s> is to be understood as the non-existence of the <s>vedanāskandha</s>
23719 (aggregate of feeling); the non-existence of the <s>vedanāskandha</s> is to be understood as the non-existence of the <s>saṃjñāskandha</s> (aggregate of perception); the non-existence of the <s>saṃjñāskandha</s> is to be understood as the non-existence of the <s>saṃskāraskandha</s> (aggregate of formations); the non-existence of the <s>saṃskāraskandha</s> is to be understood as the non-existence of the <s>vijñānaskandha</s> (aggregate of consciousness); the non-existence of the <s>vijñānaskandha</s> is to be understood as the non-existence of space;
23720 the non-existence of space is to be understood as the non-existence of the Great Vehicle; the non-existence of the Great Vehicle is to be understood as the non-existence of the immeasurable,
23721 incalculable, and boundless; the non-existence of the immeasurable, incalculable, and boundless is to be understood as
23722 the non-existence of all <s>dharmas</s>. Thus, <s>Subhūti</s>, in that Great Vehicle there is room for immeasurable, incalculable, and boundless beings. For what reason?
23723 For, <s>Subhūti</s>, that which is the self, up to all those <s>dharmas</s> — all of these are not apprehended.

Furthermore, <s>Subhūti</s>, by the non-existence of self and beings, the non-existence up to the knower and seer should be understood. By the non-existence of the knower and seer, the non-existence of the eye should be understood. By the non-existence of the eye, the non-existence of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind should be understood. By the non-existence of the mind, the non-existence of space should be understood. By the non-existence of space, the non-existence of the <s>Mahāyāna</s> should be understood. By the non-existence of the <s>Mahāyāna</s>, the non-existence of the immeasurable, innumerable, and boundless should be understood. By the non-existence of the immeasurable, innumerable, and boundless, the non-existence of all <s>dharmas</s> should be understood. Thus, <s>Subhūti</s>, in that <s>Mahāyāna</s> there is room for immeasurable, innumerable, and boundless beings. For what reason? Because, <s>Subhūti</s>, the self, and all <s>dharmas</s> — none of these are to be apprehended. Furthermore, by the non-existence of self and beings up to the knower and seer, the non-existence of the perfection of generosity (<s>dānapāramitā</s>) should be understood. By the non-existence of the perfection of generosity, the non-existence of the perfection of morality (<s>śīlapāramitā</s>), patience (<s>kṣāntipāramitā</s>), vigor (<s>vīryapāramitā</s>), meditation (<s>dhyānapāramitā</s>), and wisdom (<s>prajñāpāramitā</s>) should be understood. By the non-existence of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, the non-existence of space should be understood. By the non-existence of space, the non-existence of the <s>Mahāyāna</s> should be understood, and by that the non-existence of the immeasurable, innumerable, and boundless, and by that the non-existence of all <s>dharmas</s>. Thus in that <s>Mahāyāna</s> there is room for immeasurable, innumerable, and boundless beings, because the self and all <s>dharmas</s> are not to be apprehended. Furthermore, by the non-existence of self and beings up to the knower and seer, the non-existence of the internal emptiness (<s>adhyātmaśūnyatā</s>), external emptiness (<s>bahirdhāśūnyatā</s>), the emptiness of both, and so on through the emptiness of the non-existence of inherent nature (<s>abhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā</s>) should be understood. By the non-existence of that, the non-existence of space, the <s>Mahāyāna</s>, the immeasurable and innumerable, and all <s>dharmas</s> should be understood. Thus in that <s>Mahāyāna</s> there is room for immeasurable beings, because self and all <s>dharmas</s> are not to be apprehended. Furthermore, by the non-existence of self and beings up to the knower and seer, the non-existence of the foundations of mindfulness (<s>smṛtyupasthāna</s>) should be understood; by the non-existence of the foundations of mindfulness, the non-existence of the right efforts (<s>samyakprahāṇa</s>); by that, the non-existence of the bases of supernatural power (<s>ṛddhipāda</s>), the faculties (<s>indriya</s>), the powers (<s>bala</s>), the factors of awakening (<s>bodhyaṅga</s>), the path (<s>mārga</s>), the fearlessnesses (<s>vaiśāradya</s>), the analytical knowledges (<s>pratisaṃvid</s>), the perfections (<s>pāramitā</s>), the powers of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, and the unique qualities of a <s>Buddha</s> (<s>āveṇika buddhadharma</s>) should be understood. By the non-existence of those, the non-existence of space, the <s>Mahāyāna</s>, and all <s>dharmas</s> should be understood. Thus in that <s>Mahāyāna</s> there is room for immeasurable beings, because self and all <s>dharmas</s> are not to be apprehended. Furthermore, by the non-existence of self and beings up to the knower and seer, the non-existence of the <s>gotrabhūmi</s> (lineage stage) should be understood; by that, the non-existence of the stage of the eighth person (<s>aṣṭamaka</s>), the stage of seeing (<s>darśanabhūmi</s>), the stage of thinning (<s>tanubhūmi</s>), the stage of freedom from passion (<s>vītarāgabhūmi</s>), and the stage of one who has done what was to be done (<s>kṛtāvibhūmi</s>). By the non-existence of that, the non-existence of space, the <s>Mahāyāna</s>, and all <s>dharmas</s> should be understood. Thus in that <s>Mahāyāna</s> there is room for immeasurable beings, because self and all <s>dharmas</s> are not to be apprehended.

Furthermore, by the non-existence of self and beings up to the knower and seer, the non-existence of the stream-enterer (<s>srotaāpanna</s>) should be understood; by that, the non-existence of the once-returner (<s>sakṛdāgāmin</s>), the non-returner (<s>anāgāmin</s>), the worthy one (<s>arhat</s>), and the solitary awakened one (<s>pratyekabuddha</s>). By the non-existence of the <s>pratyekabuddha</s>, the non-existence of space, the <s>Mahāyāna</s>, and all <s>dharmas</s> should be understood. Thus in that <s>Mahāyāna</s> there is room for immeasurable, innumerable, and boundless beings, because self and all <s>dharmas</s> are not to be apprehended. Furthermore, by the non-existence of self and beings up to the knower and seer, the non-existence of the <s>śrāvakayāna</s> (vehicle of hearers) should be understood; by that, the non-existence of the <s>pratyekabuddhayāna</s> (vehicle of solitary awakened ones); by that, the non-existence of the <s>Tathāgata</s>; by that, the non-existence of <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> (knowledge of all aspects). By the non-existence of <s>sarvākārajñatā</s>, the non-existence of space, the <s>Mahāyāna</s>, and all <s>dharmas</s> should be understood. Thus in that <s>Mahāyāna</s> there is room for immeasurable, innumerable, and boundless beings, because self and all <s>dharmas</s> are not to be apprehended. Just as, <s>Subhūti</s>, in the realm of <s>nirvāṇa</s> (<s>nirvāṇadhātu</s>) there is room for immeasurable, innumerable, and boundless beings, just so, <s>Subhūti</s>, in that <s>Mahāyāna</s> there is room for immeasurable, innumerable, and boundless beings. Just as, <s>Subhūti</s>, in space there is room for immeasurable, innumerable, and boundless beings, just so, <s>Subhūti</s>, in that <s>Mahāyāna</s> there is room for immeasurable, innumerable, and boundless beings.

the <s>smṛtyupasthānas</s> (foundations of mindfulness) of the past, future, and present will be apprehended. Likewise, the <s>samyakprahāṇas</s> (right efforts) are not apprehended in the past, future, and present times. The <s>ṛddhipādas</s> (bases of power) are not apprehended in the past, future, and present times. [Likewise, the <s>indriyas</s> (faculties), <s>balas</s> (powers), <s>bodhyaṅgas</s> (factors of awakening), the path, the <s>apramāṇas</s> (immeasurables), <s>dhyānas</s> (meditations), formless attainments, <s>Tathāgata</s>-powers, <s>vaiśāradyas</s> (fearlessnesses), and <s>pratisaṃvids</s> (analytical knowledges) are not apprehended in the past, future, and present times.] How much less, in the equality of the three times, would the eighteen exclusive <s>buddhadharmas</s> be apprehended?
Furthermore, <s>Subhūti</s>, an ordinary person (<s>pṛthagjana</s>) is not apprehended from the standpoint of the past, is not apprehended from the standpoint of the future, is not apprehended from the standpoint of the present. Through the equality of the three times, an ordinary person is not apprehended. For what reason? Because of the non-apprehension of beings. Likewise <s>śrāvakas</s> (hearers), <s>pratyekabuddhas</s> (solitary buddhas), and <s>bodhisattvas</s>. A <s>Tathāgata</s> is not apprehended from the standpoint of the past, is not apprehended from the standpoint of the future, is not apprehended from the standpoint of the middle [present]. Through the equality of the three times, a <s>Tathāgata</s> is not apprehended. For what reason? Because of the non-apprehension of beings. Thus, <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, standing in <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> and training in the three times, should fulfill <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> (knowledge of all aspects). This, <s>Subhūti</s>, is the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva's</s> <s>Mahāyāna</s> (Great Vehicle) through the equality of the three times. Standing here, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, overcoming the world with its gods, humans, and <s>asuras</s>, will go forth to <s>sarvākārajñatā</s>. [This is the final going-forth.]
Then the venerable <s>Subhūti</s> said to the Blessed One: 'Excellent, excellent, Blessed One! Well spoken is this by the Blessed One — the <s>Mahāyāna</s> of the <s>bodhisattvas mahāsattvas</s>. In this <s>Mahāyāna</s>, Blessed One, <s>bodhisattvas mahāsattvas</s> of the past, training here, attained <s>sarvākārajñatā</s>. <s>Bodhisattvas mahāsattvas</s> of the future, training in this <s>Mahāyāna</s>, will attain <s>sarvākārajñatā</s>. And those <s>bodhisattvas mahāsattvas</s>, Blessed One, who are presently in innumerable world-systems in the ten directions — they too, having trained in this <s>Mahāyāna</s>, are attaining <s>sarvākārajñatā</s>. Therefore, Blessed One, this is the <s>Mahāyāna</s> of the <s>bodhisattvas mahāsattvas</s> — namely, [the vehicle] of those in the equality of the three times.' Then the Blessed One said to the venerable <s>Subhūti</s>: 'So it is, <s>Subhūti</s>, so it is. Having trained in this <s>Mahāyāna</s>, <s>bodhisattvas mahāsattvas</s> of the past, future, and present have attained, will attain, and are attaining <s>sarvākārajñatā</s>.'

<s>Subhūti</s> said: 'Which, Blessed One, are the wholesome <s>dharmas</s> that are factors of awakening — <s>dharmas</s> of <s>śrāvakas</s>, <s>dharmas</s> of <s>pratyekabuddhas</s>, <s>dharmas</s> of <s>bodhisattvas</s>, and <s>buddhadharmas</s> — that all converge in <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>?'

These, <s>Subhūti</s>, are the wholesome <s>dharmas</s> that are factors of awakening — <s>dharmas</s> of <s>śrāvakas</s>, <s>pratyekabuddhas</s>, [<s>bodhisattvas</s>, and <s>buddhadharmas</s> — all converging in <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.]
Furthermore, <s>Subhūti</s>, the <s>Mahāyāna</s>, the <s>dhyānapāramitā</s>, <s>vīryapāramitā</s>, <s>kṣāntipāramitā</s>, <s>śīlapāramitā</s>, <s>dānapāramitā</s>, and <s>rūpa</s> (form), <s>vedanā</s> (feeling), <s>saṃjñā</s> (perception), <s>saṃskāras</s> (formations), <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness), the eye, ear, [nose, tongue, body, mind, forms, sounds, smells, tastes, tangibles, <s>dharmas</s>, the six consciousnesses, the six contacts, the six contact-born feelings,] [the four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts, the four bases of power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of awakening, the noble eightfold] path, the immeasurables, the meditations, the formless attainments —

For the non-existence of beings, and all up to the middle — all this is undivided. By the non-existence of form, the <s>bodhisattva</s> does not approach (things) from the standpoint of the past, the future, or the middle. By the emptiness of form, the separateness of form, and the lack of inherent nature of form, the <s>bodhisattva</s> does not approach from the standpoint of the past, future, or middle. Likewise for feeling, perception, and volitional formations. By the non-existence of consciousness, the <s>bodhisattva</s> does not approach from the standpoint of the past, future, or middle. By the emptiness, separateness, and lack of inherent nature of consciousness, the <s>bodhisattva</s> does not approach from the past, future, or middle. Likewise it should be stated for the sense-bases (<s>āyatana</s>), the elements (<s>dhātu</s>), and the links of dependent origination (<s>pratītyasamutpāda</s>) — the <s>bodhisattva</s> does not approach from the past, future, or middle. By the non-existence of the perfection of generosity (<s>dānapāramitā</s>), the <s>bodhisattva</s> does not approach from the past, future, or middle. By the emptiness, separateness, and lack of inherent nature of the perfection of generosity, the <s>bodhisattva</s> does not approach from the past, future, or middle. Likewise for the perfection of morality, patience, vigor, and meditation. By the non-existence of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, and by the emptiness, separateness, and lack of inherent nature of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s> does not approach from the past, future, or middle. For what reason? Because, Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, in the non-existence, emptiness, separateness, and lack of inherent nature of the perfections of generosity, morality, patience, vigor, meditation, and wisdom, the past, future, and middle are not to be apprehended. And, <s>Śāriputra</s>, non-existence is not one thing, emptiness another, separateness another, lack of inherent nature another, the <s>bodhisattva</s> another, the perfection of generosity another, the perfection of morality, patience, vigor, meditation another, <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> another, and the past, future, and middle yet another.
