children.translated_text: The <s>adhyātmaśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of the internal) is non-existent, empty, isolated, and without intrinsic nature; up to and including <s>abhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of the non-existence of intrinsic nature) is non-existent, empty, isolated, and without intrinsic nature; and the <s>bodhisattva</s>, and the past, future, and middle — all of this is without duality (<s>advaidhīkāra</s>). By this method, Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s> does not approach the past, future, or middle. Furthermore, Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, because the <s>smṛtyupasthānas</s> (foundations of mindfulness) are non-existent, empty, isolated, and without intrinsic nature, the <s>bodhisattva</s> does not approach the past, future, or middle. Because the <s>samyakprahāṇas</s> (right exertions) are non-existent, empty, isolated, and without intrinsic nature, the <s>bodhisattva</s> does not approach the past, future, or middle. Because the <s>ṛddhipādas</s> (bases of supernatural power) are non-existent, empty, isolated, and without intrinsic nature, the <s>bodhisattva</s> does not approach the past, future, or middle. Because the <s>indriyas</s> (faculties) are non-existent, empty, isolated, and without intrinsic nature, the <s>bodhisattva</s> does not approach the past, future, or middle. Because the <s>balas</s> (powers) are non-existent, empty, isolated, and without intrinsic nature, the <s>bodhisattva</s> does not approach the past, future, or middle. Because the <s>bodhyaṅgas</s> (limbs of awakening) are non-existent, empty, isolated, and without intrinsic nature, the <s>bodhisattva</s> does not approach the past, future, or middle. Because the <s>mārgas</s> (path-factors) are non-existent, empty, isolated, and without intrinsic nature, the <s>bodhisattva</s> does not approach the past, future, or middle. Because the immeasurable <s>dhyānas</s> (meditations) and formless attainments (<s>ārūpyasamāpattis</s>) are non-existent, empty, isolated, and without intrinsic nature, the <s>bodhisattva</s> does not approach the past, future, or middle. Because the <s>Tathāgata</s> powers (<s>tathāgatabalas</s>) are non-existent, empty, isolated, and without intrinsic nature, the <s>bodhisattva</s> does not approach the past, future, or middle. Because the confidences (<s>vaiśāradyas</s>) are non-existent, empty, isolated, and without intrinsic nature, the <s>bodhisattva</s> does not approach the past, future, or middle. Because the analytical knowledges (<s>pratisaṃvids</s>) are non-existent, empty, isolated, and without intrinsic nature, the <s>bodhisattva</s> does not approach the past, future, or middle. Because the <s>buddhadharmas</s> (buddha-qualities) are non-existent, empty, isolated, and without intrinsic nature, the <s>bodhisattva</s> does not approach the past, future, or middle. What is the reason? For, Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, in the non-existence, emptiness, isolation, and absence of intrinsic nature of the foundations of mindfulness, up to the non-existence, emptiness, isolation, and absence of intrinsic nature of the buddha-qualities, the past, future, and middle are not apprehended. And, <s>Śāriputra</s>, the non-existence is not one thing, the emptiness another, the isolation another, the absence of intrinsic nature another, the <s>bodhisattva</s> another, and the past, future, and middle yet another. For indeed, Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, the foundations of mindfulness — their non-existence, emptiness, isolation, and absence of intrinsic nature — up to the buddha-qualities — their non-existence, emptiness, isolation, and absence of intrinsic nature — and the <s>bodhisattva</s>, and the past, future, and middle — all of this is without duality. By this method, Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s> does not approach the past, future, or middle. Furthermore, Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, because all <s>samādhis</s> (concentrations) are non-existent, because all <s>dhāraṇīmukhas</s> (gateways of retention) are non-existent, because the <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of reality) is non-existent, because <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) is non-existent, because <s>bhūtakoṭi</s> (the limit of reality) is non-existent, because the limit of reality is empty, isolated, and without intrinsic nature — the <s>bodhisattva</s> does not approach the past, future, or middle. What is the reason? For, Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, in the non-existence of <s>samādhis</s>, up to the non-existence of <s>bhūtakoṭi</s>, in their emptiness, isolation, and absence of intrinsic nature, the past, future, and middle are not apprehended. And, <s>Śāriputra</s>, the non-existence is not one thing, the emptiness another, the isolation another, the absence of intrinsic nature another, the <s>bodhisattva</s> another, and the past, future, and middle yet another. For indeed, Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, the <s>samādhis</s> — their non-existence, emptiness, isolation, and absence of intrinsic nature — up to <s>bhūtakoṭi</s> — its non-existence, emptiness, isolation, and absence of intrinsic nature — and the <s>bodhisattva</s>, and the past, future, and middle — all of this is without duality. By this method, Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s> does not approach the past, future, or middle. Furthermore, Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, because <s>śrāvakas</s> (disciples) are non-existent, empty, isolated, and without intrinsic nature, the <s>bodhisattva</s> does not approach the past, future, or middle. Because <s>pratyekabuddhas</s> (solitary awakened ones) are non-existent, because <s>bodhisattvas</s> are non-existent, because <s>sarvajñatā</s> (omniscience) is non-existent, empty, isolated, and without intrinsic nature — the <s>bodhisattva</s> does not approach the past, future, or middle. What is the reason? For, Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, in the non-existence of <s>śrāvakas</s>, up to the non-existence of <s>sarvajñatā</s>, in their emptiness, isolation, and absence of intrinsic nature, the past, future, and middle are not apprehended. And, <s>Śāriputra</s>, the non-existence is not one thing, the emptiness another, the isolation another, the absence of intrinsic nature another, the <s>bodhisattva</s> another, and the past, future, and middle yet another. For indeed, Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, <s>śrāvakas</s> — their non-existence, emptiness, isolation, and absence of intrinsic nature — up to <s>sarvajñatā</s> — its non-existence, emptiness, isolation, and absence of intrinsic nature — and the <s>bodhisattva</s>, and the past, future, and middle — all of this is without duality. By this method, Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s> does not approach the past, future, or middle. children.translated_text: Just as, Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, the past of space is not apprehended, the future is not apprehended, and the middle is not apprehended — by virtue of its endlessness and boundlessness, it is conventionally designated 'space' — just so, Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, the past of form is not apprehended, the future is not apprehended, and the middle is not apprehended. For what reason? Because of the emptiness of form. And the past, future, or middle of emptiness is not apprehended. Likewise for feeling, perception, volitional formations — the past, future, or middle of consciousness is not apprehended. For what reason? Because of the emptiness of consciousness. And the past, future, or middle of emptiness is not apprehended — yet it is conventionally designated 'emptiness.' By this method, Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, by the boundlessness of form, the boundlessness of the <s>bodhisattva</s> should be understood. Likewise for feeling, perception, and volitional formations — by the boundlessness of consciousness, the boundlessness of the <s>bodhisattva</s> should be understood. Likewise for the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), <s>dhātus</s> (elements), <s>āyatanas</s> (sense-bases), and links of dependent origination, whether taken individually or collectively, up to old age, death, grief, lamentation, suffering, dejection, and tribulation. The foundations of mindfulness (<s>smṛtyupasthāna</s>), right efforts (<s>samyakprahāṇa</s>), bases of supernatural power (<s>ṛddhipāda</s>), faculties (<s>indriya</s>), powers (<s>bala</s>), factors of awakening (<s>bodhyaṅga</s>), path, immeasurables (<s>apramāṇa</s>), <s>dhyānas</s>, formless attainments (<s>ārūpyasamāpatti</s>), ten powers (<s>daśabala</s>), fearlessnesses (<s>vaiśāradya</s>), analytical knowledges (<s>pratisaṃvid</s>), and the eighteen unique qualities of a <s>Buddha</s> (<s>āveṇika buddhadharma</s>), Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, are equal to space. For what reason? Just as, Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, the beginning, end, or middle of space is not apprehended — by virtue of its endlessness and boundlessness it is conventionally designated 'space' — just so, Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, the beginning, end, or middle of the <s>Buddha</s> qualities is not apprehended, because of the emptiness of the <s>Buddha</s> qualities. And the past, future, or middle of emptiness is not apprehended. By this method, Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, by the boundlessness of the <s>Buddha</s> qualities, the boundlessness of the <s>bodhisattva</s> should be understood. As for your statement, Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>: 'For what reason is form not found or apprehended as the <s>bodhisattva</s>? And feeling, perception, volitional formations, and consciousness are not found or apprehended as the <s>bodhisattva</s>?' — form, Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, is empty of form; feeling, perception, volitional formations, and consciousness, Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, are empty of consciousness. The instruction and admonition is not found in <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> and is not apprehended. <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is not found in the instruction and admonition and is not apprehended. Thus indeed, Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, all <s>dharmas</s> are such that, through their being-found-ness and through non-apprehension, a <s>bodhisattva</s> is not found and is not apprehended. [Thus in the going-forth through attainment, the negation of the attainer.]
Furthermore, as the Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> said thus: 'For what reason is it a mere designation, namely "<s>bodhisattva</s>"?'—for what reason, Venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, do you say thus: 'This designation is adventitious, imposed—namely "<s>bodhisattva</s>"'? Because, Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, a name does not come from any of the ten directions, does not go anywhere, does not stand anywhere. Even the names of all <s>dharmas</s> and of <s>bodhisattvas</s> do not come from anywhere, do not go anywhere, do not stand anywhere. This designation is adventitious, for what is designated as form, feeling, perception, formations, or consciousness—that is not form, not feeling, not perception, not formations, not consciousness. Furthermore, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, it is merely a designation that '<s>dānapāramitā</s>' (perfection of generosity) [is spoken of]. The name is not in the <s>dānapāramitā</s>, nor is the <s>dānapāramitā</s> in the name. For what reason? Both the name and the <s>dānapāramitā</s> are not found and not apprehended. Therefore it is merely a designation that '<s>bodhisattva</s>' [is spoken of]. Likewise, it is merely a designation that '<s>śīlapāramitā</s>' (perfection of morality), '<s>kṣāntipāramitā</s>' (perfection of patience), '<s>vīryapāramitā</s>' (perfection of vigor), '<s>dhyānapāramitā</s>' (perfection of meditation), and '<s>prajñāpāramitā</s>' (perfection of wisdom) [are spoken of]. [The name is not in the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, nor is the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> in the name. For what reason? Both the name and the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> are not found and not apprehended. Therefore it is merely a designation that '<s>bodhisattva</s>' is spoken of.] This is adventitious (<s>āgantuka</s>), merely a designation, that '<s>bodhisattva</s>' [is spoken of].
It is merely a designation that '<s>adhyātmaśūnyatā</s>' (internal emptiness), '<s>bahirdhāśūnyatā</s>' (external emptiness), '<s>adhyātmabahirdhāśūnyatā</s>' (internal-external emptiness), up to '<s>abhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā</s>' (emptiness of the non-existence of own-nature) [are spoken of]. The name is not in <s>adhyātmaśūnyatā</s>, nor are <s>adhyātmaśūnyatā</s>, <s>bahirdhāśūnyatā</s>, <s>adhyātmabahirdhāśūnyatā</s>, up to <s>bhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā</s> in the name. For what reason? For the name, <s>adhyātmaśūnyatā</s>, <s>bahirdhāśūnyatā</s>, <s>adhyātmabahirdhāśūnyatā</s>, and up to <s>bhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā</s> — all these are not found and not apprehended. By this method, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, it is merely a designation that '<s>bodhisattva</s>' [is spoken of]. This is adventitious, merely a designation, that '<s>smṛtyupasthānas</s>' (foundations of mindfulness) [are spoken of]. The name is not in the <s>smṛtyupasthānas</s>, nor are the <s>smṛtyupasthānas</s> in the name. [For what reason? Both the name and the <s>smṛtyupasthānas</s> are not found and not apprehended. This is adventitious, merely a designation, that '<s>samyakprahāṇas</s>' (right efforts) [are spoken of]. Likewise for <s>ṛddhipādas</s> (bases of power), <s>indriyas</s> (faculties), <s>balas</s> (powers), <s>bodhyaṅgas</s> (factors of awakening), the path, <s>apramāṇadhyānas</s> (immeasurable meditations), formless attainments, the ten powers, <s>vaiśāradyas</s> (fearlessnesses), <s>pratisaṃvids</s> (analytical knowledges),] [and the eighteen exclusive <s>buddhadharmas</s> — the name is not in the eighteen exclusive <s>buddhadharmas</s>, nor are the eighteen exclusive <s>buddhadharmas</s> in the name. For what reason? Both the name and the eighteen exclusive <s>buddhadharmas</s> are not found and not apprehended.]
This is adventitious, merely a designation, that '<s>samādhi</s>' (concentration) up to '<s>sarvajñatā</s>' (omniscience) [is spoken of]. The name is not in <s>sarvajñatā</s>, nor is <s>sarvajñatā</s> in the name. For what reason? For both the name and <s>sarvajñatā</s> are not found and not apprehended.
Now, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, as to your statement: 'For what reason is it said "self" (<s>ātman</s>) — it is indeed called "self," yet ultimately the self is unproduced?' — <s>Śāriputra</s>, the self is ultimately not found and not apprehended. How then could there be attachment to it? Ultimately, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, a being (<s>sattva</s>), a life-force (<s>jīva</s>), a nourisher (<s>poṣa</s>), [a person (<s>puruṣa</s>), an individual (<s>pudgala</s>), a human (<s>manuja</s>), a youth (<s>mānava</s>), a doer (<s>kāraka</s>), an experiencer (<s>vedaka</s>), a knower (<s>jānaka</s>),] a seer (<s>paśyaka</s>) is not found and not apprehended. How then could there be attachment to any of them? Ultimately, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, <s>rūpa</s> (form) is not found and not apprehended. How then could there be attachment to it? <s>Vedanā</s> (feeling), <s>saṃjñā</s> (perception), <s>saṃskāras</s> (formations) — ultimately, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness) is not found and not apprehended. How then could there be attachment to it? [Ultimately, the eye, ear, nose, tongue, body, mind, forms, sounds, smells, tastes, tangibles, <s>dharmas</s>, the six consciousnesses, the six contacts — none of these are found or apprehended. How then could there be attachment to any of them?]

Ultimately, Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, <s>adhyātmaśūnyatā</s> (internal emptiness) is neither found nor apprehended — how then could its establishment come about? Likewise, <s>bahirdhāśūnyatā</s> (external emptiness), <s>adhyātmabahirdhāśūnyatā</s> (internal-external emptiness), up to: ultimately, Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, <s>abhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of the nature of non-existence) is neither found nor apprehended — how then could its establishment come about? Ultimately, Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, the <s>smṛtyupasthānas</s> (foundations of mindfulness) are neither found nor apprehended — how then could their establishment come about? Likewise, the <s>samyakprahāṇas</s> (right exertions), <s>ṛddhipādas</s> (bases of miraculous power), <s>indriyas</s> (faculties), <s>balas</s> (powers), <s>bodhyaṅgas</s> (factors of awakening), <s>mārgas</s> (paths), <s>apramāṇas</s> and <s>dhyānas</s>, formless attainments, ten powers, fearlessnesses, and analytical knowledges.
25202 Ultimately, Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, the eighteen unique <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s> are neither found nor apprehended — how then could their establishment come about? Ultimately, the <s>samādhis</s> and <s>dhāraṇīmukhas</s> (gateways of retention) are neither found nor apprehended — how then could their establishment come about? Ultimately,
25203 a <s>Śrāvaka</s>, a <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>, a <s>bodhisattva</s>, a <s>Tathāgata</s>, an <s>Arhat</s>, a Perfectly Awakened One is neither found nor apprehended — how then could its establishment come about?

25205 unestablished.
25206 Furthermore, as Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> has said: 'All <s>dharmas</s> are without own-nature' —
25207 so it is. For what reason? For, Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, there is no conjunctive own-nature.
25208 <s>Śāriputra</s> said: Of what, Venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, is there no conjunctive own-nature?

25210 <s>saṃjñā</s> (perception), <s>saṃskāras</s> (formations), and <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness), Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, there is no conjunctive own-nature.
25211 Of the eye, Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, there is no conjunctive own-nature; of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind, Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, there is no conjunctive own-nature; of form [as object], Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, there is no conjunctive own-nature; of sound, smell, taste, touch, and mental objects, Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, there is no conjunctive own-nature; of eye-consciousness, Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, there is no conjunctive own-nature; of ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-consciousness, Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, there is no conjunctive own-nature; of eye-contact, Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, there is no conjunctive own-nature; of ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact, Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, there is no conjunctive own-nature; of feeling conditioned by eye-contact, Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, there is no conjunctive own-nature; of feeling conditioned by ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact, Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, there is no conjunctive own-nature.
25212 Of the <s>dānapāramitā</s>, Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, there is no conjunctive own-nature; of the <s>śīlapāramitā</s>, <s>kṣāntipāramitā</s>, <s>vīryapāramitā</s>, <s>dhyānapāramitā</s> — there is no conjunctive own-nature of the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>

25214 Furthermore, Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, all <s>dharmas</s> are impermanent — not through the passing away of anything.

25217 Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, are impermanent, not through the passing away of anything. For what reason? For, Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>,
25218 that which is impermanent is non-existent and subject to destruction. Likewise, [all <s>dharmas</s> are] suffering, non-self, peaceful, empty, signless,
25219 and wishless — not through the passing away of anything. All <s>dharmas</s> are wholesome, blameless, without outflows,
25220 free from defilements, transcendent, without purification, and unconditioned. For what reason? For,
25221 Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, that which is unconditioned is non-existent and subject to destruction. By this method, Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, all <s>dharmas</s> are without own-nature,
25222 not through the passing away of anything.
25223 Furthermore, <s>Śāriputra</s>, all <s>dharmas</s> are neither stationary nor destructible.

<s>Subhūti</s> said: Form, Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, is neither immutable nor perishable. For what reason? Because this is its nature. <s>Vedanā</s> (feeling), <s>saṃjñā</s> (perception), <s>saṃskāras</s> (formations)—<s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness), Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, is neither immutable nor perishable. For what reason? Because this is its nature. Likewise the wholesome and the unwholesome, the blameworthy and the blameless, that with outflows and that without outflows, the defiled and the undefiled, the worldly and the supramundane, the conditioned and the unconditioned, affliction and purification, <s>saṃsāra</s> and <s>nirvāṇa</s>—are neither immutable nor perishable. For what reason? Because this is their nature. By this manner of explanation, Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, all <s>dharmas</s> are without self-nature.
As to what the Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> said: 'For what reason is form unconditioned? Likewise <s>vedanā</s>, <s>saṃjñā</s>, <s>saṃskāras</s>—for what reason is <s>vijñāna</s> unconditioned?'
<s>Subhūti</s> said: Because, Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, form has not arisen into actual existence; <s>vedanā</s>, <s>saṃjñā</s>, <s>saṃskāras</s>, <s>vijñāna</s> have not arisen into actual existence. For what reason? Because, Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, there is no conditioner. The eye, Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, is unconditioned. For what reason? Because, Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, there is no conditioner. Likewise the ear, nose, tongue, body—the mind is unconditioned. For what reason? Because, Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, there is no conditioner. Furthermore, <s>Śāriputra</s>, form, sound, smell, taste, touch, and <s>dharmas</s> are unconditioned. For what reason? Because no conditioner is apprehended. And so on up to: all <s>dharmas</s> are unconditioned. For what reason? Because no conditioner is apprehended. By this manner of explanation, Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness have not arisen into actual existence.
As to what the Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> further said: 'For what reason is what has not arisen into actual existence neither form, nor feeling, nor perception, nor formations, nor consciousness?'
<s>Subhūti</s> said: Because, Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, form is empty by nature. And what is empty by nature—for that there is no arising and no destruction. And for what has no arising and no destruction, no alteration is discerned. <s>Vedanā</s>, <s>saṃjñā</s>, <s>saṃskāras</s>, <s>vijñāna</s>—are empty by nature. And what is empty by nature—for that there is no arising and no destruction. And for what has no arising and no destruction, no alteration is discerned. Likewise, and so on up to: all <s>dharmas</s> are empty by nature. And for those that are empty by nature, there is no arising and no destruction. And for those for which there is no arising and no destruction, no alteration is discerned. By this manner of explanation, Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, what has not arisen into actual existence is neither form, nor feeling, nor perception, nor formations, nor consciousness.

children.translated_text: As for your further statement, Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>: 'For what reason do you say: "Shall I instruct and admonish non-retrogression in <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> which is itself non-retrogression (<s>anabhinivṛtti</s>)?"' — Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, that which is non-retrogression is <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, and that which is <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is non-retrogression. Thus <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> and non-retrogression are non-dual and undivided. By this method, Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, I say: 'Shall I instruct and admonish non-retrogression in <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> which is itself non-retrogression?' As for your further statement, Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>: 'Apart from non-retrogression, no <s>bodhisattva</s> is to be apprehended who would practice for awakening' — Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, coursing in <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, does not perceive non-retrogression as one thing and the <s>bodhisattva</s> as another. For non-retrogression and the <s>bodhisattva</s> are non-dual and undivided. Nor does he perceive form apart from non-retrogression — for non-retrogression and form are non-dual and undivided. Likewise, non-retrogression and feeling are non-dual and undivided; non-retrogression and perception are non-dual and undivided; non-retrogression and volitional formations are non-dual and undivided; non-retrogression and consciousness are non-dual and undivided. Non-retrogression and the eye are non-dual and undivided; likewise the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind. Non-retrogression and form (visible objects), sound, smell, taste, tangible objects, and <s>dharmas</s> (mental objects) — each is non-dual and undivided with non-retrogression. Non-retrogression and eye-consciousness, ear-consciousness, nose-consciousness, tongue-consciousness, body-consciousness, and mind-consciousness — each is non-dual and undivided. Non-retrogression and eye-contact, ear-contact, nose-contact, tongue-contact, body-contact, and mind-contact — each is non-dual and undivided. Non-retrogression and feeling conditioned by eye-contact, ear-contact, nose-contact, tongue-contact, body-contact, and mind-contact — each is non-dual and undivided. Non-retrogression and the right efforts (<s>samyakprahāṇa</s>), bases of supernatural power (<s>ṛddhipāda</s>), faculties (<s>indriya</s>), powers (<s>bala</s>), factors of awakening (<s>bodhyaṅga</s>), the path, the immeasurables (<s>apramāṇa</s>), <s>dhyānas</s>, and formless attainments (<s>ārūpyasamāpatti</s>) — each is non-dual and undivided. Non-retrogression and the perfection of generosity (<s>dānapāramitā</s>), the perfection of morality (<s>śīlapāramitā</s>), patience (<s>kṣāntipāramitā</s>), vigor (<s>vīryapāramitā</s>), meditation (<s>dhyānapāramitā</s>), and wisdom (<s>prajñāpāramitā</s>) — each is non-dual and undivided. Non-retrogression and the ten powers (<s>daśabala</s>), fearlessnesses (<s>vaiśāradya</s>), and eighteen unique qualities of a <s>Buddha</s> (<s>āveṇika buddhadharma</s>) — these are non-dual and undivided. And finally, non-retrogression and all <s>dharmas</s> are non-dual and undivided. By this method, Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, apart from non-retrogression, no <s>bodhisattva</s> is to be apprehended who would practice for awakening. As for your further statement, Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>: 'For what reason do you say: "If, when a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> is being thus instructed, his mind does not sink down, does not become depressed, does not feel regret, is not terrified, not frightened, does not fall into dread — then the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> courses in <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>"?' — Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> perceives all <s>dharmas</s> as without impulse, like an illusion, like a dream, like a mirage, like an echo, like a reflection, like a mirror-image, like a magical creation, like a city of <s>gandharvas</s>. By this method, Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, when the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> is being thus instructed, his mind does not sink down, does not become depressed, does not feel regret, is not terrified, not frightened, does not fall into dread — and the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> courses in <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Subhūti</s> spoke thus to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: "At the time, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, when a <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s>, practicing in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> (Perfection of Wisdom), examines these <s>dharmas</s>, at that time he does not approach <s>rūpa</s> (form), does not take it up, does not abide in it, does not become attached to it, and does not designate 'this is <s>rūpa</s>.' At the time, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, when a <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s>, practicing in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, examines these <s>dharmas</s>, at that time he does not approach <s>vedanā</s> (feeling), does not take it up, does not abide in it, does not become attached to it, and does not designate 'this is <s>vedanā</s>.' At the time when a <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s>, practicing in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, examines these <s>dharmas</s>, at that time he does not approach <s>saṃjñā</s> (perception), does not take it up, does not abide in it, does not become attached to it, and does not designate 'this is <s>saṃjñā</s>.' At the time when a <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s>, practicing in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, examines these <s>dharmas</s>, at that time he does not approach the <s>saṃskāras</s> (volitional formations), does not take them up, does not abide in them, does not become attached to them, and does not designate 'these are <s>saṃskāras</s>.' At the time when a <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s>, practicing in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, examines these <s>dharmas</s>, at that time he does not approach <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness), does not take it up, does not abide in it, does not become attached to it, and does not designate 'this is <s>vijñāna</s>.' At the time when a <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s>, practicing in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, examines these <s>dharmas</s>, at that time he does not approach the eye, does not take it up, does not abide in it, does not become attached to it, and does not designate 'this is the eye.' Likewise, at that time he does not approach the ear, does not take it up, does not abide in it, does not become attached to it, and does not designate 'this is the ear.' He does not approach the nose and does not designate 'this is the nose.' He does not approach the tongue and does not designate 'this is the tongue.' He does not approach the body and does not designate 'this is the body.' He does not approach the mind and does not designate 'this is the mind.' He does not approach visible form and does not designate 'this is visible form.' He does not approach sound and does not designate 'this is sound.' He does not approach smell and does not designate 'this is smell.' He does not approach taste and does not designate 'this is taste.' He does not approach the tangible and does not designate 'this is the tangible.' He does not approach <s>dharmas</s> (mental objects) and does not designate 'this is a <s>dharma</s>.' He does not approach eye-consciousness and does not designate 'this is eye-consciousness.' He does not approach ear-consciousness, nose-consciousness, tongue-consciousness, body-consciousness, or mind-consciousness, and does not designate 'this is mind-consciousness.' At that time he does not approach <s>dānapāramitā</s> (perfection of generosity), does not take it up, does not abide in it, does not become attached to it, and does not designate 'this is <s>dānapāramitā</s>.' Likewise he does not approach <s>śīlapāramitā</s> (perfection of morality), <s>kṣāntipāramitā</s> (perfection of patience), <s>vīryapāramitā</s> (perfection of vigor), <s>dhyānapāramitā</s> (perfection of meditation), or <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> (perfection of wisdom), and does not designate them as such. At that time he does not approach <s>adhyātmaśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of the internal), does not take it up, does not abide in it, does not become attached to it, and does not designate 'this is <s>adhyātmaśūnyatā</s>.' Likewise he does not approach <s>bahirdhāśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of the external), <s>adhyātmabahirdhāśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of the internal and external), <s>śūnyatāśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of emptiness), <s>mahāśūnyatā</s> (great emptiness), <s>paramārthaśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of the ultimate), <s>saṃskṛtaśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of the conditioned), <s>atyantaśūnyatā</s> (absolute emptiness), <s>anavarāgraśūnyatā</s> (emptiness without beginning or end), <s>prakṛtiśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of inherent nature), <s>sarvadharmaśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of all dharmas), <s>svalakṣaṇaśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of own-characteristics), <s>anupalambhaśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of non-apprehension), <s>abhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of the nature of non-existence), <s>bhāvaśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of existence), <s>abhāvaśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of non-existence), <s>svabhāvaśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of own-nature), or <s>parabhāvaśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of other-nature), and does not designate them as such. At that time he does not approach the <s>smṛtyupasthānas</s> (foundations of mindfulness), does not take them up, does not abide in them, does not become attached to them, and does not designate 'these are the <s>smṛtyupasthānas</s>.' Likewise he does not approach the <s>samyakprahāṇas</s> (right exertions), the <s>ṛddhipādas</s> (bases of supernatural power), the <s>indriyas</s> (faculties), the <s>balas</s> (powers), the <s>bodhyaṅgas</s> (factors of awakening), the <s>mārgas</s> (path factors), the <s>apramāṇas</s> (immeasurables) and <s>dhyānas</s> (meditations), the <s>ārūpyasamāpattis</s> (formless attainments), the ten powers (<s>daśabala</s>), the <s>vaiśāradyas</s> (fearlessnesses), the <s>pratisaṃvids</s> (analytical knowledges), or the eighteen distinctive <s>Buddha-dharmas</s> (<s>aṣṭādaśāveṇikabuddhadharma</s>), and does not designate them as such. At that time, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, a <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s>, practicing in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, examines these <s>dharmas</s> — at that time he does not approach the gates of <s>samādhi</s> (concentration) and <s>dhāraṇī</s> (retention), does not become attached to them, and does not designate 'these are the gates of <s>samādhi</s> and <s>dhāraṇī</s>.' What is the reason? For indeed, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> practicing in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> does not perceive <s>rūpa</s> (form), nor does he perceive the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), <s>dhātus</s> (elements), and <s>āyatanas</s> (sense-bases) in their separate and combined aspects, nor does he perceive <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination). He does not perceive the thirty-seven <s>bodhipakṣa dharmas</s> (factors conducive to awakening). He does not perceive the <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections). He does not perceive the <s>apramāṇas</s> (immeasurables), the <s>dhyānas</s> (meditations), the <s>ārūpyasamāpattis</s> (formless attainments), the ten powers (<s>daśabala</s>), the <s>vaiśāradyas</s> (fearlessnesses), the <s>pratisaṃvids</s> (analytical knowledges), the eighteen distinctive <s>Buddha-dharmas</s>, nor even <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> (omniscience). What is the reason? For indeed, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, that which is the non-arising (<s>anutpāda</s>) of <s>rūpa</s> is not <s>rūpa</s>. That which is the non-arising of <s>vedanā</s> (feeling), <s>saṃjñā</s> (perception), and <s>saṃskāras</s> (formations) — that which is the non-arising of <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness) is not <s>vijñāna</s>; for <s>vijñāna</s> and non-arising are non-dual (<s>advaya</s>), undivided (<s>advaidhīkāra</s>). That which is the non-arising of the eye, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, is not the eye. That which is the non-arising of the ear, nose, tongue, body — that which is the non-arising of the mind is not the mind; for the mind and non-arising are non-dual, undivided. That which is the non-arising of visible form, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, is not visible form. That which is the non-arising of sound, smell, taste, the tangible — that which is the non-arising of <s>dharmas</s> (mental objects) is not a <s>dharma</s>; for <s>dharma</s> and non-arising are non-dual, undivided. That which is the non-arising of eye-consciousness, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, is not eye-consciousness. That which is the non-arising of ear-consciousness, nose-consciousness, tongue-consciousness, body-consciousness — that which is the non-arising of mind-consciousness is not mind-consciousness; for mind-consciousness and non-arising are non-dual, undivided. That which is the non-arising of <s>dānapāramitā</s>, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, is not <s>dānapāramitā</s>. That which is the non-arising of <s>śīlapāramitā</s>, <s>kṣāntipāramitā</s>, <s>vīryapāramitā</s>, <s>dhyānapāramitā</s> — that which is the non-arising of <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> is not <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>; for <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> and non-arising are non-dual, undivided. That which is the non-arising of <s>adhyātmaśūnyatā</s>, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, is not <s>adhyātmaśūnyatā</s>. That which is the non-arising of <s>bahirdhāśūnyatā</s>, <s>adhyātmabahirdhāśūnyatā</s>, <s>śūnyatāśūnyatā</s>, <s>mahāśūnyatā</s>, <s>paramārthaśūnyatā</s>, <s>saṃskṛtaśūnyatā</s>, <s>atyantaśūnyatā</s>, <s>anavarāgraśūnyatā</s>, <s>anavakāraśūnyatā</s>, <s>prakṛtiśūnyatā</s>, <s>sarvadharmaśūnyatā</s>, <s>svalakṣaṇaśūnyatā</s>, <s>anupalambhaśūnyatā</s>, <s>abhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā</s>, <s>bhāvaśūnyatā</s>, <s>abhāvaśūnyatā</s>, <s>svabhāvaśūnyatā</s> — that which is the non-arising of <s>parabhāvaśūnyatā</s> is not <s>parabhāvaśūnyatā</s>; for <s>parabhāvaśūnyatā</s> and non-arising are non-dual, undivided. That which is the non-arising of the <s>smṛtyupasthānas</s> (foundations of mindfulness), O <s>Bhagavān</s>, is not the <s>smṛtyupasthānas</s>. That which is the non-arising of the <s>samyakprahāṇas</s>, <s>ṛddhipādas</s>, <s>indriyas</s>, <s>balas</s>, <s>bodhyaṅgas</s>, <s>mārgas</s>, <s>apramāṇas</s> and <s>dhyānas</s>, <s>ārūpyasamāpattis</s>, the ten powers, the <s>vaiśāradyas</s>, the <s>pratisaṃvids</s> — that which is the non-arising of the eighteen distinctive <s>Buddha-dharmas</s> is not the <s>Buddha-dharmas</s>; for the <s>Buddha-dharmas</s> and non-arising are non-dual, undivided. That which is the non-arising of <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of dharmas), O <s>Bhagavān</s>, is not the <s>dharmadhātu</s>. That which is the non-arising of <s>tathatā</s> (suchness), of the element of space (<s>ākāśadhātu</s>), of the limit of reality (<s>bhūtakoṭi</s>), of the inconceivable realm (<s>acintyadhātu</s>), of awakening (<s>bodhi</s>) — that which is the non-arising of <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> (omniscience) is not <s>sarvākārajñatā</s>; for <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> and non-arising are non-dual, undivided. What is the reason? For indeed non-arising is not one, not two, not many, and not separate. Therefore, that which is the non-arising of <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> is not <s>sarvākārajñatā</s>. That which is the cessation (<s>vyaya</s>) of <s>rūpa</s> (form), O <s>Bhagavān</s>, is not <s>rūpa</s>. That which is the cessation of <s>vedanā</s> (feeling), <s>saṃjñā</s> (perception), <s>saṃskāras</s> (formations) — that which is the cessation of <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness) is not <s>vijñāna</s>; for the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates) and cessation are non-dual, undivided. What is the reason? For indeed cessation is not one, not two, not many, and not separate. Therefore, that which is the cessation of the five <s>skandhas</s> is not the five <s>skandhas</s>. 25601 the destruction of the <s>dānapāramitā</s> — that is not the <s>dānapāramitā</s>. That which is, <s>Bhagavān</s>, the destruction of the <s>śīlapāramitā</s> — that is not the <s>dānapāramitā</s>. [Likewise] the destruction of the <s>kṣāntipāramitā</s>, the destruction of the <s>vīryapāramitā</s>, the destruction of the <s>dhyānapāramitā</s>, the destruction of the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> — that is not the <s>dānapāramitā</s>.
25602 That which is, <s>Bhagavān</s>, the destruction of <s>adhyātmaśūnyatā</s> (internal emptiness) — that is not <s>adhyātmaśūnyatā</s>; the destruction of <s>bahirdhāśūnyatā</s> (external emptiness) — that is not <s>bahirdhāśūnyatā</s>; the destruction of <s>adhyātmabahirdhāśūnyatā</s> (internal-external emptiness) — that is not <s>adhyātmabahirdhāśūnyatā</s>; [likewise for] <s>śūnyatāśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of emptiness), <s>mahāśūnyatā</s> (great emptiness), <s>paramārthaśūnyatā</s> (ultimate emptiness), <s>saṃskṛtaśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of the conditioned), <s>atyantaśūnyatā</s> (absolute emptiness), <s>anavarāgraśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of beginninglessness), <s>anavakāraśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of non-dispersal), <s>prakṛtiśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of nature), <s>sarvadharmaśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of all dharmas), <s>svalakṣaṇaśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of own-characteristics), <s>anupalambhaśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of non-apprehension), <s>abhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of the nature of non-existence), <s>bhāvaśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of existence), <s>abhāvaśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of non-existence), <s>svabhāvaśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of own-nature), <s>parabhāvaśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of other-nature); the destruction of the <s>smṛtyupasthānas</s> (foundations of mindfulness) — those are not the <s>smṛtyupasthānas</s>; [likewise for] the <s>samyakprahāṇas</s>, <s>ṛddhipādas</s>, <s>indriyas</s>, <s>balas</s>, <s>bodhyaṅgas</s>, <s>mārgas</s>, <s>apramāṇas</s> and <s>dhyānas</s>, formless attainments, ten powers, fearlessnesses, analytical knowledges, and the eighteen unique <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s> — the destruction of the <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s> is not the <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>. For the <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s> and their destruction are non-dual, undivided. For what reason? For destruction is neither one nor two nor many,
25603 nor separate. Therefore, the destruction of the <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s> is not the <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>.
25604 As for, <s>Bhagavān</s>, the expression '<s>rūpa</s>' — this is a designation of the non-dual. <s>Vedanā</s>, <s>saṃjñā</s>, <s>saṃskāras</s> —
25605 as for the expression '<s>vijñāna</s>' — this is a designation of the non-dual. As for the expressions '<s>rūpa</s>'
25606 up to '<s>sarvākārajñatā</s>' — these are designations of the non-dual. [Thus, in the departure through attainment,
25607 the negation of the relationship between what is attained and what attains.]
25608 Then Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> said to Venerable <s>Subhūti</s>: How, Venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, does a <s>bodhisattva</s>-
25609 <s>mahāsattva</s> practicing the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> examine these <s>dharmas</s>? Which, Venerable <s>Subhūti</s>,
25610 is the <s>bodhisattva</s>? Which is the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>? Which is the
25611 examination? <s>Subhūti</s> said: As Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> has said: 'Which is the <s>bodhisattva</s>?' — <s>bodhi</s>
25612 itself is the <s>sattva</s> (being); therefore it is called <s>bodhisattva</s>. And through that <s>bodhi</s>, one knows the aspects of all <s>dharmas</s>,
25613 yet does not settle into it.
25614 The aspects of which <s>dharmas</s> does one know? One knows the aspects of <s>rūpa</s>,
25615 yet does not settle into it. One knows the aspects of <s>vedanā</s>, yet does not settle into it; the aspects of <s>saṃjñā</s>, yet does not settle into it; the aspects of <s>saṃskāras</s>, yet does not settle into it; one knows the aspects of <s>vijñāna</s>, yet does not settle into it. Likewise,
25616 one knows the aspects of the <s>skandhas</s>, <s>dhātus</s>, and <s>āyatanas</s>, severally and collectively, and of <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination), and of the thirty-seven <s>bodhipakṣa</s>
25617 <s>dharmas</s> (factors conducive to awakening), yet does not settle into them. Likewise, one knows the aspects of the <s>apramāṇas</s>, <s>dhyānas</s>, formless attainments,
25618 <s>pāramitās</s>, powers, fearlessnesses, analytical knowledges, and unique <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>,
25619 yet does not settle into them.
25620 <s>Śāriputra</s> said: What, <s>Subhūti</s>, are those aspects of all <s>dharmas</s>?
25621 <s>Subhūti</s> said: Those aspects, Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, those marks, those signs by which forms, sounds, smells, tastes,
25622 tangibles, and mental objects — or internal and external <s>dharmas</s>, conditioned or unconditioned — [are characterized], those aspects by which
25623 they are so designated — these are called the aspects of all <s>dharmas</s>.
25624 As for Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>'s question: 'Which is the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>?' —

children.text:
25701 āratā āramitaiṣā {āyuṣman} {śāriputra} tenocyate prajñāpāramiteti/ kuta āratā
25702 āramitā/ skandhebhyo dhātubhya āyatanebhya pratītyasamutpādād dānapāramitāyāḥ
25703 śīla{pāramitāyāḥ} {{kṣāntipāramitāyā vīryapāramitāyā dhyānapāramitāyāḥ}} prajñāpāramitāyā āratā āramitā/ adhyātmaśūnyatāyā
25704 {{bahirdhāśūnyatāyā adhyātmabahirdhāśūnyatāyā}} yāvad abhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatāyā āratā āramitā/ smṛtyupasthānebhya
25705 āratā āramitā/ samyakprahāṇ{{ebhya ṛddhipādebhya indriyebhyo balebhyo bodhyaṅgebhyo mārgebhyo 'pramāṇadhyānebhya ārūpyasamāpattibhyo daśabalebhyo vaiśāradyebhyaḥ pratisaṃvidbhyo 'ṣṭādaśāveṇikebhyo}} buddhadharmebhya āratā āramitā/
25706 yāvat sarvajñatāyā āratā āramitā/ eṣā tenocyate prajñāpāramiteti/ ane-
25707 n{āyuṣman} {śāriputra} paryāyeṇa āratā āramitā eṣā yad uta prajñāpāramitā/
25708 yat punar {āyuṣman} {śāriputra} evaṃ vadasi/ katamā upaparīkṣaṇeti/ ih{āyuṣman} {śāriputra} {bodhisattvo}
25709 mahāsattvaḥ prajñāpāramitāyāṃ caran rūpaṃ na nityam ity upaparīkṣate nānityam iti
25710 na sukham iti na duḥkham iti nātmeti nānātmeti na śāntam iti nāśāntam iti
25711 na śūnyam iti nāśāunyam iti na nimittam iti nānimittam iti na praṇihitam iti
25712 nāpraṇihitam iti upaparīkṣate/ na viviktam iti nāviviktam ity upaparīkṣate/
25713 na vedanāṃ na saṃjñāṃ na saṃskārān na vijñānaṃ nityam ity upaparīkṣate/ nānityam iti
25714 {{na sukham iti na duḥkham iti nātmeti nānātmeti na śāntam iti nāśāntam iti na śūnyam iti nāśāunyam iti na nimittam iti nānimittam iti na praṇihitam iti nāpraṇihitam ity upaparīkṣate/ na viviktam iti nāviviktam ity upaparīkṣate/}} evaṃ cakṣuḥ śrotraṃ ghrāṇaṃ jihvāṃ kāyaṃ mano na nityam iti
25715 {{upaparīkṣate/ nānityam iti na sukham iti na duḥkham iti nātmeti nānātmeti na śāntam iti nāśāntam iti na śūnyam iti nāśāunyam iti na nimittam iti nānimittam iti na praṇihitam iti nāpraṇihitam ity upaparīkṣate/ na viviktam iti nāviviktam ity upaparīkṣate/}} evaṃ rūpaśabdagandharasaspraṣṭavyadharmā na nityā iti
25716 {{upaparīkṣante/ nānityā iti na sukhā iti na duḥkhā iti nātmāna iti nānātmāna iti na śāntā iti nāśāntā iti na śūnyā iti nāśāunyā iti na nimittā iti nānimittā iti na praṇihitā iti nāpraṇihitā ity upaparīkṣante/ na viviktā iti nāviviktā ity upaparīkṣante/}} evaṃ cakṣurvijñānaṃ {{na nityam ity upaparīkṣate/ nānityam iti na sukham iti na duḥkham iti nātmeti nānātmeti na śāntam iti nāśāntam iti na śūnyam iti nāśāunyam iti na nimittam iti nānimittam iti na praṇihitam iti nāpraṇihitam ity upaparīkṣate/ na viviktam iti nāviviktam ity upaparīkṣate/ na śrotravijñānaṃ na ghrāṇavijñānaṃ na jihvāvijñānaṃ na kāyavijñānaṃ na manovijñānaṃ nityam ity upaparīkṣate/ nānityam iti na sukham iti na duḥkham iti nātmeti nānātmeti na śāntam iti nāśāntam iti na śūnyam iti nāśāunyam iti na nimittam iti nānimittam iti na praṇihitam iti nāpraṇihitam ity upaparīkṣate/ na viviktam iti nāviviktam ity upaparīkṣate/}}
25717 evaṃ cakṣuḥsaṃsparśo {{na nitya ity upaparīkṣate/ nānitya iti na sukha iti na duḥkha iti nātmeti nānātmeti na śānta iti nāśānta iti na śūnya iti nāśāunya iti na nimitta iti nānimitta iti na praṇihita iti nāpraṇihita ity upaparīkṣate/ na vivikta iti nāvivikta ity upaparīkṣate/ na śrotrasaṃsparśo na ghrāṇasaṃsparśo na jihvāsaṃsparśo na kāyasaṃsparśo na manaḥsaṃsparśo nitya ity upaparīkṣate/ nānitya iti na sukha iti na duḥkha iti nātmeti nānātmeti na śānta iti nāśānta iti na śūnya iti nāśāunya iti na nimitta iti nānimitta iti na praṇihita iti nāpraṇihita ity upaparīkṣate/ na vivikta iti nāvivikta ity upaparīkṣate/}}
25718 evaṃ cakṣuḥsaṃsparśapratyayavedanā {{na nityety upaparīkṣate/ nānityeti na sukheti na duḥkheti nātmeti nānātmeti na śānteti nāśānteti na śūnyeti nāśāunyeti na nimitteti nānimitteti na praṇihiteti nāpraṇihitety upaparīkṣate/ na vivikteti nāviviktety upaparīkṣate/}}
25719 {{na śrotrasaṃsparśapratyayavedanā na ghrāṇasaṃsparśapratyayavedanā na jihvāsaṃsparśapratyayavedanā na kāyasaṃsparśapratyayavedanā na manaḥsaṃsparśapratyayavedanā nityety upaparīkṣate/ nānityeti na sukheti na duḥkheti nātmeti nānātmeti na śānteti nāśānteti na śūnyeti nāśāunyeti na nimitteti nānimitteti na praṇihiteti nāpraṇihitety upaparīkṣate/ na vivikteti nāviviktety upaparīkṣate/}} evaṃ dānapāramitā {{na nityety upaparīkṣate/ nānityeti na sukheti na duḥkheti nātmeti nānātmeti na śānteti nāśānteti na śūnyeti nāśāunyeti na nimitteti nānimitteti na praṇihiteti nāpraṇihitety upaparīkṣate/ na vivikteti nāviviktety upaparīkṣate/}}
25720 {{na śīlapāramitā na kṣāntipāramitā na vīryapāramitā na dhyānapāramitā na prajñāpāramitā nityety upaparīkṣate/ nānityeti na sukheti na duḥkheti nātmeti nānātmeti na śānteti nāśānteti na śūnyeti nāśāunyeti na nimitteti nānimitteti na praṇihiteti nāpraṇihitety upaparīkṣate/ na vivikteti nāviviktety upaparīkṣate/}} evam adhyātmaśūnyatā {{na nityety upaparīkṣate/ nānityeti na sukheti na duḥkheti nātmeti nānātmeti na śānteti nāśānteti na śūnyeti nāśāunyeti na nimitteti nānimitteti na praṇihiteti nāpraṇihitety upaparīkṣate/ na vivikteti nāviviktety upaparīkṣate/}}
25721 {{na bahirdhāśūnyatā nādhyātmabahirdhāśūnyatā na śūnyatāśūnyatā na mahāśūnyatā na paramārthaśūnyatā na saṃskṛtaśūnyatā nātyantaśūnyatā nānavarāgraśūnyatā nānavakāraśūnyatā na prakṛtiśūnyatā na sarvadharmaśūnyatā na svalakṣaṇaśūnyatā nānupalambhaśūnyatā nābhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā na bhāvaśūnyatā nābhāvaśūnyatā na svabhāvaśūnyatā na parabhāvaśūnyatā nityety upaparīkṣate/ nānityeti na sukheti na duḥkheti nātmeti nānātmeti na śānteti nāśānteti na śūnyeti nāśāunyeti na nimitteti nānimitteti na praṇihiteti nāpraṇihitety upaparīkṣate/ na vivikteti nāviviktety upaparīkṣate/}} evaṃ smṛtyupasthānāni na nityānīti {{upaparīkṣante/ nānityānīti na sukhānīti na duḥkhānīti nātmānīti nānātmānīti na śāntānīti nāśāntānīti na śūnyānīti nāśāunyānīti na nimittānīti nānimittānīti na praṇihitānīti nāpraṇihitānīty upaparīkṣante/ na viviktānīti nāviviktānīty upaparīkṣante/}}
25722 evaṃ samyakprahāṇāni {{ṛddhipādā indriyāni balāni bodhyaṅgāni mārgā apramāṇadhyānāni ārūpyasamāpattayo daśabalāni vaiśāradyāni pratisaṃvidā aṣṭādaśāveṇikā}} buddhadharmāḥ/ samādhayaḥ sarva-
25723 dhāraṇīmukhāni sarvajñatā na nityeti {{upaparīkṣate/ nānityeti na sukheti na duḥkheti nātmeti nānātmeti na śānteti nāśānteti na śūnyeti nāśāunyeti na nimitteti nānimitteti na praṇihiteti nāpraṇihitety upaparīkṣate/ na vivikteti nāviviktety upaparīkṣate/}} evaṃ hy {āyuṣman} {śāriputra}
25724 {bodhisattvo} mahāsattvaḥ prajñāpāramitāyāṃ caran imān dharmān upaparīkṣate/
25725 {śāriputra} āha/ kena kāraṇen{āyuṣman} {subhūte} evaṃ vadasi yo rūpasyānutpādo na tad rū-
25726 pam/ yo vedanāyāḥ saṃjñāyāḥ saṃskārāṇāṃ yo vijñānasyānutpādo na tad vijñānam/
25727 evaṃ vyastasamasteṣu skandhadhātvāyatanapratītyasamutpādeṣu pāramitāsu sarvaśūnya-
25728 tāsu sarvabodhipakṣeṣu dharmeṣu apramāṇadhyānārūpyasamāpattiṣu baleṣu vaiśāradyeṣu
children.translated_text:
has gone far (<s>āratā āramitā</s>). This, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, is why it is called <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. Gone far from what? Gone far from the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), <s>dhātus</s> (elements), <s>āyatanas</s> (sense-bases), <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination), the <s>dānapāramitā</s>, <s>śīlapāramitā</s>, [<s>kṣāntipāramitā</s>, <s>vīryapāramitā</s>, <s>dhyānapāramitā</s>,] and <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> — gone far. Gone far from <s>adhyātmaśūnyatā</s> (internal emptiness), [<s>bahirdhāśūnyatā</s> (external emptiness), <s>adhyātmabahirdhāśūnyatā</s> (internal-external emptiness),] up to <s>abhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of the non-existence of own-nature) — gone far. Gone far from the <s>smṛtyupasthānas</s> (foundations of mindfulness), [<s>samyakprahāṇas</s> (right efforts), <s>ṛddhipādas</s> (bases of power), <s>indriyas</s> (faculties), <s>balas</s> (powers), <s>bodhyaṅgas</s> (factors of awakening), the path, <s>apramāṇadhyānas</s> (immeasurable meditations), formless attainments, the ten powers, <s>vaiśāradyas</s> (fearlessnesses), <s>pratisaṃvids</s> (analytical knowledges), the eighteen exclusive] <s>buddhadharmas</s> — gone far. Up to <s>sarvajñatā</s> (omniscience) — gone far. This is why it is called <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. By this method, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> has gone far.
Now, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, as to your question: 'What is examination (<s>upaparīkṣaṇa</s>)?' Here, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, practicing <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, examines <s>rūpa</s> (form) as neither permanent nor impermanent, neither pleasant nor painful, neither self nor non-self, neither peaceful nor non-peaceful, neither empty nor non-empty, neither with signs nor signless, neither with wishes nor wishless, neither isolated nor non-isolated. He does not examine <s>vedanā</s> (feeling), <s>saṃjñā</s> (perception), <s>saṃskāras</s> (formations), or <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness) as permanent or impermanent, [nor as pleasant or painful, neither self nor non-self, neither peaceful nor non-peaceful, neither empty nor non-empty, neither with signs nor signless, neither with wishes nor wishless, neither isolated nor non-isolated.] Likewise the eye, ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind [are examined in the same way]. Likewise forms, sounds, smells, tastes, tangibles, and <s>dharmas</s> [are examined in the same way]. Likewise the eye-consciousness [and the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-consciousness are examined in the same way]. Likewise eye-contact [and ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-contact are examined in the same way]. Likewise the contact-born feelings [are examined in the same way]. Likewise <s>adhyātmaśūnyatā</s> (internal emptiness) [and all the other types of emptiness up to <s>parabhāvaśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of other-nature) are examined as neither permanent nor impermanent, neither pleasant nor painful, neither self nor non-self, neither peaceful nor non-peaceful, neither empty nor non-empty, neither with signs nor signless, neither with wishes nor wishless, neither isolated nor non-isolated.] Likewise the <s>smṛtyupasthānas</s> (foundations of mindfulness) [are examined in the same way. Likewise the <s>samyakprahāṇas</s> (right efforts), <s>ṛddhipādas</s> (bases of power), <s>indriyas</s> (faculties), <s>balas</s> (powers), <s>bodhyaṅgas</s> (factors of awakening), the path, immeasurable meditations, formless attainments, the ten powers, <s>vaiśāradyas</s> (fearlessnesses), <s>pratisaṃvids</s> (analytical knowledges), the eighteen exclusive] <s>buddhadharmas</s>, concentrations (<s>samādhis</s>), all <s>dhāraṇī</s>-gates, and <s>sarvajñatā</s> (omniscience) [are all examined as neither permanent nor impermanent, neither pleasant nor painful, neither self nor non-self, neither peaceful nor non-peaceful, neither empty nor non-empty, neither with signs nor signless, neither with wishes nor wishless, neither isolated nor non-isolated.] Thus, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, practicing <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, examines these <s>dharmas</s>.
<s>Śāriputra</s> said: 'For what reason, venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, do you say: "The non-arising of <s>rūpa</s> is not <s>rūpa</s>; the non-arising of <s>vedanā</s>, <s>saṃjñā</s>, <s>saṃskāras</s> — the non-arising of <s>vijñāna</s> is not <s>vijñāna</s>"? in the <s>pratisaṃvids</s> (analytical knowledges), in the <s>samādhi</s>- and <s>dhāraṇī</s>-gates, in the <s>abhijñās</s> (superknowledges), in the eighteen <s>āveṇika-buddhadharmas</s> (unique qualities of a Buddha)—the non-arising of <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> (omniscience in all aspects) is not <s>sarvākārajñatā</s>.
<s>Subhūti</s> said: Form, Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, is empty of form. And, Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, that emptiness is neither form nor arising. By this manner of explanation, Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, the non-arising of form is not form. <s>Vedanā</s> (feeling), <s>saṃjñā</s> (perception), <s>saṃskāras</s> (formations)—<s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness) is empty of <s>vijñāna</s>. And, Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, that emptiness is neither <s>vijñāna</s> nor arising. By this manner of explanation, Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, the non-arising of <s>vijñāna</s> is not <s>vijñāna</s>. <s>Dānapāramitā</s> (perfection of giving), Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, is empty of <s>dānapāramitā</s>. And, Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, that emptiness is neither <s>dānapāramitā</s> nor arising. By this manner of explanation, Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, the non-arising of <s>dānapāramitā</s> is not <s>dānapāramitā</s>. <s>Śīlapāramitā</s> (perfection of morality), <s>kṣāntipāramitā</s> (perfection of patience), <s>vīryapāramitā</s> (perfection of vigor), <s>dhyānapāramitā</s> (perfection of meditation)—<s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> (perfection of wisdom) is empty of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. And, Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, that emptiness is neither <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> nor arising. And, Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, that emptiness is neither <s>adhyātmaśūnyatā</s> nor arising. By this manner of explanation, the non-arising of <s>adhyātmaśūnyatā</s> is not <s>adhyātmaśūnyatā</s>. <s>Bahirdhāśūnyatā</s> (external emptiness), <s>adhyātmabahirdhāśūnyatā</s> (internal-external emptiness), <s>śūnyatāśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of emptiness), <s>mahāśūnyatā</s> (great emptiness), <s>paramārthaśūnyatā</s> (ultimate emptiness), <s>saṃskṛtaśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of the conditioned), <s>atyantaśūnyatā</s> (absolute emptiness), <s>anavarāgraśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of beginninglessness), <s>anavakāraśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of non-rejection), <s>prakṛtiśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of nature), <s>sarvadharmaśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of all dharmas), <s>svalakṣaṇaśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of own-characteristics), <s>anupalambhaśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of non-apprehension), <s>abhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of non-existence of self-nature), <s>bhāvaśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of existence), <s>abhāvaśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of non-existence), <s>svabhāvaśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of self-nature)—<s>parabhāvaśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of other-nature) is empty of <s>parabhāvaśūnyatā</s>. And, Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, that emptiness is neither <s>parabhāvaśūnyatā</s> nor arising. By this manner of explanation, the non-arising of <s>parabhāvaśūnyatā</s> is not <s>parabhāvaśūnyatā</s>.
The <s>smṛtyupasthānas</s> (foundations of mindfulness), Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, are empty of the <s>smṛtyupasthānas</s>. And, Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, that emptiness is neither the <s>smṛtyupasthānas</s> nor arising. By this manner of explanation, the non-arising of the <s>smṛtyupasthānas</s> is not the <s>smṛtyupasthānas</s>. The <s>samyakprahāṇas</s> (right efforts), <s>ṛddhipādas</s> (bases of power), <s>indriyas</s> (faculties), <s>balas</s> (powers), <s>bodhyaṅgas</s> (factors of awakening), <s>mārga</s> (path-factors), <s>apramāṇas</s> (immeasurables), <s>dhyānas</s>, <s>ārūpyasamāpattis</s> (formless attainments), the ten powers, <s>vaiśāradyas</s> (fearlessnesses), <s>pratisaṃvids</s> (analytical knowledges), the eighteen <s>āveṇika-buddhadharmas</s>, <s>sarvākārajñatā</s>—is empty of <s>sarvākārajñatā</s>. <s>Śāriputra</s> said: For what reason, Venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, do you say thus: 'The destruction of form is not form; the destruction of <s>vedanā</s>, <s>saṃjñā</s>, <s>saṃskāras</s>—the destruction of <s>vijñāna</s> is not <s>vijñāna</s>'? Non-arising is not other than consciousness; consciousness itself is non-arising, and non-arising itself is consciousness. By this method, Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, when one says 'form,' this designation has been made of the non-dual. Likewise for feeling, perception, and volitional formations — when one says 'consciousness,' this designation has been made of the non-dual. Likewise for the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), <s>dhātus</s> (elements), <s>āyatanas</s> (sense-bases), links of dependent origination, <s>pāramitās</s>, all the emptinesses, all the factors conducive to awakening (<s>bodhipakṣya dharma</s>), the immeasurables, <s>dhyānas</s>, formless attainments, powers, fearlessnesses, analytical knowledges, and gateways of <s>samādhi</s> and <s>dhāraṇī</s>, whether taken individually or collectively. For, Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, non-arising is not other than <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> (knowledge of all aspects); non-arising itself is <s>sarvākārajñatā</s>, and <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> itself is non-arising. By this method, Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, when one says '<s>sarvākārajñatā</s>,' this designation has been made of the non-dual. Furthermore, the Venerable <s>Subhūti</s> said this to the Blessed One: At the time, Blessed One, when a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, coursing in <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, examines these <s>dharmas</s>, at that time he perceives the non-arising of form, based on absolute purity. Likewise for feeling, perception, and volitional formations — he perceives the non-arising of consciousness, based on absolute purity. He perceives the non-arising of the self, based on absolute purity. Likewise for being, life-force, sustainer, person, individual, human, youth, doer, experiencer, knower, and seer — he perceives the non-arising (of each), based on absolute purity. Likewise for the <s>skandhas</s>, <s>dhātus</s>, <s>āyatanas</s>, links of dependent origination, and superknowledges (<s>abhijñā</s>), whether taken individually or collectively. He perceives the non-arising of the perfection of generosity (<s>dānapāramitā</s>), based on absolute purity; likewise for the perfections of morality, patience, vigor, meditation, and wisdom; the internal emptiness (<s>adhyātmaśūnyatā</s>), external emptiness, the emptiness of both, emptiness of emptiness, great emptiness, ultimate emptiness, the emptiness of the conditioned, absolute emptiness, the emptiness of what is without beginning or end, the emptiness of non-rejection, the emptiness of inherent nature, the emptiness of all <s>dharmas</s>, the emptiness of own-characteristics, the emptiness of non-apprehension, the emptiness of the non-existence of inherent nature, the emptiness of existence, the emptiness of non-existence, the emptiness of own-nature, and the emptiness of other-nature. He perceives the non-arising of the foundations of mindfulness (<s>smṛtyupasthāna</s>), based on absolute purity; likewise the right efforts, bases of supernatural power, faculties, powers, factors of awakening, path, immeasurables, <s>dhyānas</s>, formless attainments, ten powers, fearlessnesses, analytical knowledges, and eighteen unique qualities of a <s>Buddha</s>. He perceives the non-arising of <s>sarvākārajñatā</s>, based on absolute purity. He perceives the non-arising of the ordinary person (<s>pṛthagjana</s>) and the <s>dharmas</s> of the ordinary person, based on absolute purity. Likewise for the stream-enterer and the <s>dharmas</s> of the stream-enterer, the once-returner and the <s>dharmas</s> of the once-returner, the non-returner and the <s>dharmas</s> of the non-returner, the <s>arhat</s> and the <s>dharmas</s> of the <s>arhat</s>, the <s>pratyekabuddha</s> and the <s>dharmas</s> of the <s>pratyekabuddha</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s> and the <s>dharmas</s> of the <s>bodhisattva</s>. He perceives the non-arising of the <s>Buddha</s> and the <s>Buddha</s> <s>dharmas</s>, based on absolute purity. <s>Śāriputra</s> said: As I understand the meaning of the Venerable <s>Subhūti</s>'s statement, form is non-arising, feeling, perception, volitional formations, and consciousness are non-arising; all the <s>skandhas</s>, whether taken individually or collectively, are non-arising; the <s>dhātus</s> are non-arising. The self is non-arising, being, life-force, sustainer, person, individual, human, youth, doer, experiencer, knower, and seer are non-arising. The <s>skandhas</s>, <s>dhātus</s>, <s>āyatanas</s>, links of dependent origination, and superknowledges are non-arising. The perfections of generosity, morality, patience, vigor, meditation, and wisdom are non-arising. All the emptinesses from internal emptiness through the emptiness of other-nature are non-arising. The foundations of mindfulness, right efforts, bases of supernatural power, faculties, powers, factors of awakening, path, immeasurables, <s>dhyānas</s>, formless attainments, ten powers, fearlessnesses, analytical knowledges, eighteen unique <s>Buddha</s> qualities, and <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> are non-arising. The ordinary person and the <s>dharmas</s> of the ordinary person are non-arising; the stream-enterer and the <s>dharmas</s> of the stream-enterer, the once-returner, the non-returner, the <s>arhat</s>, the <s>pratyekabuddha</s>, and the <s>bodhisattva</s> and their respective <s>dharmas</s> are non-arising. The <s>Buddha</s> is non-arising; the <s>Buddha</s> <s>dharmas</s> are non-arising. But if, Venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, form too is non-arising, and the <s>Buddha</s> <s>dharmas</s> too are non-arising — then surely the <s>śrāvaka</s> (hearer) has already attained the awakening of a <s>śrāvaka</s>, the follower of the <s>pratyekabuddha</s> vehicle has already attained the awakening of a <s>pratyekabuddha</s>, and the <s>bodhisattva</s> has already attained <s>sarvākārajñatā</s>! 26001 the path must be cultivated for the abandonment of the three fetters. By a once-returner, the path must be cultivated for the diminishment of passion, hatred,
26002 and delusion. By a non-returner, the path must be cultivated for the abandonment of the five lower
26003 fetters. By an <s>Arhat</s>, the path must be cultivated for the abandonment of the five upper
26004 fetters. By those on the <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> vehicle, the path must be cultivated for the attainment of <s>Pratyekabodhi</s>.
26005 For what reason does a <s>bodhisattva</s> practice difficult practices, experiencing
26006 the sufferings of beings one by one? For what reason has the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly
26007 Awakened One, awakened to unsurpassed perfect awakening? For what reason has the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly
26008 Awakened One, turned the wheel of <s>Dharma</s>?
26009 <s>Subhūti</s> said: I do not, Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, wish for the attainment of an unarisen <s>dharma</s>, nor for its
26010 realization. I do not wish for a stream-enterer of non-arising, nor for the fruit of stream-entry, nor for a once-returner, nor for the fruit of once-returning, nor for a non-returner, nor for the fruit of non-returning,
26011 nor for <s>Arhatship</s>, nor for the fruit of <s>Arhatship</s>. I do not wish for <s>Pratyekabodhi</s> of non-arising, nor for <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>hood. Nor do I,
26012 Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, wish for a <s>bodhisattva</s> practicing difficult practices, nor does the <s>bodhisattva</s> practice with the notion
26013 of difficulty. For what reason? For it is not possible, Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, while abiding in the notion of difficulty,
26014 to benefit immeasurable, incalculable, and boundless beings. Rather,
26015 Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, by generating the perception of all beings as mother, the perception of them as father, brother, son, and self —
26016 [only then] is it possible to benefit immeasurable, incalculable, and boundless beings.
26017 Moreover, Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, the <s>bodhisattva-mahāsattva</s> should generate this thought: Just as
26018 the self is called 'self,' yet ultimately the self is unarisen — even so, with regard to all internal and
26019 external <s>dharmas</s>, such a perception should be generated. If one generates such a perception, there will be no notion
26020 of difficulty. For what reason? For those <s>bodhisattvas</s> do not produce, do not apprehend, in every way, altogether,
26021 any <s>dharma</s> whatsoever. I do not, Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, wish for a <s>Tathāgata</s> of non-arising,
26022 nor for unsurpassed perfect awakening, nor for the turning of the wheel of <s>Dharma</s>, nor do I wish for
26023 an unarisen attainment being attained by an unarisen <s>dharma</s>.
26024 <s>Śāriputra</s> said: But, Venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, is an arisen attainment attained by an unarisen <s>dharma</s>?
26025 Or is an unarisen attainment attained by an arisen <s>dharma</s>?

26101 <s>Subhūti</s> said: I do not, Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, wish for an unarisen attainment being attained
26102 by an arisen <s>dharma</s>, nor for an arisen attainment being attained by an unarisen <s>dharma</s>.
26103 <s>Śāriputra</s> said: Then, Venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, do you wish for attainment by an unarisen <s>dharma</s>?
26104 Or do you wish for attainment by an arisen <s>dharma</s>?
26105 <s>Subhūti</s> said: I do not, Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, wish for attainment by an unarisen <s>dharma</s>,
26106 nor do I wish for attainment by an arisen <s>dharma</s>.
26107 <s>Śāriputra</s> said: Then, Venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, is there no attainment and no realization?
26108 <s>Subhūti</s> said: There is, Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, attainment and realization, but not through duality. Moreover,
26109 Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, attainment and realization are designated by worldly convention;
26110 a stream-enterer, a once-returner, a non-returner, an <s>Arhat</s>, a <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>,
26111 a <s>bodhisattva</s>, or a <s>Buddha</s> is designated by worldly convention. But in the ultimate sense, there is no attainment, no realization,
26112 no stream-enterer, no once-returner, no non-returner, no <s>Arhat</s>, no <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>, no <s>bodhisattva</s>,
26113 no <s>Buddha</s>.
26114 <s>Śāriputra</s> said: Venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, you are inspired to discourse on 'unarisen <s>dharma</s>.'
26115 <s>Subhūti</s> said: As you say, Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, 'unarisen <s>dharma</s>, unarisen <s>dharma</s> — you are inspired
26116 to discourse [on this]' — non-arising too, Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, is [something one] is inspired to discourse on.
26117 For what reason? For, Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, the unarisen <s>dharma</s>, and inspired discourse, and discourses,
26118 and non-arising — all these <s>dharmas</s> are neither conjoined nor disjoined, immaterial, invisible,
26119 non-obstructive, of a single characteristic, namely characterlessness.
26120 <s>Śāriputra</s> said: Venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, non-arising is also a discourse; non-arising is inspired speech;
26121 non-arising is a <s>dharma</s>; those <s>dharmas</s> too are unarisen with reference to which one is inspired to discourse.
26122 <s>Subhūti</s> said: So it is, Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, non-arising is a discourse;
26123 non-arising is inspired speech; non-arising is a <s>dharma</s>; those <s>dharmas</s> too are unarisen with reference to which one is inspired to discourse. For what reason? For, Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>,
26124 <s>rūpa</s> (form) is non-arising. Likewise, <s>vedanā</s>, <s>saṃjñā</s>, and <s>saṃskāras</s>. <s>Vijñāna</s> is non-arising. Likewise, severally and collectively, the <s>skandhas</s>, <s>dhātus</s>,
26125 <s>āyatanas</s>, <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s>, <s>pāramitās</s>, all emptinesses, all <s>bodhipakṣa dharmas</s>, <s>apramāṇas</s>, <s>dhyānas</s>, formless attainments, powers, fearlessnesses, analytical knowledges, <s>samādhis</s>, <s>dhāraṇīmukhas</s>, <s>abhijñās</s>, and the eighteen unique <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s> — all are non-arising.

a <s>srotaāpanna</s> (stream-enterer), [a <s>sakṛdāgāmin</s> (once-returner), an <s>anāgāmin</s> (non-returner), an <s>arhat</s>,] a <s>pratyekabuddha</s>, a <s>bodhisattva</s>, an omniscient one, a knower of all aspects — even <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> (knowledge of all aspects) is non-arising.
<s>Śāriputra</s> said: 'So it is, venerable <s>Subhūti</s>. Non-arising is counsel (<s>mantra</s>), [non-arising is eloquence (<s>pratibhāna</s>), non-arising is <s>dharma</s>, and those <s>dharmas</s> too are unarisen on account of which one speaks eloquently and gives counsel.] Up to the <s>skandhas</s>, <s>dhātus</s>, <s>āyatanas</s>, [<s>pratītyasamutpāda</s>, <s>pāramitās</s>, all types of <s>śūnyatā</s>, all <s>bodhipakṣadharmas</s>, immeasurable meditations, formless attainments, the powers, fearlessnesses, analytical knowledges, <s>samādhi</s>-gates, <s>dhāraṇī</s>-gates, <s>abhijñās</s> (superknowledges), the eighteen exclusive] <s>buddhadharmas</s> — abbreviated — up to even <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> is non-arising.'
<s>Śāriputra</s> said: 'Furthermore, venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, just as attainment and realization exist by way of worldly convention, does the distinction of the five destinies (<s>gatis</s>) also exist by worldly convention but not in the ultimate sense?'
<s>Subhūti</s> said: 'So it is, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, so it is. Just as attainment and realization [exist by worldly convention, so the distinction of the five destinies exists by worldly convention but not in the ultimate sense.] Not indeed by the ultimate sense. For what reason? For, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, in the ultimate sense (<s>paramārtha</s>) there is no <s>karma</s> (action), no <s>vipāka</s> (result), no arising, no cessation, no defilement, and no purification.'
<s>Śāriputra</s> said: 'Furthermore, venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, does an unarisen <s>dharma</s> arise, or does an arisen <s>dharma</s> arise?'
<s>Subhūti</s> said: 'I do not wish for the arising of an arisen <s>dharma</s>, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, nor do I wish for the arising of an unarisen <s>dharma</s>.'
<s>Śāriputra</s> said: 'Of which unarisen <s>dharma</s>, venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, do you not wish the arising?'
<s>Subhūti</s> said: 'I do not wish, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, the arising — which is empty of own-nature (<s>svabhāvaśūnya</s>) — of <s>rūpa</s> (form) as an unarisen <s>dharma</s>. [Likewise for <s>vedanā</s> (feeling), <s>saṃjñā</s> (perception), <s>saṃskāras</s> (formations).] I do not wish, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, the arising — which is empty of own-nature — of <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness) as an unarisen <s>dharma</s>. Likewise, separately and collectively, for <s>skandhas</s>, <s>dhātus</s>, <s>āyatanas</s>, [<s>pratītyasamutpāda</s>, <s>pāramitās</s>, all types of <s>śūnyatā</s>, all <s>bodhipakṣadharmas</s>, immeasurable meditations, formless attainments, powers, fearlessnesses, analytical knowledges, <s>samādhi</s>-gates, <s>dhāraṇī</s>-gates, <s>abhijñās</s>, the eighteen exclusive] <s>buddhadharmas</s> — I do not wish, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, the arising of <s>bodhi</s> (awakening) which is unarisen and empty of own-nature.'
<s>Śāriputra</s> said: 'Furthermore, venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, does arising (<s>utpāda</s>) arise, or does non-arising (<s>anutpāda</s>) arise?'
<s>Subhūti</s> said: 'Neither does arising arise, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, nor does non-arising arise. For what reason? For, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, both arising and non-arising — these two <s>dharmas</s> — are neither conjoined nor disjoined, formless, invisible, non-resistant, of a single characteristic, namely no-characteristic. By this method, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, neither does arising arise, nor does non-arising arise. By this method, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, non-arising is counsel, non-arising is eloquence. Non-arising is <s>dharma</s>, and those <s>dharmas</s> too are unarisen on account of which one speaks eloquently and gives counsel.'

<s>Śāriputra</s> said: The Venerable <s>Subhūti</s> should be placed foremost among those who have the <s>dharmakāya</s> (truth-body). For what reason? Because whatever the Venerable <s>Subhūti</s> is questioned about, from each and every question he emerges [with the answer].
<s>Subhūti</s> said: This is the <s>dharmatā</s> (nature of reality), Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s disciples who are non-reliant upon all <s>dharmas</s>—from wherever they are questioned, from there they emerge [with the answer]. For what reason? Because all <s>dharmas</s> are non-reliant.
<s>Śāriputra</s> said: How, Venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, are all <s>dharmas</s> non-reliant?
<s>Subhūti</s> said: Form, Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, is empty by nature. That is not supported internally, not supported externally, nor is it apprehended in between. <s>Vedanā</s> (feeling), <s>saṃjñā</s> (perception), <s>saṃskāras</s> (formations)—<s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness), Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, is empty by nature. That is not supported internally, not supported externally, nor is it apprehended in between. The eye, Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, is empty by nature. That is not supported internally, not supported externally, nor is it apprehended in between. The ear, nose, tongue, body—the mind, Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, is empty by nature. That is not supported internally, not supported externally, nor is it apprehended in between. Form, Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, is empty by nature. That is not supported internally, not supported externally, nor is it apprehended in between. Sound, smell, taste, touch—<s>dharmas</s>, Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, are empty by nature. They are not supported internally, not supported externally, nor are they apprehended in between. Eye-consciousness, Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, is empty by nature. That is not supported internally, not supported externally, nor is it apprehended in between. Ear-consciousness, nose-consciousness, tongue-consciousness, body-consciousness—mind-consciousness, Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, is empty by nature. That is not supported internally, not supported externally, nor is it apprehended in between. The <s>smṛtyupasthānas</s> (foundations of mindfulness), Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, are empty by nature. They are not supported internally, not supported externally, nor are they apprehended in between. The <s>samyakprahāṇas</s> (right efforts), <s>ṛddhipādas</s> (bases of power), <s>indriyas</s> (faculties), <s>balas</s> (powers), <s>bodhyaṅgas</s> (factors of awakening), the <s>mārga</s> (path-factors), the <s>apramāṇas</s> (immeasurables), <s>dhyānas</s>, <s>ārūpyasamāpattis</s> (formless attainments), the ten powers, the <s>vaiśāradyas</s> (fearlessnesses), the <s>pratisaṃvids</s> (analytical knowledges)—the eighteen <s>āveṇika-buddhadharmas</s> (unique qualities of a Buddha), Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, are empty by nature. They are not supported internally, not supported externally, nor are they apprehended in between. By this manner of explanation, Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, all <s>dharmas</s> are non-reliant, on account of being empty by nature.
Thus, Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> practicing the six <s>pāramitās</s> should purify form. <s>Vedanā</s>, <s>saṃjñā</s>, <s>saṃskāras</s>—<s>vijñāna</s> should be purified. Likewise, singly and collectively, the <s>skandhas</s>, <s>dhātus</s>, <s>āyatanas</s>, <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination), the <s>pāramitās</s>, all forms of <s>śūnyatā</s>, all <s>bodhipakṣa</s> (factors of awakening) <s>dharmas</s>, the <s>apramāṇas</s>, <s>dhyānas</s>, <s>ārūpyasamāpattis</s>, the powers, fearlessnesses, <s>pratisaṃvids</s>, <s>samādhi</s>- and <s>dhāraṇī</s>-gates, <s>abhijñās</s> (superknowledges), the eighteen <s>āveṇika-buddhadharmas</s> should be purified. And so on up to: <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> (omniscience in all aspects) should be purified. [Thus the going forth to <s>sarvākārajñatā</s>.]
<s>Śāriputra</s> said: How, Venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, does a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> practicing the six <s>pāramitās</s> purify the <s>bodhisattva</s> path?

<s>Śāriputra</s> said: Which, Venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, is the worldly <s>dānapāramitā</s>, and which is the supramundane?
