shelter, lodging, livelihood, personal effects, accessories, bedding, seats, or medicine—he gives food, drink, vehicles, garments, perfume, garlands, ointments, flowers, incense, powders, cloth, shelter, lodging, or whatever else—livelihood, personal effects, accessories, and medicine. To those wanting sons he gives sons. To those wanting daughters he gives daughters. To those wanting wives he gives wives. To those wanting kingdoms he gives kingdoms. To those wanting a head he gives his head. To those wanting limbs he gives limbs. To those wanting flesh, blood, and marrow he gives flesh, blood, and marrow.
But he relinquishes this with reliance. He thinks thus: 'I give, this one receives, this is the gift. I am without jealousy. I relinquish all that I have. I am carrying out the <s>Buddha</s>'s instruction. I am practicing the <s>dānapāramitā</s>. Having made this gift common to all beings, I dedicate it to <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> (supreme perfect awakening)—and this through the method of non-apprehension. And through this gift and the fruit of this gift, may all beings in this very life be happy and may they attain <s>parinirvāṇa</s> without clinging.' He gives this gift attached by three attachments. Which three? Namely, the perception of self, the perception of other, and the perception of the gift. Attached by these three attachments, he gives the gift. [This is called the worldly <s>dānapāramitā</s>.]
Because, Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, it does not move from, does not rise above, does not pass beyond the world—therefore it is called the worldly <s>dānapāramitā</s>.
And what is the supramundane <s>dānapāramitā</s>? Namely, the purity of the three spheres (<s>trimaṇḍalapariśuddhi</s>). And what is the purity of the three spheres? Here a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, while giving a gift, does not apprehend a self, does not apprehend a recipient, does not apprehend a gift, and does not apprehend its result. This, Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, is the purity of the three spheres of a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>. Furthermore, Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, while giving a gift, does not deliver that gift to all beings. He does not apprehend beings. He does not apprehend a self. And he dedicates that gift to <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> (supreme perfect awakening), yet he does not apprehend <s>bodhi</s>. [This is called the supramundane <s>dānapāramitā</s>.]

children.translated_text: For what reason is it called the transcendent (<s>lokottara</s>) perfection of generosity? Because, Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, it moves, rises above, and crosses beyond the world. For that reason it is called the transcendent perfection of generosity. Likewise for the perfection of morality, patience, vigor, and meditation. <s>Śāriputra</s> said: Which, Venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, is the worldly (<s>laukikī</s>) <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>? And which is the transcendent? <s>Subhūti</s> said: The worldly <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, is this: Here a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> gives gifts while relying on apprehension, thinking 'I must overcome the thought of miserliness.' Relying on the perception of self, being, gift, and awakening, he relinquishes all possessions — whether external or internal, whether grasped or ungrasped — there is nothing he does not relinquish. And those wholesome roots he dedicates to awakening, making them shared with all beings, while relying on apprehension. He cultivates morality, established in the <s>dhūtaguṇas</s> (ascetic qualities), relying on the apprehension of body, speech, and mind. While following those ten wholesome paths of action, relying on the view of self, the view of beings, and the view of wholesome, apprehending awakening, he dedicates his morality — shared with all beings — to awakening, and that too with apprehension. He praises himself and disparages others. He patiently endures the misdeeds of all beings, relying on the view of self, being, patience, and (awakening). Those wholesome (roots) he dedicates to <s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s> (unsurpassed perfect awakening), making them shared with all beings, through the method of apprehension. He exerts vigor while apprehending the body, apprehending the mind, apprehending the accumulation of merit, apprehending the accumulation of knowledge, apprehending the self, apprehending awakening — and he is conceited about that exertion of vigor. That too, making it shared with all beings, he dedicates through the method of apprehension to unsurpassed perfect awakening. He cultivates loving-kindness (<s>maitrī</s>), compassion (<s>karuṇā</s>), sympathetic joy (<s>muditā</s>), and equanimity (<s>upekṣā</s>); he enters into the <s>dhyāna</s> attainments and rises from them and relishes them. Relishing them, he is conceited. And those wholesome roots, shared with all beings, he dedicates to awakening with the view of apprehension. [This is called the worldly <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.] He cultivates emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>), (yet) apprehends that 'form is empty.' Likewise for feeling, perception, and volitional formations — he apprehends that 'consciousness is empty.' He even apprehends <s>buddhabodhi</s> (awakening of the <s>Buddha</s>) through the method of apprehension. Those wholesome roots, making them shared with all beings, he dedicates to unsurpassed perfect awakening. That

children.translated_text: [This is called the worldly <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.] And which is the transcendent (<s>lokottarā</s>) <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>? Through the non-apprehension of self, being, gift, and awakening, and through the purification of the three spheres (<s>trimaṇḍalapariśuddhi</s>), he purifies the perfection of generosity (<s>dānapāramitā</s>). For the sake of awakening, through the non-apprehension of self, being, morality, and awakening, and through the purification of the three spheres, he purifies the perfection of morality (<s>śīlapāramitā</s>). For the sake of awakening, through the non-apprehension of self, being, forbearance, and awakening, and through the purification of the three spheres, he purifies the perfection of patience (<s>kṣāntipāramitā</s>). For the sake of awakening, through the non-apprehension of self, body, mind, vigor, merit, knowledge, and awakening, and through the purification of the three spheres, he purifies the perfection of vigor (<s>vīryapāramitā</s>). For the sake of awakening, through the non-apprehension of self, being, <s>dhyāna</s>, <s>samādhi</s>, attainment, and awakening, and through the purification of the three spheres, he purifies the perfection of meditation (<s>dhyānapāramitā</s>). For the sake of awakening, through the non-apprehension of self, being, and all <s>dharmas</s>, and through the purification of the three spheres, he purifies <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. For the sake of awakening, he dedicates all wholesome roots to unsurpassed perfect awakening through a dedication that is without distinction, unsurpassed, equal to the unequalled, inconceivable and incomparable, and immeasurable.

children.translated_text: [This is called the transcendent <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.] For what reason is it called worldly (<s>laukikī</s>)? Those (perfections) by which the world comes into being; or those by which one turns the world around; or those which are equal to the world; or those which are given for the world; or those by which one goes out from the world; or those which serve for the existence of the world; or those which involve existence in the world — those are called worldly. And which is the transcendent? Those by which one raises up the world; or those by which one lifts the world; or those by which one is raised beyond the world; or those which serve for illumination; or those by which one goes forth from the world; or those which serve for the crossing over of the world; or those which are superior in the world — those are called transcendent. Thus, Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>, coursing in the six <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections), purifies the path to awakening (<s>bodhimārga</s>). <s>Śāriputra</s> said: Which, Venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, is the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s>'s path to awakening?

26701 <s>Subhūti</s> said: The four <s>smṛtyupasthānas</s> (foundations of mindfulness), Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, are the <s>bodhisattva-mahāsattva</s>'s path to
26702 awakening. The four <s>samyakprahāṇas</s> (right exertions), four <s>ṛddhipādas</s> (bases of miraculous power), five <s>indriyas</s> (faculties), five <s>balas</s> (powers),
26703 <s>bodhyaṅgas</s> (factors of awakening), the noble eightfold path, the <s>śūnyatāvimokṣamukha</s> (gateway of liberation through emptiness), <s>animittavimokṣamukha</s> (gateway of liberation through signlessness), <s>apraṇihitavimokṣamukha</s> (gateway of liberation through wishlessness),
26704 <s>adhyātmaśūnyatā</s> (internal emptiness), <s>bahirdhāśūnyatā</s> (external emptiness), <s>adhyātmabahirdhāśūnyatā</s> (internal-external emptiness), up to <s>abhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of the nature of non-existence), all <s>samādhis</s>,
26705 all <s>dhāraṇīmukhas</s> (gateways of retention), the four <s>apramāṇas</s> (immeasurables), four <s>dhyānas</s>, four formless
26706 attainments, ten <s>Tathāgata</s> powers, four fearlessnesses, four analytical knowledges, eighteen
26707 unique <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>, and <s>mahākaruṇā</s> (great compassion) — this, Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, is called the <s>bodhisattva-mahāsattva</s>'s
26708 path to awakening.
26709 <s>Śāriputra</s> said: Of which <s>pāramitā</s>, Venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, is this the endeavor?
26710 <s>Subhūti</s> said: Of the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, is this the endeavor. For what
26711 reason? For, Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is the genetrix of all wholesome <s>dharmas</s>,
26712 of <s>Śrāvaka</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> <s>dharmas</s>, of <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>dharmas</s>, and of <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>. The <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>,
26713 is the receptacle of all wholesome <s>dharmas</s>, of <s>Śrāvaka</s>, <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>, and <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>dharmas</s>. Having trained
26714 in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, those former <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones, awakened to unsurpassed
26715 perfect awakening. Future <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>,
26716 Perfectly Awakened Ones too, Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, will awaken to unsurpassed perfect awakening by training in this very <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.
26717 Those <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones too who presently, Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, abide, endure, sustain, and teach the <s>Dharma</s>
26718 in the world-systems of the ten directions — they too, all of them, having trained in this very
26719 <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, have awakened to unsurpassed perfect awakening.
26720 If, moreover, Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, when this <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is being taught, the <s>bodhisattva</s>-
26721 <s>mahāsattva</s> has no wavering, has no hesitation — it should be known, Venerable
26722 <s>Śāriputra</s>, that this <s>bodhisattva-mahāsattva</s> abides in this abiding and is not separated from this mental attention,
26723 namely the mental attention of rescuing all beings, the mental attention of not abandoning all beings, the mental attention
26724 of <s>mahākaruṇā</s> (great compassion).
26725 <s>Śāriputra</s> said: Since Venerable <s>Subhūti</s> says: 'This <s>bodhisattva-mahāsattva</s> abides in this
26726 abiding and is not separated from this mental attention' — then, Venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, all beings too would

26801 become <s>bodhisattvas</s>. For what reason? For, Venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, all beings

26803 <s>Subhūti</s> said: Well said, well said, Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>! I shall commend you — the meaning has indeed been grasped
26804 by Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> through an expression of truth. For what reason? By the non-existence of beings, Venerable
26805 <s>Śāriputra</s>, the non-existence of mental attention is to be understood. By the emptiness of beings, the emptiness of mental attention is to be understood.
26806 By the naturelessness of beings, the naturelessness of mental attention is to be understood. By the seclusion of beings, the seclusion
26807 of mental attention is to be understood. By the non-awakening of beings, the non-awakening of mental attention
26808 is to be understood. By the non-existence of <s>rūpa</s> (form), its emptiness, its naturelessness, its seclusion,
26809 and its non-awakening, the non-awakening of mental attention is to be understood. <s>Vedanā</s>, <s>saṃjñā</s>,
26810 <s>saṃskāras</s> — by the non-existence of <s>vijñāna</s>, its emptiness, its naturelessness, its seclusion, and its non-awakening, the non-awakening of mental attention is to be understood. Likewise, severally and collectively, in the
26811 <s>skandhas</s>, <s>dhātus</s>, <s>āyatanas</s>, <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s>, <s>pāramitās</s>, all emptinesses, all <s>bodhipakṣa dharmas</s>, <s>apramāṇas</s>, <s>dhyānas</s>, formless attainments, powers, fearlessnesses, analytical knowledges, <s>samādhis</s>, <s>dhāraṇīmukhas</s>, <s>abhijñās</s>, and the eighteen unique <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s> — by the non-existence of <s>sarvākārajñatā</s>, its
26812 emptiness, its naturelessness, its seclusion, and its non-awakening, the non-awakening of mental attention is to be understood. By this abiding, Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, and by this
26813 mental attention, the <s>bodhisattva-mahāsattva</s> is not separated [from it].
26814 Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> uttered words of commendation to Venerable <s>Subhūti</s>: Well said, well said, <s>Subhūti</s>!
26815 Thus indeed, <s>Subhūti</s>, should the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> be taught to <s>bodhisattva-mahāsattvas</s> — just as you teach it.
26816 And just as by the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s power the <s>bodhisattva-mahāsattva</s> should practice the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>
26817 — just as you teach.

26819 the trichiliocosm (<s>trisāhasramahāsāhasra lokadhātu</s>) trembled in six ways, up to: shaking and quaking in the northeastern, southern,
26820 and western intermediate directions.
